author: Maria Martha Bruno
title: Derrota dos Republicanos nos EUA tem mais a ver com economia que democracia, diz socióloga
content:
Com a vitória avassaladora do Partido Democrata nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos (as chamadas 

midterms

), o “recado das urnas”, na opinião da socióloga e cientista política Gisele Agnelli, foi a economia. 

A promessa central que elegeu Donald Trump em 2024 — a 

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra — “não se materializou na percepção de grande parte dos eleitores”.




Membro do Hoosier Women Forward, um dos movimentos de lideranças femininas do Partido Democrata, ela afirma que o resultado não aponta para um alinhamento da população com o partido. Para Agnelli, os eleitores reprovaram o mandato do presidente republicano e cobraram o não cumprimento da principal promessa de campanha, a redução do custo de vida das famílias norte-americanas.




Por isso, antes de apontar semelhanças entre a vitória de Lula e a derrota de Trump, ela ressalta que os motivos que moveram os eleitores em ambos os países foram distintos, embora a ameaça antidemocrática estivesse em jogo nos dois pleitos: 

“Não acredito que a defesa da democracia tenha sido o fator decisivo das 

midterms

“.




No futuro, ela vislumbra oportunidades para o Brasil e um cenário exige “reflexão estratégica do governo Lula e, particularmente, do PT”. Com os canais diplomáticos oficiais quase monopolizados pelo bolsonarismo instalado nos EUA, ela aponta a chance do governo estabelecer contato com o próprio Congresso norte-americano, agora com maioria democrata no Senado e na Câmara dos Representantes (equivalente à nossa Câmara dos Deputados).




“A esquerda brasileira precisa distinguir a crítica histórica ao intervencionismo dos EUA da capacidade de construir alianças institucionais dentro da própria democracia americana”, analisa.




E antes de que muitos se empolguem com os resultados, Agnelli destaca que as dificuldades para Trump não necessariamente se traduzirão no desmonte da poderosa estrutura administrativa e política montada por ele. Gisela também não acredita “que veremos menos agressividade” por parte do presidente. “Um presidente com menos espaço no Legislativo pode recorrer ainda mais aos instrumentos unilaterais no Executivo”, aponta.




Qual sua avaliação geral sobre as 

midterms

?




O grande derrotado foi Trump, mas não necessariamente o vencedor foi o Partido Democrata. O presidente acabou se tornando o principal alvo do descontentamento expresso nas urnas.




As eleições confirmaram, de forma contundente, uma máxima clássica da ciência política: as 

midterms

 funcionam como um referendo sobre a popularidade presidencial, a percepção do desempenho econômico e o desejo do eleitorado de contrabalançar o poder do partido que ocupa a Casa Branca.




Embora Trump também tenha se consolidado como um fator de desestabilização institucional, 

o recado mais significativo das urnas foi econômico.

 A promessa central de sua campanha de 2024 — a 

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra das famílias americanas — não se materializou para grande parte dos eleitores.




Os democratas exploraram essa frustração com uma campanha essencialmente pragmática, concentrada no custo da alimentação, da moradia, dos combustíveis e dos serviços de saúde. 

Em vez de restringir a disputa à defesa abstrata da democracia ou à condenação moral do trumpismo, conseguiram traduzir o descontentamento em questões concretas do cotidiano.




A contradição entre promessa e governo foi agravada pelas próprias escolhas da administração Trump. A guerra contra o Irã, com seus efeitos sobre os preços da energia, e a política tarifária, que pressionou custos, contribuíram para alimentar a percepção de perda de poder aquisitivo.




Há também uma contradição política fundamental: Trump foi eleito prometendo “America First”, a priorização dos interesses domésticos e o fim do envolvimento americano em guerras externas custosas. No entanto, 

seu governo dedicou enorme energia política e recursos à agenda internacional, em detrimento das promessas econômicas para o eleitor americano.

 Essa ruptura desgastou sua popularidade e também aprofundou divisões dentro do próprio campo republicano.




Que aspecto da eleição mais chamou sua atenção?




O primeiro é o 

limite do redistritamento eleitoral

 como instrumento de preservação do poder. Mesmo diante de mapas distritais redesenhados para favorecer candidaturas republicanas, em alguns casos com consequências especialmente negativas para a representação de minorias, 

a insatisfação do eleitorado mostrou capacidade de superar vantagens estruturais.




O segundo é o limite do dinheiro na competição eleitoral. O protagonismo de Elon Musk como grande financiador individual, os gastos republicanos de centenas de milhões de dólares e o volume extraordinário de recursos mobilizados em disputas em estados como Texas, Michigan e Kansas demonstraram que 

nem mesmo campanhas financeiramente poderosas conseguem neutralizar um eleitorado muito insatisfeito.
















O bilionário americano Elon Musk teria despejado quase meio bilhão de dólares na campanha de republicanos no Texas, que perderam no estado




O dinheiro pode ampliar a exposição de um candidato, financiar publicidade e fortalecer estruturas partidárias. Mas não é capaz, por si só, de transformar frustração econômica em aprovação política.




Outro elemento decisivo foi o comportamento dos eleitores independentes. Eles funcionaram como fiéis da balança, aproximando-se dos democratas não necessariamente por identificação ideológica com o partido, mas pela disposição de derrotar Trump.




O eleitorado latino também merece atenção especial.

 Longe de ser um bloco homogêneo, esse segmento apresentou oscilações importantes nos últimos ciclos eleitorais. Em 2024, preocupações econômicas aproximaram parte significativa desses eleitores do Partido Republicano, rompendo padrões tradicionais de identificação com democratas.




Agora, a combinação entre frustração econômica e a política migratória agressiva do governo, especialmente a atuação do ICE, contribuiu para penalizar candidaturas republicanas. A experiência concreta com as políticas de governo voltou a pesar mais do que as identificações partidárias.




Por isso, 

seria precipitado interpretar os resultados como uma transformação estrutural do eleitorado americano em direção ao Partido Democrata.

 O próprio partido enfrenta problemas de popularidade, identidade e capacidade de mobilização.




O que as urnas revelaram foi menos uma adesão entusiasmada aos democratas do que uma rejeição contundente ao trumpismo no exercício do poder. Essa distinção é fundamental. 

O eleitor que ajudou a eleger Trump em 2024 não necessariamente se tornou democrata em 2026.

 Em muitos casos, simplesmente concluiu que as promessas que justificaram seu voto não foram cumpridas.




Não se trata necessariamente de uma guinada ideológica à esquerda. Trata-se de um eleitorado cobrando a conta de um governo que prometeu melhorar sua vida — e que, na sua percepção, falhou em entregar.







O eleitor que ajudou a eleger Trump em 2024 não necessariamente se tornou democrata em 2026. Em muitos casos, simplesmente concluiu que as promessas que justificaram seu voto não foram cumpridas.







Quais as implicações das 

midterms

 para os bolsonaristas que moram nos EUA?




Em 30 de outubro, 25 congressistas democratas, liderados por Sydney Kamlager-Dove e Dina Titus, solicitaram explicações ao secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, sobre a eventual participação de autoridades americanas na saída de Flávio Bolsonaro do Brasil e em sua entrada nos EUA, apesar das restrições judiciais brasileiras.




Uma maioria democrata poderia aprofundar essa fiscalização

, examinando decisões migratórias, comunicações diplomáticas, eventual assistência de órgãos governamentais e utilização de recursos públicos. Isso não permitiria ao Congresso determinar unilateralmente uma extradição ou deportação. Mas poderia transformar uma controvérsia bilateral em uma investigação institucional sobre a conduta do próprio governo americano.
















Agnelli ressalta a limitação do poder econômico na campanha: “Nem mesmo campanhas financeiramente poderosas conseguem neutralizar um eleitorado muito insatisfeito”.




Com a derrota de Trump e dos Bolsonaro em eleições tão distintas e com menos de dez dias de intervalo, você identifica algum tipo de “recado das urnas” similar em ambos os países?




É difícil estabelecer uma comparação direta entre uma eleição presidencial no Brasil e uma eleição de meio de mandato nos EUA. São disputas de naturezas diferentes. Mas há elementos importantes a considerar.




No Brasil, a eleição ocorreu em um contexto no qual a estabilidade democrática e institucional estava diretamente em disputa. A candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro representava a continuidade de um projeto político familiar associado às tentativas de ruptura democrática e à contestação das instituições brasileiras.




Nos EUA, apesar da instabilidade institucional produzida por Trump, da deterioração dos mecanismos democráticos e do avanço de um projeto de concentração de poder que considero autocrático, não acredito que a defesa da democracia tenha sido o fator decisivo das 

midterms

.




O eleitor americano me parece ter agido de maneira muito mais pragmática. A eleição foi, sobretudo, um julgamento da incapacidade de Trump de cumprir uma de suas principais promessas de 2024: melhorar o custo de vida da população.




O eleitor está punindo Trump porque sente que sua vida piorou, não necessariamente porque compreendeu a dimensão do processo de erosão democrática em curso.




Vejo ainda um certo ceticismo da sociedade norte-americana em relação à possibilidade de uma autocracia se consolidar nos EUA. A força histórica das instituições democráticas talvez contribua para a percepção de que elas seriam capazes de resistir indefinidamente às investidas autoritárias.




Isso não significa que a defesa da democracia esteja ausente da sociedade. As mobilizações populares, particularmente os protestos do movimento “No Kings”, demonstraram que existe uma resistência social expressiva à concentração de poder e às práticas autoritárias da administração Trump.




As duas eleições revelam formas diferentes de reação a projetos políticos associados à erosão democrática.

 No Brasil, a ameaça institucional ocupou um lugar mais explícito na disputa presidencial. Nos EUA, a reação eleitoral parece ter sido impulsionada principalmente pela frustração econômica.




O eleitor americano pode ter imposto uma derrota política importante a Trump sem necessariamente ter rejeitado, de maneira consciente e definitiva, o projeto de poder que ele representa.







Embora cargos no Executivo federal, onde estão importantes aliados do bolsonarismo, como o secretário de Estado Marco Rubio, não estivessem em jogo, o resultado das 

midterms

 pode trazer alguma mudança na interlocução entre Brasil e EUA?







Existe um paradoxo especialmente interessante. O Brasil iniciará 2027 com um presidente de centro-esquerda e um Congresso de maioria conservadora. Os EUA devem apresentar uma configuração quase inversa: um presidente da direita radical e um Legislativo controlado pelos democratas, cuja coalizão reúne desde progressistas até liberais moderados.




Essa assimetria cria oportunidades de interlocução que ultrapassam as afinidades entre governos. 

Brasília e Washington poderão encontrar convergências institucionais entre seus respectivos Executivos e Legislativos, mesmo quando as maiorias parlamentares de cada país estiverem ideologicamente distantes de seus presidentes.




Em outubro de 2025, cinco senadores republicanos já se uniram aos democratas para aprovar uma resolução contra as tarifas impostas ao Brasil. O precedente é importante porque demonstra que determinadas políticas de Trump podem produzir coalizões bipartidárias, especialmente quando seus custos econômicos atingem consumidores, empresas e produtores norte-americanos.




Para o Brasil, a mudança mais significativa não seria necessariamente encontrar um Trump mais moderado, mas um Trump com menor capacidade política de impor unilateralmente suas decisões.




Esse cenário exige uma reflexão estratégica do governo Lula e, particularmente, do PT.




A esquerda brasileira mantém uma desconfiança histórica em relação aos EUA, compreensível diante do intervencionismo americano na América Latina. Essa memória histórica é legítima e não deve ser relativizada.




Entretanto, 

seria um erro transformar essa experiência em uma interpretação estática dos EUA como um ator político homogêneo. A política americana não se resume ao presidente.




Em 2026, encontramos novamente parlamentares democratas questionando iniciativas da administração Trump relacionadas ao Brasil, incluindo o tratamento conferido à embaixadora brasileira [os EUA 

revogaram

 o visto da embaixadora brasileira em Washington, Maria Luiza Viotti, em agosto deste ano] e as circunstâncias da entrada de Flávio Bolsonaro nos EUA. Esses episódios revelam que existem interlocutores americanos interessados na preservação da relação bilateral e no respeito às instituições brasileiras, mesmo quando o Executivo norte-americano adota uma orientação distinta.




A esquerda brasileira precisa distinguir a crítica histórica ao intervencionismo dos EUA da capacidade de construir alianças institucionais dentro da própria democracia americana.




A soberania brasileira não depende de manter distância dos EUA. Depende de preservar autonomia decisória enquanto o país amplia seus interlocutores e suas possibilidades de negociação. Nesse sentido, uma eventual maioria democrata pode oferecer ao Brasil uma oportunidade política que não deveria ser desperdiçada.




A política doméstica brasileira passou a integrar disputas e redes de influência nos EUA. Nesse contexto, seria limitado que o governo brasileiro concentrasse sua atuação exclusivamente na interlocução com Trump. 

O Brasil precisa desenvolver uma diplomacia parlamentar e política mais ativa em Washington

, preservando a diplomacia oficial conduzida pelo Itamaraty.




Como isso poderia ser feito na prática?




Isso significa ampliar o diálogo entre os congressos de ambos os países, entre dirigentes partidários e seus interlocutores internacionais, além de fortalecer a comunicação institucional com comissões que acompanham comércio exterior, relações internacionais, direitos humanos e segurança nacional.




O PT e outras forças democráticas brasileiras também podem desenvolver canais transparentes com diferentes correntes do Partido Democrata, desde sua ala progressista até os parlamentares mais moderados.




O aspecto essencial é preservar uma divisão institucional clara. Lula deve continuar negociando com Trump como chefe de Estado. O Itamaraty precisa manter relações com o Departamento de Estado e os demais órgãos da administração americana, independentemente da orientação partidária do governo. Paralelamente, o Congresso brasileiro pode aprofundar relações com seus equivalentes americanos, enquanto partidos e organizações políticas desenvolvem suas interlocuções.




Há, contudo, uma complexidade: o novo Congresso brasileiro será majoritariamente conservador e não necessariamente compartilhará as prioridades internacionais do governo Lula. Por isso, a diplomacia parlamentar brasileira também dependerá da capacidade de construir convergências internas em temas como tarifas, investimentos, exportações e autonomia nacional. O objetivo não deve ser substituir a interlocução com republicanos pela interlocução com democratas, mas impedir que a relação entre os países fique monopolizada por uma única corrente política.




Trump poderá preservar sua disposição para exercer pressão comercial e diplomática, mas vai enfrentar restrições políticas crescentes para sustentá-la. Isso pode ampliar a margem de negociação brasileira, sobretudo em questões que também produzam resistência entre empresários, produtores agrícolas e parlamentares americanos.




Nesse contexto, 

considero estrategicamente relevante a possibilidade de que negociações sensíveis sobre tarifas, minerais críticos e controvérsias diplomáticas sejam conduzidas em um ambiente posterior às 

midterms

, quando a correlação de forças em Washington estiver mais clara.




Na agenda de minerais críticos, essa mudança poderá ser especialmente importante. Na competição entre EUA e China por recursos estratégicos, o Brasil pode encontrar oportunidades para ampliar a discussão sobre as condições econômicas e tecnológicas desses investimentos. A existência de diferentes centros de influência em Washington pode ampliar os interlocutores brasileiros em negociações sobre financiamentos, cadeias de suprimentos e compromissos de longo prazo.




O que acontece com as ações que tentaram frear medidas do governo Trump, diante da nova configuração do Senado e da Câmara?




Durante os dois primeiros anos do segundo mandato de Trump, a maioria republicana no Congresso ofereceu ao Executivo um ambiente politicamente favorável à expansão de seus poderes. Isso ficou evidente na utilização da lei International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) para justificar tarifas internacionais.




A Constituição atribui ao Congresso americano competência sobre tarifas e comércio exterior. A Suprema Corte precisou intervir, em fevereiro de 2026, para estabelecer que a IEEPA não autorizava o presidente a impor aquelas tarifas. O episódio demonstrou os limites jurídicos da autoridade presidencial, mas também a fragilidade dos contrapesos políticos quando o Legislativo não contesta o Executivo.




Uma maioria democrata pode modificar substancialmente esse cenário, respondendo mais rapidamente a medidas semelhantes, convocando autoridades e promovendo investigações.




Não seria, entretanto, um poder absoluto. 

Trump conservaria o direito de vetar legislação, e a derrubada de um veto exige dois terços dos votos nas duas Casas.
















Após derrota nas urnas, Donald Trump sinalizou que vai usar o poder de veto para frear democratas




Há, porém, limites institucionais decisivos. Os democratas não conquistaram 60 cadeiras no Senado, número geralmente necessário para encerrar o debate. Isso significa que a nova maioria precisará negociar votos com republicanos para aprovar parte de sua agenda. Também não dispõe de dois terços em cada Casa para derrubar sozinha vetos presidenciais.




No caso do impeachment, é importante fazer uma distinção: a Câmara pode aprovar a acusação por maioria simples, mas a condenação e remoção de um presidente exigem dois terços dos senadores. 

Portanto, a vitória democrata não equivale a um poder irrestrito de legislar ou destituir Trump.




O principal instrumento será o 

congressional oversight

, a prerrogativa de fiscalização do Executivo com as comissões parlamentares. Com uma maioria democrata, essas comissões poderão conduzir investigações, emitir intimações, convocar autoridades e exigir documentos.




Uma frente particularmente sensível envolve os possíveis conflitos entre interesses públicos e privados na administração Trump. Os negócios da família presidencial, suas relações com investidores e decisões que possam ter beneficiado interesses particulares poderão ser examinados com maior profundidade.




Outro campo de fiscalização será a política externa. 

As operações militares americanas no Caribe, por exemplo, poderão enfrentar maior escrutínio.

 Os parlamentares não conseguirão necessariamente impedir cada ação militar, mas poderão aumentar significativamente os custos políticos e institucionais de sua continuidade.




Essa formulação expressa um paradoxo da Presidência americana: 

a perda de capacidade legislativa não implica necessariamente redução da iniciativa presidencial.

 Pode produzir um deslocamento do exercício do poder para as áreas em que o Executivo preserva maior autonomia. Diante de um Congresso hostil, Trump poderá ter mais dificuldades para aprovar reformas, ampliar programas e modificar estruturalmente a legislação. Mas continuará controlando instrumentos significativos nas áreas de diplomacia, segurança nacional, imigração, sanções e política comercial.




Isso pode estimular uma dependência ainda maior de ordens executivas, decisões administrativas e instrumentos de pressão internacional.




A derrota republicana acentua sua condição política de 

lame duck

 [pato manco], o presidente que se aproxima do fim de seu ciclo sem poder disputar uma nova eleição presidencial. Ele continuaria sendo presidente até janeiro de 2029, mas poderia enfrentar uma redução progressiva de sua capacidade de disciplinar a coalizão republicana.




Esse enfraquecimento eleitoral não significa, contudo, que Trump tenha deixado de ser um Executivo poderoso. Nos dois primeiros anos do Trump 2, ele construiu e consolidou uma presidência extraordinariamente fortalecida. 

A derrota nas urnas não desmonta automaticamente essa estrutura administrativa e política.

 Por isso, não acredito que veremos necessariamente menos agressividade. Um presidente com menos espaço no Legislativo pode recorrer ainda mais aos instrumentos unilaterais no Executivo.




Ao mesmo tempo, vejo a condição de 

lame duck

 como uma inflexão favorável ao Brasil e ao mundo. Um Congresso politicamente forte na oposição pode diminuir a perspectiva de consolidação e continuidade, para além de Trump, de um projeto de extrema direita que, na minha análise, ameaça a democracia norte-americana. Ele continua poderoso até o fim do mandato, mas o horizonte de longo prazo desse projeto passa a enfrentar obstáculos institucionais maiores.

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Tuberculosis documentary shows healing through sharing stories
content:
Iqaluit’s Astro Theatre was filled with people Tuesday evening for the première of a documentary that follows a group of tuberculosis survivors and youth as they find closure over their forced relocations decades ago.




Between the 1940s-1960s, the federal government transported thousands of Inuit to southern sanatoriums for tuberculosis treatment without their consent or without informing them about what was happening.




Many Inuit never returned home.




Taqqut Productions joined hands with The SeeChange Initiative to create 

Our Elders are so Important to Us: A Tuberculosis Sanatorium Healing Journey

, a 29-minute documentary that follows youth and survivors as they connect over these relocations, in an effort to provide healing and closure.




“If we value our elders as much as we say we do as Inuit, why not listen to their stories,” asked Naomi Tatty, the intercultural health lead at SeeChange, a non-profit and one of the leads for the documentary.




“Why not put their words out there and help us younger generations, and the generations ahead of us, understand what our families went through?”




She was on site for the screening and to help facilitate discussion afterwards, at the Storehouse.
















Tuberculosis is an airborne bacterial disease characterized by a cough, weight loss, night sweats, and a fever. Without treatment, it can cause serious complications and death.




In 2025, a group of TB survivors who had been relocated while sick, alongside others who were affected by the relocation of family members, made a journey to the former Mountain Sanatorium site in Hamilton, Ont. While there, they shared their history with youth and discussed how tuberculosis continues to affect people to this day.




Astro Theatre was filled with survivors, youth, health-care workers and community members to view the film and participate in the discussion afterward.




The idea for the healing journey was sparked by former prime minister Justin Trudeau’s 2019 

apology

 over TB sanatoriums, and his subsequent announcement of the The Nanilavut Initiative, a collaborative project that helps Inuit locate family members who never came home.




Tatty told Nunatsiaq News that her mother, or anaana, Ida Atagoyuk, was a TB survivor who spent three and a half years alone in treatment. She was present when the apology was given. But she wondered, Tatty said, what else was being done for healing. The 2025 healing journey was a product of that question, and the documentary followed.




Tatty also highlighted the importance of youth for facilitating healing how important it is to share stories.
















“Hopefully there’s a ripple effect of the younger generation to be able to have a mindset of understanding and to gain that knowledge and more understanding towards their upbringing and their homes,” she said to Nunatsiaq News.




Tuberculosis is still a crisis within Inuit Nunangat, and Nunavut has the highest rate of active tuberculosis of any province or territory in Canada.




So far this year, there have been 32 tuberculosis cases reported in seven communities.

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.




In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”




The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.




“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”




Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.




Cybersecurity experts assessing damage




Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.




“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”




He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.




He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.




“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”




At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”




“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”




Company will contact affected parties




He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.




“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.




“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”




Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.




“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”




Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.




“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”




 




The post 

Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers

 appeared first on 

APTN News

.

author: Anele Mbi
title: Polls close and the counting of votes has begun
content:
The Western Cape electoral officer, Michael Hendrickse told reporters that there were more people who voted in this year’s local government elections compared the previous poll in 2021. By 18h00, over 1.5 million people had voted. “Its clear that the number of voters is going upwards and will surpass the number of voters in the local government elections in 2021. But, there were fewer registered people in 2021 compared to this year. So, I’m not comparing the turnout as a proportion but looking at the numbers of people who voted,” he said.




Hendrickse said that there were still people waiting to vote at around 21h45 as they were in the queue by 21h00.




In Cape Town




Elitsha

 

reported earlier

 that voters in Khayelitsha and Mitchells Plain said that youth unemployment and lack of basic services are some of the issues that the next council should prioritise. Zine Malusi from ward 89 in Khayelitsha pleaded with political parties to work together to improve the lives of the poor even if they end up in coalition governments.




Her views were echoed by Fiona Jacobs from Portlands who said there was a need for the media to play an educational role in the elections to make sure that voters are clear who to vote for.




In Johannesburg




In Alexandra, unemployment and poor municipal services featured prominently in the concerns of young voters.




Bonang Makola, a first-time voter, said unemployment and the deteriorating state of Johannesburg influenced her decision at the ballot box. She had followed interviews in which political parties outlined their plans to reduce unemployment over the next five years, and their proposals helped shape her choice.




“As a young person, unemployment is one of the biggest issues. Some parties said they would reduce it by 0%, while others said they would reduce it by 2% every year. That influenced my decision on which party to vote for,” she said.




Makola said residents in her community continue to experience electricity problems, water interruptions and poor refuse collection. The accumulation of rubbish in Alexandra, she added, had become a serious health concern.




Thato Couch, a resident of Tsutsumani in Alexandra and a first-time voter, believes that the growing dissatisfaction with political parties has contributed to voter apathy. She said some residents no longer saw the point of voting because they felt that elections had brought little improvement to their circumstances. “People choose not to vote because they think it’s useless. There’s no change, no progress and nothing is actually moving. We just keep voting for the same thing,” she said.




Municipal workers fixing a blocked drain outside ward 89 voting station in Khayelitsha

.




Meanwhile, Rene, a Sandton resident, said Johannesburg’s deteriorating infrastructure requires urgent intervention, regardless of whether the next administration was formed by a single party or a coalition. She supports coalition governments provided political parties cooperate and share a commitment to fighting corruption and improving service delivery. “Johannesburg is falling apart. There has to be a party, whether it’s a coalition or a single party, that fixes this wonderful city because it’s broken through neglect,” she said.




Rene argued that political disagreements and leadership disputes should never take precedence over residents’ basic needs. “We’re the people. We pay our taxes and rates, yet our streets are full of potholes, we have no water, no electricity and the garbage isn’t being collected,” she said.




She also highlighted the dangers posed by poorly maintained roads, particularly for elderly motorists navigating streets without adequate lighting and road markings.




Across the interviews, voters expressed different perspectives on political parties and coalition government but shared a common expectation: those elected must demonstrate accountability and deliver tangible improvements. For Johannesburg residents, the real test of the elections will not simply be who wins political power, but whether that power translates into jobs, functioning infrastructure and reliable basic services.




In KuGompo City




Mdantsane residents, in Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality, said that youth unemployment and service delivery should be one of the key things that the next council should focus on. 




According to Nosiseko Adonisi (79) who voted at Zanokukhunya Primary in Ward 20, the next local government should prioritise young people in terms of job creation and skills development. “There must be job creation for young people, and the government must assist them to get skills. We want a total change. Our lives must not be the same,” Adonisi said.




“Our roads are full of potholes, forcing cars to dodge. We also want officials to assist us properly when we visit government offices,” she added.




Ayanda Maphongolo said the first problem the new government must attend to is the roads. “We always must fix tires. It is no longer potholes, but we call them graveyards. Whoever is gonna come must make us happy as citizens. The new government must be able to fix all the problems we encounter at BCM.




“I don’t know why I have voted because there is no benefit from voting. There is no change and there won’t be change no matter who wins because they give jobs to themselves. Not all of us are able to be ANC volunteers I get employed. Look now I am busy selling chicken feet on the road and I don’t have time to volunteer.  We have nothing, no houses and no jobs but I have just voted for the sake of voting,” said Thotyelwa Halutyana.




Neliswa Nomji, a pensioner who stays in Cuba informal settlement, which is part of ward 14, felt that political parties need to meet with people first to decide which parties to go into coalition with. “Political parties must meet with the people first. They cannot just choose who to form coalition with on their own. They must meet with the people”,Nomji said.

author: Lisa Xu
title: Reform Candidate Says UFCW Rep Tailed Him for 300 Miles to Thwart Petition Effort
content:
In a union that has been headed by one family with no competitive elections since 1984, a group of grocery workers is organizing for change. But this week, they say, union staff who back the incumbent administration went to outrageous lengths in an attempt to make sure there’s no election this year either.




On Monday afternoon, Eric Marcuz, a veteran Northern California Safeway worker, stopped at the union office to pick up blank petitions to get on the ballot in the union’s upcoming election. Marcuz is running for president on the 

At What Cost

 slate in the 23,000-member United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the union.




To get on the ballot, Marcuz and his slate-mates have to collect 443 petition signatures—2 percent of the local’s active members—in the next two weeks. If they don’t get enough signatures, no election will be held.




After Marcuz picked up the petitions from the local’s Roseville office, he got in his car to drive three hours south to Fresno, to start collecting signatures with another candidate on his slate at a Save Mart store there. (The local spans a 10-hour stretch from Bakersfield up to the Oregon border). 




When Marcuz stopped for gas, he said he noticed that a black Dodge Ram pickup stopped as well. When he got back on the freeway, so did the truck.  




At the next gas stop, Marcuz spoke to the man driving the truck. It was Jeff Berns, a staff representative for Local 8-GS. His brother, Mark, is also a rep for the union—and the local’s election chair, responsible for overseeing the election. 




Marcuz asked Jeff Berns why he was following him. According to Marcuz, Berns said he wanted to make sure that all the members got the “accurate information” that Marcuz’s slate was going to “divide” the union. He said he was going to follow him the entire time Marcuz was out, all the way back to Marcuz’s house in Redding, several hours north. Marcuz jokingly asked him if he needed a place to stay. Berns said he didn’t—because he’d been staying a lot in the Redding area lately himself, which Marcuz said he thought was “creepy” because that’s where Marcuz lives with his family (and is not where Berns lives).




Berns would live up to his promise—following Marcuz for the next 300 miles, through every stop, exit, and U-turn. He even followed him inside the Fresno Save Mart, and camped out for an hour with another union rep while Marcuz ate dinner at a supporter's house 100 miles north in Modesto.




NO COMPETITIVE ELECTIONS




At the gas station, Berns repeated the mantra, “Solidarity works!” That’s the motto of the incumbent president, Jacques Loveall, who is heading the 

Solidarity Works Team

 slate in this election. 




Loveall was appointed to lead the union in 2004, when his father, Jack Loveall, stepped down. The elder Loveall had held the top office since 1984; when he retired he was one of the highest-paid union officers in the country, earning the equivalent of $1 million today. (The 

Contra Costa Times

 reported that he had a $28,000-a-year country club membership and “two pilots on staff to chauffeur him in a private jet.”) Neither father nor son has ever faced a competitive election in the local.




Back on the freeway, Marcuz called a Department of Labor agent whom he had already been in touch with. They had previously spoken about the local’s apparent attempt to 

cancel the election

 by merging with a mysterious organization called the Staffing Agencies Federated Employees, an entity which listed one of Loveall’s relatives as its president on its initial filing. The agent told him to report the intimidation to the election chair and tell him to get the rep to back off.




Marcuz then called Mark Berns, the election chair, who he said told him he would talk to staff about acting in a professional manner. 




MORE REPS




However, when Marcuz arrived at the Save Mart store in Fresno to begin collecting petition signatures, he and another slatemate, Mike Romero, said that three union reps were waiting for them, including Jeff Berns. One of the others was John Micheletti, a longtime Local 8 vice president. Far from being called off, they said, the intimidation had actually intensified.




Marcuz and Romero said the reps interfered with every conversation they attempted to have with workers about signing their nomination petition. The very first worker they engaged about signing, a longtime acquaintance of Romero’s, fled once a rep entered the conversation and became confrontational. The worker did not sign the petition.




“They were everywhere inside the store,” said Marcuz. At least one of the interactions was filmed on a phone.




Marcuz said that Berns told him, “I’m going to make sure everyone knows who you are and not to sign that.” And additionally, “We’re going to invalidate every single signature that you get.” 




It is illegal for union staff and officers to campaign on union time. Berns said he was on vacation.




Romero, who has worked at Save Mart for 30 years, said, “This is the most I’ve seen of union staff in six months.” He said a fourth rep turned up after Marcuz left.




SEEN THIS BEFORE




These tactics—following opposition candidates and invalidating signatures—have both been alleged by previous members of the local who attempted to challenge the Lovealls. 




A 

Contra Costa Times

 article published in 2004 reported that supporters of Loveall’s father got members to rescind their signatures to keep dissident candidate Jack Nordby off the ballot in 1997. A 

book

 written by then-Local 588 reform activist Doug Slaydon states that as many as 150 signatures were removed. (Local 588 merged with another local to form Local 8-GS in 2006—postponing a potential competitive election that year.) 




Nordby also alleged that he was tailed by a pickup truck while collecting ballot signatures, followed around by union reps in stores, and once, chased in his car while driving his wife and two daughters to church. 




The 

Contra Costa Times

 also reported allegations that Local 588 staffers staked out the home of a member of UFCW Local 1179 who had led a successful rank-and-file opposition campaign to an attempted merger of the two locals and “tailed him in union cars.” “In June 1994,” reported the 

Times

, the member, Michael Ross-Smith, “was rear-ended in Walnut Creek by three UFCW 588 business agents following him too closely in a white 1993 Ford Thunderbird leased to the union, according to a traffic collision report from the Walnut Creek police department.”




TAILED FOR SEVEN HOURS




Marcuz and Romero said they quickly realized that they wouldn’t be able to collect petition signatures with this level of interference. Marcuz’s next stop was going to be to drop off petition forms with a supporter at the Turlock Safeway, over an hour to the north, but he made plans to meet the supporter at their house in Modesto instead.




When Marcuz left the parking lot of the Fresno store, Romero said three vehicles followed him. Romero also realized that one of the reps had stayed behind, and he became worried that he would be followed as well. He drove around for a long time before going home, to make sure he wasn’t followed.




Marcuz, meanwhile, said that Berns and Micheletti followed him for 90 miles, all the way to Modesto. They stayed parked outside the house while Marcuz ate burritos with the supporter—finally leaving after an hour, after 8 p.m.




"It's crazy that they would literally go two hours out of their way to make sure nobody else can talk to the employees,” Romero said. 




Marcuz said he almost canceled his plans to stay alone in a hotel in Roseville overnight, worried he would be tailed there, and contemplated driving for four more hours home to Redding. In total, he estimates he was followed for seven hours, over a distance of 300 miles.




SCARE TACTICS?




Section 610 of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA) forbids the threat or use of force or violence to restrain, coerce, or intimidate union members from exercising their right to nominate candidates or to vote in union officer elections, while Section 401(e) bars “improper interference” in the rights of union members to run for and support candidates for local union office. 




“It makes me think of everyone that has known there’s been a need for change in the past, and has been scared away from pursuing it,” Marcuz said. While Marcuz and his slate are standing strong, he said, “this might work. They might intimidate and scare enough people out of participating.”




In the morning, Marcuz filed a police report with the Roseville Police Department alleging stalking and harassment, citing the time and distance he was followed and the behavior he encountered in the Fresno store. 




Local 8 did not respond to requests for comment.




Petition signatures are due November 17, and ballots will be mailed November 21.

author: groundxero
title: পশ্চিমবঙ্গে সংখ্যালঘুদের উপর বাড়তে থাকা আক্রমণ, এসআইআর, ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প-এর বিরোধিতায় সাংবাদিক সম্মেলন
content:
ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে একের পর এক ঘটে চলা সংখ্যালঘু খ্রিষ্টান গীর্জার উপর হামলা, SIR প্রক্রিয়ায় ভোটারদের নাম বাদ দেওয়া, রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প তৈরি ও বেআইনি ভাবে সাধারণ মানুষদের সেখানে আটক করার বিরূদ্ধে ৩ নভেম্বর, মঙ্গলবার কলকাতার প্রেস ক্লাবে এক সংবাদিক সম্মেলন ডাকা হয়ে। 

মৈনাক দত্ত

-র প্রতিবেদন।




 




কলকাতা, ৩ নভেম্বর ২০২৬




 




নতুন সরকার পশ্চিমবঙ্গে ক্ষমতায় আসার পর কেটেছে মাত্র পাঁচ মাস। ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে ৪৮টি খ্রিষ্টান উপাসনালয়ে হামলা চালিয়েছে হিন্দুত্ববাদী দুষ্কৃতিরা। কিন্তু এফআইআর হয়েছে মাত্র ১৫ টি। এমনকি বহু জায়গায় পুলিশ এফ.আই.আর নিচ্ছে না। ‘কারওয়ানে মহব্বত’, ‘সবর ইনস্টিটিউট’ ও ‘আমরা এক সচেতন প্রয়াস’ নামক সংগঠনগুলির মিলিত তথ্যান্যসন্ধানে উঠে এসেছে এমনই বাস্তবচিত্র।




 




ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে একের পর এক ঘটে চলা সংখ্যালঘু খ্রিষ্টান গীর্জার উপর হামলা, SIR প্রক্রিয়ায় ভোটারদের নাম বাদ দেওয়া, রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প তৈরি ও বেআইনি ভাবে সাধারণ মানুষদের সেখানে আটক করার বিরূদ্ধে ৩ নভেম্বর, মঙ্গলবার কলকাতার প্রেস ক্লাবে এক সংবাদিক সম্মেলনের ডাক দেয় এই সংগঠনগুলি। সংবাদিক সম্মেলনে বক্তা হিসেবে উপস্থিত ছিলেন প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার জহর সরকার, প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও সমাজকর্মী হর্ষ মন্দার, প্রাক্তন আইএএস ওয়াজাহাত হাবিবুল্লাহ, সংবাদিক আকার প্যাটেল, মানবাধিকার জন দয়াল এবং মানবাধিকার কর্মী বিদ্যা ডিঙ্কার।




 




জহর সরকার নিজের বক্তব্যে সরাসরি বলেন, “পাড়ার কিছু গুণ্ডারা পার্টির নাম ব্যবহার না করে ‘বিশ্ব হিন্দু পরিষদ’, ‘হিন্দু জাগরণ মঞ্চ’ এসব সংগঠনগুলোর নাম করে একের পর এক হামলা চালাচ্ছে। চারিদিকে যেন একটা কম্পিটিটিভ কমিউনালিজম চলছে। এই নতুন নতুন গুন্ডারা এসব ঘটাচ্ছে পার্টির তরফ থেকে একটু নজর যাতে তাঁদের উপরে পরে।” SIR প্রসঙ্গে তিনি যোগ করেন “সারা ভারতে ১৩ কোটি ভোটার বাদ দিয়েছে। বাংলায় প্রায় ১ কোটি মানুষকে লাইনে দাঁড় করানোর পর সম্প্রতি একটি আরটিআই-এর জবাব দিতে গিয়ে নির্বাচন কমিশন জানিয়েছে মাত্র ১৬০০ জনকে তাঁরা বিদেশি হিসেবে সন্দেহ করছেন। মাত্র ১৬০০ জনকে খুঁজতে গিয়ে তাঁরা সারা ভারতবর্ষে তাণ্ডব চালিয়েছে।”




 




এদিনের সাংবাদিক সম্মেলনে স্পষ্ট করা হয় SIR প্রক্রিয়া যে সংখ্যালঘু সম্প্রদায়, মুসলিম সম্প্রদায়কে বাদ দেওয়ার জন্য করা হয়েছিল তা সবর ইনস্টিটিউট তাঁদের প্রকাশিত রিপোর্টের মাধ্যমে প্রমাণ করে দিয়েছে। যেভাবে রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প গড়ে উঠছে এবং বিভিন্ন মানুষকে রাতের অন্ধকারে বেআইনিভাবে আটক করা হচ্ছে তাঁর বিরুদ্ধেও প্রশ্ন তোলা হয়।




 




প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও ভারতের সংখ্যালঘু কমিশনের চেয়ারম্যান ওয়াজাহাত হাবিবুল্লাহ বক্তব্যের শুরুতেই মনে করিয়ে দেন – ভারতের সংবিধানের ধারণা কেবল একটি লিখিত দলিলের মধ্যেই সীমাবদ্ধ নয়। এটি একটি গভীর আধ্যাত্মিক ধারণা, যার শিকড় হাজার হাজার বছরের ইতিহাসে বিস্তৃত।




 




আলোচনায় যে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রশ্ন তিনি তোলেন তা হল – “ভারতের সংবিধান কেবল একটি সাংবিধানিক দলিল নয়। এটি আমাদের কাছে ভারত নামক দেশটির অস্তিত্বের সংজ্ঞা নির্ধারণ করে। ভারত কী? এর উত্তর হল— ভারতের সংবিধান। এই রাষ্ট্র কি এখনও ভারতের সংবিধানের কাঠামোর মধ্যে থেকে পরিচালিত হচ্ছে? যখন আমরা লিখিতভাবে ভারতের সংবিধানকে সংজ্ঞায়িত করেছি, তখন একজন ভারতীয় হিসেবে, আপনাদের সকলের মতো আমিও এই প্রশ্ন তুলতে বাধ্য— যাঁরা আমাদের দেশে ক্ষমতায় নির্বাচিত হয়েছেন, তাঁরা কি সেই সংবিধানকে রক্ষা করার দায়িত্ব পালন করছেন? তাঁরা কি ভারতের এই ধারণাটিকে সুরক্ষিত রাখছেন?”




 




তিনি তুলে আনেন আরটিআই প্রসঙ্গ। ভারতের সংবিধানের ১৯ নম্বর অনুচ্ছেদে বাক্‌স্বাধীনতা ও মতপ্রকাশের স্বাধীনতার অধিকার স্বীকৃত হয়েছে, যা বাস্তবায়নের অন্যতম প্রধান হাতিয়ার হল তথ্যের অধিকার আইন বা RTI Act। এই প্রসঙ্গেই তিনি বলেন, “তথ্যের অধিকার আইনকে কি যথাযথ সম্মান জানানো হচ্ছে? আইনটি মেনে চলা তো দূরের কথা, তাকে কি আদৌ গুরুত্ব দেওয়া হচ্ছে? সম্প্রতি SIR-সহ বিভিন্ন ঘটনাবলি নিয়ে আমরা যে অনুসন্ধান করেছি, তার উত্তর হল— না।”




 




বেআইনি নির্বাসন নিয়ে তাঁর বক্তব্য, বাংলাদেশি হিসাবে চিহ্নিত করা ব্যক্তিদের  শনাক্ত করার জন্য যে পদ্ধতি ব্যবহার করা হচ্ছে, তার কোনও নির্ভরযোগ্য ভিত্তি নেই। বাস্তবে কোনও প্রমাণ ছাড়াই দাবি করা হচ্ছে, তাঁরা বাংলাদেশ থেকে এসেছেন। এক্ষেত্রে যে জরুরি প্রশ্নগুলো উঠে আসে তা হল – কীভাবে তাঁদের বাংলাদেশ সরকারের হাতে তুলে দেওয়া হচ্ছে? তাঁদের অধিকার ও স্বাধীনতা রক্ষার জন্য কি কোনও পদক্ষেপ নেওয়া হচ্ছে? সংবিধানের অংশ হিসেবে আমাদের যে দায়িত্ব রয়েছে, তার ভিত্তিতে কি তাঁদের সুরক্ষা নিশ্চিত করা হচ্ছে?”




 




প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও সমাজকর্মী হর্ষ মন্দার তাঁর বক্তব্যে এই বিষয়ের উপরেই জোর দেন যে প্রত্যর্পণ একটি আইনি প্রক্রিয়া, যারজন্য অন্য দেশটির সরকারের সঙ্গে আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে যোগাযোগ করতে হয়। সরকার দাবি করছে সন্দেহভাজন ব্যক্তিদের চিহ্নিত করে দেশ থেকে ফেরত পাঠানো হচ্ছে। “অথচ এখানে যা ঘটছে, সেই মানুষগুলির বাংলাদেশি হওয়ার কোনও প্রমাণ সরকারের হাতে নেই। আপনাকে অন্য দেশের সরকারের কাছে নিজের প্রমাণ পেশ করতে হবে। তারপর সেই সরকার ওই ব্যক্তিকে নিজেদের নাগরিক হিসেবে গ্রহণ করে ফিরিয়ে নেবে। এখানে তেমন কোনও আইনি প্রত্যর্পণ প্রক্রিয়া নেই। যা চলছে, তা সম্পূর্ণ বিচারবহির্ভূত একটি ব্যবস্থা। এমন অসহায় মানুষদের সীমান্তের ওপারে ঠেলে দেওয়া হচ্ছে, যাঁরা হয়তো প্রয়োজনীয় নথিপত্র দেখাতে পারেননি।




 




এখান থেকে বন্দুকের মুখে তাঁদের সীমান্তের ওপারে ঠেলে দেওয়া হচ্ছে। আর ওপারেও তাঁদের দিকে তাক করা রয়েছে বন্দুক। চারদিকে শুধুই আতঙ্ক। গভীর রাতে মানুষকে সীমান্তের দিকে ঠেলে দেওয়া হচ্ছে। তাঁরা জানেন না, কোথায় নিয়ে যাওয়া হচ্ছে তাঁদের। একের পর এক ভয়াবহ ঘটনার কথা সামনে আসছে।




 




মানুষ নিখোঁজ হয়ে যাচ্ছেন। তাঁদের কাছে খাবার নেই। প্রাণ বাঁচানোর তাগিদে কোনওরকমে সীমান্ত পেরিয়ে অন্য পারে যাওয়ার চেষ্টা করছেন। অথচ বাংলাদেশের সীমান্তরক্ষীদের বন্দুক তখন তাঁদের দিকে তাক করা।”




 




সংখ্যালঘু সম্প্রদায়ের মানুষদের উপর ক্রমাগত আক্রমণ প্রতিহত করা ও গণতন্ত্র রক্ষায় নাগরিক সমাজ ও মানবাধিকার কর্মী, সমাজ কর্মী ও রাজনৈতিক কর্মীদের ঐক্যবদ্ধ লড়াই দীর্ঘস্থায়ী ও দৃঢ় হবে বলেই এদিন বক্তারা জানান।




 




গত ১৮-২০ অক্টোবর, দুর্গা পূজা চলাকালীন সময়ে পশ্চিম মেদিনীপুর জেলার চন্দ্রকোনায় তিনটি খ্রিষ্টান পরিবারের উপর বজরং দলের সদস্যরা আক্রমণ চালায়। শারীরিক হেনস্থার পাশাপাশি তাঁদের তথাকথিত শুদ্ধিকরণ করা ও পুষ্পাঞ্জলি দিতে বাধ্য করা হয়।




 




ঘটনার সূত্রপাত ১৮ তারিখ, যেদিন বাড়িতে হামলা চালিয়ে বজরং দলের সমর্থকেরা খ্রিষ্টান পরিবারগুলির সদস্যদের মারধোর, মহিলাদের পোশাক ছিঁড়ে দেওয়া, টাকা লুট করে। চলে শুদ্ধিকরণ। ১৯ তারিখ পুজা মন্ডপে টেনে নিয়ে গিয়ে পুষ্পাঞ্জলি দেওয়ানো হয়। ২০ তারিখ পুরুষদের ভয় দেখানো হয় এই ঘটনা পুলিসে রিপোর্ট না করতে এবং পরিবারগুলিকে চাপ দেওয়া হয় খ্রিষ্টধর্ম ত্যাগ করার জন্য। পরবর্তী সময়ে এই ঘটনায় এফ আই আর দায়ের হয় ও ১৩ জনকে গ্রেফতার করা হয়।




 




গত ২ নভেম্বর পশ্চিমবঙ্গে ধর্মীয় সংখ্যালঘুদের উপর ক্রমবর্ধমান হিংসা, নিপীড়ন ও বৈষম্যের অভিযোগ খতিয়ে দেখতে কলকাতায় দু’দিনের গণশুনানি ও আলোচনা সভা অনুষ্ঠিত হয়েছে। ২ ও ৩ নভেম্বর কলকাতার মুসলিম ইনস্টিটিউটে আয়োজিত এই কর্মসূচিতে আকক্রান্ত পরিবারগুলি, তথ্যানুসন্ধানী দল, আইনজীবী, গবেষক, নাগরিক সমাজের প্রতিনিধি, বিশেষজ্ঞ ও ছাত্র-ছাত্রীরা অংশ নেন। এই গণশুনানিতে ২০২৪ সাল থেকে রাজ্যে বিজেপির ক্ষমতায় আসার পর গত ছয় মাসে এবং ২০২৫ সাল জুড়ে বিভিন্ন জেলায় ঘৃণাজনিত অপরাধ, যৌন নিপীড়ন, গণহিংসা ও লক্ষ্যভিত্তিক হয়রানির অন্তত ৬০টি ঘটনার সাক্ষ্য নথিবদ্ধ করা হয়। সাক্ষ্যগুলিতে গির্জার প্রার্থনা ও ধর্মীয় অনুষ্ঠান ব্যাহত করা, উপাসনালয়ে ভাঙচুর, যাজক ও পুরোহিতদের উপর হামলা, হুমকি, সামাজিক বয়কট এবং জোর করে ধর্মীয় আচার পালনে বাধ্য করার অভিযোগ উঠে আসে।




 




দু’দিনের এই কর্মসূচিতে ধর্মীয় সংখ্যালঘুদের উপর লক্ষ্যভিত্তিক হিংসা বন্ধ করা, অপরাধীদের জবাবদিহির আওতায় আনা এবং সংবিধান-প্রদত্ত অধিকার, সমান নাগরিকত্ব ও আইনের শাসন সুনিশ্চিত করার দাবি জানানো হয়। বৈষম্যের বিরুদ্ধে লড়াই এবং প্রান্তিক সম্প্রদায়ের অধিকার ও মর্যাদা রক্ষায় তথ্য নথিবদ্ধকরণ, জনপরিসরে আলোচনা ও সম্মিলিত উদ্যোগের গুরুত্বও তুলে ধরা হয়।

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Nunavut to receive $65.3M in additional federal funding for housing
content:
Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. will receive $65.3 million in federal funding for Inuit housing over five years, an expenditure MP Lori Idlout says is welcome but must be part of a long-term commitment to address the territory’s housing crisis.




“I know that when I still go to the communities, housing is always the first thing that’s mentioned to me as an important issue,” Idlout said in an interview Wednesday. 

“It’s great to see our government hearing that.”




The funding comes from a $130.3-million top up to the federal government’s Urban, Rural and Northern Indigenous Housing Strategy, which Crown-Indigenous Relations Minister Rebecca Alty and Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty announced Oct. 30 in Kuujjuaq.




The money will go to the four Inuit Treaty Organizations, including $32.5 million to Makivvik, nearly $17 million to the Inuvialuit Regional Corp. and $15.5 million to the Nunatsiavut Government.




The federal government previously allocated $197.5 million, bringing the total to $327.8 million, according to the government’s news release.




The money can support Inuit-led housing projects and programs, including new construction, repairs, transitional housing, shelters, rent subsidies and short-term accommodations for students, the release said.




In a Sept. 16 letter to Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne, in which she outlined her recommendations for the 2026 budget, Idlout called for $810 million in funding for 400 affordable units across Nunavut through an Inuit-led initiative.
















“I think we just need to make sure these are not one-time funding announcements,” Idlout said.




The federal government did not provide a target for how many homes the additional funding is expected to build, Idlout said.




Under the strategy, Inuit Treaty Organizations will determine how to direct the money, the release said.




“

We are proud to support Inuit-led housing approaches that put decision-making in the hands of Inuit partners and communities,” Gull-Masty said in the release.




In addition to being Indigenous services minister, Gull-Masty is the MP for Abitibi—Baie-James—Nunavik—Eeyou, the sprawling Quebec riding that includes Nunavik.




“

This investment will help advance housing projects that reflect local priorities, strengthen community well-being, and create safe, affordable, and culturally appropriate homes for Inuit families and future generations.”

author: Anikibawal
title: Festival MANOJO – INFANCIAS Y ARTES ESCÉNICAS. Una experiencia enfocada en la primera infancia donde se reúnen las artes escénicas, mediación y juego libre en la ciudad de Temuco este 6 y 7 de noviembre.
content:
Durante esta semana, los días viernes 6 y sabado 7 de noviembre, desde las 12:00 a las 19:00 hrs, se realizara la Primera Version del 

Festival Manojo – Infancias y artes escénicas

, un festival enfocado en la primera infancia (de 0 a 7 años) el cual tendra lugar en el Museo Regional de la Araucanía, en especifico en el parque que alberga el lugar, conversamos con Brenda Lizama Farfán, psicóloga, bailarina de danza contemporánea y directora del Festival Manojo, quien nos cuenta en sus palabras 

“Manojo es un festival de primeras infancias, dirigido también hacia esas edades, de 0 a 7 años y a sus cuidadores y cuidadoras, es una propuesta en el exterior, por lo tanto permite otras experiencias en relación a la exhibición de obras y a la apreciación de artes vivas.”




En su primera versión, el festival trae como impronta ser una de las primeras iniciativas de artes escénicas enfocadas de forma exclusiva en las primeras infancias, sus familias, cuidadores y cuidadoras en Temuco, entrelazando diversas disciplinas tales como la danza, circo contemporáneo, títeres y narración oral, junto con instalaciones de mediación y juego libre pensadas para la estimulación de las niñeces.




El festival desde su propuesta curatorial viene a buscar la recuperación de espacios naturales dentro de la comuna de Temuco principalmente, como lo es el Museo Regional de la Araucanía, desde la dirección del festival reflexionan respecto a “

el museo regional es un espacio que no abre por ejemplo, los domingos o que no abre después de las 5:30 hrs, donde sabemos que la mayoría de las personas trabajamos en ese horario, entonces, ¿En qué momento llevamos a nuestras niñeses a esos espacios? habitarlos, conocerlos explorando, y ¿De qué manera también les invitamos a explorar? ¿Pueden tocar lo que existe en ese lugar? Entonces, esas son las preguntas también que nos hicimos al momento de seleccionar este espacio para realizar nuestro festival”.




El festival cuenta con una parrilla programática qué incluye 6 obras de artes escénicas, a continuación Brenda, su directora, nos habla sobre las actividades y los fundamentos qué dieron vida al festival 

“Manojo cuenta con una parrilla programática de 6 obras de artes escénicas, además contamos con una experiencia que es un laboratorio de exploración de juego y movimiento libre para bebés de entre 10 y 36 meses que se llama Danzas Sensibles, que es un proyecto que vengo investigando ya hace cuatro años aproximadamente, y además va a estar la Tribu Reverdecer de danza porteo, que también es un proyecto que da inicio también a toda esta propuesta de festival, fue mi primer trabajo después de ser madre. Desde ahí también vienen todas estas preguntas que les he comentado respecto a cómo las madres habitamos estos espacios: ¿dónde somos bienvenidas y dónde podemos criar en comunidad? Entonces, esta tribu fue un proyecto de acompañamiento psicocorporal y psicoemocional a madres, mujeres puerperas junto a sus bebés desde los 3 meses después del parto y desde ahí surge la danza en movimiento libre… , gracias también al poeta bebé nuestras piernas nuestros cuellos para poder danzar con nuestros bebés… eso también se va a presentar ese día del festival, somos nueve mujeres danzando con nuestros bebés. Creo que también es una propuesta reivindicadora de la maternidad, que visibiliza también a las madres, el puerperio, en un espacio y en un contexto territorial que muchas veces no es tan visto, no es tan visible y que creo que es muy importante tener ese gesto político dentro de este festival, que ya es una gran propuesta política que va a remover ciertas maneras de ver la danza en particular y también las artes escénicas y las artes vivas en el territorio»

, de esta forma, el festival invita a las niñeces, sus familias, cuidadores y cuidadoras, a pasar la tarde en el parque que antecede al Museo Regional de la Araucanía, incentivando a llevar alimentos para consumo propio y/o una manta qué permitan a las infancias ocupar los jardines del lugar.







Esta información se publicó en 

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Andrew Crocker
title: We’re Asking the Ninth Circuit to Hold Reverse Location Warrants Categorically Unconstitutional
content:
Yesterday, along with the ACLU, EFF filed an 

amicus brief

 in the Ninth Circuit court of appeals in 

United States v. Spurlock

, a case involving a “tower dump” warrant. These overbroad warrants require cellular providers to turn over location data about every phone in a given area at a given time. This is the first such case to be heard by a federal appeals court since the 

US Supreme Court ruled this summer

 that highly similar “geofence” warrants are searches under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.




Spurlock 

involves an investigation into two murder victims discovered on the side of a rural California highway. Police also found a car belonging to one of the victims several miles away on the same highway. They quickly sought a tower dump warrant for an area covering this stretch of road, which eventually revealed location data on nearly 1,700 unique phones. Faced with a motion to suppress, the district court relied on a 

Fifth Circuit court of appeals decision

 about geofence warrants to hold that tower dumps are similarly categorically unconstitutional “general warrants” that violate the Fourth Amendment. However, the court refused to suppress evidence on the basis of the “good faith doctrine.”




Our amicus brief on appeal makes several key arguments.




First, we point out that the Supreme Court’s decision in the geofence case 

Chatrie v. United States 

this summer only strengthens the arguments that tower dumps are unconstitutional general warrants. Tower dumps are a somewhat older technique than geofence warrants, but they are both “reverse location searches,” in which police “tap into an all-encompassing database, allowing them to undertake nearly perfect, retrospective surveillance of countless persons and places.” This is the sort of untargeted “general warrant” the framers of the Fourth Amendment wanted to prevent. As we write in the brief, “Searching all people in an area without probable cause to believe they were all involved in the criminal activity under investigation reproduces the evils of general warrants and is not constitutionally permitted.” It’s this rule of law that prevents police from searching the houses of a hundred, or even a thousand people in the vicinity of a crime.




Second, we note that even if high courts continue to allow tower dump and geofence warrants in any cases, core Fourth Amendment law requires strict limits to protect the privacy of innocent bystanders, including limits on the scope and duration of the warrants, as well notice to affected individuals and after-the-fact deletion and minimization of irrelevant data.




Finally, we argue that the Fourth Amendment requires the court to set aside the good faith doctrine in cases like these and actually decide the constitutional issue. Too often courts pass the buck in cases involving novel surveillance techniques, leading to situations where police can continue using the technique for years or even decades without a definitive ruling.

title: Kurdish writer Gülazer Akın released after 30 years in prison
content:
Kurdish political prisoner and writer Gülazer Akın has been released from Bünyan Women’s Prison in Turkey’s Kayseri province after 30 years of imprisonment. She was welcomed outside the prison by family members, representatives of the prisoners’ solidarity association TUHAYDER and numerous supporters. Akın, who had been imprisoned since November 1996, endured numerous health problems during her decades behind bars, completed a university degree and wrote several literary works.




Upon her release, Akın said she had not believed until the very end that she would actually be able to leave prison. The release of a fellow prisoner had previously been postponed by a decision of the Prison Administration and Observation Board. She therefore feared that her own release might also be blocked.




“As long as even one of our friends remains in prison, I will not feel that I have truly been released,” Akın said. She also welcomed the peace process that had begun: “We have matured and returned. A new process has begun. I said this before the board as well. A new process has begun, and I support it. There is probably nothing more beautiful than freedom.”




Following her remarks, Akın released a white dove as a symbol of peace.




TUHAY-DER calls for the release of political prisoners




During the welcome gathering, the prisoners’ solidarity association TUHAY-DER criticized the continued imprisonment of seriously ill prisoners and the repeated postponement of scheduled releases. Representatives of the association stated that genuine freedom could only be achieved when all political prisoners and Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan were released.




The decisions of Prison Administration and Observation Boards have faced criticism from human rights and prisoners’ rights organizations for years. These organizations accuse the boards of delaying the release of long-term prisoners for political reasons, despite their having met the necessary requirements for release.




Three decades behind prison walls




Gülazer Akın was born in 1975 in Ahlat, in the province of Bitlis. She joined the Kurdish freedom movement in 1993. On November 3, 1996, she was arrested in Istanbul and placed in pretrial detention. A Turkish State Security Court later sentenced her to life imprisonment on charges of separatism.




During her imprisonment, Akın was held in various prisons across Turkey. Despite health problems, she continued her education and graduated with a degree in public administration from Anadolu University.




At the same time, she devoted herself extensively to literature. Her experiences of imprisonment, social exclusion and women’s lives became central themes in her writing.




Writing against oblivion




Akın’s first novel, 

Tencerenin Dibi

 (

The Bottom of the Cooking Pot

), was published in 2013. The book was introduced by Turkish writer Adil Okay, who drew attention to the extraordinary circumstances under which she produced her literary work in an accompanying text.




Okay quoted from a letter Akın had written after 18 years of imprisonment. In it, she described how an entire generation had grown up behind prison walls while life continued outside:




“We were still almost children when we entered prison. Many of us grew up and matured while staring at walls. As the walls deteriorated, we grew more mature.”




Akın offered a particularly poignant account of her encounters with family members whose growth she could witness only during prison visits:




“When we entered prison, our siblings, nieces and nephews were still babies. Today, they are adults. We could only watch all of this through the small window of the prison. With every visit, we were amazed all over again and asked: When did you grow so big?”




According to Akın, this experience created an almost unbearable sense of injustice. Adil Okay praised her novel as a work written under conditions in which even colored pencils had reportedly been prohibited. Despite these restrictions, the writer developed her own literary voice to bring attention to experiences that were barely acknowledged beyond the prison walls.




Confronting patriarchal social structures




With her 2017 book 

Cinsiyetçiliğin Yaratımı

 (

The Creation of Sexism

), Akın also turned her attention to theoretical questions concerning women’s liberation. In the book, she examines sexism as a system of social domination and explores the significance of women’s self-determination in transforming social structures.




“We know that sexism is a male construct,” Akın writes. She emphasizes that women have both the right and the need to understand themselves, develop their abilities and independently determine their role in society.




She views women’s liberation not merely as individual emancipation but as a foundation for building a society based on solidarity and coexistence.

title: Ecocide continues in Şırnak: Hundreds of oak trees cut down
content:
Environmental destruction continues in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. Footage recorded by local residents yesterday in the Besta region shows hundreds of oak trees cut down across a vast area, leaving large sections of the forest stripped of trees.




While activities carried out under the guise of mining exploration on Mount Cudi and oil exploration on Mount Gabar for nearly a decade have already caused significant environmental damage, tree felling continues in the Besta region under the pretext of commercial activity.




According to reports, oak trees, some of them up to a century old, have been cut down by village guards under military supervision. Footage recorded in the Kaniya Kolanan and Dergê Gêzna areas showed numerous trees being cut down at their bases with chainsaws. The logging site is reportedly accessible only through a military checkpoint, and around ten people were said to be operating in the area with vans and chainsaws.




DEM Party Şırnak MP Mehmet Zeki İrmez shared the footage on his social media account, condemning the tree felling and tagging the Şırnak Governor’s Office and the Provincial Directorate of Agriculture.










https://twitter.com/zekiirmez/status/2117663598902161603










İrmez stated that deforestation continued despite previous assurances that it would end. He accused public institutions of turning a blind eye to the destruction and said that the activities of local collaborators were making ecocide a permanent reality in the region.




Emphasizing that social peace could not be approached from a single perspective, İrmez stressed that protecting nature was also an essential component of peace. He called for an immediate halt to the tree felling and demanded that those responsible be held accountable.




Meanwhile, deforestration work is also reported to be continuing in rural areas around the villages of Cilbiya and Biliga in Silopi.




According to reports, village guards have been transporting the felled trees by tractor to the towns of Şêxan (Hilal) and Sêgirk (Şenoba). A local resident recorded footage of the trees being transported by tractor near the İnceler Dam.

author: Unknown
title: Vigil in Geneva enters its 69th month: ‘Öcalan’s status must be officially recognized’
content:
A vigil by the Democratic Kurdish Community in Switzerland has been taking place in front of the UN headquarters in Geneva since 25 January 2021. Every Wednesday, activists stage a protest in front of the United Nations building to demand the release of Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan. The action is carried out as part of the 'Dem dema azadiye' [Time for Freedom] campaign and is directed against the isolation of the Kurdish leader on the Turkish prison island of Imrali, the Turkish occupation attacks on Kurdistan, the massacres committed in Kurdish territories and the silence of the UN. Demonstratos call on international institutions to fulfill their responsibilities to secure Öcalan’s physical freedom.




This week's demonstration, which is held at a tent set up in Nations Square where the UN Office is located, began with a moment of silence in memory of those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle.




During this week’s demonstration, participants from Kurdistan once again called on international institutions to fulfill their responsibilities in securing the physical freedom of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who has been held in Imralı Island Prison since 1999.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/079bead5_20261104154836_2026-11-04-cenevre-onder-apo-icin-ozgurluk-nobeti-bm-ofisi-onunde-69-aylinda-devam-ediyor-1.mp4










Xebat Veysel Kuşkanadı, spokesperson for the “Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, A Democratic Solution to the Kurdish Question” campaign committee, spoke about the ongoing peace process launched in Turkey following Öcalan’s February 27, 2025 ‘Call for Peace and Democratic Society.’ He expressed respect and appreciation for the Kurdish leader’s intensive efforts and work toward peace.




Stating that Öcalan sought an end to the conflicts in Turkey and the Middle East and a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question, Xebat Veysel described this approach as an important demonstration of political will and goodwill toward peace.




Veysel accused the Turkish state of deliberately prolonging the process without taking concrete steps, emphasizing that the Kurdish people did not accept this approach.




Xebat Veysel outlined their demands as follows: “The Turkish state must take genuine and serious steps, and Leader Öcalan’s status must be clearly defined and officially recognized. Leader Öcalan must be provided with conditions that allow him to work freely.”




Osman Tekin, Co-Chair of the Geneva Democratic Kurdish Community Association, then took the floor, emphasizing that the Kurdish question was fundamentally an issue of rights.




Tekin stated that autonomy for local administrations, constitutional guarantees for the Kurdish language and securing Öcalan’s physical freedom were key elements of a resolution.




Stressing the need for new legislation and reforms, Tekin said that Öcalan must be allowed to communicate with members of the press, civil society representatives, the Peace Mothers and his comrades.




Tekin stressed that only if these steps were taken could they believe in the Turkish state’s sincerity regarding the process.

author: Unknown
title: Rojhilat Alliance: Member parties in favor of continuing dialogue
content:
The Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group issued a written statement regarding its meeting with representatives of four member parties of the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan.




The statement said: “In order to activate the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan, which was established more than eight months ago, and to identify the obstacles preventing it from functioning effectively, the Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group invited the Alliance’s six parties to a consultative meeting.




The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), the Organization of Struggle of Iranian Kurdistan (Sazmana Xebat a Kurdistana Îranê), the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I), and the Association of Kurdistan Toilers attended the meeting.




Only the Komala Party stated that it was not prepared to attend the meeting. In addition, a few days before the meeting, the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I) withdrew without providing any explanation.




On Sunday (1 November 2026), a three-hour meeting was held between the Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group and representatives of four parties belonging to the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan.”




The statement noted that the four parties regarded the political alliance as an important and long-term necessity. It added that the Political Alliance could become more active and effective in the near future by adopting a charter, defining roles and responsibilities, and establishing mechanisms for joint work.




Regarding the possibility of dialogue with the Iranian state, the statement said that the parties had agreed that, should an opportunity for dialogue arise and the need for negotiations emerge, no member party of the Alliance should independently enter into negotiations with the Islamic Republic of Iran without the Alliance’s participation and coordination.




The statement described the meeting as a positive step, noting the willingness to discuss directly the challenges facing the Political Alliance—an initiative that deserved support and further development. It added that representatives of all the parties had expressed positive assessments of the meeting.




The statement also emphasized that the parties should refrain from accusing one another in order to avoid undermining trust between them and jeopardizing the continuity of their joint work.
