author: Daron Letts
title: Cambridge Bay’s runway to be paved
content:
Cambridge Bay’s gravel airport runway is one step closer to being paved, says Nunavut’s transportation minister.




Almost $3.5 million towards planning and design of the project will come from the Department of National Defence’s capital assistance program, George Hickes told Nunatsiaq News Friday in an interview.




The update comes after Cambridge Bay MLA Fred Pedersen pressed Hickes in the legislative assembly Monday during question period about the state of his community’s runway.




“It’s obvious the efficiencies that would be achieved through paving,” Hickes said to Pedersen in response.  “It’s a no-brainer.”




Pedersen had asked

 if the minister agreed with comments made by Buffalo Airways general manager Mikey McBryan, who called on the federal government in September to pave the runway. McBryan made the comments at a House of Commons Indigenous and Northern Affairs Committee meeting in Ottawa on Sept. 24.




The design is expected to be complete by fall 2027, Hickes said in an interview Friday.




As for the paving itself — “the sooner the better after that,” he said.
















Cambridge Bay’s airport is located three kilometres southwest of the hamlet. Its 

gravel runway is a little more than 5,000 feet long and 150 feet wide.




The gravel limits the size of aircraft that can land in the community.




The airport can accomodate Buffalo Air’s Lockheed Electra and 737-200 aircraft, which burn about 20 per cent more fuel and haul about 10,000 pounds less that the airline’s Boeing 737-300 twin engine jetliner.




But a 737-300 needs to land on a paved runway, McBryan, with Buffalo Air, told federal leaders in September.




“Paving the runway in Cambridge Bay would instantaneously bring the cost of living down the next day,” McBryan said to

 Nunavut MP Lori Idlout, who had asked if paving the territory’s runways could help keep dollars inside the territory.




“I don’t care if it’s military funding, if it’s private funding or if it’s government funding: Pave it. It’ll make everything better,” McBryan said during the committee meeting.
















The federal government 

announced

 in March a $2.7-billion 

plan

 to expand the military’s presence in the Arctic, with upgrades to support military in five Arctic communities, including Cambridge Bay.




The paving project is part of the preparation for Cambridge Bay’s bigger role in the country’s defence network, Hickes said.




Pedersen said he’s “excited” to hear about the funding.




“All airlines will save money and I’m hoping that even passenger airfares will go down,” he said in an interview.




“Having a paved runway and hopefully better airfield lighting and instrument landing systems will help in inclement weather getting things to land.”
















Nunatsiaq News asked the Department of National Defence for a comment on the runway paving but did not receive a response Friday morning.

author: Unknown
title: Sciopero generale: l’Italia si blocca
content:
Giornata di sciopero generale: numeri ancor più massicci delle prime manifestazioni dell’autunno scorso. Blocchi in tutta Italia e cortei da decine di migliaia di persone, dalle metropoli alle province. 




Contro la guerra, contro il carovita, contro il riarmo voluto dal governo Meloni. E ancora, contro una vita precaria e indignitosa, per dire basta ai sacrifici che il governo italiano, insieme ai governi di tutta Europa, vogliono imporre alla popolazione. La partecipazione è stata impressionante, da Sud a Nord, oltre un milione in tutta Italia. Il Paese che per anni è stato narrato come il bacino dell’indifferenza e che nei migliori dei casi avrebbe voluto “fare come in Francia” in queste settimane, sull’onda del ciclo di movimento iniziato un anno fa a sostegno della Palestina e contro la complicità dei governi con il genocidio, sta dando un segnale chiaro: è giunto il tempo di alzare la testa. 




Grazie ai giovani che a fronte del peso di un futuro rubato stanno occupando scuole e università da un mese per affermare la propria esistenza, ai giovani che con rabbia calciano indietro la sfrontatezza dell’ingiustizia, oggi grazie alla chiamata allo sciopero generale indetto dall’Unione Sindacale di Base, si sono uniti i lavoratori e le lavoratrici che non hanno nessuna garanzia di vedere riconosciuto il proprio lavoro. Ma precarietà e sfruttamento non sono più un orizzonte accettato. Gli agricoltori e gli autotrasportatori che al Sud hanno bloccato le merci lo dicono da settimane, insieme a studenti, famiglie e a chiunque individua la causa di questa situazione alle scelte politiche dall’alto, sottomesse ai diktat europei e trumpiani: non c’è più disponibilità. 




Il governo Meloni deve fare i conti con il fatto che in piazza c’è il paese che porta avanti l’ingranaggio di questo sistema e che se decide di fermarsi non ci sarà alcuna prova di forza in grado di reggere il confronto. Le briciole di una finanziaria che tenta di mascherare in ogni modo che l’unico interesse governativo è trovare i soldi per il riarmo non hanno alcuna possibilità di convincere la popolazione. 




A Bologna, Pisa, Livorno, Roma, Torino, Treviso, Milano, Reggio Calabria, Palermo, Bari, Trieste, Pavia, Vicenza, Modena, Padova, Mestre, Cosenza, Napoli, Genova sono state bloccate le arterie principali delle città, gli snodi delle tangenziali e i porti. 




Livorno: la mattinata parte con il blocco del porto, prosegue poi con un corteo di oltre 20 mila persone e continua con il blocco della circolazione al varco Zara. 




Bologna: 50 mila persone nonostante i blocchi della polizia aprono un varco e arrivano a inondare l’autostrada. 




Modena: giovani e famiglie in corteo contro guerra e carovita.




Torino: un corteo diramato in tutta la città, dal centro alla tangenziale, raggiunge quota 100 mila persone, viene rilanciato l’appuntamento alle 18 per un altro corteo cittadino. 




Cosenza: corteo di massa di 7mila persone ha invaso le strade della città e bloccato autostrada e superstrada.




Pisa: un corteo di 20 mila persone si conclude con l’occupazione del Palazzo della Sapienza, nel pomeriggio appuntamento per una grande assemblea.




Brescia: 10 mila persone in corteo hanno tentato di raggiungere l’autostrada, cariche della polizia. 




Milano: 80 mila persone raggiungono la tangenziale. 




Pavia: grande manifestazione contro guerra e carovita. 




Qui le dirette di 

Radio Blackout

 e di 

Radio Onda d’Urto

 con i collegamenti dalle piazze in tutta Italia.

author: paradox-a
title: Die falsche Welt des Gute-Laune-Faschismus
content:
Zum Posterboy des Gute-Laune-Faschismus wurde Ulrich Siegmund gekürt, der AfD-Ministerpräsident in spe aus Sachsen-Anhalt. Die AfD fuhr hier mit 43,8% ihr bislang bestes Ergebnis ein. Je strukturschwächer, gottverlassener und migrationsärmer die Gegenden sind, desto stärker ist der Zuspruch zum nationalistischen Autoritarismus. So bereisen die ewig grinsenden Rattenfänger das Land und punkten unter Deutschen, die die Überwindung ihrer eigenen bürgerlichen Existenz herbeisehnen und hoffen dies auf dem Weg der Zerstörung der liberalen Demokratie zu erreichen.




Der Wohlfühl-Faschismus ist ein Phänomen, das vor zwanzigdreißig Jahren noch völlig unvorstellbar gewesen wäre. Und in zweidrei Jahrzehnten werden wir uns ebenfalls fragen, was in dieser Phase eigentlich passiert ist. Wer sie verstehen will, muss sich dazu nicht nur die Wahlkampf-Strategien der AfD anschauen, sondern auch kultur- und medienwissenschaftlich vorgehen. So ist es kein Zufall, das seit Anfang des Jahres 2026 massenhaft KI-generierte Songs bei Youtube erscheinen. Aufgrund ihrer hohen Klickzahlen landen diese wiederum durch die Algorithmen sehr schnell in der Vorschlagleiste.




Die extrem rechte Propaganda-Maschinerie bedient sich somit nahezu perfekt abgestimmt der Mittel, die der Plattform-Kapitalismus entwickelt hat. Und sie greift auf eine künstlich-sentimentale Popkultur zurück, die unterm Strich meistens schon sehr schlicht und beschränkt war. Ob volkstümelnd wie Heino, oder neu-deutsch-hart wie Rammstein, sülzig wie Julia Juls, Runa&Rebellin oder pop-rockig wie Weimar, Sleipnir und andere – Vorbilder für die extrem rechte Computermusik gibt es genug…




Sicher könnte man auch dagegen halten und sagen, dass die Generierung von Musik und Video-Material durch technische Sprechapparate von allen möglichen Leute mit kommerziellen Absichten, um Aufmerksamkeit zu erhalten oder einfach nur aus Langeweile generiert wird. Und das stimmt auch. Bedenkt man, wie durchproduziert und geglättet kommerziell erfolgreiche Musik heute ist, scheint der Schritt zur sogenannten KI klein zu sein. Dennoch gibt es eine spezielle Affinität von faschistischem Denken zur offensichtlich künstlichen Kultur, die den Anschein von menschlicher Kreativität verlässt und damit post-human ist. Laut Jason Stanley wird damit auf die Herstellung von „Unwirklichkeit“ abgezielt.




Um ein paar Beispiele von viralen KI-generierten Songs und „Künstler“ zu nennen, sind da beispielsweise:


– „Spätestens HIER wacht jeder auf! Der Sound des Wandels“ („Aufbruch Deutschland“, 501.537 Aufrufe)


– „Steh auf, wenn du Deutscher bist | Stolz auf Heimat und Kultur“ („Ottilie“, 339.081 Aufrufe)


– „Was ist aus unserem Land geworden? | Ein Lied über den Verlust der Heimat“ („Fenja“, 338.697 Aufrufe)


– „Dorfmarie – So war es, so soll es wieder sein“ („Dorfmarie“, 160.534 Aufrufe)


– „DIE WACHT AM RHEIN (LIVE) | Rock-Version eines historischen Gedichts“ („Julia im Exil“; 113.198 Aufrufe)


– „Kein schöner Land… WO DIE EICHEN STEH’N“ („Freya“; 18.974 Aufrufe)


– „Thüringen Ein Land Eine Geschichte Ein Herz“ („Der Heimatklang“, 4334 Aufrufe)


– „Heimweh nach Deutschland“ („Liv Eisen“, 2067 Aufrufe)




Die Titel verraten schon das Wesentliche. Wenn man die Textzeilen hört oder liest, wird deutlich, dass die immer gleichen Narrative, endlos wiederholt werden. Stets geht es um den Verlust einer imaginären „Heimat“ oder glorreichen „Nation“, um eine angebliche „Überfremdung“, anknüpfend an den Verschwörungsmythos eines „großen Austauschs“. Der Gute-Laune-Faschismus lebt in der ewigen Wiederholung von Mustern immer gleicher Opfer-Inszenierungen, dem Streicheln narzisstischer Kränkungen, sowie der Vorstellung einer zukünftigen Größe, die nur durch die Erniedrigung der ausgemachten Feinde erreicht werden kann. All dies sind Produkte einer staatlich-kapitalistischen Gesellschaftsform, die mit Patriarchat, Rassismus und Naturbeherrschung verknüpft ist. Zusammengefasst ist die Computer-produzierte Lyrik in ihrem billigen Abklatsch armselig – und faschistisch.


Dabei darf man nicht vergessen, dass auch der historische Nationalismus keine naturwüchsige Volksbewegung war, sondern ein Elitenprojekt, das eine Nation und eine darin angeblich ursprünglich vorhandene Kultur verordnete, anerzog und drillte.




Hört man die künstlich erzeugten Lieder und ihre Texte an, greifen Form und Inhalt ineinander. Bekanntlich ist den Fans derartiger wohlfühlfaschistischer Erzeugnisse vollkommen egal, ob sie ein KI-generiertes Lied hören. Ganz im Gegenteil müssen Kulturprodukte, die sie ansprechen kitschig, einfach und manipulativ sein, um auf Interesse zu stoßen. Wenn ein paar hunderttausend oder wenige Millionen Leute neofaschistische KI-Songs feiern, könnte man sagen: geschenkt, dieser faschistische oder mit dem Faschismus sympathisierende Teil der Bevölkerung ist verloren und nicht zu überzeugen. Als Nebenprodukt einer bestimmten Herrschaftsordnung erstarkt er in ihrer Krise, kann aber nur mit dieser überwunden werden. Und das ist richtig. Dennoch ist es gerade der melodiöse Gute-Laune-Faschismus, dem die Anschlussfähigkeit an immer weitere Bevölkerungsteile gelingt. Doch woran liegt das?




Was damit klanglich und sprachlich angesprochen wird, ist das Gefühl einer umfassenden und tiefgreifenden Entfremdung. Im Kunstprodukt, dass seine eigene Künstlichkeit ironisiert und dadurch jede potenziell authentische Erfahrung verunmöglicht, kommt ein faschistisches Begehren zum Ausdruck. Dieser Computer-Kitsch ist das ästhetische Pendant zur Untergrabung jeglichen Wahrheitsgehalts von Aussagen durch deren absolute Relativierung mittels „alternativen Fakten“, die sich in der Lyrik niederschlagen.


Wie bei den Grundregeln der Werbung gilt hier: Die Rezipient*innen müssen vom Gehörten und Gesehenen nicht überzeugt werden – es reicht, ihnen solange Lügen einzuhämmern, nein, einzusäuseln, bis sie kapitulieren und diese als mögliche Wahrheit akzeptieren.




So weitet sich die bürgerliche Toleranz auf fatale Weise aus und lässt vormals überzeugte Demokrat*innen zweifeln: „Die Faschisten glauben eben, das ihre schöne Heimat verloren gegangen ist. Nun ja, ich weiß nicht, aber wenn sie das so fühle? Aber sie sind stolze Kämpfer und lassen sich das nicht bieten. Nun ja, immerhin stehen sie für was! Sie holen ihr Land zurück und wollen eigentlich nur, das am Ende alle glücklich sind.“ Außer jene, die abgeschoben, inhaftiert oder ermordet wurden. Abgesehen von denen, deren Arbeitsbedingungen schlechter, deren Lebensbedingungen prekärer werden, während die öffentliche Infrastruktur weiter zerbröckelt und die Ökosysteme komplett zusammenbrechen.




Daher ist die Musik des Gute-Laune-Faschismus auch ein Vorschein der schönen neuen Autokratie, die damit errichtet werden soll. Es wird schon hör- und sichtbar, womit jene ruhiggestellt werden sollen, die dazu beitragen, ihre eigene Lebensgrundlage zu vernichten. Der Grund dafür liegt wiederum in der tiefgreifenden Entfremdung der Menschen – von ihren Produkten, von der Mitwelt, von ihren Mitmenschen und von sich selbst: Wer sich von seinen Tätigkeiten und Produkten entfremdet, mag zum Schluss kommen, das heimtückische „Globalisten“ die naturwüchsige Automobilproduktion nach China verlagern; Er mag von deutschen Wäldern schwärmen, aber den Rest davon durch den Klimawandel vertrocknen lassen; Er kann mit den Schultern zucken, wenn die nicht-weißen und/oder oppositionellen Nachbar*innen abgeholt werden und sich über seine Teilhabe an der Volksgemeinschaft freuen; und schließlich mag er sich den Rhythmen der nationalistischen Autokratie unterwerfen und gleichzeitig tief empfinden, das Demokratie eigentlich diktatorisch wäre…




Somit dockt der Wohlfühl-Faschismus an die Entfremdung an, die ein Produkt der industriell-modernen Herrschaftsordnung ist und verstärkt sie zugleich. Denn es wäre ja ohnehin alles egal, alles falsch, alles zerrüttet. Also kann man auch KI-generierten Glitzer-Schleim darüber gießen um von kräftiger Jugendlichkeit, wilder Männlichkeit, sanfter Weiblichkeit, ursprünglicher Natürlichkeit, rechtschaffener Arbeit, schicksalhafter Volksgemeinschaft, heroischem Kampf und glorreicher Nation zu träumen… Was soll man dazu sagen? Außer trotzig: Wer zuletzt lacht, werden wir noch sehen. Und: mehr als drei der faschistischen KI-Songs sollte man sich nicht anhören, wenn man halbwegs klar im Kopf bleiben möchte.

author: Agenda2029
title: Sabotage gegen Rheinmetall – Niemals Kriegstüchtig!
content:
In Kassel soll das größte Panzerwerk Europas gebaut werden. Wir stellen uns dagegen, zur Rüstungshauptstadt für die kommenden Kriege zu werden. Deshalb haben wir in der Nacht die Baustelle des Logistikzentrums von Rheinmetall in Kassel-Calden sabotiert und mehrere Bagger und Radlager angezündet.




Zeitenwende in Nordhessen




Wer in Nordhessen lebt, spürt was Zeitenwende heißt. Tag für Tag überschlagen sich die Nachrichten von Rüstungsinvestitionen. Fast kein Abend vergeht ohne Panzer in unseren Straßen zu sehen, die in die Kriegsgebiete der Welt exportiert werden. Kaum ein Kommunalpolitiker, mittelständisches Unternehmen oder Forschungsstandort der nicht hofft, etwas von den Milliarden der Zeitenwende abzubekommen.




Wir haben uns dafür entschieden, dabei nicht länger zuzuschauen und ein zentrales Projekt der Aufrüstungskampagne angegriffen: den Defence Hub Nordhessen von Rheinmetall.




Der Defence Hub Nordhessen umfasst den Ausbau des Panzerwerks in Kassel sowie den Bau eines Logistikzentrums auf 30.000 Quadratmetern und eines militärischen Drohnenzentrums am Kassel-Airport. Mit 260 Millionen Euro von Rheinmetall und über 20 Millionen Euro vom Land Hessen soll das Projekt bis Ende 2027 hochgezogen werden.




Für das Pressespektakel zum Auftakt verkündete Rheinmetall Chef Armin Papperger stolz: Kassel wird zukünftig das größte Panzerwerk Europas und „eine neue Drehscheibe“ der Rüstungsindustrie sein. Boris Rhein ergänzte: Der kriselnde Flughafen Kassel-Calden wird „künftig noch stärker als militärische Drehscheibe, für Trainingsflüge der Bundeswehr sowie zur Erforschung und Erprobung neuer Drohnen-Technologie“ dienen.




Während jeden Monat Millionen an Steuergeldern in einen leeren Flughafen versenkt werden, von dem nur die Privatjets von Superreichen starten, soll das Aufrüstungsprogramm nun die Rettung sein: Drohnen, Bundeswehrflüge und Logistik ersetzen die Passagiere und Urlaubsgäste, die partout nicht kommen wollen.




Mit Staatsgeldern in die Krise




Was in Kassel-Calden passiert, ist ein Sinnbild für die Zeitenwende in Deutschland: Der Staat tritt als Auftraggeber auf und versucht mit Milliarden an Rüstungsinvestitionen die schwächelnde Wirtschaft anzukurbeln. Deutschland tritt die Flucht nach vorne an. Wenn die Autoproduktion auf dem Weltmarkt nicht mehr konkurrenzfähig ist, dann immerhin der Leopard-Panzer und vielleicht auch bald wieder das deutsche Heer.




In einer Zeit, die weltweit von imperialistischen Konflikten und Kriegen geprägt ist, will die Bundesrepublik ihre Krise durch militärische Aufrüstung lösen und zukünftig ohne die USA an der Spitze Europas stehen können. Was uns als notwendige Investitionen in die Verteidigungsfähigkeit verkauft wird, ist die Option, die eigenen Interessen wie Zugang zu Ressourcen und Handelsrouten mit militärischen Mitteln außerhalb Deutschlands durchsetzen zu können. Der Bau von eigenen Langstreckenwaffen oder die Befugnisse der Geheimdienste zur Sabotage im Ausland sind offensive Fähigkeiten. Es ist die Möglichkeit, künftig weiter die Konfrontation mit dem russischen Regime um die Vormachtstellung in Osteuropa eingehen zu können.




Von der Drehscheibe …




Wir wissen aus allen Konflikten der Großmächte, dass am Ende die einfachen Menschen, die Frauen und die Jugendlichen am meisten unter den Folgen des Krieges leiden werden. Nicht Armin Papperger und Boris Rhein oder deren Kinder sollen im Schützengraben von der Drohne zerfetzt werden, sondern wir. Wenn wir den Kriegsvorbereitungen nicht international entgegen treten, haben wir bald keine Perspektive für unser Leben mehr.




Je mehr Geld in die Rüstungsprojekte fließt und je weiter der Umbau ziviler Wirtschaft zur Kriegsindustrie voranschreitet, desto größer wird auch hier die wechselseitige Abhängigkeit und die Verflechtung zwischen Rüstungskonzernen und den staatlichen Auftraggebern werden. Gleichzeitig gehen die Panzer, die am Ende von Rheinmetall und Co. durch Staatsgelder produziert werden, nicht wieder produktiv in den Wirtschaftskreislauf ein. Die Aufrüstung wird die Krise der letzten Jahre nicht lösen, sondern höchstens verschieben.




Wenn in ein paar Jahren die Hallen voll mit Panzern und Sprengköpfen sind, werden die Probleme der deutschen Schwerindustrie und der mittelständischen Zulieferer nicht gelöst sein. Für Kassel bedeutet das: Geht die staatliche Nachfrage nach Kriegswaffen in ein paar Jahren wieder zurück, wird auch die davon abhängige Industrie zusammenbrechen und zahlreiche Menschen ihre Arbeit verlieren. Wird das Kriegsgerät im Einsatz verbraucht, hält das zwar die Produktion am Laufen, macht Kassel aber auch in kommenden Kriegen erneut zur Zielscheibe. Während sich die Aktionäre und Vorstände von Rheinmetall, KNDS und Co. die Taschen voll machen, können wir bei dieser Kalkulation langfristig nur verlieren.




…zum Ort des Widerstands




Lasst uns Nordhessen von einer Drehscheibe der Aufrüstung zum Ort des Widerstand gegen den Kriegskurs der Eliten machen. Lasst uns gemeinsam dafür Kämpfen, dass Menschen nicht mehr vor der Entscheidung stehen, ihren Job zu verlieren oder zu Rheinmetall zu wechseln. Lasst uns dafür sorgen, dass Elbit Systems und Co. nicht in Ruhe produzieren können und aus Kassel nicht länger Krieg und Genozid in die Welt exportiert wird.




In Gedenken an den Kasseler Studierenden Yousef Shaban, der am 24. Oktober 2023 mit seinen Familienangehörigen durch die IDF in Gaza ermordet wurde.




In Verbundenheit mit den russischen Kriegsgegner:innen und Saboteuren, die heute entweder im Straflager sitzen oder vom Regime getötet wurden.




In Solidarität mit allen, die weltweit gegen den Imperialismus kämpfen und sich hier der Militarisierung ihres Lebens widersetzen.




Ob an der Universität, an die die Kassler Rüstungskonzerne drängen. Ob an den Schulen, wo gegen die Wehrpflicht gestreikt wird. Ob in den Betrieben bei Daimler und Alstom, wo jetzt für den Tod produziert werden soll. Ob in den Krankenhäusern, die zukünftig Platz für die Kriegsopfer der Front machen sollen.




Niemals Kriegstüchtig!


Nicht heute


Nicht 2029


Nie wieder




Agenda2029

author: Aldrey Olegario
title: ‘Primavera Brasileira’: como ato de estudantes virou onda global contra extrema direita
content:
Na noite de 4 de outubro, quando Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) terminou à frente de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no 1.º turno das eleições, a seguinte mensagem chegou num grupo de WhatsApp de alunos da Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF): “O momento pede ação”. Na noite seguinte, 5 de outubro, o Brasil assistiu ao primeiro ato dos jovens.




“Nós vimos a vitória do Flávio de uma forma muito acachapante. Ninguém estava esperando. Aquilo gerou um sentimento de descrença muito forte no campo progressista. Mas na Faculdade de Direito da UFF, pela nossa história, enxergamos de forma contrária: com esperança e com vontade de ir à luta”, diz Kayky Moraes, aluno do curso de direito da UFF que participou do primeiro levante.




Realizada em Niterói, na região metropolitana do Rio de Janeiro, a marcha dos estudantes saiu do prédio da Faculdade de Direito rumo à reitoria da universidade. 

As imagens tomaram as redes e iniciaram um efeito dominó que impulsionou mobilizações estudantis nos cinco cantos do país. “Ali a gente sentiu que dava para brigar.”







Neste momento manifestação contra Bolsonaro pelos estudantes nas ruas Niterói 

pic.twitter.com/7sqGGEq7TV

— Fã do Rei Pelé e da Rainha Marta 

 

 

 (@silvaS1963) 

October 5, 2026







O resultado desse “efeito borboleta” veio no dia 25 de outubro, três semanas depois. Um feito histórico: Lula virou o jogo e 

venceu as eleições

 por uma vantagem de 4,4 milhões de votos, algo que nenhum candidato a presidente que terminou como segundo colocado no 1º turno havia conseguido fazer antes. Os eleitores de Lula e os estrategistas de campanha do PT tiveram apenas três semanas para mudar a rota. “Essa foi a campanha menos organizada que participei desde 1989”, chegou a dizer o presidente Lula em uma reunião com parlamentares em Brasília.




“Os jovens tomaram as ruas de forma orgânica e organizada para defender um projeto de país, mas também um projeto de ser humano. Quando Lula disse aquela frase para a gente ser ele amanhã, porque ele já foi a gente ontem e para a juventude botar a cara a tapa, acho que é isso mesmo”, diz Kayky, em referência a um trecho da entrevista de Lula para o podcast Flow. 

“Estamos fadados a viver o futuro e a gente tem que construir o futuro que a gente quer.”




A “primavera brasileira”, como começou a ser apelidada a vitória eleitoral frente à extrema direita, também pode ser vista por como uma posição do Brasil 

como símbolo de resistência aos interesses dos Estados Unidos, defende Mayra Goulart, doutora em ciência política pela UERJ.




“O Brasil será um pólo da resistência à relação imperial que os Estados Unidos tentam restabelecer. Na última assembleia geral da ONU, Lula disse que o Brasil não iria ser o quintal de ninguém. O presidente Lula recupera a tradição de não alinhamento automático da diplomacia brasileira a potências estrangeiras e a adoção de um caminho próprio e soberanista. Isso é entendido muitas vezes como um caminho que vem a liderar outros países periféricos”, diz.




A “Primavera Brasileira” vista do exterior




No México e na Espanha, a virada eleitoral brasileira foi recebida não apenas com alívio geopolítico, mas como um estudo de caso sobre como conter a ascensão da extrema direita.




Para Homero Campa Butrón, cientista político e professor da Universidade Nacional Autônoma do México (UNAM), a manutenção do governo progressista no Brasil evita o isolamento regional no continente. “Brasil e México representam 55% da população da América Latina e 60% da economia da região. O resultado no Brasil foi vital para o governo mexicano, pois evita o isolamento diante da onda de vitórias da direita na região nos últimos meses”, analisa Campa, destacando que a comunicação entre a presidenta mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum e Lula é direta e estratégica.




O impacto também ressoa na Europa. “Se o Brasil conseguiu, a Espanha também consegue”, disse o primeiro-ministro da Espanha Pedro Sánchez

, em um comício em Gijón, na região de Astúrias, realizado na segunda-feira, 26 de outubro. “Vamos fazer o mesmo que Lula fez no Brasil. O mundo está olhando para nós”, completou.




Com eleições gerais agendadas para o próximo mês na Espanha, onde as pesquisas têm indicado a predileção do eleitorado à direita, o desfecho brasileiro renovou o ânimo das forças de esquerda. “Certamente, no México e na Espanha, percebe-se um enorme interesse no modelo de mobilização social promovido por meio das redes sociais, coordenado pelo deputado André Janones. Entende-se que a estratégia de comunicação digital foi um fator fundamental no resultado”, diz o professor da UNAM.




A 

Agência Pública

 identificou que ao menos três grupos de WhatsApp internacionais reproduzem as táticas de engajamento de Janones para mobilizar apoiadores.

 É do caso do “Frenteamplistas” (37 mil seguidores), da Espanha, “L’équipe de Mélenchon” (152 mil seguidores), da França, e do “Ejército del Peronismo” (61 mil seguidores), da Argentina.
















Canais de Whatsapp internacionais reproduzem estratégia digital de André Janones




“A mobilização nas redes sociais é uma tendência global. O Brasil adere a isso de uma maneira muito acelerada e acredito que essa tendência seja muito similar em outros países. Ao mesmo tempo, isso não desconsidera a importância dos atores tradicionais, como o movimento estudantil e sindicatos, que foram acionados a partir das redes, mas permitiram um engajamento muito grande no mundo real. Se é que podemos dizer em uma fórmula, ela deve ser buscada na sinergia entre o mundo físico e as redes sociais”, pontua Goulart.




Ainda nesta semana, viralizou um vídeo compartilhado por Ada Colau, ex-prefeita de Barcelona e candidata à presidência da Espanha pela Frente Ampla, no qual ela pede para que os apoiadores ergam as mãos em “L”

 — um aceno ao presidente brasileiro. “Vamos todos levantar o braço com o ‘L’ de Lula”, disse ela, durante ato no município de Móstoles na quarta-feira (28).




“Eu me lembro desse momento. O gesto de Acolau foi bastante simbólico e foi num dia próximo ao da notícia da vitória de Lula. Acho que foi uma surpresa para todo mundo. Acho que a maioria das pessoas dava como certo que a probabilidade do filho do [Jair] Bolsonaro ganhar era muito alta. O gesto reafirma a vitória de Lula e diz que nós, por aqui, também temos plena capacidade de fazer o mesmo”, conta Euge, 22, morador da cidade de Madrid que esteve no comício organizado pela Frente Ampla.




“Acredito que Lula tem sido um vislumbre de esperança para as pessoas de esquerda e para os trabalhadores da Espanha e do mundo todo. Estamos vivendo um momento em que temos governos de extrema direita como nunca antes. Lula conseguiu vencer com a maioria das pesquisas dizendo o contrário. A mensagem que chegou aqui na Espanha foi de que, ainda que pareça que tudo está contra, é possível vencer. Se conseguirmos mobilizar todas as pessoas progressistas, nós venceremos”, continua ele.




Também fizeram o “L” de Lula, a presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, o senador do México Gerardo Fernández e parlamentares do Congresso Nacional do Chile.

 Já utilizado como chacota, especialmente entre bolsonaristas, o “L” agora ganha espaço no cenário político mundial como símbolo da mobilização contra o avanço da direita.







 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

View this post on Instagram

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 







“O Brasil desponta como liderança da resistência à extrema direita em termos globais. A extrema direita é globalizada, sistêmica e se reúne em fóruns, como a CPAC [Conservative Political Action Conference]. A esquerda começa a se articular e essa articulação pode ter como centro a liderança do presidente Lula”, diz Goulart.




Nascido na cidade de Getafe, ao sul da região de Madri, Euge se interessou por política ainda na adolescência. Em 2019, aos 15 anos, decidiu participar do Más Madrid, um partido de esquerda com atuação a nível municipal em Madri. Para Euge, a participação de jovens na política é importante, mas não se distingue do papel das outras faixas etárias. “Sempre falam aos jovens: ‘vocês são o futuro!’ Bom, não é que a gente seja o futuro, somos o presente de um país. Temos que estar em igualdade tanto de reconhecimento quanto de possibilidade de participar da vida pública e da vida política. As decisões que os governos tomam nos afetam da mesma forma, e muitas delas ainda mais do que ao resto das pessoas.”




Sobre o recado que deseja que as próximas eleições da Espanha passem ao mundo, Euge diz esperar que seja o mesmo que o do Brasil: “Uma mensagem de que não baixamos os braços, que demos de tudo e conseguimos mobilizar a população com temas essenciais para sua vida, como moradia, pensão e serviços públicos.”




A mobilização da juventude




Além do protesto organizado pelos estudantes da UFF logo após o resultado do primeiro turno, outra engrenagem importante passou a se movimentar: os fandoms (comunidade de fãs) brasileiros.

 Longe de se restringirem ao entretenimento, esses grupos já vinham consolidando uma ponte direta com a política institucional.




No final de agosto deste ano, o 

Palácio do Planalto

 recebeu representantes desses grupos em uma cerimônia oficial, na qual o presidente Lula assinou um decreto com novas regras para a venda de ingressos de shows e eventos culturais no país. A medida, voltada ao combate do cambismo digital e à falta de transparência nas plataformas, foi fruto das demandas levadas pelos próprios fãs ao governo federal.




E esse pode ter sido um grande 

efeito borboleta

 da campanha: a mesma capacidade de mobilização que esses jovens utilizam para apoiar seus ídolos foi redirecionada no momento mais decisivo da disputa eleitoral, sendo uma das principais apostas da chapa Lula-Alckmin para furar bolhas e alcançar a virada. Para o leitor que ainda busca entender como esse movimento funciona, os fandoms são comunidades hiperconectadas e altamente disciplinadas, capazes de organizar mutirões de votação e subir hashtags mundiais.




Assim, as páginas passaram a publicar conteúdos de conscientização política, convocando mutirões de engajamento, dialogando com seguidores indecisos e pedindo o posicionamento de artistas sobre a defesa da democracia no Brasil.


















































































A relevância do movimento foi tamanha que o candidato à reeleição abriu sua fala reconhecendo a força dessa articulação num dos discursos proferidos na Avenida Paulista após o 1º turno.







“Eu não sei se eu começo a minha fala dizendo ‘companheiros e companheiras’ ou se eu começo dizendo: fandoms do Brasil, obrigado pela iniciativa de vocês!”

O presidente Lula agradecendo à juventude organizada em fandoms por puxar o ato de hoje na Paulista 

#FandomsComLula

 

pic.twitter.com/dWPL8ISHS6

— ERIKA HILTON (@ErikakHilton) 

October 11, 2026







Janonismo cultural e a urgência de regulamentação das Big Techs




Ao longo desta primeira semana pós 2º turno, o livro 

Janonismo Cultural: O uso das redes sociais e a batalha pela democracia no Brasil

, de André Janones, figurou entre os 10 títulos mais vendidos da Amazon no nicho de Política e Ciências Sociais.

 Exitoso ao encabeçar a estratégia digital de Lula, Janones foi destacado no primeiro discurso do presidente reeleito.




Apesar do otimismo com a capacidade da sociedade brasileira de reverter os algoritmos, Campa faz um alerta sobre a vulnerabilidade desse modelo: “a falta de regulamentação das grandes empresas de tecnologia constitui um perigo para a vida pública no mundo inteiro. O que ocorreu no Brasil foi muito positivo: uma reação social massiva e bem organizada para reverter o algoritmo. No entanto, receio que essas empresas estejam tomando nota do que aconteceu no Brasil para introduzir controles maiores e evitar que se repita”, pontua Homero.




A 

Pública

 mostrou em 

reportagens

 como a moderação da Meta atingiu de forma desproporcional as candidaturas, beneficiando em vários casos a de Flávio em detrimento da de Lula.




Nesse cenário, a regulamentação das plataformas surge como uma demanda democrática, observa Goulart. “No discurso de vitória, Lula disse que um dos objetivos do governo seria regulamentar as plataformas para que elas aumentem a isonomia das entregas entre diferentes grupos. É importantíssimo que isso seja feito. Caso contrário, a valorização desproporcional dos conteúdos da extrema direita quando comparados com outros conteúdos irá continuar, principalmente com o sistema de recomendação e hierarquização do feed.”




Para o analista mexicano, a esquerda global precisará acelerar sua adaptação aos novos modelos de comunicação, ao mesmo tempo em que pressiona por regras claras contra a interferência de grandes corporações de tecnologia nas democracias. “A mensagem que fica do Brasil é de otimismo e confiança na sociedade diante dos grandes grupos tecnológicos e da ultradireita. O Brasil demonstrou uma liderança inegável para todo o Sul Global” conclui.




Na visão de Kayky, da UFF, a mobilização não se encerra com o resultado das urnas. “Acho que daqui nasce a esperança de um futuro melhor. O recado de um levante que começou aqui em Niterói está se espalhando pelo mundo. Dá para ver o jardim da primavera florescendo pelo mundo todo. Mas é sempre importante manter a vigilância e continuar nas ruas para defender essa visão de mundo.”

El miércoles 28 se realizó una nueva jornada de la protesta de jubilados y jubiladas que es un ejemplo de resistencia frente al Gobierno de Milei. Sus reclamos sobre el incremento de haberes, la entrega de medicamentos y el financiamiento del PAMI son urgentes, pero desoídos por la gestión. Sin recibir respuesta, mantienen su ronda por la Plaza del Congreso, a la que se suman manifestantes de distintas organizaciones.

author: rimsha syed
title: Houston Activists Are Working to Disrupt the Flow of Weapons to Israel
content:
Organizers and workers around the world are highlighting the invisible complicity of logistics companies in genocide.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

On October 30, port workers in over 100 locations across the world stood in principled resistance to Israel’s ongoing genocide through an international strike meant to constrict the arms trade and physically halt munitions destined to be used in Palestine. From coast to coast, linking arms in the struggle against maritime transport has been a historic strategy to intervene in the material transport of weapons, ammunition, and military equipment, through coordinated direct action by the working class.

Three years into Israel’s livestreamed genocide, actions of international magnitude underscore the immediate and collective need to stop the flow of artillery into Gaza. Following the repeated demands of the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions to “urgently halt the arms trade with Israel” and “take action against complicit companies involved in implementing Israel’s brutal and illegal siege,” several grassroots arms embargo campaigns in port cities across the United States — including New York City, Oakland, and Houston — have been mobilizing alongside dockworkers, transportation crews, and unions.

In New York, the “Break the Chain” campaign is fighting to halt explosives and F-35 bomber components from reaching Gaza through the JFK Airport. In Oakland, the People’s Arms Embargo gathered hundreds outside FedEx’s massive Air Freight Center in East Oakland to protest the company’s complicity in shipping arms to Israel. Last year, the Palestinian Youth Movement shared a report stating that in 2025, at least 280 military cargo shipments, including parts for one of the world’s most lethal fighter jets, reached Gaza via Oakland’s airport. Now, the Houston arms embargo campaign is calling on Texans to join their week of action to confront logistics executives complicit in unfathomable violence and destruction at the 2026 Houston International Maritime Conference.

In the sweltering September Houston heat, at a cafe with “ICE not welcome” signs plastered on every door and window, arms embargo organizers hosted a teach-in about the city’s port — a key transportation hub for the global weapons supply chain. Elsewhere in the cafe, others hand-crafted banners with calls that read “A Future Without Genocide, A Port for the People” as a response to the conference’s slogan “Lessons from the Past, Strategies for the Future.”

The fifth annual maritime conference, hosted from November 2-5, presents a unique opportunity to directly confront executives from logistics companies responsible for supplying the Israeli military with weapons. Roshni Ahmed, a member of the outreach working group, said that the arms embargo demands aren’t new: “Many people in the past three years have felt a deep sense of hopelessness and heartbreak watching the genocide unfold.” In May 2024, the Palestinian Youth Movement launched the #MaskOffMaersk campaign, in which Houston has played a critical role through a myriad of ongoing organizing strategies.

“Through coordinated pressure, boycotts, and refusal to handle military cargo, the world can make these genocidal supply chains politically untenable.”

“Arms embargo campaigns, such as this one in Houston, give people a very tangible way to stop the genocide by cutting off the very weapons that are used to kill Palestinians,” said Ahmed. The movement against the blood-soaked military industrial complex in Houston centers on Lockheed Martin’s massive aeronautics production plant in nearby Fort Worth, where the F-35 fighter jet is assembled from components transported on Maersk container ships before being flown directly to the Nevatim Airbase and used to bomb the besieged population in Palestine. “From 2020 to 2025, Houston’s port processed 85 percent of all Israeli shipments of F-35 fighter jet parts,” said Ahmed, noting how logistics companies like Maersk directly facilitate U.S. and Israeli wars.

Logistics companies like Maersk “are integral to the arms pipeline sustaining Israel’s genocidal assault in Gaza and its brutal military occupation of the West Bank,” said Dr. Jake Alimahomed-Wilson, a professor of sociology at California State University. Over 2 million Palestinians are being intentionally starved in the Gaza Strip, a tactic engineered by Israel to exact maximum suffering as bombardments continue. Israel’s blockade on essential humanitarian aid cannot be understood in isolation from commercial networks that perpetuate these war crimes, and “through coordinated pressure, boycotts, and refusal to handle military cargo, the world can make these genocidal supply chains politically untenable,” Dr. Alimahomed-Wilson said.

Organizers hope to use the week of action to emphasize that Houston residents are invested in using the city’s infrastructure to better their communities rather than continue facilitating genocide. Simply put, the arms embargo campaign demands that no military cargo for Israel moves through Houston’s port. Through a multi-pronged approach that takes inspiration from previous organizing wins within the context of Palestinian liberation and beyond, Houston activists have planned several demonstrations throughout the week: a region-wide protest with Palestine Youth Movement chapters across the state, a picket with union and faith group members, and an installation honoring Palestinians killed by Israel alongside a people’s panel that will happen concurrently outside the conference at Hilton Americas in downtown Houston.

“The installations are incredibly powerful visuals to understand the depth of the organizing that has happened nationally and internationally,” said Ahmed. “The installation focused on logistics shipping company Maersk depicts the many wins we’ve seen around the globe from dockworker strikes across ports in Morocco and Italy, and Spain’s arms embargo as well as stopping trade with illegal settlements.” The October 30 International Port Strike brings together unions from France, Greece, the Basque Country, Turkey, Morocco, and Italy, representing workers from more than 40 European and Mediterranean ports. In a similar vein, Houston-based organizers are pushing for direct action initiatives to intervene in one of the material conditions that makes genocide possible: the invisible complicity of logistics companies.

The Houston arms embargo campaign is a fragment of the global struggle for a liberated Palestine. Organized worker strikes across the globe have gained momentum as ordinary people of conscience decide that their government’s complicity and inaction mean taking matters into their own hands. Arms embargo campaigns in Houston, as well as across the country and the globe, demonstrate vulnerabilities in the weapons supply chain that have historically been deemed “choke points” and thus targets of collective pressure.

“In fact, there’s a long history of dockworkers, seafarers, and other workers taking coordinated action to refuse to work cargo or commodities to protest injustice, imperialism, fascism, and war,” said Dr. Peter Cole, a professor of history at Western Illinois University and scholar of dockworker activism. It’s clear that the United States is committed to its multi-billion-dollar defense agreements with the Israeli military, and as Israel’s biggest arms supplier, “the thing [logistics and] business executives would most likely respond to is if their profits are interrupted,” said Dr. Cole. “Stopping work or being community activists who are able to stop the work seems like an effective tactic.”

“There’s a long history of dockworkers, seafarers, and other workers taking coordinated action to refuse to work cargo or commodities to protest injustice, imperialism, fascism, and war.”

Each vein of the campaign, from confronting logistics executives to tapping into the diverse organizing ecosystem in Houston, is meant to cultivate stronger relationships between allied organizations that support peace and justice. In doing so, arms embargo activists have called on labor unions, student movements, faith groups, and community-based organizations to join the week of action to halt the flow of capital and logistics that fund the Israeli death machine. On September 27, the Texas State Employees Union (TSEU)/ CWA Local 6186 voted unanimously to endorse the arms embargo campaign and join the ranks of union solidarity with Palestine, refusing business as usual.

Josiah Rector, a representative of TSEU, a union representing nearly 10,000 state agency and public university employees and retirees across Texas, co-sponsored the resolution to endorse the week of action, stating that “this week of action is an opportunity to increase pressure on Port of Houston officials, on war profiteers like Maersk, and on all other actors who are actively or passively complicit in this machinery of death and destruction.” After attending several arms embargo workshops and trainings in preparation for Houston’s week of action, Rector noted, “Houston is also headquarters to multinational oil and gas companies like Chevron and ExxonMobil that literally fuel the war machine.”

“Here in the state of Texas, public sector unions (except for police and firefighters) have no collective bargaining rights and no right to strike,” said Rector. “It is still important for us to stand in solidarity with Palestinian trade unions and the international working class by all the means at our disposal: passing resolutions, showing up at protest actions, doing public education, and generally participating in these campaigns.”

As these words are penned, more than 3,300 Palestinians have been forced from their homes in Hebron as Israel’s brutal lockdown of the besieged West Bank continues past Israel’s elections. As Israel’s rearmament continues, requiring a growing involvement of logistics companies and transportation schemes, a network of unionized masses and grassroots arms embargo campaigns is but one example of a path forward. Warehouses, ports, and distribution sites are inseparable from war, and the fate of Palestinians, as well as people in Lebanon, Syria, Iran, and all other nations destroyed by war profiteers, requires our continued steadfast resistance. From Spain to Oakland, from Morocco to New York City, people are using all the tools at their disposal to disrupt the networks that make Israel’s genocide possible. Houston’s week of action is an essential node in the international struggle for liberation.

author: David Swanson
title: The 10 Worst Congressional Excuses for Voting for More Military Spending
content:
Economic Cost, Immorality, Law, Myth of Necessity, North America, What to do

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 30, 2026

Every year for many years now, the bitterly divided, grid-locked, virtually civil-war-waging United States Congress (as it’s commonly depicted) has harmoniously voted for vastly more money in war spending than it had done the year before. Our lords and misrepresentatives are threatening the same again right now.

It’s a heartwarming story of cooperation and understanding, no doubt, but how can you, as an elected official, explain to constituents living third-world lives in a wealthy nation that, not only can you not tax the rich or the corporations, but you also cannot afford to fund education, energy, environment, transportation, retirement, healthcare, or housing because the weapons dealers just want more and more?

The trick, of course, in most cases is to keep your head down and your mouth shut until a bigger military spending bill than last year’s is guaranteed to pass no matter how you vote, and then vote No. You’ll be untouchable. It’s golden. You won’t have publicly organized your colleagues or used various available procedures to actually try to reduce the war spending, but you’ll have an “I voted No” shield, and that’s all you’ll need. Constituents will fall for it without fooling any weapons dealers.

But what if it’s your turn? What if you’ve drawn the short string this year? What if you can either vote Yes or anger your party’s “leader”?

Never fear! That’s what this handy guide is for! Here are 10 popular categories of excuses that have proven effective through the past quarter-century.

You can easily depict an increase to military spending as a decrease if it’s a smaller increase than someone — ideally the president — had initially proposed. This one is in the works right now and may prove very successful. A variation on this is to claim that the bad political party (the one you’re not in) would have gotten a larger increase if you hadn’t hurried or stalled, depending on which party is gaining or losing a majority.

Almost foolproof is the oft-used explanation that you focused your efforts on doing exactly what the peace activists wanted by removing some nasty section from the bill. “You didn’t want the U.S. and Israeli militaries to merge. You said to only vote for the bill if that was removed. We got it removed on condition that we vote for the bill. This is how things work in the real world.” This excuse gets a 5 out of 5 on Yelp. Anyone who objects is a silly dreamer, so you need not address their concerns.

Almost matching the batting record of #2 (removing something) is adding something. It hardly matters how absurd the thing or how out of place in an institution of mass-murder and destruction, as long as it’s humanitarian. Create an agency of environmentally sustainable carpet bombing, or eliminate discrimination against transgendered pilots, or establish a proactive contracting program to minority-owned surveillance companies. Whatever. Anyone who objects will be objecting to that thing you voted for. You should be clear that it is only that thing for which you voted; nothing else exists.

If you cannot use the top three steaming turds of the coming apocalypse, or don’t have time to come up with anything concrete, just fall back on troopism. You voted to fund the troops. Anyone objecting hates the troops, wants the troops left in the wars but their armor and weaponry carefully collected and brought home without them. If you can, grab an actual troop or three to stand in front of and ask one of them to slap you in the face really quickly until there are tears visible in your eyes before the cameras are ready.

Numerous other excuses can work beautifully, depending on the circumstances. There’s always a most-unpopular war among the current wars. Right now, for example, some people are more upset about the crumbs going to the war on Iran than about the mountain of loafs going to the Pentagon in its entirety. So, here’s what you do. You make getting a war powers resolution on Iran vetoed part of a grand bargain in which you vote for the money to create 10 more similar wars. Or you join in a lawsuit against the war on Iran. Or you actually include in the spending bill or elsewhere a ban on spending money on that particular crime — but make clear to everyone that it’s part of a grand bargain on a 4-D chessboard. You voted for increased war money FOR PEACE and so that you could end THE war!

While changing the topic is a losing argument when done too blatantly, it can be very, very effective when done through omission and media saturation. If you can make something else the big story and do something peace-ish on that big thing, you can get huge mileage out of it. For example, you vote for more war money but you also VOTE TO IMPEACH HEGSETH. That doesn’t remove Hegseth, much less the guy whose every whim he obeys, but it’s AWESOME!

Pretty darn powerful, as well, is the futile legislation ploy (FLP). You may vote to increase military spending by 20 percent, but if you are a cosponsor and champion of separate legislation that would reduce military spending by 10 percent, your peace-loving constituents will understand that you are with them.

You don’t actually need me to tell you this. You know it’s there when the time is right. Anyone who objects to your war votes is anti-Semitic. QED.

Sure, you may have voted for increased spending on wars, but you’re in a super-purple district. If you were to give the forces of darkness the chance to label you “weak on defense” then your constituents would end up with a racist, sexist pig voting for increased mass-murder funding in place of you doing it. Which would they rather have?

Thanks for addressing this and we definitely can stop the apocalypse. We’ll be fine if we keep at it. Reply

author: Jillian Kestler-D’Amours
title: Masked White Supremacists Are Stoking Residential School Denialism in Canada
content:
“We have endured fear, and we will not be intimidated,” one Indigenous leader said.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

It was 3:00 am when Doug George-Kanentiio first arrived at the Mohawk Institute Residential School in Brantford, Ontario, in 1967.

He was 11 years old, and he would go on to spend 18 months at the abusive institution, which was Canada’s longest-running residential school. The notorious school operated for more than 140 years before it closed in 1970.

“They weren’t places of learning, they were places of confinement,” George-Kanentiio said.

Decades later, he still remembers the hunger, fear, and brutality that he and the other Indigenous children who were forced to attend the Mohawk Institute endured there every day.

“Anything you could imagine [being done] to a child, when it comes to abuse, that’s what these individuals did,” said George-Kanentiio, who is from Akwesasne, a Kanien’kehá:ka (Mohawk) community on the U.S.-Canada border, between New York state and the provinces of Ontario and Quebec.

“It was physically painful and extraordinarily cruel,” he told Truthout.

More than 150,000 First Nations, Metis, and Inuit children were separated from their families and forced to attend residential schools across Canada between the 1870s and the mid-1990s.

The institutions — which aimed to forcibly assimilate Indigenous children into the country’s predominantly white European culture — were rife with physical, sexual, and psychological abuse.

The children were barred from speaking their languages, and thousands are believed to have died while in attendance due to abuse, malnutrition, and rampant disease that resulted from squalid conditions. In 2015, a federal commission of inquiry said the system amounted to “cultural genocide.”

Yet while George-Kanentiio and other survivors have spoken about their abuse for years, efforts to downplay, minimize, and distort facts about the residential school system are getting louder in Canada.

The rising wave of residential school denialism has drawn widespread alarm as Indigenous community leaders and other experts say right-wing figures are trying to derail truth and reconciliation — the process of investigating and redressing the devastating impacts of Canada’s colonial policies, including its residential school system — while harming survivors in the process.

Niigaanwewidam Sinclair, an Indigenous studies professor at the University of Manitoba, likened residential school denialism to Holocaust denialism.

“They’ll say, ‘We’re just asking questions, it’s free speech, we’re trying to just tell the other side,’” he told Truthout.

“They weren’t places of learning, they were places of confinement.”

But he emphasized that residential school denialists are not really interested in a “good-faith conversation.” Instead, Sinclair said, they have two main goals: to “monetize ignorance” and to gain public attention.

“They’re trying to profit off of the fact that for 150 years Canadians were miseducated about Indigenous peoples and residential schools in particular,” he explained.

The issue came to a very public head last month when a group of about two dozen masked men affiliated with white nationalist group Second Sons Canada gathered on the lands of Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc, an Indigenous (First Nation) community in the province of British Columbia.

Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc has faced years of pressure from denialists since it announced in 2021 that a preliminary radar search of the grounds of the former Kamloops Indian Residential School had uncovered the potential remains of more than 200 children.

The discovery sparked a reckoning across Canada as people demanded justice for the myriad crimes committed at residential schools, which were funded by the government but run by various churches.

But the findings in Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc also fueled denialism, with far right activists and politicians seizing on early reporting errors to accuse the community and media outlets of lying.

“The entire country is motivated and moving towards implementing truth and reconciliation,” whereas denialists are “trying to slow things down, and they’re trying to profit,” said Sinclair.

The men who entered Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc in late September hung a banner on an overpass that day reading, “Got bones?” — a reference to the 2021 discovery of possible remains.

The incident drew widespread condemnation, including from Prime Minister Mark Carney, who called it a “disgusting display of hate.”

For its part, the Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc community said it would not stop “continuing to share the truth.”

“White supremacy will not instill fear in generations of Survivors and Intergenerational Survivors who have already carried fear for far too long,” Kúkwpi7 (chief) Rosanne Casimir said in a statement. “We have endured fear, and we will not be intimidated.”

Sean Carleton, an expert on residential school denialism who also teaches at the University of Manitoba, said the incident marked “a Canadian Charlottesville moment,” referring to the 2017 white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Carleton said it’s not a coincidence that the Second Sons Canada “stunt” came just days before millions of Canadians took part in National Day for Truth and Reconciliation rallies and other events.

“Using the tactics of the American far right — because many of them are influenced by this — this [was] basically a stunt by 30 masked dudes trying to derail and distract, deliberately provoking, [and] using racism and the rhetoric of denialism to change the conversation,” he told Truthout.

But Carleton warned that while it may be easy to denounce residential school denialism “when it looks like fascism and white supremacist groups marching in masks,” the phenomenon can be slyer, too.

“We need to have a flexible enough definition to be able to see all of [it], such that we don’t say in this country, ‘Well anything that’s not a provocative banner drop is OK,’” he said. “We need to understand that [denialism] takes different forms and they’re all equally repugnant.”

The Canadian government has acknowledged the issue, saying residential school denialism “compounds the harms” that survivors and Indigenous people across the country experience.

“It was physically painful and extraordinarily cruel.”

In a September statement, the minister of Crown-Indigenous relations, Rebecca Alty, said Ottawa earmarked $3.5 million ($5 million Canadian) for public education on residential schools.

A focus, she said, would be placed “on delivering informative and accessible content that clearly addresses misinformation and denialist claims.”

But many say education alone can’t fix the problem, and calls are growing for Canada to criminalize residential school denialism in the same way that Holocaust denial is criminalized.

The Assembly of First Nations (AFN), a national advocacy group, recently passed an emergency resolution calling for residential school denialism to be categorized as a hate crime.

“This country perpetuates hate crimes, they condone it,” Grand Chief Garrison Settee of Manitoba Keewatinowi Okimakanak, which represents 26 First Nations in Manitoba, said after the unanimous July vote.

“And this is not acceptable to our people, to our survivors, and those that did not survive,” he said.

In 2021, the government also established the Residential Schools Missing Children Community Support Fund to help communities find and commemorate unmarked burial sites.

Efforts to downplay, minimize, and distort facts about the residential school system are getting louder in Canada.

But three years later, in 2024, Ottawa attempted to cap the amount of funding that would be available, drawing fierce criticism. The decision was later reversed due to public pressure.

“Funding for search activities is an essential part of the debt of justice owed to the families and Nations whose children were forcibly taken away,” Stephanie Scott, executive director of the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, said at the time. “Funding must be determined by need, not by arbitrary formula.”

According to George-Kanentiio in Akwesasne, a focus should be placed on finding the children who never came home from the residential schools. He said that means making sure communities who are committed to identifying and uncovering the unmarked graves have the funding to do that work.

“We have to find the children because their spirits still have not been released to go on to their respective journey,” he explained.

“We need to do that, and we are committed to that. Whenever we have a gathering, we reaffirm that — that there’s no peace unless those children are found, and unless the children are found, there’s no justice.”

Truthout is funded almost entirely by readers — that’s why we can speak truth to power and cut against the mainstream narrative. But independent journalists at Truthout face mounting political repression under Trump.
