title: Tuncay Yılmaz: We want to build a united front of resistance in Europe - Part One
content:
As the rise of the far right, war policies, hostility towards migrants and attacks on democratic rights continue across Europe, political and social organisations from Turkey and Kurdistan are strengthening their efforts to build a common struggle. On 17 October, 25 organisations gathered in Cologne, Germany, and decided to establish a new alliance to unite their struggles for peace, democracy, equality and freedom. At the meeting, 20 organisations representing different political traditions declared their willingness to become founding members. The democratic resolution of the Kurdish question and the Peace and Democratic Society Process were also among the main issues discussed.




ANF spoke to Tuncay Yılmaz, founding co-chair of the Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP), about the outcomes of the Cologne meeting, the need for a common struggle, the situation of left-wing and democratic forces in the face of the rising far right in Europe, and the roadmap for the proposed alliance.




On 17 October, 25 organisations from different political traditions came together in Cologne. Similar attempts to build alliances have been made in Europe before. Why has the need to establish a common platform for struggle emerged again today? What distinguishes this meeting from previous initiatives?




As you said, organisations from different political traditions and social groups in Europe have come together at various times. Previously, there was the European Assembly for Peace and Democracy (ABDEM). We then extended the organisation of the Peoples' Democratic Congress (HDK) in Turkey to Europe, establishing a broad organisation under the name HDK Europe. This organisation later became the European Democratic Forces Union (ADGB) and continued its activities under that name. Most recently, ahead of the NATO summit, a joint initiative called PANEV was established against imperialist aggression, wars and the NATO.




All these initiatives emerged from efforts to find ways for the forces of democracy, peace, equality and freedom to become better organised in Europe and pursue more effective political action against the enormous aggressive power confronting us.




The alliances we established at different times sometimes lost their effectiveness, both because of changes in the objective conditions in which they were formed and, to speak frankly, because of our own shortcomings. This is a reality, and we are aware of it. Indeed, this was one of the issues on the agenda of our meeting. We want to learn from our previous experiences.




However, the mistakes we made in the past or the changes we have experienced should not prevent us from bringing democratic forces together again and carrying out a common struggle. And indeed, they are not preventing us. One of the main motivations that brought us together at this meeting was the growing hostility towards migrants in the European countries where we live, the rise of the right, fascist movements coming to power and increasing state violence. The fact that laws targeting asylum seekers have reached almost inhumane proportions is also deeply concerning to all of us. We want to build a united front of resistance against all of this.




At the same time, however, all our attention, thoughts and concerns are focused on developments in Turkey. Looking at Turkey, we see a totalitarian regime being built step by step. Everyone who opposes it becomes a target. Presidential candidates are arrested. Selahattin Demirtaş has been imprisoned for years, as has Figen Yüksekdağ. Ekrem İmamoğlu was subsequently arrested. The Republican People's Party (CHP), which prides itself on being the founding party of the state, is also under serious pressure. Attempts are being made to divide the party, and many of its representatives have been arrested.




Alongside all this, a negotiation process has begun. It has not yet reached the stage of a peace process. However, this negotiation process has the potential to generate a collective strength capable of pushing back attacks on democracy through the positive developments it could bring to the country's political life. Despite this, we see that the political authorities are acting with appalling arbitrariness in this process as well.




To speak frankly, this process has been made possible by the determination and goodwill of Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. After all, decisions were taken to lay down arms and dissolve the organisation. These decisions represent a profound transformation in the movement's historical existence.




Despite this, the state continues to display an extremely indifferent and unserious attitude towards taking steps on these issues, potentially jeopardising the process. Its actions could allow the anti-democratic practices it maintains throughout the country to continue in different forms in this area as well. We can all see that, for months, instead of implementing the legal arrangements brought onto Parliament's agenda with broad support, the authorities have merely continued saying, "We want this as well, and we want that too."




Frankly, they are acting entirely with the mentality of a trader. Instead of seriously addressing such a fundamental problem facing the state, the regime and the country, and taking steps to resolve it, the process is being conducted through demands such as, "What did you get? What did you give? Do this as well, do that as well."




Considering all these developments, we see that, as social and political organisations in Europe, we cannot pursue a politics focused solely on protecting ourselves, withdrawing into our own circles and limiting ourselves to our own concerns. The Confederation of European Alevi Unions (AABK), the Kurdistan Democratic Communities Congress in Europe (KCDK-E) and many socialist groups are part of this alliance.




When we assess developments in Turkey, Europe, the region and the world together, the necessity of carrying out a common struggle against them becomes clear. I believe this is precisely why we were able to organise such a broad gathering on 17 October.




As the far right gains strength in Europe, hostility towards migrants, racism and war policies are increasingly being debated. Yet left-wing and democratic forces appear to be struggling to act together. What do you think are the main reasons for this fragmentation? What role could the alliance being established in Cologne play in changing this situation?




It is very clear that we are moving towards a major transformation of the international system established after the Second World War. Very negative changes are taking place both in the balance of power between imperialist centres and in the relations between the ruling classes and oppressed sections of society.




I would like to explain this through a few examples. The developments taking place today in the Middle East, Syria, Palestine, Lebanon, all four parts of Kurdistan and Iran are connected to tensions over which powers will control the world's trade routes, valuable minerals and energy resources. Essentially, the world is being redesigned. This is not limited to the Middle East. The restructuring process is creating tensions across the entire world.




Secondly, certain gains regulating economic and social life, which the capitalist-imperialist bloc was compelled to accept in some form during the existence of the Soviet Union, are now being rejected. For example, there are discussions in Germany about raising the retirement age to 70.




Why are young people taking to the streets in such large numbers in France? Why do they refuse to leave the streets despite such intense state violence? What are the fundamental demands that have brought the student movement in Serbia towards success? What lies behind the developments in Albania?




At the root of all this is the following reality: the ruling classes do not see a strong alternative or opposition capable of challenging them. Consequently, they are introducing measures aimed at securing as many advantages as possible in line with their own interests, both internationally and nationally.




The left, on the other hand, has frankly failed to create a comprehensive and renewed alternative. Without a coherent programme that society can embrace, internalise and stand behind, support for the left inevitably declines.




However, there are examples where this situation has been overcome. I believe these experiences offer important lessons about what we need to do.




Take Brazil, for example. Despite the support of the United States and major technology companies, from Elon Musk to Meta, Bolsonaro lost and Lula managed to win. The decisive factor was the creation of a common programme that brought together the demands not only of the working class but also of Indigenous peoples, poor peasants, young people and women.




In other words, movements that can bring together different sections of society opposed to the existing ruling system and unite them around a common programme can achieve success.




We see a similar experience in France. Yes, Macron remains in power, and the far right represented by Le Pen is in a strong position. However, the experience of La France Insoumise (France Unbowed) and the New Popular Front demonstrates that, despite all the risks, different opposition groups can come together around shared democratic demands.




What matters here is developing a programme capable of responding to society's most fundamental and pressing problems. People look at what you are concretely proposing to address the problems they face.




For example, the reason Elif Eralp has been able to come to the fore in Berlin against the Social Democratic Party (SPD), which enjoys the backing of major capital interests, is that she has developed a programme addressing society's fundamental problems. Similarly, the Communist Party's electoral victories over three terms in Graz, Austria, provide another example.




The existing system claims that it can set housing prices as it wishes and transform the healthcare system to the detriment of society. Society, in turn, is reacting against this.




In short, the left has not yet managed to develop a comprehensive response to this new situation confronting it globally. For this reason, a powerful global wave of the left has not emerged to counter the rising right. Nevertheless, there are important experiences demonstrating that such a development is possible.




We must build a bridge between the struggle in Europe and Turkey




We discussed the contribution that the alliance we want to establish in Cologne could make from two perspectives at our meeting.




First, as people living in Europe, we are directly affected by the problems here. The housing crisis is our problem too. Changes to the healthcare system, environmental policies and attacks on social rights are also our problems. Therefore, through this alliance, we will become directly involved in social struggles across Europe.




Second, we need to provide strong support from the diaspora for the struggle in Turkey. However, this support cannot be achieved simply by saying, "We stand with those struggling in Turkey."




We must bring international social forces to a position where they can support the struggle in Turkey. We must embrace the struggle being waged in Turkey from Europe and create pressure on governments here and international institutions. Only in this way can we provide effective support for the ongoing struggle for peace and democracy in Turkey.




Of course, protesting developments in Turkey in the central squares of European cities is important. We cannot underestimate this. However, we must also recognise that this alone is not enough.




The most fundamental role our alliance can play is to build a bridge between internationalist struggles and the ongoing struggle for peace and democracy in Turkey. This is particularly important in bringing political and social forces in Europe together with the struggle in Turkey.




We have organisations with considerable experience and connections in this field. The diplomatic relations of the Confederation of European Alevi Unions, the connections of the Kurdish Freedom Movement and KCDK-E across Europe, and the ties established by socialist movements with socialist forces in other countries represent an important accumulation of experience and relationships.




Let me give you an example. You may have noticed that an organisation called the Anti-Imperialist League (AIL) was among those listed in the statement we published after the meeting. This is an internationalist bloc organised in 37 countries worldwide, including 14 European countries.




Representatives of this organisation also attended our meeting and stated clearly: "We attach importance to the revolutionary and democratic struggle in Turkey. We are aware of its significance for the Middle East. We know about the struggle of the Kurdish Freedom Movement and other democratic forces. We will closely follow this alliance and carry out joint activities, both to receive support from that struggle and to provide support to it."




This is precisely the point I am trying to make. I believe the alliance we have established will serve as an important bridge between international democratic and social forces and the struggle in Turkey.







25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity

25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together differe...

title: Kurdish businessman arrested in Belgium
content:
Businessman Muhsin Talay, who sought refuge in Belgium, has been arrested in Brussels on the basis of an Interpol notice issued at Turkey’s request. Talay, who was acquitted in a murder trial before a court in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), is now in custody. His asylum proceedings in Belgium are still pending. His family warns of possible extradition to Turkey and calls on the Belgian authorities to grant him protection.




Murder accusation despite court acquittal




The arrest is linked to the murder of Murat Baycan, who was killed under unclear circumstances in Amed in 2005. Baycan is alleged to have worked as an informant and agent for the Turkish intelligence service (MIT). Muhsin Talay was accused of involvement in the killing but was acquitted in the subsequent proceedings before the 4th High Criminal Court in Amed.




According to his family, Talay continues to be linked to the murder despite his acquittal. The allegations are reportedly based on a report by the Turkish intelligence service (MIT), even though the evidence presented during the trial was discredited. The family accuses the Turkish authorities of seeking to prosecute and sentence Talay again on this basis.




Talay was reportedly subjected to repeated pressure from MIT during the court proceedings. Fearing mistreatment and renewed prosecution, he eventually left Turkey and applied for asylum in Belgium. While his application was still under review, he was arrested in Brussels on the basis of an Interpol notice.




Family calls for protection against extradition




According to the family, other relatives are also unable to return to Turkey. Two of Talay’s uncles are likewise living in Europe as asylum seekers or refugees and consider themselves unable to return. The family appeals to the Belgian authorities not to extradite Muhsin Talay to Turkey and to grant his asylum application. They fear that he could face mistreatment and renewed penalty if returned.




They are also calling on the Kurdish public, democratic organizations, and human rights groups to support Talay and mobilize public pressure against his possible extradition.

title: YJK-E and KON-MED launch campaign against femicide and patriarchal violence
content:
The Kurdish Women’s Association in Germany (YJK-E) and the Confederation of Kurdistan Communities in Germany (KON-MED) are launching a nationwide campaign against femicide, patriarchal violence, and the structural oppression of women on November 1. Under the slogan “We are intensifying our social struggle against femicide and patriarchal mindsets,” seminars, educational programs, and public events are planned through International Women’s Day on March 8. The campaign will focus on developing democratic family structures, promoting gender equality, and protecting women’s lives.




In their joint statement, the two umbrella organizations criticize the fact that women are subjected to violence in all areas of life, even in a country like Germany, which professes a commitment to fundamental democratic values and human rights. According to the organizations, a total of 105 women have been killed since the beginning of 2026, with Kurdish women accounting for approximately ten percent of the victims. “These women are not just numbers. Each of them had a life, dreams, a family, children, and a future that was taken away from her,” the statement reads.




Patriarchal violence does not begin with femicide




YJK-E and KON-MED do not regard femicides as isolated acts of violence, but as the most extreme consequence of patriarchal power structures deeply embedded in society: “Women are particularly likely to experience violence within their own families or intimate relationships. The belief that men have the right to control women’s clothing, social contacts, employment, or way of life forms a fundamental basis of this oppression.”




“As long as a mindset that teaches boys superiority and girls obedience remains unchanged, the roots of violence will not be eliminated,” the organizations say. The campaign therefore explicitly addresses the social conditions in which gender-based inequality emerges and is passed down through generations. Economic dependence, traditional gender roles, and the expectation that women should tolerate violence for the sake of family unity are among the structures that must be overcome.




As an alternative, the organizations advocate the concept of a democratic family, in which equality, mutual respect, and shared decision-making form the foundation of family life. Children should be able to grow up as free individuals, regardless of their gender. “No tradition, no concept of family, and no social value takes precedence over a woman’s right to life,” YJK-E and KON-MED emphasize.




Calls for investigations into deaths in refugee accommodation facilities




Another key focus of the statement is the situation of refugee women and young people in Germany. Many people who have fled war, persecution, and violence face isolation, discrimination, psychological distress, and inadequate protection in accommodation facilities. The organizations are particularly critical of deaths in refugee accommodation facilities that have officially been recorded as suicides. They call for transparent investigations into the circumstances of these deaths, as well as independent inquiries where there is evidence of neglect, violence, or other criminal offenses.




“No one should be made invisible because they are a refugee, and no death should ever become normalized,” the statement reads. The organizations stress the need for dignified accommodation conditions, safe spaces, psychosocial support, and reliable access to legal advice. Women and young people, in particular, must be protected from violence and social isolation.




Women’s freedom as a shared struggle across borders




The organizations also place their initiative within the broader context of the Kurdish women’s freedom struggle. They recall the genocide perpetrated by the Islamic State (ISIS) against the Yazidi population of Shengal and the systematic abduction and enslavement of Yazidi women. They also explicitly address the threats to the achievements of the women’s revolution in Rojava, as well as state repression and death sentences imposed on women in Iran and Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan).




“Although the forms and circumstances of violence differ, protecting women’s lives, autonomy, and freedom is a shared responsibility,” the organizations declare. In Germany, YJK-E and KON-MED call in particular for the expansion of women’s shelters and counseling centers, effective measures to prevent femicide, and consistent support for women who have experienced violence or are at risk of it. They stress that the protection of women must not become a political issue only after a murder has occurred.




Nationwide educational activities through March 8




Through their campaign, the two umbrella organizations aim to bring the issue of patriarchal power structures more prominently into public debate. Nationwide seminars and educational programs are planned, focusing particularly on what constitutes a democratic family, how such family structures can be developed, and their significance for women’s freedom. November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, will serve as a major focal point for mobilization. On this occasion, efforts will be made to raise awareness of the various forms of gender-based violence and the living conditions of women affected by it.




The initiative is explicitly aimed not only at women but at society as a whole. “Violence against women is not just a women’s issue, but a problem that concerns society as a whole. Therefore, the struggle against it must also be a collective social struggle,” YJK-E and KON-MED say.




The campaign is set to continue until March 8. Its goal is to create a society in which women can live without fear at home, in the workplace, on the streets, and in refugee accommodation facilities, and where their right to self-determination is fully recognized. “We defend life against femicide! We defend women’s freedom against patriarchal mindsets! Jin, Jiyan, Azadî!” the joint statement concludes.

title: Yol tartışmasında öğrenci servisine saldırdı
content:
Tokat'ta yol verme tartışmasında otomobil sürücüsü, lise öğrencilerinin içinde bulunduğu öğrenci servis minibüsüne saldırdı. O anlar, öğrenciler tarafından cep telefonu kamerasıyla kaydedildi.

Olay, kent merkezinde Köprübaşı mevkisinde meydana geldi. Lise öğrencilerini taşıyan servis minibüsünün şoförü ile bir otomobilin sürücüsü arasında yol verme meselesi yüzünden tartışma çıktı. Tartışmanın büyümesi üzerine aracından inen otomobil sürücüsü, içinde lise öğrencilerinin bulunduğu servis minibüsüne saldırdı. Minibüs sürücüsü geri manevra yapıp yol verirken, otomobil sürücüsü ise bölgeden uzaklaştı.

Öğrenciler, o anları cep telefonuyla görüntüledi.

title: İZDEDA İzmir Depremi’nde yaşamını yitirenleri andı: Önlemler alınırsa yeni felaketin önüne geçilir
content:
İzmir – İzmir Depremzedeleri Dayanışma Derneği (İZDEDA), 30 Ekim İzmir Depremi’nin 6. yıl dönümünde anma düzenledi. Bayraklı Deprem Anıtı önünde yapılan anmada basın metnini İZDEDA Başkanı Haydar Özkan okudu.

Altı yıl önce bugün, birkaç saniye içinde hayatların değiştiğini söyleyen Özkan, “Evler yıkıldı, aileler parçalandı, anneler evlatsız, evlatlar annesiz ve babasız kaldı. Kimi sevdiklerine ulaşabilmek için enkaz başında saatlerce bekledi, kimi bir daha hiç kavuşamayacağı yakınlarının haberini bekledi. O gün yalnızca binalar yıkılmadı. Hayaller, hatıralar, ailelerin gelecek planları da enkaz altında kaldı” dedi.

Depremde evlerini kaybeden bazı vatandaşların yeniden yapılacak evlerine kavuşmayı beklerken hayatlarını kaybettiğini belirten Özkan, “Bir gün yuvalarına döneceklerini, yeniden mahallelerinde yaşayacaklarını umut ettiler. Fakat o günleri göremediler. Bugün onların da adını, hatırasını ve yarım kalan umutlarını unutmamalıyız.

Altı yıldır mahallesine, evine, okuluna kavuşmayı bekleyen ailelerimiz var. Çocuklar büyüdü, hayatlar değişti. İnsanlar yalnızca evlerini değil; komşularını, sokaklarını, alıştıkları yaşamı kaybetti” ifadelerini kullandı.

Bu bekleyişin ekonomik yükünün de her geçen gün ağırlaştığını vurgulayan Özkan, “Yükselen kiralar, yetersiz kalan kira yardımları ve geçim sıkıntısı depremzedelerimizi eziyor. İnsanlar bir yandan evlerine kavuşmayı beklerken diğer yandan hayatlarını sürdürebilmek için mücadele ediyor. Biz bugün yalnızca acılarımızı anlatmak için değil, bu acıların bir daha yaşanmaması ve geride kalanların daha fazla mağdur edilmemesi için de konuşuyoruz” ifadelerini kullandı.

Depremin engellenemeyeceğini ancak bilimsel planlama, güvenli yapılaşma, etkin denetim ve hazırlıkla yıkımın felakete dönüşmesinin önlenebileceğini belirten Özkan, “Marmara’dan Van’a, Elazığ’dan İzmir’e ve 6 Şubat Kahramanmaraş depremlerine kadar yaşadığımız her felaket bize bunu gösterdi. İzmir’de hâlâ başlamayan inşaatlar, sözleşmelere rağmen ek ücret talepleri, yarım kalan projeler ve iskân sorunları var. Vatandaşlarımız haklarını ararken uzun sürecek hukuki mücadelelerin endişesini taşıyor” dedi.

Bütün yetkililere çağrıda bulunan Özkan şunları söyledi: “Kaybettiğimiz canları anmak kadar, geride kalanların sorunlarını çözmek de sorumluluğumuzdur. Depremzedeleri yalnızca yıl dönümlerinde hatırlamayın. Bekleyen konutları tamamlayın, ekonomik yüklerini hafifletin ve haklarını koruyacak mekanizmaları hayata geçirin.”

İZDEDA olarak 30 Ekim 2020’den bu yana bu mücadelenin içinde olduklarını söyleyen Özkan, “Bizim için bu mücadele bir siyasi mesele değil, insan hayatı ve hak mücadelesidir. Bugün burada kaybettiğimiz 117 canımızın hatırası önünde saygıyla eğiliyoruz. Bir daha aynı acıları yaşamamak, kaybettiklerimizi unutmamak ve geride kalanları yalnız bırakmamak zorundayız. Unutursak kaybederiz; hazırlanırsak güçleniriz” dedi.

Özkan son olarak taleplerini sıraladı;

Depremzedelerin hukuki ve teknik destek alabileceği, ilgili kurumlara ulaşabileceği ve başvurularının sonuçlarını takip edebileceği bir Depremzede Hak Takip Masası kurulmalı.

Dünya Bankası kredisinde iki yıllık ödemesiz dönem sağlanmalı.

Müteahhitlerin bu kredi modelinden uzaklaşmasını önlemek ve inşaatların aksamamasını sağlamak için hak ediş ödemeleri hızlandırılmalı.

Günümüzün inşaat maliyetleri dikkate alınarak kredi miktarı artırılmalı.

Belediyelerde ruhsat işlemleri hızlandırılmalı, deprem nedeniyle yeniden yapılacak konutlar sıradan projeler gibi değerlendirilmemeli, güvenlikten taviz vermeden öncelikli bir işleyiş oluşturulmalı.

title: UNHCR: Yemen’de çatışmalar 280 binden fazla kişiyi yerinden etti
content:
Birleşmiş Milletler Mülteciler Yüksek Komiserliği (UNHCR) Sözcüsü Matthew Saltmarsh, Yemen’de devam eden çatışmaların 280 binden fazla kişiyi yerinden ettiğini açıkladı.




Anadolu Ajansı

’nın haberine göre, Saltmarsh, BM Cenevre Ofisi’nin haftalık basın toplantısında Yemen’deki insani duruma ilişkin bilgi verdi.



















"Suudi Arabistan ve Suriye, Yemen'e savaşçı sevkini görüşüyor"




22 Ekim 2026










Saltmarsh’a göre, çatışmalar nedeniyle yerinden edilen çok sayıda kişi, güvenlik koşulları nedeniyle hayat kurtarıcı insani yardımlara erişemiyor.




Saltmarsh, Yemen’de on binlerce mülteci ve sığınmacının hayatta kalma mücadelesi verdiğine değinerek, “Artan güvensizlik, ekonomik çöküş, tükenen kaynaklar ve insani yardıma erişim konusundaki ciddi kısıtlamaların, on binlerce insanı gidecek hiçbir yeri olmayan bir duruma sürüklediğini” söyledi.




Yerinden edilenler yardım noktalarına ulaşamıyor




Yardımların ciddi şekilde kısıtlandığına değinen Saltmarsh, erişim imkanı bulduklarında yardımları ulaştırdıklarını ancak bunun oldukça güç bir süreç olduğunu kaydetti.




Saltmarsh, “Yerinden edilmiş pek çok insanın, bizim yardım malzemelerimizin bulunduğu noktalara ulaşamadığına dair haberler alıyoruz. Çoğu durumda ise bizim onlara ulaşmamız aşırı tehlikeli hale geliyor” dedi.




Yemen’deki insani ihtiyaçları karşılamak için mevcut kaynakların yetersiz kaldığına değinen Saltmarsh, Yemen için yaptıkları yardım çağrısının yalnızca yüzde 19 oranında finanse edilebilmiş durumda olduğunu vurguladı.







Yemen’de neler oluyor?




2014’te başlayan iç savaş, Suudi Arabistan öncülüğündeki koalisyonun 2015’te askeri müdahalede bulunmasıyla bölgesel bir çatışmaya dönüştü.




İran’ın desteklediği Ensarullah Hareketi (Husiler), başkent Sana dahil ülkenin kuzeybatısındaki geniş bölgeleri kontrol ediyor. Suudi Arabistan’ın desteklediği Başkanlık Konseyi yönetimi ise ülkenin güneyinde ve doğusunda etkili.




Birleşmiş Milletler’in (BM) arabuluculuğuyla Nisan 2022’de başlayan ateşkes, geniş çaplı çatışmaları önemli ölçüde azalttı. Ancak ABD ve İsrail’in 28 Şubat’ta İran’a saldırmasıyla başlayan bölgesel savaş, Yemen’deki gerilimi yeniden artırdı. Ensarullah güçleri mart sonunda İsrail’e saldırılar düzenledi. Hürmüz Boğazı’nda deniz taşımacılığının aksaması da Kızıldeniz ve Babülmendep Boğazı’nın stratejik önemini artırdı.




Suudi Arabistan, 2026’da Yemen’e yönelik hava saldırılarını yeniden başlattı. Riyad yönetimi ocak ayında BAE Güney Geçiş Konseyi’ne bağlı güçleri, sonraki aylarda ise Ensarullah’ın kontrolündeki bölgeleri hedef aldı.




Eylül ve ekim aylarında çatışmalar yoğunlaştı. Ensarullah güçleri Kızıldeniz kıyısında ilerlerken, Suudi Arabistan’ın hava desteği sağladığı Aden yönetimine bağlı birlikler karşı saldırılar düzenledi. Ensarullah da Suudi Arabistan’daki askeri tesislere, enerji altyapısına ve havalimanlarına füze ve İHA saldırıları gerçekleştirdi.




BM Yemen Özel Temsilcisi Hans Grundberg, 9 Ekim’de BM Güvenlik Konseyi’ne sunduğu değerlendirmede Yemen’in yeniden geniş çaplı savaşa sürüklendiği uyarısında bulundu.




BM verilerine göre Yemen’de 22,3 milyon kişi insani yardıma ihtiyaç duyuyor. Yaklaşık 18,3 milyon kişi akut gıda güvensizliği yaşıyor, 5,2 milyon kişi ise ülke içinde yerinden edilmiş durumda. Beş yaşından küçük 2,2 milyon çocuk da akut yetersiz beslenmeyle karşı karşıya.







*Avrupa Komisyonu’nun 23 Ekim 2026 tarihli haritası, Yemen’de çatışmalar nedeniyle yerinden edilen kişilerin bölgelere göre dağılımını ve Avrupa Birliği’nin insani yardım faaliyetlerini gösteriyor. Haritaya göre yerinden edilme özellikle ülkenin güney ve batı bölgelerinde yoğunlaşıyor. (Görsel: Avrupa Komisyonu / ERCC-DG ECHO)

author: Rachel Santarsiero
title: President Trump Unveils EPA’s New Contradictory Methane Proposal at Campaign Rally
content:
At a Tuesday campaign rally for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Lubbock, Texas, President Trump announced the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposal to roll back a Biden-era methane rule, setting up a likely future showdown in how the agency oversees climate pollution under the Clean Air Act.




The proposal marks a break from the agency’s previous approaches to greenhouse gas regulation by maintaining that — for now — the EPA still has the authority to regulate climate pollution from the oil and gas industry, though it might revisit this decision later. With affordability top of mind for many midterm voters, however, the President framed the move in economic terms.   




“Tonight I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations,” Trump announced to the crowd, located near the oil-rich Permian Basin. The new plan would loosen federal requirements for oil and gas operators to detect and repair leaks, ease restrictions on gas flaring, and eliminate the Super Emitter Program, a third-party monitoring and reporting system designed to identify major releases of methane, known as a 

climate super pollutant

.




Trump said the proposal, which addressed a 2024 rule known as OOOOb/c, would “save consumers and energy producers $45 billion in costs, unlock vast quantities of Texas natural gas, and produce 210 million barrels of oil.” Under President Biden, the 

EPA estimated the rule

 would prevent the release of 58 million tons of methane and 16 million tons of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), leading to major public health and climate benefits. 

Climate change already is raising costs

 for American households by an estimated $400 to $900 annually, according to a 2025 Brookings report.  




Trump’s Lubbock announcement follows a series of sweeping deregulatory moves by the EPA in which the agency has stated it does not have the authority to regulate the greenhouse gas emissions that cause climate change under the Clean Air Act. EPA’s most notable decision came in February when the agency 

rescind

ed

 

the

 

2009 endangerment finding

, the U.S. government’s scientific finding that greenhouse gases harm human health and the environment and the legal basis for its rules addressing climate change. More recently, the EPA stated in September that it would no longer limit 

climate

 

pollution

 

for power plants

, a move which would likely extend the lifespan of coal-fired power plants. 




In the wake of these decisions, however, legal experts and environmental advocates say that the EPA is attempting to assert power unevenly. On the one hand, the agency says it lacks the legal authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions from cars, trucks, power plants, and industrial sources under the Clean Air Act. On the other, the latest EPA proposal relies on, in some cases in the same section of, the Clean Air Act to regulate methane, a greenhouse gas, from the oil and gas industry.




In its latest proposed rule

, the EPA addresses this tension, acknowledging that “stakeholders have also raised concerns” about the agency’s authority to regulate the oil and gas sector’s greenhouse gas emissions under the landmark air pollution law. Depending on the agency’s final handling of the issue with fossil fuel-fired power plants, the EPA states it could then use a “future rulemaking” to resolve the issue in the oil and gas sector. (

The EPA is accepting public comments

 on its proposed repeal of its authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions for fossil fuel-fired power plants until Nov. 2.)

Sign Up










Send me intelligence from:







All

UK/Europe team




























Attacking EPA’s ‘flawed legal basis’




In 1999, the oil and gas industry’s largest trade group, the 

American Petroleum Institute

 (API), organized a meeting over whether it should “coordinate a multi-industry, trade group response” to the threat of what it called 

EPA’s “flawed legal basis” for regulating greenhouse gas pollution

, including carbon dioxide and methane, under the Clean Air Act. In 2024, the 

API

 

filed a legal challenge

 over the OOOOb/c rule, which was eventually 

consolidated into a lawsuit

 with states and other industry trade groups. That suit has been paused while the agency reconsiders the rule.




Parts of the oil and gas industry have flagged this distinction in how the Trump EPA is handling two different greenhouse gases under the same law. Shortly after the EPA repealed the endangerment finding, the Domestic Energy Producers Alliance (DEPA), an oil and gas trade association founded by fracking magnate and Trump donor 

Harold Hamm

, wrote a letter to the EPA, thanking the agency for “restoring the rule of law.” The group called out “methane and other greenhouse gas emission requirements for the oil and gas sector” among its examples of “major regulations based on the Endangerment Finding.”




A flare burns over oilfield infrastructure in West Texas’ Permian Basin in 2020. Credit: Justin Hamel/DeSmog




A few months later, after the agency published an update on its proposed reconsideration of the OOOOb/c methane rule, DEPA wrote in an 

internal newsletter that EPA

 “does not explain its legal reasoning for continuing to regulate methane emissions when it has found that it does not have the authority to regulate carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from vehicles and has proposed it does not have the authority to regulate power plants’ CO2 emissions.”




On Tuesday in Corpus Christi, the 

p

resident called out Hamm

 by name at another midterms rally shortly before the one announcing the methane rule rollback. “Harold Hamm is here, the great oilman,” said Trump, looking around the audience. “Hi, Harold.” 




‘The Very Definition of Arbitary’




Legal experts and environmental advocates say the EPA’s inconsistency leaves unresolved important legal questions about the federal government’s authority to regulate climate pollution, potentially keeping the door open to upend federal methane regulation entirely.




“Treating similar pollutants under the same statute differently, with no stated reason or evidence, is the very definition of arbitrary and capricious decision making,” said Alejandro Camacho, a law professor at the University of California, Los Angeles.




Camacho argues that if the EPA adopts a broad theory limiting its authority over greenhouse gases, it must explain why that theory doesn’t also undermine its authority to regulate methane. “States have already sued over the power plant repeal, as have health and environmental groups, and they can and should attack this inconsistency too,” he added.




A lone pumpjack in Loving County, Texas, in the Permian Basin. Credit: Justin Hamel/DeSmog




The EPA’s proposal nods to the industry’s questioning of its authority and points to the agency’s history of handling the 

oil and gas sector

 

separately

, “but the agency hasn’t explained how it will navigate it,” said Rosalie Winn, senior director and lead counsel on methane and clean air policy for the Environmental Defense Fund.




Mary Sasso, an attorney for the Clean Air Task Force, said the agency’s decision to defer the question could leave the future of methane regulation uncertain. “I think that there’s very real concerns that we could see changes to EPA’s interpretation of its own authority finalized in some type of regulation that would be really damaging for public health and the environment,” she said.




Camacho agrees, and warned that the deferral could foreshadow future agency backtracking. “The deferral is less a reasoned distinction than a placeholder for the next rollback,” he said.




The administration also argues that the proposed changes will reduce regulatory costs, encourage domestic energy production, and help lower prices for consumers. “Since day one, President Trump has been putting real money back into the hands of American people by putting American energy back in the hands of the American workers, businesses, and communities,” said Interior Secretary Doug Burgum in a 

press statement

 about the proposal.




Consumer savings uncertain




Although the EPA estimates that the proposed rollback to the methane rule would save consumers tens of billions of dollars, the relationship between domestic production and consumer prices is more complicated, according to the 

U.S. Energy Information Administration

. In an emailed response to DeSmog, the EPA said its estimate reflected the anticipated cost oil and gas operators would save by not having to comply with regulations, their excess profits, and consumer savings. The proposed rule reflects this calculation in its Regulatory Impact Analysis section, but does not provide further details on how the agency determined these figures. These figures are not independently established consumer savings.




“As much as it would be easy to paint oil executives as cartoonish villains hiking prices while families suffer, individuals have little to no control over benchmark oil prices,” said Kelly Mitchell, the executive director of the oil and gas watchdog Fieldnotes.




“The administration may claim that new rules will incentivize new production, bringing online supply to counter the barrels trapped behind the Strait of Hormuz,” Mitchell said. “However, these new rules are primarily designed to help operators of marginal wells — wells that produce fewer than 15 barrels per day.”




Flaring methane gas in the Permian Basin, Texas. Credit: Justin Hamel/DeSmog




Mitchell questioned whether the benefits of the rollback would reach consumers, arguing that changes would primarily reduce costs for oil and gas operators without guaranteeing lower prices at the pump. “We’re left with an outcome where oil companies get to war profiteer, avoid using any of those profits to clean up a major pollution source, and fail to reduce prices. Now they have the gall to look us in the eyes and tell us this is a gift to the American consumer.”




Since rescinding the endangerment finding, the EPA no longer accounts for the cost of harms from additional climate pollution — only the economic harms — which does not figure into the new rule’s estimated savings. Meanwhile, in a 

study recapping the last decade

 of climate-induced health harms, the 

Lancet

 reported a record high of 710,000 heat-related deaths in 2023 — and almost 72 percent of them caused by climate change.




The proposed rule places particular emphasis on a class of low-producing facilities known as marginal wells, which typically produce relatively small amounts of oil and gas. The Trump administration alleges that regulations established under the previous administration stymied these wells. “Under crooked Joe Biden, ‘Dumocrats’ crushed the small oil and gas operators,” Trump said during the rally Tuesday. “There are small operators, they’re great operators too, I know so many of them — with crippling regulations and methane that caused prices to skyrocket.”




The EPA says many of these wells are family-owned operations that struggle with the costs of complying with Biden-era standards, but an Environmental Defense 

analysis

 found that nearly half of all marginal wells are owned by just 93 corporations.




The proposed methane rule reconsideration is the latest development in a broader campaign to weaken federal methane protections under the purview of Aaron Szabo, a former registered lobbyist for a member of a major trade group pushing for these rollbacks. Earlier this month, 

Szabo stepped down

 as the head of the EPA Office of Air and Radiation. Last month, DeSmog reported that members of the oil and gas industry had simultaneously voiced public support for 

federal methane rules while covertly working to

 

“eviscerate”

them during the second Trump administration, according to an 

investigation

 published by Fieldnotes.




The proposed changes to the OOOOb/c methane rule are not yet final. The EPA says it will provide at least 

45 days for public comment

after publication in the Federal Register, including a public hearing.










The post 

President Trump Unveils EPA’s New Contradictory Methane Proposal at Campaign Rally

 appeared first on 

DeSmog

.

author: anred
title: BDS reclama a Lula que rompa los vínculos económicos y militares con Israel: «es hora de pasar de las palabras a los hechos”
content:
Imagen: @cois4ruim




La reelección de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en Brasil generó expectativas en el movimiento internacional de solidaridad con Palestina, pero también reabrió el debate sobre la continuidad de los vínculos económicos, comerciales y militares entre Brasil e Israel. Andressa Oliveira Soares, co-coordinadora de políticas para América Latina del Comité Nacional Palestino del movimiento de Boicot, Desinversión y Sanciones (BDS), calificó el resultado electoral como “una pequeña gota de esperanza”, aunque reclamó que el próximo mandato traduzca las declaraciones diplomáticas en medidas concretas contra Israel. “Brasil ha frustrado los planes imperialistas de Estados Unidos en la región. Ahora, Brasil debe poner su peso geopolítico y económico al servicio de la defensa del derecho internacional”, sostuvo. Entre las principales exigencias, planteó interrumpir las exportaciones de petróleo a Israel, terminar los contratos militares, cancelar el tratado de libre comercio entre el Mercosur e Israel y suspender las importaciones de agrotóxicos, además de cortar los vínculos académicos, deportivos y culturales, por el genocidio que lleva adelante el gobierno de Benjamin Netanyahu contra el pueblo palestino en Gaza. 

Por ANRed.







La 

reelección de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva para su cuarto mandato en Brasil

 abrió nuevas expectativas y también exigencias en el movimiento internacional de solidaridad con Palestina. En un pronunciamiento difundido el lunes 26 de octubre, el 

Comité Nacional Palestino del movimiento de Boicot, Desinversión y Sanciones (BDS)

planteó que el nuevo mandato presidencial 

debe traducir las posiciones diplomáticas de Brasil contra el genocidio en Gaza en medidas concretas contra Israel

.




“La reelección de Lula en Brasil representa para Palestina una pequeña gota de esperanza para quienes creen en la justicia social y los derechos humanos en Latinoamérica y más allá. 

El pueblo brasileño ha rechazado contundentemente a la ultraderecha, que en toda América Latina ha avanzado para fortalecer su alianza con el genocida Israel

. Brasil ha frustrado los planes imperialistas de Estados Unidos en la región. Ahora, 

Brasil debe poner su peso geopolítico y económico al servicio de la defensa del derecho internacional

. Esta victoria debe traducirse en acciones decisivas en apoyo del derecho internacional para los pueblos oprimidos, desde Palestina hasta Brasil”, remarca el documento, que lleva la firma de 

Andressa Oliveira Soares

, co-coordinadora de políticas para América Latina del movimiento.




El pronunciamiento reconoce las posiciones que Lula y sus anteriores gobiernos sostuvieron respecto de Palestina, pero advierte sobre la distancia entre esas declaraciones y las políticas económicas y comerciales: “

los gobiernos previos de Lula han sido favorables al reconocimiento de algunos derechos del pueblo palestino y se han manifestado contra el genocidio

. Sin embargo,

 aún no han dado pasos concretos para imponer sanciones legales efectivas a Israel, tal como lo estableció la Corte Internacional de Justicia

”, en referencia a las medidas provisionales dictadas en el proceso iniciado por Sudáfrica contra Israel por violaciones de la Convención para la Prevención y la Sanción del Delito de Genocidio.




En su momento, 

Lula calificó de genocidio las acciones israelíes contra la población palestina y en septiembre de 2025 anunció que Brasil intervendría en el proceso iniciado por Sudáfrica ante la Corte Internacional de Justicia

. El 17 de septiembre de ese año, el país presentó formalmente una declaración de intervención en virtud del artículo 63 del Estatuto de la Corte, en tanto Estado firmante de la Convención contra el Genocidio. Sin embargo, 

estas decisiones no implicaron una ruptura de las relaciones diplomáticas ni la suspensión integral de los vínculos comerciales con Israel

.




Uno de los principales puntos señalados por BDS es la continuidad del intercambio económico

. El tratado de libre comercio entre el Mercosur e Israel, firmado en 2007 y vigente para Brasil desde abril de 2010, continúa en funcionamiento. Según datos del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores brasileño, el intercambio comercial bilateral alcanzó los 1.900 millones de dólares durante 2025: Brasil exportó bienes por 568,6 millones e importó aproximadamente 1.300 millones.

 Entre las principales exportaciones brasileñas se encuentran carne bovina, soja y café, mientras que las importaciones incluyen fertilizantes y productos químicos

.




La relación también tiene una dimensión energética y militar: de acuerdo con los registros de comercio internacional recopilados por el Banco Mundial, 

Brasil exportó a Israel petróleo crudo por un valor de 215,89 millones de dólares durante 2024

. En materia de armamento, la organización británica 

Campaign Against Arms Trade (CAAT)

 documentó 

vínculos entre empresas israelíes y la industria militar brasileña

, incluidos acuerdos de cooperación y contratos con compañías como Elbit Systems e Israel Aerospace Industries. La adquisición de obuses ATMOS 2000 a Elbit, por ejemplo, quedó suspendida tras el inicio de la ofensiva israelí en Gaza, pero no fue formalmente cancelada según el relevamiento publicado por CAAT en octubre de 2025.




Frente a este escenario, el Comité Nacional Palestino del BDS plantea una agenda de medidas que excede el plano diplomático y apunta a interrumpir las relaciones económicas, militares e institucionales que considera funcionales al sistema de opresión israelí: “debemos trabajar para garantizar que Brasil, ahora en el cuarto mandato de un gobierno que ha expresado su apoyo a los derechos palestinos, finalmente pase de las palabras a los hechos. Esto significa 

cortar los vínculos energéticos y económicos con el sistema de opresión israelí: garantizar que no se exporte petróleo, poner fin definitivamente a todos los contratos militares que Brasil mantiene actualmente con el genocida Israel, cancelar el tratado de libre comercio con Israel y detener todas las importaciones de agrotóxicos, así como cortar los vínculos académicos, deportivos y culturales

”.




El movimiento BDS es una campaña internacional impulsada por organizaciones de la sociedad civil palestina desde 2005, que promueve acciones no violentas de boicot, desinversión y sanciones para presionar a Israel por el cumplimiento del derecho internacional y los derechos del pueblo palestino. Su convocatoria fundacional fue respaldada por más de 170 organizaciones palestinas, entre sindicatos, asociaciones profesionales, organizaciones de mujeres, redes de refugiados y movimientos sociales.

title: Nach Venezuela nimmt Trump Kuba ins Visier: Der Stopp aller Öllieferungen soll die Insel in die Knie zwingen
content:
Dossier




„

Nach Venezuela nimmt Trump Kuba ins Visier. Der Stopp aller Öllieferungen soll die Insel in die Knie zwingen. Kann Havanna dem standhalten? Eine Woche nach den völkerrechtswidrigen Angriffen auf Venezuela und der Entführung von Präsident Nicolás Maduro hat US-Präsident Donald Trump nun dessen wichtigsten Verbündeten Kuba ins Visier genommen. In einem Post auf seiner Social-Media-Plattform „Truth Social“ forderte Trump am Sonntag die Regierung in Havanna, auf „einen Deal zu machen, bevor es zu spät ist“. Was dieser „Deal“ beinhalten sollte oder was passiert, wenn Kuba sich weigert, ließ er offen. Dafür hielt er die Idee für gut, US-Außenminister Marco Rubio zum Präsidenten Kubas zu machen… 

“ Eine 

Analyse von Marcel Kunzmann vom 12. Januar 2026 in Telepolis

 

 („Trumps nächstes Ziel: Kommt nach Venezuela jetzt Kuba?“) und mehr dazu:







UN-Generalversammlung fordert das Ende der US-Blockade gegen Kuba – Deutschland enthielt sich erstmals und beugte sich damit der Drohung aus Washington 







UN-Generalversammlung fordert Ende der US-Blockade gegen Kuba: Botschafter verwiesen auf UN-Charta. Deutschland enthielt sich erstmals und folgte damit dem Druck aus Washington




„In der Generalversammlung der Vereinten Nationen ist über die Resolution mit dem Titel „Notwendigkeit der Aufhebung der von den USA gegen Kuba verhängten Wirtschafts-, Handels- und Finanzblockade“ abgestimmt worden. Für die Resolution und damit ein sofortiges Ende der US-Blockadepolitik gegen Kuba votierten 130 Staaten, dagegen 17. 25 Staaten enthielten sich der Stimme, 20 nahmen an der Abstimmung nicht teil. Vorausgegangen waren in der Generaldebatte die Statements von 35 Staaten, in denen zu der Resolution Stellung bezogen wurde. (…) Mit Nachdruck wurde auf das Leid und die Entbehrungen hingewiesen, denen die Bevölkerung Kubas derzeit ausgesetzt sei, die von der US-Blockade verursacht bzw. verschärft würden. Mehrere Staaten verlangten, dass eine bloß verbale und symbolische Unterstützung Kubas nicht ausreiche, sondern dass praktische Hilfe notwendig sei. Dass das jetzige Votum zur Abschaffung der US-Blockadepolitik nicht so eindeutig ausfiel wie bisher, dürfte unter anderem auf diverse Hetzkampagnen der USA zurückzuführen sein. (…) Zudem wurde deutlich, welche Staaten von den USA abhängig und unter ihrem besonders starken Einfluss stehen. Das hatte zum Hintergrund, dass die US-Regierung in den letzten Monaten noch vehementer als je zuvor intensiven Druck auf andere Regierungen ausübte. Dokumente belegen, dass sie deutlich forderte, diesmal nicht wieder für die Resolution zu stimmen. Diese Politik des Drucks und der Einschüchterung, in den USA seit der Hochphase der Mafia bekannt, die während der Besatzung Kubas auch dort einflussreich war, scheint für manche Regierungen Wirkungen zu zeigen. Auch die Bundesregierung hat sich diesem Druck gebeugt und sich erstmals seit 34 Jahren bei solchen UN-Abstimmungen der Stimme enthalten. (…) In zahlreichen Statements wurde ein Dialog zwischen Kuba und den USA gefordert. Wer die US-Politik beobachtet, dürfte in dem Eindruck bestärkt werden, dass die bisherige Politik gegen Kuba sowie der Auftritt der US-Vertretung in der UN-Generalversammlung keinen Beitrag zum Dialog darstellen, sondern eine tiefgehende, unerbittliche feindselige Haltung offenbaren. Das UN-Votum zeigt letztlich eine starke Polarisierung zwischen dem Globalen Nordwesten und dem Süden sowie den Regierungen und deren Gesellschaften. In den USA sind jüngsten Umfragen gemäß 72 Prozent der Wahlbevölkerung gegen die US-Blockadepolitik.“

 

Beitrag von Edgar Göll vom 29. Oktober 2026 in amerika21

 




USA drohen Kuba-Unterstützern




„

Vor der Abstimmung in der UN-Generalversammlung über die Blockade Kubas durch die USA setzt Washington Länder unter Druck. Kuba wehrt sich.




Die USA kennen mit Kuba kein Erbarmen. Seit der Intervention in Venezuela zu Jahresbeginn werden die Sanktionen gegen die Karibikinsel weiter verschärft und die Regierung in Havanna mit Einschüchterungsversuchen eingedeckt. Vor der alljährlichen UN-Abstimmung am 27. oder 28. Oktober über die Aufhebung der jahrzehntelangen US-Blockadepolitik gegen Kuba hat der kubanische Außenminister Bruno Rodríguez eine beispiellose Druckkampagne der Vereinigten Staaten angeprangert und das Vorgehen der US-Justiz gegen Raúl Castro scharf verurteilt. (…)


Rodríguez präsentierte ein Schreiben des US-Außenministeriums, das US-Botschaften anweist, Druck auf Regierungen auszuüben, damit diese gegen die Resolution stimmen, sich der Stimme enthalten oder während der Abstimmung den Saal verlassen. Die Drohungen umfassen demnach die Androhung von Strafzöllen, die Einstellung von Kooperationsprogrammen, Visabeschränkungen für Amtsträger und deren Angehörige, die Unterstützung von Oppositionskräften sowie Sekundärsanktionen gegen Einrichtungen, die Beziehungen zu Kuba unterhalten. »Es handelt sich um ein Bündel von Methoden, die echter politischer Gewalt, Nötigung und Erpressung gleichkommen«, erklärte er. Ein nicht genanntes lateinamerikanisches Land habe »unter dem Druck der US-Regierung« zudem seinerseits versucht, auf andere Staaten einzuwirken, damit diese Havanna nicht unterstützen. (…)


Die Bundesregierung hat bei allen diesen Abstimmungen in der UN gemäß Grundgesetz und UN-Charta für die kubanische Resolution gestimmt und die US-Blockadepolitik gegenüber Kuba stets verurteilt. Bei einer Sonderdebatte am 7. Juli in der UN-Generalversammlung zur Verschärfung der US-Sanktionen allerdings enthielt sich Deutschland in der Abstimmung über den Antrag Kubas. Dieser fand die Unterstützung von 136 Staaten, neun stimmten dagegen, bei 30 Enthaltungen.




Wadephul sieht in der US-Blockade keine Blockade




Zuvor hatte der deutsche Außenminister Johann Wadephul (CDU) mit der Aussage irritiert, dass es die US-Blockade gegen Kuba nicht gebe

…“ 

Artikel von Andreas Knobloch vom 27.10.2026 in ND online

 




In der Dunkelheit. Die Zahl der Einbrüche und Diebstähle nimmt in Kuba zu. Das ist eine neue Realität der Krise




„

Am vergangenen Wochenende wurde in Deutschland die Zeit umgestellt; in Kuba wäre es in der kommenden Woche so weit. Wäre. Denn Kuba verzichtet in diesem Jahr auf die Umstellung auf die Normalzeit und behält die Sommerzeit bei. Die Regierung begründet den Schritt mit der Verschärfung der Energieblockade durch die Vereinigten Staaten. Da die Uhr um eine Stunde vorgestellt bleibt, geht die Sonne nach offizieller Zeit später unter. Durch weniger künstliche Beleuchtung und mehr Solarstrom erhofft sich die Regierung Stromeinsparungen in den Abendstunden, wenn die Nachfrage am höchsten ist..

.“ 

Artikel von Andreas Knobloch vom 27.10.2026 in ND online

 










Kuba: Überleben im Würgegriff Washingtons




„

Die US-Energieblockade sollte Havanna binnen Monaten zu Fall bringen. Das Land hält durch, mit Improvisation und Solarpanelen. Doch die Schlinge zieht sich zu.




In Holguín, im Viertel Alcides Pino, stehen heute Elektro-Dreiräder, wo einst Benzin verkauft wurde. Auf dem Gelände einer ehemaligen Tankstelle betreibt ein Privatunternehmen seit Juni die Solinera „El Girasol“: 30 Solarpanele, 40 Kilowatt Leistung, vollständig unabhängig vom Netz. Zwei Stunden täglich können Anwohner dort kostenlos Handys, Lampen und Ventilatoren laden. (…) Seit Anfang Januar gilt eine faktische Ölblockade der USA gegen Kuba. Venezolanische Öllieferungen bleiben aus, während auf dem Weltmarkt bestellte Tanker von der US-Küstenwache abgefangen werden. (…) Dennoch trat der von Washington erhoffte Zusammenbruch nicht ein. (…)Präsident Miguel Díaz-Canel führt das auf Kubas „kreativen Widerstand“ zurück: Chinesische Elektro-Motorräder und E-Rikschas ersetzen spritfressende Oldtimer und den eingestellten Busverkehr. Bars laufen mit umgerüsteten Erdgasgeneratoren, eines der wenigen verlässlichen Energieträger, da Kuba das Gas selbst fördert. Ein Betreiber zahlte so am Monatsende nur 50 Pesos, rund sechs Cent, für Energie. Der Staat forscht parallel mit Hochdruck an Möglichkeiten, das schwefelhaltige heimische Rohöl zu Treibstoffen zu raffinieren. (…) Zugleich verwandelt Washington die Blockade in ein Kontrollinstrument. Laut dem US-Cuba Trade and Economic Council beliefen sich die US-Treibstoffexporte nach Kuba im August auf 74,8 Millionen Dollar, seit Januar auf 231,7 Millionen. Den größten Posten bildete bleifreies Benzin aus Miami mit 23,8 Millionen Dollar. Die Lieferungen genehmigt das US-Finanzministerium im Einzelfall im Rahmen einer Ausnahmeregelung, sie dürfen nur an Privatbetriebe gehen. Profiteure sind laut Handelsrat vor allem Reedereien und Händler in Florida. Alle anderen Quellen werden dagegen gekappt. (…) Das erklärte Ziel ist der Sturz der kubanischen Regierung im Sinne der neu aufgelegten Monroe-Doktrin: Amerika den USA, China und „der Kommunismus“ (dessen Welthauptstadt Kuba sei), müssen raus. Rubio kündigte an, hierfür „alle verfügbaren Mittel“ einzusetzen, militärische Invasionsdrohungen standen dieses Jahr bereits mehrfach im Raum. (…) Havanna antwortet auf die Situation an zwei Fronten. Im Juni kündigte die Regierung ein umfangreiches Reformprogramm an. 176 Maßnahmen räumen Markt und Privatsektor bisher ungekannte Spielräume ein. (…) Parallel wächst die Solarkraft: 1,4 Gigawatt in 144 Parks liefern inzwischen 21,4 Prozent des Strombedarfs, nach drei Prozent Anfang 2025. Neue Anreize ermöglichen den privaten Ausbau und Netzeinspeisungen. Doch nachts, wenn der Bedarf am höchsten ist, fehlen Speicher; erst eines von vier geplanten Batteriespeichersystemen ist am Netz. (…) Ob die Reformen den freien Fall bremsen, ist offen. Die UN-Wirtschaftskommission Cepal erwartet für 2026 ein BIP-Minus von 10,3 Prozent; die Inflation soll auf rund 27 Prozent steigen. (…) Die Bundesregierung hat sich indes entschieden, hierbei möglichst nicht in Washington anzuecken. Als der deutsche Außenminister Johann Wadephul (CDU) diesen Sommer von einem Bürger gefragt wurde, warum die Bundesregierung die US-Blockade gegen Kuba nicht deutlicher als illegal und völkerrechtswidrig kritisiere, antwortete er: „eine derartige Blockade, wie Sie sie beschrieben haben, sehe ich nicht“. Laut Informationen der Berliner Zeitung überlegt Berlin noch, ob man bei der jährlichen UN-Abstimmung zum Thema dieses Jahr wirklich für die Resolution zur Aufhebung der US-Blockade gegen Kuba stimmen soll. Es wäre es das erste Mal seit 2002, dass sich eine deutsche Regierung hierbei so klar an Seiten der USA positionieren würde.“

 

Beitrag von Marcel Kunzmann vom 14. Oktober 2026 bei Telepolis

 




Weltweit wächst die Kuba-Solidarität, in Deutschland auch gewerkschaftliche und in den USA wächst der Widerstand gegen Trumps Kubapolitik 







»Unblock Cuba«: Was heißt Kuba-Solidarität für einen Gewerkschafter?




„Arbeiter und DGB-Mitglieder sind bereit, sich mehr als bisher für das kubanische Volk zu engagieren, sagt Andreas Nolte




[Auf dem Gewerkschaftstag der IG Metall 2023 wurde ein Beschluss verabschiedet, der auch ein Ende der US-Blockade Kubas fordert. Weshalb braucht es die im März dieses Jahres gegründete Gruppe »Gewerkschafter:innen für Kuba«?]




Wir wollen, dass der Gedanke der internationalen Solidarität wieder stärker in unseren Gewerkschaften verankert wird. Die Initiative haben wir also aus der Erkenntnis heraus gegründet, dass die DGB-Gewerkschaften die internationale Solidaritätsarbeit seit Jahren eingestellt haben. Für die IG Metall kann ich sagen, dass das vor etwa 15 Jahren entschieden wurde. Man hat dann Mittel umgruppiert und zum Beispiel regelmäßige Reisen und Jugendreisen der IG Metall nach Kuba leider eingestellt. Das hat viele sehr geärgert.




Ich habe dann im Frühjahr 2023 Kontakt zu den kubanischen Industriegewerkschaften aufgenommen und sie gefragt, ob sie Interesse haben, mit uns zu kooperieren. Da haben sie gesagt: »Natürlich haben wir Interesse!« Das hat mich zusätzlich motiviert, den Antrag und die Diskussion innerhalb der IG Metall voranzubringen. (…) Ich erlebe bei den betrieblichen Kollegen sowie bei den Funktionären der IG Metall inzwischen regelmäßig, dass auch hier Offenheit für das Thema und auch die Bereitschaft, zu spenden, bestehen. Das trifft auch auf andere Gewerkschaften zu: Bei der IG BAU gibt es schon länger einen Beschluss dazu, dass tatkräftig Solidaritätsarbeit geleistet werden soll. Und dafür haben wir im März die Gewerkschaftsinitiative für Kuba gegründet, bundesweit. Da sind die IG Metall, die IG BAU, die EVG, die NGG und Verdi im Unterstützerkreis dabei. Wir sind seit der Gründung auch bundesweit stets gewachsen

…“ 

Interview von Kim Chi Luu in der jungen Welt vom 18.09.2026

 




In den USA wächst der Widerstand gegen Trumps Kubapolitik: Bündnis sieht Blockade gegen Kuba als Kriegshandlung und fordert daher Abstimmung im Kongress. Weltweite Solidarität mit Kuba




„Nach acht Monaten der totalen und völkerrechtswidrigen Energieblockade Kubas durch die USA wächst im eigenen Land der Widerstand. Nun forderte ein Bündnis zivilgesellschaftlicher Organisationen die Führung der Demokratischen Partei im Repräsentantenhaus dazu auf, über eine Resolution zu den Kriegsbefugnissen der Regierung bezüglich Kuba abstimmen zu lassen. Das Bündnis besteht aus 45 religiösen, friedenspolitischen, gewerkschaftlichen, gesundheitsbezogenen und politischen Gruppen. Sie richteten sich direkt an den Fraktionsvorsitzenden der Demokraten im Repräsentantenhaus, Hakeem Jeffries, sowie an die ranghöchsten demokratischen Ausschussmitglieder Gregory Meeks und Jim McGovern. Die Organisationen forderten eine umgehende Abstimmung über die von der ebenfalls demokratischen Abgeordneten Nydia Velázquez eingebrachte Resolution zu den Kriegsbefugnissen bezüglich Kuba (H.Con.Res. 106). In ihrem Schreiben an die Demokraten drängte das Bündnis auf die Beendigung der Ölblockade der USA gegen die Karibikinsel. „Kuba leidet unter einer menschengemachten wirtschaftlichen und humanitären Katastrophe, die maßgeblich durch bewusste politische Entscheidungen der Vereinigten Staaten verursacht wurde“, hieß es darin. Nach Ansicht der Organisationen kommt die Blockade bereits einer Kampfhandlung gleich, die jedoch vom Kongress nicht genehmigt wurde. Die Zustimmung des Kongresses zu Kampfhandlungen ist in der Verfassung der USA vorgeschrieben. (…) Zeitgleich läuft in den USA die Kampagne „Kein Krieg gegen Kuba“, initiiert von Gruppen, die sich für Kuba und eine andere Politik einsetzen. Koordiniert vom US-Netzwerk Cuba rufen die beteiligten Gruppen zu einer besonderen politischen Aktion zur Verteidigung Kubas auf. Vom 15. September bis zum 1. Oktober wollen sie sich verstärkt für Initiativen im Kongress, Briefkampagnen und persönliche Gespräche mit Abgeordneten einsetzen. (…) Auch in anderen Ländern zeigen zivilgesellschaftliche Gruppen Unterstützung für Kuba. Ziel ist es, die vom Weißen Haus geforderten Bedingungen durchzusetzen und Kuba wieder zum Vasallenstaat zu machen. (…)


Die Folgen dieser Krise lasten insbesondere auf den Schultern der Arbeiter*innenklasse, insbesondere auf Menschen afrikanischer Herkunft, Frauen und Kindern, die am stärksten betroffen sind. Von der Situation verschont sind die privilegierten Schichten, die mit der herrschenden Bürokratie und den Streitkräften verbunden sind – darunter auch GAESA, der vom Militär geführte halbstaatliche Mischkonzern, der einigen Schätzungen zufolge 40 Prozent der Wirtschaft kontrolliert. Auch die neue Bourgeoisie, die sich um private Unternehmen herum gebildet hat, kann sich einen höheren Konsum leisten. Havanna trägt, wie ganz Kuba, die Folgen der von der Regierung vorangetriebenen Reformen und der daraus resultierenden zunehmenden Ungleichheit. (…)


Verstärkt wird die wachsende Ungleichheit von den unter den letzten Regierungen vorangetriebenen Reformen, darunter die Gründung von Joint Ventures und die Öffnung für Investitionen kubanisch-amerikanischer Bürger*innen, wie der »Gusano«-Bourgeoisie aus Miami, in strategischen Wirtschaftssektoren. Diese Reformen, die von der herrschenden Bürokratie als einzige gangbare Antwort auf die Krise dargestellt werden, haben kapitalistische Verhältnisse gestärkt und neue Räume für private Akkumulation eröffnet. Gleichzeitig stellen sie Sparmaßnahmen dar, die die Arbeiter*innenklasse hart treffen, während eine zunehmend wohlhabende Minderheit wirtschaftlich profitiert. (…) In diesem Zusammenhang erzählt uns Roberto, Forscher an der Universität: »Es gibt keine offiziellen Umfragen in Kuba, doch die Zustimmung zur Regierung erreicht heute kaum noch 20 Prozent. Außerdem hat (Präsident Miguel) Díaz-Canel weder das Ansehen noch das Charisma von Fidel (Castro).« (…)


Doch Kritik und Widerstand gegen die Regierung Díaz-Canel sind nicht gleichbedeutend mit Unterstützung für eine imperialistische Intervention. Viele lehnen eine Einmischung der USA ab. Zum Beispiel Alma, die mehr als zwölf Stunden am Tag in einem kleinen Unternehmen arbeitet. Nachdem sie über die wachsende Ungleichheit in Kuba und ihre Kritik an der »neuen Bourgeoisie« spricht, sagt sie auch: »Die Lage ist nicht einfach. Wir könnten das Wenige verlieren, was von dem, was wir erreicht haben, noch übrig ist.« Ihr bedeute die kubanische Revolution viel. Ramón, ein Veteran der kubanischen Intervention in Angola und Mitglied der kritischen kubanischen Linken, hält seine Meinung nicht zurück: »Ich bin gegen die Regierung. Aber wenn die Yankees kommen, werde ich wieder zu den Waffen greifen.« Die meisten in der kubanischen Linken teilen diese Haltung gegen eine Intervention. (…)


Infolge der Wirtschaftsreformen der Regierung haben sich in der Vergangenheit auch Proteste formiert, darunter am 11. Juli 2021. Obwohl die Regierung behauptete, dass Rechte dahinter gesteckt hätten, waren diese Proteste tatsächlich das Ergebnis der sozialen Unzufriedenheit über die Wirtschaftspolitik, der wachsenden Ungleichheit und der Repression der Díaz-Canel-Regierung. Diese reagierte darauf mit noch mehr Unterdrückung. Tausende Arbeiter*innen und arme Jugendliche wurden inhaftiert – viele von ihnen erhielten lange Haftstrafen. (…) In den letzten Jahren hat sich das herausgebildet, was heute als die kritische kubanische Linke bekannt ist. Sie vereint politische und soziale Aktivist*innen, Künstler*innen, Journalist*innen und Kulturschaffende. Es handelt sich um einen heterogenen Raum, der von Sozialdemokrat*innen, von denen einige eine gemischte Wirtschaft unter staatlicher Kontrolle befürworten, bis hin zu jenen reicht, die sich in der revolutionären sozialistischen Tradition sehen. Diese Opposition verdient Anerkennung dafür, dass sie Kritik an der Regierung mit einer prinzipiellen Haltung gegen imperialistische Interventionen verbindet, was viele als Verteidigung der nationalen Souveränität betrachten. Wir führten zahlreiche Gespräche mit Mitgliedern dieses politischen und kulturellen Raums, was uns ermöglicht hat, die kubanische Realität und die Widersprüche, mit denen die kritische Linke konfrontiert ist, besser zu verstehen. (…)


In Kuba selbst ist es dringend notwendig, eine sozialistische Perspektive wiederaufzubauen. Eine Perspektive, die mit der Vorstellung aufräumt, die einzigen Alternativen seien entweder eine Rückkehr des Kapitalismus unter Vormundschaft von Trump und den »Gusanos« aus Miami oder aber die Aufrechterhaltung des von der herrschenden Bürokratie geführten politischen Regimes. Ausgehend vom Antiimperialismus, der Teil der Tradition des kubanischen Volkes ist, gilt es, eine sozialistische Perspektive von unten zu entwickeln, die auf demokratischer Selbstorganisation, auf Vereinigungs- und Organisationsfreiheit, auf dem Recht auf Legalität für politische Organisationen basiert, die sich die Verteidigung der Revolution und ihrer Errungenschaften zum Ziel setzen und zugleich für ein Ende der wirtschaftlichen und sozialen Privilegien der Bürokratie und ihrer repressiven Politik eintreten. Die Arbeiter*innenklasse und die sectores populares können die unter den Regierungen von Raúl Castro und Díaz-Canel ergriffenen Maßnahmen – einschließlich der Zugeständnisse an ausländisches Kapital – demokratisch einer gründlichen und radikalen Überprüfung unterziehen. Gleichzeitig gilt es, der aktuellen Krise und den Drohungen imperialistischer Intervention zu begegnen und die Unterstützung und Solidarität der Arbeiter*innen und Völker der Region zu suchen, die die wahren Verbündeten der kubanischen Bevölkerung sind. Das ist der Weg, um die verbleibenden Errungenschaften der Revolution zu verteidigen und für eine antiimperialistische, internationalistische und sozialistische Perspektive zu kämpfen.“

April 1960 beschreibt der Mitarbeiter des US-Außenministeriums Lester D. Mallory dem damaligen US-Präsidenten Dwight D. Eisenhower den strategischen Hintergrund der Blockade. Mallory schildert darin die Notwendigkeit, Kuba Geld und Waren zu enthalten, »Geld- und Reallöhne zu senken, Hunger und Verzweiflung zu schüren«, um so die Castro-Regierung zu stürzen. (…) In einem weiteren, mittlerweile deklassifizierten CIA-Bericht von 1982 wird zugegeben, dass »die Sanktionen für sich selbst oder in Verbindung mit anderen Maßnahmen« keine ihrer Ziele erreicht hätten. Auf einer internationalen Solidaritätskonferenz am 2. Mai in Havanna mit über 700 Delegierten aus 30 Ländern machte der kubanische Präsident die Haltung seiner Regierung klar: »Wir haben keine Angst vor Krieg, auch wenn wir ihn nicht wollen.« Was die USA mit Kuba anstellten, könnten sie danach auch mit jedem anderen Land machen, sagte er. »Auf Kuba wird die Würde der Völker verteidigt.«“
