author: Julius Gavroche
title: October 17th, or the Return of Playfulness
content:
from 

lundimatin

 #539, 26/10/2026







“Opportunistic delinquency,” “holiday-strike,” “lack of political maturity,” “childish cosplay,” “reckless destruction,” “acts of rage” — all these hostile terms used to discredit the ongoing uprising have given rise to their political antonyms: “material reappropriation,” “demands for better study conditions,” “political awareness,” “joyful staging,” and so on. October 17th has been the occasion for a prolific and all-encompassing production of a staggering number of counter-interpretations, theoretical texts, and hypotheses about what drives the movement. Yet, a subterranean dimension to its actions, omnipresent throughout, still seems to be ignored: playfulness [

le ludique

]. Without returning to a thorough examination of the underlying causes of the movement, nor to a prescriptive reading of its aftermath—most often guided by the intention to “manage” the movement—we wanted here to recapture the passion at work behind the riotous gestures and the high school fervour.




“Je te tiens, tu me tiens, par la barbichette, le premier de nous deux qui rira aura une tapette!”

[“I hold you, you hold me, by the goatee, the first one to laugh will get a light slap!”)

[1]




The Game Begins




Our hypothesis, which can coexist with others, posits that the “playful” comes into play as a uniquely effective concept for understanding the fundamentally joyful riotous activity around which the subjectivities of those participating in the insurrection were emotionally bound and organised.







Whether in the charivaris, carnivals, or parades of high school students dressed as comic book superheroes, the fact remains: play coupled with laughter constitutes an undeniable domain of tactics and stratagems allowing one to temporarily break free from the grip of a dominant power. But this playful aspect is neither a simple formal reversal of positions nor a powerless parody of power. It is a refutation in action of learned protest techniques and other demands. The weariness of traditional activist circles is left behind, and already a new horizon of joyful and creative acts is emerging.




The high school students’ strategic skill lies in reusing codes deemed harmless and far too childish to be repressed or even considered: superheroes, costumes, TikTok trends, and so on. Yet, each time, they repurpose these codes in a context of assault and offensives, leading to physical or non-physical confrontations with law enforcement. For example, Captain America launches an attack followed by hundreds of individuals dressed in black. These actions further expose the fundamental illegitimacy of police officers using force. And besides, what can a police officer do against a Batman who starts dancing in front of him? Get enraged, strike, or experience boredom, or endure his docility (the latter two obligations usually being reserved for high school students). How do you stop a battle of auras, the apotheosis of absurdity and humour? By no other means than as a spoilsport. One last thing: what can a police officer do when faced with a left-wing activist, some kind of proselytizer, megaphone in hand, shouting the same old slogans? Ignore them like any other piece of scenery.




Rediscovered Lucidity(ies)




One of the obvious attributes of the complicity present before and during October 17th (Gen Z, students, temporary workers, suburbanites, subordinates, Yellow Vests—in short, subjectivities in the process of proletarianisation) is their propensity for the “playful”. The innocuous act of triggering an aura battle, like smashing a shop window, even if they share no fundamental equivalence, manifests this same playful relationship to the metropolitan imposition of a commercial space. It would be wrong to oppose acts of rage and destruction to the expression of newfound joy, or in other words, acts of looting and arson to role-playing, aura battles, and dressing up as superheroes. They condense and stem from the same affects: in short, a joy in destruction or the anticipation of destroying with joy. Against the contained, regular, and monotonous movements and displacements of the urban and commercial world, always assigned to a goal, they also oppose and demonstrate the here and now possibility of free activity, of a reclaiming of space, without a stated goal or pre-established function. In 

Homo Ludens

, Johan Huizinga defines play as follows:




Summing up the formal characteristics of play we might call it a free activity standing quite consciously outside “ordinary” life as being “not serious”, but at the same time absorbing the player intensely and utterly. )t is an activity connected with no material interest, and no profit can be gained by it. It proceeds within its own proper boundaries of time and space according to fixed rules and in an orderly manner. It promotes the formation of social groupings which tend to surround themselves with secrecy and to stress their difference from the common world by disguise or other means

.

[2]




Material appropriation through the destruction of property or self-reduction, and amusement in its various forms of staging, are found within the realm of play. Ultimately, there is nothing surprising about this return of play if we understand it and situate it within the long decline of the school system, which has relentlessly sought to ward off all possible manifestations of play and the reappropriation of daily life: distractions, amusement, subversion, and even, until recently, the use of the telephone. Playfulness must be distinguished from the petit-bourgeois conception of fighting as festive folklore, with its infamous techno dances, the vanguard of militant harmlessness.




In front of high schools and elsewhere, these acts serve to expose adult seriousness and its posturing of exemplary behavior, the last vestiges of a still-latent complicity with repressive educational institutions (how many outraged and revealing reactions were provoked by the burning of the Nelson Mandela Secondary School in Nantes?). Suspending boredom, escaping the rigid, academic environment, learning skills independent of their commercial and professional applications, refusing to succumb to resignation and inaction in the face of catastrophe—these are the areas in which play offers an option.




But why claim that this playful quality can shed light on last Saturday’s astonishing and powerful offensive? Does not a better analysis require discerning, within the material circumstances, what underlay the movement? Surely.




Often, the desire to explain the causes of an insurrectionary process contains a prescriptive intent. The aim is to better understand it and make its continuation even more efficient. The effort is commendable. But it often amounts to saying what happened in order to better explain what should happen next. As Walter Benjamin pointed out in his time: “The destructive character has no interest in being understood.”

[3]

 The efforts made in this direction seem superficial to it. Being understood is a bourgeois affair. The destroyer, for its part, does not care. It does not want disciples. It prefers to be alone, for it is the only way for it to bear witness to the solitude of what is destroyed. The incomprehension provoked by looting must sometimes be accompanied by a refusal of any time-consuming explanation, any attempt to make oneself respectable. Nevertheless, considering this activity as minimally “playful,” that breaking a shop window, breaking into stores, sometimes stealing merchandise blindly and as quickly as possible, saying that it is an act of play, is often clearer than any imaginable justification. Learning from the effectiveness of October 17th must therefore be done without trying to deduce, fix, or project desirable forms of future insurrection. Otherwise, the risk is that the event will be reincorporated into a militant body of manners, gestures, and knowledge that is profoundly antithetical and impotent.




Against Vigilance




The audacious act of October 17th stemmed in part from a combination of playful exuberance and a rejection of the usual anxieties about “consequences”. Indeed, the high school students’ offensive also lay in its ability to bypass the vigilance reflexes of informed, autonomous activists. The acts were regularly carried out openly, broadcast live, and sometimes the rioters even posed proudly with their “trophies.”




Some comrades noticed this and appreciated it, while others, more numerous, and based on the series of convictions, deplored it. We are not advocating blindly attacking shop windows without considering the extent of the surveillance and resources mobilised afterward; or, more simply and foolishly, encouraging everyone to rush headlong into the fray. But within this playful unleashing of looting, there is a kind of impulsive, reckless impulse that comes first, an unconsciousness that ultimately reflects what this struggle represents: an existential stake, a life force expressed in a “whatever-it-takes-it” and a “regardless-of-the-repercussions” attitude. Far from establishing a politics of rioting or providing a perfect tool for understanding, this “recklessness” allows us to shift our traditional conceptions of commitment, so often linked to the fear of repression. Rather than conceiving of the struggle as a rational calculation of contingencies and risks (“how to risk less and do more?”), the riotous act refuses to be confined to this accounting logic. We must act here and now, rediscover a 

kairos

 compatible with collective desire, before even considering anticipating the worst and, consequently, relegating revolutionary action to a fictitious future detached from our time. Because what the spread of anti-repression practices as a whole carries with it, however welcome they may always be, is a desire for post-insurrection stabilisation, a yearning to present a serene and comprehensible model of revolt. Yet, by its very nature, the continuation of revolt is a leap into the utter unknown, a novelty with which we must strive to come to terms.




Moreover, while prisons and endless trials may frighten us, the existence that awaits us is remarkably similar. In these circumstances, rediscovering playfulness can also mean, like 

Ritchy Thibault

 and his irreverent public hearings, refusing to bow to the legal charade and its deceptive games.




Maintaining this playful irresponsibility short-circuits the deterrent power of the pervasive security rhetoric, characterised by a continuous dissemination of new measures, tools, and sophisticated repressive forces: the use of AI, 

DNA guns

, liquids that permanently soak into clothing, the deployment of the 

RAID

, the 

GIGN

, the Army… There is no need to elaborate on the arsenal at the state’s disposal for counter-insurgency. High school students and Gen Z, the new professional conspirators in chief, are showing us the way to neutralise them; to ward off risk, to embrace irresponsibility.







[1]

 A traditional French children’s nursery rhyme and staring game known as “Le jeu de la barbichette” (

Wikipedia

)

.




[2]

 Johan Huizinga, 

Homo Ludens: A Study of the Play-Element in Culture

 [1938], Routledge and Kegan Paul, 1949, p. 13.




[3]

 Walter Benjamin, “The Destructive Character”, originally published in the 

Frankfurter Zeitung

, November 20th 1931 (

The Anarchist Library

).

title: Comunicato delle cinque attiviste italiane arrestate e deportate da Israele
content:
Riceviamo e pubblichiamo il comunicato delle cinque attiviste italiane arrestate lo scorso 22 ottobre dalle forze di occupazione israeliane a Masafer Yatta, nella Cisgiordania occupata, e successivamente espulse dal Paese. Le cinque si trovavano insieme ad altre sei persone internazionali in visita a una famiglia palestinese quando sono state fermate da coloni israeliani e successivamente detenute dalla polizia. Nel comunicato denunciano le condizioni della detenzione, il ruolo delle autorità italiane e, soprattutto, la sistematica violenza dell’occupazione israeliana contro la popolazione palestinese, che continua a essere oscurata dall’attenzione mediatica riservata agli attivisti internazionali.




Di seguito il comunicato integrale.




Siamo le cinque ragazze italiane arrestate ed deportate dalle forze di occupazione israeliane.

Il 22 ottobre undici attivistə internazionali, oltre a noi una tedesca, un britannico, un irlandese, uno statunitense, un’austriaca e un’ ungherese, sono statə detenutə da coloni israeliani e poi dalla polizia israeliana mentre visitavano una famiglia palestinese a Masafer Yatta, nella West Bank occupata.

Non c’è davvero differenza tra esercito e coloni: in diversi posti viene delegato proprio a questi ultimi il controllo del territorio. E quando non è così, la comunicazione e la complicità tra esercito, polizia e coloni è più che stretta.




La stampa racconta che la Farnesina ha ottenuto il nostro rimpatrio. Ma qui non c’è proprio nulla da ottenere: noi non volevano essere espulse, volevamo restare in solidarietà con il popolo palestinese.




Quello che la Farnesina dovrebbe ottenere è, al contrario, una spiegazione delle ragioni per cui siamo state arrestate e detenute per 48 ore, rinchiuse in delle celle senza avere accesso a un processo e a contattare i nostri affetti.




Il governo dovrebbe chiedere perché nei territori palestinesi persone internazionali non possano stare accanto alle famiglie indigene mentre raccolgono le olive nella loro terra e cercano semplicemente di vivere la propria quotidianità. Come mai le loro case e le loro terre vengono arbitrariamente sottratte, occupate, dichiarate zone di addestramento militare, cacciando le famiglie che ci abitano da sempre.




Ci chiediamo inoltre come sia possibile che criminali di guerra possano godersi le vacanze in Italia, all’interno di resort privati, scortati da Digos e polizia senza subire alcuna conseguenza.




Come sempre nei media europei, fa notizia l’arresto di persone internazionali e non la violenza sistemica che i Palestinesi subiscono ogni giorno dalla Nakba del 1948 e ancora prima.




Le famiglie palestinesi vivono sotto un regime di apartheid e terrore imposto dall’occupazione israeliana e sotto la costante minaccia di espulsione e pulizia etnica. Vedono negati i permessi per costruire le proprie case o di accedere alle loro terre, dove i coloni indisturbati possono pascolare i loro greggi rubati ai palestinesi e costruire strade e colonie illegali sotto la legge internazionale. Le persone sono tagliate fuori dalle proprie fonti di acqua, i loro pozzi, le strade e le case, vengono distrutti. Una violenza costante per costringere la gente ad abbandonare la propria terra.




Non possiamo evitare di pensare alle proteste dei contadini e gli autotrasportatori del Sud Italia, che piangono vicino ai loro alberi di ulivo e al fatto che il lavoro di una vita non permetta loro di arrivare a fine mese. Non possiamo dimenticare delle migliaia di armi che escono dalle industrie della Leonardo a partecipazione statale e alle innumerevoli mobilitazioni contro il riarmo che hanno invaso le strade, le scuole, i porti e le stazioni durante questi anni. Davanti a tutto questo, il Governo è rimasto in silenzio. Al posto di ascoltare le proteste contro il carovita e dare delle risposte alle piazze, continua a finanziare la macchina di morte che porta avanti il genocidio, l’occupazione e lo sterminio in Palestina.




Quello che ci è successo è inaccettabile ma la situazione delle persone palestinesi è cento volte peggiore. Sono arrestate ogni giorno, nessun ministero degli esteri interviene per loro conto, nessun media si mobilita in loro difesa. Anche bambine e bambini sono detenuti illegalmente nelle carceri israeliane al cui interno gli vengono inflitte violenze fisiche, psicologiche e sessuali e nelle quali spesso muoiono, nel silenzio assordante del mondo.

Lo sappiamo bene, anche perchè durante la nostra detenzione abbiamo ricevuto minacce e derisioni. Un agente ha alluso a come si sarebbe divertito con noi la mattina della partenza, e alla potenziale minaccia di uno stupro. Paura con la quale abbiamo dovuto convivere tutta la notte nella nostra cella.




Chiediamo alla comunità internazionale di smettere di trattare la violenza sionista come una nota a piè di pagina. Chiediamo che il Governo italiano non si limiti semplicemente a delle note di condanna che non hanno alcun risultato né significato reale. Che si attivi per garantire protezione alle famiglie palestinesi di Hebron e di tutta la Palestina occupata. Vogliamo lo stop delle deportazioni e dei ban per gli attivisti, vogliamo la rottura di qualsiasi tipo di rapporto economico e commerciale con l’entità sionista. Chiediamo la chiusura delle ambasciate israeliane in italia e la fine di ogni tipo di complicità. Lo Stato deve fare pressione affinché

i coloni responsabili dello sterminio della popolazione in West Bank come a Gaza, e tutte le strutture statali che li rendono possibili, rispondano delle proprie azioni; e che si ponga fine all’impunità che rende la vita dei palestinesi sacrificabile.




Solidarietà con il popolo di Massafer Yatta. Solidarietà con la Palestina. Non smetteremo mai di lottare per una Palestina libera e per la libertà di tutte le popolazioni oppresse.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Re-elected Ottawa councillor wants Inuit-led housing projects in city
content:
Stéphanie Plante says she wants to see more Inuit-led housing and culturally appropriate services in Ottawa as she begins a second term as the councillor in Rideau-Vanier, a ward encompassing an area known as “Little Nunavut” because of its urban Inuit community.




Plante won almost 54 per cent of the votes in Monday’s municipal election, defeating five other candidates also in the running, according to unofficial results published by the City of Ottawa. 




Plante was first elected in 2022. Her new four-year term begins Nov. 15.




In an interview Tuesday, Plante said homelessness, mental health and addiction were among the most common concerns raised by residents during the campaign.




“We need to better spread our social services around the city,” she said.




“

We need to make sure every ward is doing its fair share, and I think we’ve gotten a bit better with that,” Plante added, pointing to the planned new Larga Baffin medical boarding facility project set for 1470 Hunt Club Rd., about five kilometres northeast of the Ottawa airport. The current boarding facility is on Richmond Road.




The six-storey, 220-room boarding home for Nunavummiut was planned as Larga Baffin’s new location, but construction has 

stalled

 as it awaits a long-term service contract from the Government of Nunavut.
















Plante said Ottawa should move away from relying on large emergency shelters and focus more on permanent housing, with services distributed across the city rather than concentrated downtown.




“If there’s housing for Inuit, it has to be led by Inuit,” Plante said. “The workers on site have to be Inuit or trained in the relevant cultural practices.”




Plante said she also wants to hear from Inuit medical travellers and their families about what the city could do to make their stay down south easier, including possible support for transit passes, culturally relevant daycare and community programming.







Before she became a councillor in 2022, Plante was an advocate for changing the name of Sandy Hill Park to 

Annie Pootoogook Park

 

in honour of the Inuk artist, who died in Ottawa. As a councillor, Plante supported changing the name of Emond Park in Vanier to 

Mary Papatsie Park

, in memory of a missing Inuk woman whose remains were found in Ottawa in 2022.




“Our amenities need to tell the stories of the people who lived here and sometimes those stories don’t have happy endings, but there’s a lesson there, and we need to learn that lesson,” Plante said.

author: Cleber Lourenço
title: Brazil’s Federal Police Probe US Companies’ Collusion With Bolsonaro’s Campaign
content:
The investigation’s main focus is on dealings involving an organization founded with the involvement of JD Vance.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On Tuesday, Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the Federal Police to investigate suspected foreign financing of Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign. Bolsonaro lost to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the runoff. The investigation will also need to determine whether any connection exists between political support for the senator and foreign interests in Brazil’s rare earth and strategic mineral resources.

Dino issued the 38 page ruling as part of ADPF 1178, a constitutional challenge originally filed by the Brazilian Mining Institute (Instituto Brasileiro de Mineração/Ibram). He ordered that an investigation be opened under the Supreme Court’s direct supervision, due to the possible involvement of members of Congress, whose parliamentary immunity can only be overridden in the nation’s highest court, in the alleged crimes under investigation.

The investigation’s main focus is on dealings involving Rockbridge Network, a U.S. organization founded with the involvement of Vice President J.D. Vance, along with Brazilian businessmen Tallis Gomes and Pedro Sang. The Federal Police must determine whether these dealings involved money, services or other economic benefits intended to help Bolsonaro’s campaign.

Investigators must also identify who was involved in the contacts between representatives of the American organization and Brazilian businessmen, and what purpose those contacts served.

Federal Police to Investigate Possible Link Between Campaign Support and Rare Earths

One of the most significant parts of the ruling is the suspicion that efforts to finance political activity may be tied to foreign economic interests in Brazilian mineral resources.

Dino explicitly ordered the Federal Police to investigate whether there is “concrete evidence linking the discussions over political financing to the reported economic interests in Brazilian rare earths and critical minerals.”

Dino also wants to determine who may have made any proposals, who they were directed to, and what might have been offered in return.

At stake are resources considered strategic for sectors including technology, energy and defense. In his ruling, Dino noted that these minerals belong to the federal government and that their extraction requires authorization or a concession from public authorities, as required by Brazil’s Constitution of 1988

If evidence emerges of negotiations involving rural land, the Federal Police must also determine whether there was an attempt to get around legal restrictions on foreign ownership of Brazilian land, including through the use of intermediaries.

Suspicions about Rockbridge first reached Brazil’s electoral courts through a complaint filed by Renan Santos, then a presidential candidate for the Missão party. The Workers’ Party later brought its own information about possible foreign financing operations to the Supreme Court.

Dino noted that the arguments presented by the two parties overlap.

Covert Advertising and Favoritism on Social Media

Another part of the investigation concerns paid promotion of content favorable to Bolsonaro by accounts based abroad, particularly posts that cited projections from Polymarket, a foreign prediction market platform barred from operating in Brazil.

According to the complaint filed by the Missão party, foreign accounts that normally didn’t cover Brazilian politics began running paid posts about Bolsonaro’s candidacy around the same time, citing estimates from that same platform.

The Federal Police must determine who paid for this content, where the money came from, and whether any Brazilian intermediaries were involved.

The ruling also addresses the role tech companies played during the campaign. Dino ordered an investigation into “intentional asymmetries and algorithmic manipulation” meant to help or hurt specific candidacies.

To support the order, Dino compiled documents from Meta’s Oversight Board, statements from United Nations experts, and a letter from U.S. lawmakers who pointed to possible inequalities in how Lula’s and Bolsonaro’s campaigns were treated.

Among the incidents cited were restrictions on boosting Lula’s posts on Instagram and improper recommendations of content linked to Bolsonaro.

Dino also cited an October 21 opinion from the Office of the Electoral Prosecutor General, which found that Meta had failed to comply with court orders, including requirements related to transparency around election ads and how its artificial intelligence tools function.

The ruling also references reporting from Intercept Brasil on payments from Bolsonaro’s campaign to Elytron, a company that offered an artificial intelligence system abroad for political influence operations. According to that reporting, the campaign recorded payments of $116,500 to the company, while the Liberal Party separately reported another $25,600.

Weighing all of this information together, Dino said the evidence points to “intensifying signs of foreign interference in the electoral process.”

Investigation Will Be Overseen by the Supreme Court

Along with ordering the investigation, Dino notified 10 federal agencies, including Abin, the Council for Financial Activities Control (Coaf), the Central Bank, the federal tax authority, the National Mining Agency and the Foreign Affairs Ministry, asking each to consider any action within its own authority.

Dino also drew on an Abin report identifying hidden financing of political groups, disinformation campaigns and cyberattacks as possible tools of foreign interference in Brazilian elections.

For Dino, the issue goes beyond foreign citizens expressing political opinions, which is protected as free speech. The problem arises when representatives of international organizations work to advance economic or institutional interests through actions meant to interfere in the election itself.

Under those circumstances, Dino said, there may be an “instrumentalization of political party activity in service of foreign interests.”

Although Dino denied the Workers’ Party’s request to join the case as a formal party, he acknowledged the relevance of the evidence presented and decided it would be more appropriate to investigate it through a separate proceeding.

The Federal Police must report the case number of the investigation to the Supreme Court. The investigation begins two days after Bolsonaro’s defeat and will aim to determine whether his contacts with foreign businessmen and organizations were limited to political and commercial exchanges, or whether they involved improper financing, covert advertising and economic interests in Brazil’s strategic resources.

So far, there is no confirmed evidence that Rockbridge illegally financed the campaign, or that any commitment was made to grant mineral rights in exchange for political support.

This article initially ran in ICL Notícias, has been translated by Panamerican Dispatch with express authorization of the editor, and can be read in its original Portuguese here.

author: Administrador
title: Zapatistische Vorbereitungen für das umarmende Treffen mit den Familien Sucherinnen.  Teil III. Umsorgen. Schützen. Bewahren.
content:
Musik: Meme del Real: »El mundo en que nací – Die Welt, in die ich geboren wurde«. Aufnahmen, Bearbeitung, Produktion: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas.

Compañeras Familien Sucherinnen.

Es grüßt Euch der Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés, Hauptkoordinator der Reise für das Leben – Kapitel Mexiko.

Nun, ich erzähle Euch, dass wir weiter fortfahren, uns vorzubereiten für die Reise, die wir machen, um Euch kennenzulernen – sowie Euren Schmerzen und Eurem Widerstand zuzuhören und davon zu lernen. Und um Euer Wort in unserem Herzen und in unserer Erinnerung zu bewahren. Wir erwarten wirklich, von Euch viel zu lernen.

Hier, wo wir uns versammelt haben, regnet es plötzlich viel und es ist kalt. Das ist ok für die, die aus den kälteren Regionen kommen; diejenigen aus wärmen Regionen leiden jedoch ein wenig, weil sie es nicht gewohnt sind. Regen sind wir alle gewohnt, denn natürlich regnet es hier in den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos viel. Im Gebirge, auf den Bergen und im Urwald regnet es so lange bis es aufhört.

Aus der Kälte wie aus der Wärme haben die zapatistischen Gemeinden delegierte Frauen, delegierte Männer sowie drei delegierte Otroas-AndEre geschickt, um sich vorzubereiten. Bis jetzt sind es zusammengerechnet 1.530. Vielleicht sinkt die Anzahl noch wegen Erkrankungen oder aus familiären Gründen. Beispielsweise hatte sich eine Compañera schlecht gefühlt; sie wurde untersucht und beim Ultraschall stellte sich heraus, sie ist schwanger. Sie musste [in ihre Gemeinde] zurückkehren, damit es ihr und ihrem heranwachsenden Kind gutgeht. Schnell meinte aber ein Compañero – der Ahnung von Tacos hat (sie zu machen, nicht, sie zu essen; denn Tacos essen, darin sind wir alle* gut trainiert) – er springt ein. Und ja, die Comandantas und Comandantes haben ihn bestätigt, denn er hat natürlich den Gesprächsrunden zugehört, die gegeben werden, um uns gut vorzubereiten.

Hier im Video zeigen wir Euch einige unserer Vorbereitungen.

Sei es die vollständige Delegation, seien es die Teile, in die wir uns organisieren: Wir bereiten uns auf Demonstrationen vor, falls es sie gibt; wie auch auf die Treffen, die Ihr uns sagt. Auf diesen Demonstrationen [marchas] – falls sie gemacht werden – ist unsere Hauptsorge nicht, was wir dort sagen, sondern die Familien Sucherinnen zu umsorgen, zu schützen und zu bewahren. Das heißt, wir sind nicht auf Tumult oder Entspannen aus, sondern Euer Wort zu hören. Und nun, wir müssen danach sehen, die Familien Sucherinnen zu umsorgen: Denn in ihrem Herzen haben sie heftige, harte Worte, welche aufzeigen und im Kampf für das Leben Richtung geben.

Wir wissen, dass wir lernen werden; dazu bringen wir Notizheft und Bleistift mit, sogar Computer, Tabletts, Smartphones. Und es kommen Compañeras, zu denen wir »Tercias Compas« sagen. Sie kennen sich mit Kamera, Aufnahmen, [Video-]Bearbeitung sowie der Übertragung der Treffen aus. Das Wichtigste jedoch ist, dass wir unseren Kopf, unser Herz, unser Innerstes mitbringen, mit der Lust zu lernen.

Im Video könnt Ihr sehen: Einige Compañeras mit ihren Babies stellen sich auf, so als wären sie für Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit demonstrierende Familien Sucherinnen; und sogleich geht unsere Delegation oder ein Teil unserer Delegation an ihre Seite und umgibt sie wie ein Schutzschild.

Selbst das Comando Popcorn [der Kinder] übt, ein Schutzschild zu bilden, welches umsorgt, schützt, bewahrt.

Denn so haben es uns unsere Vorgänger*innen gelehrt, die uns sagten: Wir sind Bewahrerinnen und Bewahrer der Erde, der allerersten Mutter.

Wie Ihr in den Aufnahmen seht: Bei so viel während den Übungen produzierten Schlamm ist es fast eher so als ob wir ausrutschen anstatt zu gehen. Nun, wir schlittern. Dabei passiert es, dass die Sandale oder der Tennisschuh steckenbleibt, und mensch kann nicht anhalten, denn hinter einem*einer kommt ja schon die Menge an Compas. Zweifellos muss bis zum Ende der Übung gewartet werden, um im Schlamm nach Sandale oder Tennisschuh zu suchen. In der Zwischenzeit bewegen wir uns wie ein hinkendes Hündchen.

Compañeras Familien Sucherinnen.

Wir kommen nicht, um spazieren zu gehen. Wir werden Euch umarmen, wenn Ihr wollt; und falls nicht, nun, wir kommen ebenso um Euer Wort zu hören.

Wir wissen, es gibt Leute, die von der Gira [der Reise für das Leben – Kapitel Mexiko] falsch reden. Sie spalten, sie möchten bestimmen, wer oder wer nicht sich mit uns treffen kann. Das heißt, sie wollen andere Gruppen draußen lassen, weil sie sich nicht vertragen; und solcherart Dinge. Der Capitán Marcos wird Euch später, an einem anderen Tag, von dem sprechen, sogar mit Namen.

Für diesen Augenblick möchten wir Euch lediglich unseren Respekt und unsere Zuneigung senden.

Aus den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos. Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés. Mexiko, Oktober 2026.

author: Amina Khan
title: EU transforms Frontex into a high-tech deportation command centre
content:
Yesterday, 27 October 2026, the European Commission tabled a new Regulation for Frontex, the EU’s border agency, expanding its powers and refocusing its mandate on deportations, preventing arrivals, and surveillance beyond EU territories and into social media. This would effectively turn Frontex into the EU’s deportation agency, equivalent of ICE in the United States.

At the centre of this reform is a budget that would almost double to nearly €12 billion for 2028–2034, leading to a massive expansion of the EU security and surveillance industrial complex. Frontex will test and deploy new technology to repress migrants, funnelling billions of taxpayer money to surveillance, security and defence contractors. EU’s hostile border security regime has for years produced systemic and massive human rights violations of migrants, refugees and racialised people, and those who stand in solidarity with them. This proposal will accelerate that.

Frontex as an ICE-style deportation enforcement agency

The proposal operationalises the recently adopted Deportations Regulation and deepens Frontex’s position as the central actor of a Europe-wide deportation machine. This will make the agency responsible for collecting and analysing data from Member States in order to “predict” deportation needs, and allocating resources to them. Frontex will now have a “Deportation Coordination Centre” that is expected to act at all stages of the deportation procedure, from detecting and identifying people that may be expulsed, booking or arranging flights and escorts, to monitoring their “reintegration” in the destination country.

Alarmingly, it expands Frontex’s powers to deport outside of the EU’s borders. Based on a simple status agreement, Frontex will be able to deport people from one third country to another, with the aim of preventing people from even reaching the EU. This will likely mean sharing sensitive data with third countries and countries of origin, where individuals may be at risk of persecution or harm.

The Frontex mandate reform comes in a package with a proposal to digitalise the management of deportation cases. The border control agency is given a key role in the harmonised technical design of EU and national digital systems, to exchange data on deportations, including sensitive data transfers to third countries (biometric data, travel documents and history, grounds for deportation, health data, etc.), and automate certain steps of the procedure, such as adding deportation orders in the Schengen Information System (SIS) to detect people.

Increased data processing and content policing

With this reform, Frontex’s practice of “debriefing interviews” is codified, particularly during the screening procedure introduced by the Migration Pact. The agency conducts these covert “voluntary” interrogations of people immediately after they disembark or cross the border. During these interviews, the agency extracts data from migrants deemed to be “suspects” of “cross-border crime”, without the possibility for migrants to seek legal counsel. Debriefing interviews have been rightfully criticised for their absence of fundamental rights monitoring and their unfairness as they take place when a person is detained and lacks privacy.

A new “Online Monitoring and Response Centre” will also surveil social media platforms to identify “suspicious behaviours or trends” in people’s movements at the EU borders, and before that, in the countries of origin and transit. Aggregated data collected online will be fed into Frontex’s “risk analysis” to guide border forces’ deployment and reaction. Social media monitoring was already declared as carrying high-risk for violating the fundamental rights of people affected, and was banned by the European Data Protection Supervisor in 2019 when first implemented by the EU Agency for Asylum.

Frontex will also seek designation as a trusted flagger under the Digital Services Act (DSA), allowing the agency to report pieces of online content to platforms for removal, effectively giving the agency extrajudicial powers to police the internet. It may also recommend national authorities to issue binding take-down notices. Frontex depriving people from finding legal support, sharing their stories or expressing solidarity is undoubtedly a serious infringement of freedom of expression.

All information collected during debriefings and online monitoring activities will contribute to Frontex’s border surveillance intelligence gathering called “European situational picture”. It may be combined with data from EUROSUR, Frontex’s information exchange framework with national border authorities, whose scope has been extended to include personal data in supposedly “exceptional” cases. Very sensitive data such as facial images, age, gender, physical and mental state may be processed to provide “situational awareness in situations posing imminent threat to the integrity of the external borders”. This could mean that individuals can be identified and targeted through cross-checking with OSINT data or AI-based identification tools like facial recognition.

Closer cooperation with Europol to further criminalise migration

Under the pretence of fighting the “facilitation of migration”, Europol, the EU’s policing agency, will be able to routinely consult personal data collected by Frontex. This could lead to individuals involved in border crossings, as survivors or supporters, to mistakenly fall under the investigation of Europol possibly with serious consequences, including impacts on their access to legal stay, detention, deportation or even criminal charges.

Quick Reaction Force for illegal pushbacks

Frontex will now also be able to deploy a “Quick Reaction Force”, to react ”flexibly” to “crisis and emergency situations” at EU borders. In this case, flexibility means outside of the usual controls and safeguards. Rather than coordinating humanitarian responses and triggering the solidarity mechanisms Member States agreed upon in the Migration Pact, the Reaction Force will likely aim to quickly and violently deport and force out people who are arriving to seek protection.

Migration repression becomes a market for arms and tech companies

The reform explicitly gives Frontex powers to research, test, and procure new technologies, including AI-enabled tools, drones, sensors and digital analytics. The agency will now be able to run trials, validate products and then procure them at scale, acting in some cases as a central purchasing body for Member States to pool technical equipment, while supplying non-EU countries with more repressive tools. This will reinforce global business for digital surveillance tech and arms, making migration repression a market of its own. The use of such technologies aims to prevent people from even reaching the EU, further outsourcing EU’s responsibility for border deaths and fundamental rights violations to private security companies and non-EU governments.

Protect Not Surveil says: Defund Frontex and resource care instead

The Commission frames migration as a “hybrid threat”, “instrumentalisation” and “weaponisation”, citing events such as Ceuta in 2026 to justify emergency powers and the expansion of Frontex’s surveillance capacities. This dangerous framing conflates individuals as security threats and removes their agency in their decision to move.

For decades, European governments and the EU have responded to migration not by addressing inequality, conflict, climate change, or the reasons people move, but by expanding a militarised border regime. Europe does not need a deportation agency. It does not need ICE. It needs a different approach to human movement: one that recognises movement as a human reality, protects people’s rights, and invests in safety, solidarity and community rather than deterrence and control.

The choice is between a Europe that responds to challenges through militarisation and exclusion, and one that responds through dignity, care, and shared responsibility.

Chloé Berthélémy, Senior Policy Advisor, EDRi, says, “With the new Frontex reform, the EU seems committed to making its borders even more deadly than they already are for people who come seeking safety and protection. The Commission has given a massive boost to the shady surveillance practices of Frontex by doubling their budget and loosening the already-lax data protection rules. The newly introduced social media surveillance, secret interrogations at borders, AI-powered sensors collecting data in real-time will all equip Fortess Europe for illegal pushbacks, more surveillance, and more misery.”

Pauline Fritz, Research and Advocacy Coordinator at the Border Violence Monitoring Network: “The Frontex regulation announced yesterday shows that impunity pays. Not only is Frontex able to receive new powers and a massive funding boost to expand its border surveillance apparatus, it can do so with full immunity for human rights violations and pushbacks that have and will continue to happen under its watch. It is deeply concerning how far the Commission is prepared to go to stop people from reaching safety and building a life in Europe.”

Sarah Chander, Director of Equinox Initiative for Racial Justice, says, “In the most substantial reform of Frontex to date, the EU transforms the agency into the central operations room for its deportation regime, with broader surveillance powers complemented by a bigger standing army.

Doubling Frontex’s budget to bolster kidnappings, prisons and ICE-like systems comes at a time when Europe’s social systems are failing. The EU is cynically distracting us from the real problems – cost of living, failure of social services and the climate crisis.”

Caterina Rodelli, EU Policy Analyst at Access Now, says “The new Frontex reform builds on years of unchecked privileged relationship between Frontex and the arms and tech companies , as in the case of Frontex Industry Days, which gave the private sector abundant face time to pitch their products and set the Agency’s priorities. Frontex will enable big profits from deadly deportation regime.”

Chiara Catelli, Advocacy Officer at the Platform for International Cooperation on Undocumented Migrants, says, “This proposal massively expands Frontex’s powers to track, control and deport undocumented people, from inside the EU to third countries and between third countries, without introducing stronger human rights safeguards. All this for an agency with a track record of allegations of complicity in fundamental rights violations.

Deportation operations and immigration detention centres in the EU are already rife with abuse, and we fear that expanding Frontex’s role will exacerbate these abuses within the EU and extend them beyond its borders. This proposal reflects a political obsession with deportations that ignores the realities of migration and Europe’s own economies.”

Emma Musty, Project Coordinator at I Have Rights, says. “At least 12 lives were lost in two shipwrecks last week and in both cases the Hellenic Coast Guards, who deploy Frontex Assets, were involved. Frontex clearly fails its human rights monitoring obligations when such incidents are so prevalent. We are deeply concerned that Frontex’s Mandate could be expanded, when what is actually needed is adequate search and rescue, accountability and safe routes.”

title: Critical mass d'octobre - vendredi 30 à 19h place Antonin Poncet ! - & soirée à l'atelier du Chat Perché
content:
LA

 

CRITICAL

 

MASS

, C'

EST

 

QUOI

 

DEJA

 

?




La “Critical Mass” est un mouvement cycliste né en 1992 à San Francisco. C'est une coïncidence organisée chaque dernier vendredi du mois, ou chacun.e est invité.e à participer selon ses motivations, convictions, envies, afin de partager les rues à vélos de tous genres (ou autre moyen de déplacement, rollers, skateboard… hors moteurs thermiques). Le principe est, ensemble, de se sentir libre et en sécurité à vélo dans les rues, en créant une masse mouvante compacte et bienveillante, résistant à la pression du trafic environnant, prenant soin les un.es des autres afin de créer un moment de partage et de bonne humeur où le temps d'une heure chacun.e peut être à vélo sans dangers. De cette sorte, le groupe prend de manière éphémère l'espace donné aux voitures, circulant sur la chaussée, la masse peut imposer son rythme en toute tranquillité, témoignant ainsi de la place occupée par les cyclistes en ville. La Critical Mass est de toustes et pour toustes, il n'y a pas d'organisateurs.trices, pas de hiérarchie ou de leader, étant spontanée, elle est créée par le groupe qui décide de se rassembler une fois par mois à un lieu et heure fixes, elle dépend de chacun.es. Libre donc de venir et de partir à tout moment, mais aussi d'y voir un moment entre amis, en famille, pour de nouvelles rencontres… Le parcours, comme les participant.es, change chaque mois. Personne ne décide seul du chemin, chacun.e s'implique comme iel le souhaite, tu es donc libre de te fondre dans la masse et te laisser porter ou bien aussi d'imprimer des tracts et communiquer sur la Masse, te placer en tête de cortège pour proposer un parcours, assurer la sécurité aux abords des intersections ou faire le vélo-balais.




Alors, que vous soyez un habitué ou curieux de découvrir la Critical Mass de Lyon, rejoignez-nous le 30 octobre

 

!

author: TGEU
title: Join the HIV Awareness Week in Berlin to establish the Emergency Support Network
content:
We are organising two free-of-charge parallel training programmes for queer and trans people that will come together on Friday, 20 November, to establish the Emergency Support Network.




This network should help people navigate services, identify realistic pathways to HIV prevention and care, and receive support without having to navigate complex systems alone. We also want to recognise that Ballroom houses, queer and trans collectives, and migrant communities already provide essential care infrastructure. We intend to strengthen these existing relationships, rather than create a parallel system disconnected from the communities themselves.




The initiative is particularly focused on two target audience groups:







Queer and trans people living with HIV who face barriers to accessing healthcare, especially those without health insurance, appropriate documentation, or access to HIV treatment and other essential services.




Queer and trans people on the move, including migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and undocumented people, who face difficulties accessing healthcare, HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and treatment.







Community HIV Training — 16, 18 and 20 November




This programme is intended for queer and trans adults, particularly queer and trans youth aged 18 and over, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, undocumented people and other people on the move.




It is especially relevant to queer and trans people who are living with HIV and face difficulties accessing treatment or healthcare, as well as those who need access to HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and other sexual health services.




The sessions will be interactive and community-led, covering HIV prevention and care, PrEP, PEP, testing, treatment, U=U, sexual health, pleasure, harm reduction and navigating healthcare systems.




An important feature is that registration for this programme is anonymous.

 Participants are not asked to provide their names, email addresses or HIV status. Anyone who wants to receive practical information or reminders can voluntarily register their email address through a separate form, which is not linked to their anonymous demographic responses.




This distinction is particularly important for people who may be reluctant to engage with services or activities because of concerns about confidentiality, stigma or their migration status.










register here










Health Champions Training — 17, 19 and 20 November




This programme is designed for trans and queer community leaders, particularly people involved in Ballroom houses, collectives and grassroots networks.




The training follows a train-the-trainer approach and will cover HIV, STIs and other infectious diseases prevention, treatment and sexual and reproductive health knowledge, and other topics like U=U, harm reduction, structural barriers to healthcare, peer education and safe healthcare navigation.




Participants will work through practical exercises such as community mapping, HIV knowledge games, real-life scenarios, role-play and referral mapping. The objective is to equip them to become trusted points of connection between their communities and healthcare services, while recognising that Health Champions are not expected to act as clinicians, legal experts or crisis responders.




On the final day, Health Champions will meet healthcare professionals, service providers and participants from the other training programme to help establish practical referral pathways and community-based support structures.










register here










Building the Emergency Support Network 

—

 

20 November 




On Friday, participants from both programmes will come together with healthcare professionals, community organisations and service providers.




The aim is to establish direct connections between people who need support, trusted community leaders and organisations capable of providing services. Participants will learn what support is available, who can access it, what barriers remain and how to make safe referrals.




The week will culminate in 

Under the Jellicle Moon Kiki Ball on Saturday, 21 November

, celebrating Ballroom culture, community leadership and the relationships developed throughout the initiative.




Note: 

All workshop participants must be 18 or older and attend all three days of their respective training. Snacks and dinner will be provided each day.




Your support makes change possible




We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.




Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

title: La culture entre en scène : appel à la mobilisation
content:
Après un mois de répression meurtrière et proto-fasciste à l'encontre du mouvement lycéen, exigeant des conditions décentes d'apprentissage, les étudiant•es et travailleur•euses de la culture luttent toujours contre la casse capitaliste du service public.


Malgré les réformes lointaines proposées en réponse à la lutte lycéenne, le Gouvernement ne renonce pas à sa politique économique austéritaire et sa dévastation sans précédent de nos conditions de vie.


En rêvant la privatisation générale des moyens de production culturelle et de leur récupération par l'extrême-droite, le Gouvernement incendie un à un les étages de la société.


Nous défendons une culture non-marchande, collective, populaire et inclusive, qui s'oppose radicalement aux idéologies réactionnaires qui abritent les dominations les plus graves et les plus destructions les plus violentes.


Nous appelons les étudiant•es et travailleureu•ses de la culture à continuer de se rassembler, à rejoindre nos canaux d'information, à se mobiliser ensemble dès ce samedi 31 octobre, à se réunir de nouveau en Assemblée Générale lundi prochain 2 novembre, et à construire la grève générale.

author: Rizomatica
title: Caso Grollmus: Chile vuelve a condenar mapuche con testigos sin rostro
content:
Ochenta años de cárcel. Eso le dio el Estado de Chile a cinco hombres mapuche en Cañete el 21 de septiembre. A otros, sesenta y cinco. A otros, treinta y cuatro. Más de mil años de prisión repartidos entre dieciocho personas. Para un hombre de treinta años, ochenta años de condena no es una pena: es morir preso.




Por: 

Daniela Sierra, abogada defensora penal







Los propios condenados lo dijeron con una claridad que ningún abogado podría mejorar. En un comunicado público firmado desde las cárceles donde hoy están, recordaron que su pueblo resistió casi trescientos años al imperio español, que la ocupación chilena de su territorio tiene apenas 143 años, y que hoy ese mismo Estado los condena a más de mil.




El ataque al fundo Grollmus fue grave y nadie lo niega. Hubo heridos y hubo dolor. Pero la gravedad de un hecho nunca autoriza a un Estado a condenar de cualquier manera. Al contrario: mientras más dura es la pena, más limpio debe ser el juicio. Y este juicio no lo fue.




Condenados por personas que nadie vio




Ninguna de las víctimas reconoció a los atacantes. Ninguna. La Fiscalía construyó su caso sobre testigos secretos, personas cuyo nombre y rostro la defensa nunca conoció. Once fueron anunciados; solo cuatro se sentaron frente al tribunal. Los condenados lo resumen sin rodeos:




«Solo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos” se dictó sentencia y veredicto».




Peor aún: hubo testigos secretos que jamás declararon. La Fiscalía renunció a ellos, pero lo que supuestamente dijeron entró igual al juicio, en boca de policías que contaron lo que otros les habrían contado. Nadie pudo preguntarles nada. Nadie pudo saber si mentían, si recibieron algo a cambio, si siquiera existen.




Y la pregunta de quiénes son esos testigos no es menor. Los presos denuncian que equipos de la PDI recorren los penales buscando internos dispuestos a declarar, a quienes luego se les pone, en sus palabras, «corbata de protegido y sin rostro». Si eso es así, Chile estaría condenando a perpetuidad sobre la palabra de personas presas, anónimas, que podrían estar negociando su propia suerte. Esa denuncia exige una respuesta, no silencio.




Pregúntese usted: ¿aceptaría ser condenado a morir en la cárcel por la palabra de alguien a quien nunca vio, que nunca habló frente a un juez, y cuyas palabras solo conoce porque un policía dice que las escuchó?




Eso no es justicia. Es una sombra con toga.




No es la primera vez. Es la misma historia.




El pueblo mapuche conoce de memoria este libreto. Primero les quitaron la tierra a punta de fusil y la llamaron «pacificación». Después los encerraron en reducciones. Y cuando reclamaron lo suyo, el Estado respondió con policías, fiscales y cárceles.




Alex Lemún tenía 17 años cuando un carabinero le disparó en la cabeza, en 2002. Matías Catrileo tenía 22 cuando otro carabinero lo mató por la espalda, en 2008; su autor no pasó un día preso. Camilo Catrillanca tenía 24 cuando lo mataron, también por la espalda, en 2018, y los uniformados destruyeron las grabaciones para ocultarlo. En 2017, la Operación Huracán encarceló a dirigentes mapuche con pruebas fabricadas por la propia policía.




Y en 2014 ocurrió algo que Chile parece haber olvidado. La Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos declaró que el Estado chileno violó los derechos humanos de lonkos, werkén y comuneros mapuche. ¿Por qué? Por condenarlos con testigos secretos. Por juzgarlos con prejuicios contra su pueblo. Por encerrarlos antes del juicio. Por dañar a sus familias. Es el caso Norín Catrimán y otros vs. Chile.




La Corte le ordenó a Chile algo muy simple: nunca más condenar a nadie basándose de manera decisiva en testigos sin rostro. Han pasado doce años. Esa orden sigue sin cumplirse. Y en Cañete, el Estado volvió a hacer exactamente lo mismo. Por eso el grito de los presos no es una consigna vacía: «¡No más testigos protegidos!» es, palabra por palabra, lo que un tribunal internacional ya le exigió a Chile.




No es casualidad. Es un patrón. Cuando el acusado es mapuche, la etiqueta llega antes que la prueba. Basta ver que el propio tribunal descartó que existiera una asociación criminal, y aun así autoridades y prensa siguen hablando de «líderes» y «organización». La condena social se dictó mucho antes que la sentencia.




La condena que pagan los niños




Una sentencia de ochenta años no la cumple un hombre solo. La cumplen sus hijos, que crecerán conociendo a su padre entre rejas y cemento. La cumplen sus madres, que envejecerán haciendo filas en la puerta de una cárcel. La cumplen sus parejas, que sostendrán solas la casa, la siembra, la crianza.




Y el Estado se encarga de hacerlo más difícil. Los condenados del caso Grollmus firman su comunicado desde el Complejo Penitenciario Biobío, el CERECO de Coronel y la cárcel de Llancahue, en Valdivia. Comunidades de la franja lavkenche, separadas de los suyos por cientos de kilómetros. Cada visita es un viaje, un gasto, un día de trabajo perdido para familias que ya lo han perdido casi todo.




Para una familia mapuche, la cárcel no solo encierra un cuerpo. Arranca a una persona de su tierra, de su lov, de sus ceremonias, de su lengua. Corta raíces que no vuelven a crecer. Empobrece.




Y el castigo empezó mucho antes de la sentencia. Un adolescente acusado llevaba casi quinientos días encerrado cuando el tribunal postergó su juicio porque no había jueces disponibles. Quinientos días de una vida joven perdidos por un problema de agenda del Estado.




Lo que pedimos




No pedimos impunidad. Pedimos lo mínimo que cualquier persona en Chile tiene derecho a exigir: un juicio justo. Que te condenen con pruebas que puedas enfrentar. Con testigos a quienes puedas mirar a la cara y preguntar. Con jueces que te juzguen por lo que hiciste, no por el pueblo al que perteneces.




Chile ya fue declarado responsable una vez por no respetar eso con el pueblo mapuche. Hoy la Corte Suprema tiene en sus manos la posibilidad de no repetir la historia. Si no lo hace, iremos de nuevo ante el sistema interamericano, y Chile tendrá que explicar por qué, doce años después, volvió a cometer el mismo atropello.




A las organizaciones de derechos humanos, a los pueblos indígenas, a los abogados y abogadas de Chile y del mundo: miren este caso. No dejen que dieciocho personas desaparezcan en la cárcel en silencio. La justicia que se le niega hoy a un mapuche es la que mañana se le negará a cualquiera.




Los presos ya dijeron lo suyo:




«No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso».




Esta información se publicó en 

Radio Kurruf

.

content:

author: Daron Letts
title: Safety a concern in Pangnirtung after increase in RCMP calls: MLA
content:
Pangnirtung MLA Johnny Mike is calling for the territorial government to help stop alcohol and drugs from entering his community after calls to Pangnirtung RCMP went up in August.




He made the comments Tuesday in the legislative assembly.




Pangnirtung MLA Johnny Mike tabled in the legislative assembly on Monday a monthly RCMP report that shows a high rate of alcohol-related calls for service. (Photo by Daron Letts)




“The safety of the people in our Nunavut communities should get more attention,” Mike said.




He had tabled the hamlet’s September RCMP detachment report, which shows 160 calls for service in August, the most for any single month this year. The number represents almost 14 per cent of the total 1,166 calls for service so far in 2026.




Mike asked Justice Minister George Hickes how the territorial government can better collaborate with RCMP and Canada Post to stem the flow of illegal substances into the hamlet.




Hickes described Mike’s comments as “very good questions at a very good time.”
















The justice minister is working with federal Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree about the issue and the pair spoke just last week, Hickes said.




Currently, one inspector is stationed in Montreal to identify illegal parcels destined for Nunavut, Hickes said.




“That’s not enough,” Hickes said, adding that parcels arrive through hubs in other centres.




Bootlegging remains a problem in the communities, Hickes and Mike both agreed.




Hickes suggested residents can help RCMP to shut down bootleggers by serving as the RCMP’s eyes and ears. 




He called on Nunavummiut to notify their local detachment whenever they become aware of illicit activities, including bootlegging, even when those activities involve neighbours, friends or family members.
















“It takes a whole community to discourage bootlegging,” Hickes said.




Education is also key, he added.




“It’s not just the RCMP that have a role to play,” Hickes said. “It’s the community members themselves, whether it be through hamlet officials — even down to the schools.”




Mike agreed, but emphasized that authorities are the ones who can take a “proactive” approach.




“The RCMP and the government have a big role to play,” Mike said.
















The force is not sure why August was so busy, said 

RCMP spokesperson Sgt. George Henrie in an email Monday.




“While there has been an increase in calls for service, the RCMP is unable to identify a specific reason for the increase, as call volumes are fluid and change consistently,” he said.




The Pangnirtung detachment is currently staffed by one sergeant and four constables.




While there are vacant positions within the detachment, relief members from outside the community fill in when needed, he added.




Detachment commander Chief Supt. Kent Pike will visit the community later this month, Henrie said.

title: Hollanda'da Dördüncü Kırmızı Çizgi Protestosu: “Soykırıma para yok!”
content:
Hollanda’da Gazze’deki soykırıma, İsrail’in Filistin topraklarındaki işgaline ve Hollanda hükümetinin bu politikalara karşı yeterli önlem almamasına tepki gösteren Kırmızı Çizgi protestolarının dördüncüsü için hazırlıklar sürüyor.

Organizatörlerin çağrısına göre gösteri, 8 Kasım Pazar günü saat 13.00’te Amsterdam’daki Museumplein’de başlayacak. Meydanda toplanacak katılımcılar, ardından kent merkezinde yürüyüş gerçekleştirecek.

2025 yılında Lahey’de düzenlenen üç büyük Kırmızı Çizgi protestosu geniş katılımla gerçekleşti. Organizatörlerin verdiği bilgilere göre, 18 Mayıs’ta 100 bin, 15 Haziran’da 150 bin kişi sokağa çıktı. 5 Ekim 2025’te düzenlenen üçüncü ve en büyük gösteriye ise 250 bin kişinin katıldığı belirtildi.

Yeni protesto, önceki eylemlerin devamı niteliğinde olmakla birlikte bu kez ekonomik ve finansal ilişkileri daha güçlü biçimde gündeme taşıyor.

Gösterinin adı da bu yaklaşımı yansıtıyor: “Kırmızı Çizginin Ötesi – Soykırıma Para Yok!”

Organizatörler, Hollanda’daki finans kuruluşlarının İsrail’in işgali, apartheid uygulamaları ve soykırımla bağlantılı olduğu belirtilen şirketlere yaptığı yatırımlara dikkat çekiyor.

Uluslararası Don’t Buy Into Occupation (İşgale Destek Vermeyin) koalisyonunun araştırmasına atıfta bulunan organizatörler, Hollandalı finans kuruluşlarının araştırma kapsamında incelenen şirketlere toplam 68 milyar avro yatırım yaptığını ifade ediyor. Açıklamada, 11 Hollanda emeklilik fonunun yatırımlarının yaklaşık 48 milyar avroya ulaştığı belirtiliyor.

Organizatörlere göre bu veriler, Hollanda’nın Filistin politikasının yalnızca diplomatik açıklamalar üzerinden değil, ekonomik ve finansal ilişkiler üzerinden de değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini gösteriyor.

Dördüncü Kırmızı Çizgi protestosu yalnızca Gazze’deki saldırılara odaklanmıyor. Eylem aynı zamanda İsrail’in Filistin topraklarındaki yasadışı işgaline, yerleşimlerin genişletilmesine ve bu politikaların sürdürülmesine katkıda bulunduğu belirtilen ekonomik ve askerî ilişkilere karşı da düzenleniyor.

Organizatörler, Hollanda hükümetinden İsrail’in işgaline ve uluslararası hukuka aykırı uygulamalarına verilen her türlü desteği sona erdirmesini istiyor. Finans kuruluşlarına ise işgal ve soykırımla bağlantılı şirketlere yönelik yatırımlarını durdurma çağrısı yapılıyor.

Protestonun temel mesajı, Filistin’de yaşananların sona ermesi için yalnızca siyasi açıklamaların yeterli olmadığı yönünde. Organizatörler, finansal kaynakların da işgal politikalarına destek vermemesi gerektiğini savunuyor.

Dördüncü Kırmızı Çizgi protestosu, 8 Kasım Pazar günü saat 13.00’te Amsterdam’daki Museumplein’de başlayacak. Organizatörler, Filistin halkıyla dayanışma göstermek ve Hollanda’nın siyasi, ekonomik ve askerî ilişkilerinde somut değişiklik talep etmek isteyen herkesi gösteriye katılmaya çağırıyor.

Demokratik İşçi Dernekleri Federasyonu (DİDF) de, Türkiye kökenli işçi ve emekçileri eylemlere katmak için yoğun bir çalışma sürdürüyor.

title: Antalya'da 4 işçinin öldüğü hortum felaketi: Müteahhit ve şantiye şefi tutuklandı
content:
Antalya — Antalya'nın Kepez ilçesinde 4 işçinin hayatını kaybettiği hortum felaketiyle ilgili başlatılan soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan 4 kişiden müteahhit ve şantiye şefi tutuklandı, diğer 2 kişi ise adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakıldı.

Kepez ilçesi Fevzi Çakmak Mahallesi 6199 Sokak'taki şantiyede, 26 Ekim'de saat 23.00 sıralarında şiddetli yağışla birlikte hortum çıktı. İşçilerin bulunduğu 2 konteyneri savuran hortum, yaklaşık 40 metre yüksekliğindeki kule vincin de devrilmesine neden oldu. İhbar üzerine olay yerine sevk edilen ekiplerin çalışmasıyla konteynerlerdeki işçiler çıkarılarak hastaneye kaldırıldı.

Olayda işçiler Aycan Kılınç (30) ile Suriyeli Muhammet Mustafa el Naim, İsa Musa el Nevaf ve Selahattin Muhammed el Naim hayatını kaybetti, inşaatın bekçisi Cumali Kurak ise yaralandı. Hortumda şantiyedeki konteynerlerin parçaları etrafa savruldu, çevredeki bir sitenin güvenlik duvarı ve yakındaki bir okulun çatısı ile bazı araçlar hasar gördü.

Hayatını kaybeden 4 işçinin cansız bedenleri, olay yerindeki incelemelerin ardından Antalya Adli Tıp Kurumu morguna konuldu. Aycan Kılınç’ın cenazesi, işlemlerinin ardından dün yakınlarına teslim edilerek memleketi Niğde’ye gönderildi. Suriyeli Muhammet Mustafa el Naim, İsa Musa el Nevaf ve Selahattin Muhammed el Naim'in ise kimlik belgelerinin bulunmaması nedeniyle kimlik tespit çalışmalarının sürdüğü öğrenildi.

Antalya Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından olayla ilgili başlatılan soruşturma kapsamında müteahhit Mevlüt Ç. ve eşi Ş.Ç. ile şantiye şefi Deniz K. ve iş güvenliği uzmanı İ.A, gözaltına alındı. 4 kişi, emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından adliyeye getirildi. Mevlüt Ç. ve şantiye şefi Deniz K. hazırlanan bilirkişi raporu doğrultusunda 'Birden fazla kişinin taksirle ölümüne sebebiyet vermek' suçundan sevk edildikleri hakimlikçe tutuklandı. Ş.Ç. ve İ.A. ise adli kontrolle serbest bırakıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Students in Rojava oppose the incorporation of their universities into state institutions
content:
The planned incorporation of the universities of Rojava and Kobanê into Syria’s state higher education system has met with resistance from students in Rojava. The Union of Patriotic Students rejects the recent decisions by the Syrian Ministry of Higher Education and warns that they threaten to undermine academic self-governance and Kurdish-language higher education. At a gathering at the University of Rojava in Qamishlo, the organization declared that it would not accept any decision that jeopardizes the educational structures built up over the years or the rights of students.




The dispute stems from two decisions by the Syrian Higher Education Council, announced on October 27. Under these decisions, the University of Rojava in Qamishlo is to be incorporated into the state-run Al-Furat University, while the University of Kobanê is to be placed under the University of Aleppo. Their faculties will henceforth fall under the authority of the respective state universities. Restrictions on the admission of new students are also planned for certain degree programs.




Kurdish-language education under renewed pressure




The decision comes amid growing disputes over the future of the Kurdish-language education system in Rojava. In late August, the Syrian Ministry of Education stipulated that Kurdish would be included in the state curriculum only as a subject taught for three hours per week. Permission to teach other subjects in Kurdish was granted only as a temporary measure.




While an independent education system with Kurdish as the language of instruction has been developed in Rojava over the years, students now fear that the future of higher education in their mother tongue is also at risk. They believe that incorporation into state universities could lead to existing degree programs being restructured, merged, or abolished.




At the gathering in Qamishlo, attended by numerous students, a statement read out in Kurdish and Arabic said: “These decisions will have a serious impact on us, as we have studied in our mother tongue, Kurdish, throughout our entire school education. The right to continue higher education in the same language is a fundamental academic right. Attempts to interfere with departments and faculties where education is provided in the mother tongue are an attack on the foundations of academia and a threat to our academic future. We will never accept this decision.”




“Integration does not mean assimilation”




The Students’ Union recalled that the establishment of independent universities in Rojava around ten years ago marked a historic step forward. For the first time, thousands of young people were given the opportunity to pursue higher education in their hometowns and in their mother tongue. These achievements must not be undone by administrative decisions, the organization said, particularly rejecting potential interference with existing faculties and degree programs.




“The abolition, merger, or restructuring of academic departments in this manner constitutes a clear violation of fundamental human rights and international conventions that guarantee the right to education in one’s mother tongue and the free, independent administration of educational institutions,” the Students’ Union declared.




The union demands that changes to the higher education system not be decided without consulting those directly affected. “Any transitional phase must be organized fairly and respect the identity of each university. Integration does not mean assimilation. Throughout the integration process, educational, logistical, legal, and academic criteria must be taken into account transparently. Otherwise, we will be faced with injustice and a betrayal of students’ rights.”




Recognition instead of dismantling independent structures




The Students’ Union emphasized that it welcomes official recognition of the universities in principle. However, it said, such recognition must not come at the expense of their autonomy or Kurdish-language degree programs. “Our wish has always been, and remains, for our university, built through dedicated efforts over the past ten years, to receive full recognition and continue fulfilling its mission without its academic programs being dismantled.”




The union pointed out that the people of Rojava have a legitimate right to universities that meet their academic needs while preserving their linguistic and cultural identity. It stressed that neither the efforts invested in establishing these universities nor the right of students to continue their chosen degree programs should be sacrificed for the sake of administrative restructuring.




In conclusion, the Union of Patriotic Students called on the Syrian transitional government, the Ministry of Higher Education, and all institutions involved to review the decisions and establish binding guarantees to protect the existing educational structures. “As a students’ union, we remain fully committed to our position and will continue our struggle for our rights by all means at our disposal. The achievements of the universities must be safeguarded, and young people’s right to higher education in their mother tongue must be protected,” the statement said.

title: Researching Peace: A Podcast Conversation with Bridget Conley
content:
Culture of Peace, How I Became a Peace Activist, Myths, Podcasts, World BEYOND War Podcast

By Marc Eliot Stein, October 28, 2026, World BEYOND War

On Episode 89 of the World BEYOND War podcast, we invited Bridget Conley, Research Director at the World Peace Foundation and host of the “Disrupting Peace” podcast, to share her perspective on many topics. We talked about the condition of our militarized planet in 2026, the absurdity of increasing military budgets to meet political quotas, the ruinous profit motive for endless war, the legacy of genocide and atrocity studies in the peace movement, recurring myths of war culture and more.

Mentioned in this episode: “The Priory of the Orange Tree” by Samantha Shannon. Musical excerpt: “Department of War” by Jesse Welles.

title: Kurdish athlete arrested after summons in Kermanshah, taken to undisclosed location
content:
Mohammad Nasseri, a Kurdish athlete who manages a bodybuilding gym in Harsin, Kermanshah Province, has been arrested after reporting to a prosecutor’s office in Kermanshah in response to a summons on charges of “propaganda against the state”.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Nasseri was arrested on 26 October after reporting to Branch 16 of the Investigating Office at Kermanshah’s Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office and was taken to an undisclosed location.




He had received the summons in recent days.

title: YJA Star guerrillas: Martyr Bêrîtan is the torch of our struggle
content:
Every year on 25 October, fighters following in the footsteps of Martyr Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş) commemorate the anniversary of her action against the line of betrayal in the free mountains. The date also marks the founding of the women's army. For this reason, guerrillas, particularly women guerrillas, mark the day with great enthusiasm. Guerrillas of the Free Women's Units (YJA Star) shared their feelings on the 34th anniversary of Bêrîtan Hêvî's martyrdom.




YJA Star guerrilla Elefterya Gabar Cizîr began by commemorating Martyr Bêrîtan with respect: “Comrade Bêrîtan became a pioneer and symbol of freedom for us. She understood the reality of Abdullah Öcalan's leadership. She became an example for us and for all women. Comrade Bêrîtan recognised the reality of free women, rebelled against the mentality of betrayal and refused to surrender. Many years may have passed, but she left us a legacy of resistance. That is why we commemorate Comrade Bêrîtan every year. She became a symbol of the will and resistance of free women. Through Martyr Bêrîtan, we came to recognise the will of free women. Through her, we came to understand our own reality. Bêrîtan's personality and action shattered the sexist mentality that underestimated women's strength. This gave us tremendous morale and spiritual strength. Thanks to those martyrs, we came to understand what real life means and the path of free women.







 







If women today have recognised their own strength and risen up, it is thanks to those pioneers. If women continue to take their place in the fields of struggle today, it is thanks to the efforts of the martyrs and Abdullah Öcalan. Abdullah Öcalan gave us strength and created the conditions for women to recognise their own will and take a leading role in society. Women have always played a pioneering role in guerrilla life and struggle as well. Great resistance has been waged in those mountains under the leadership of free women. Comrade Bêrîtan has always been an example for us. We will always struggle to develop ourselves along Bêrîtan's path, strengthen our struggle and fulfil her dreams.”




‘We will always follow Bêrîtan's path’




Guerrilla Bişeng Brûsk Vejîn also commemorated all the martyrs of the revolution through Martyr Bêrîtan and continued: “We must always commemorate Comrade Bêrîtan and introduce her to all women. When we look at the history of the freedom struggle, we see the pioneering role played by Comrade Bêrîtan. As women guerrillas in particular, we strive to follow in her footsteps. We will always take her path as our guiding principle because she is our pioneer and heroic commander. It is a great privilege for us to struggle along Bêrîtan's path and commemorate her in the free mountains today. Comrade Bêrîtan rejected surrender and carried out an action in which she put her life on the line against the path of betrayal. She is the pioneer and torch of our struggle. The existence of women who seek freedom and keep Bêrîtan's name alive today is extremely valuable to us. As those who follow in Comrade Bêrîtan's footsteps, we are striving to develop ourselves along her path and take determined steps forward.”

title: KRG Interior Ministry opposes Shengal integration, calls for implementation of 9 October Agreement
content:
On 26 October 2026, a ceremony was held in Shengal attended by YBŞ-YJŞ fighters and officials from the Iraqi Federal Government. During the ceremony, it was announced that 4,165 members of the YBŞ-YJŞ would be integrated into the federal security system.




The Yazidi community welcomed the move, expressing satisfaction that the Iraqi state had recognised Shingal’s defence forces. They also stated that Yazidi rights should be recognised in the Iraqi Constitution in the future.




On Tuesday night, the Kurdistan Region’s Ministry of Interior issued a statement calling for a return to the 9 October 2020 Agreement, which was signed in partnership between the KDP, the Turkish state and then-Prime Minister Mustafa al-Kadhimi, under the supervision of the United Nations.




The agreement stated that the Yazidi community should not have its own defence force and proposed the dissolution of the YBŞ, YJŞ and Êzidxan Asayish forces, which had been established to protect the population during the days of the 

ferman

 (the term used by Yazidi to refer to genocidal persecution and massacres).




The Yazidi community rejected the agreement, describing it as a new attempt at genocide and stating that it disregarded their will.




In yesterday’s statement, the Ministry of Interior said that all agreements concerning Shengal should be made with due regard to the will and demands of its population. However, the statement overlooked the fact that the members of the YBŞ-YJŞ are Yazidis who live in Shengal.
