Την Τετάρτη 28 του μηνός στη Θεσσαλονίκη, ανάμεσα στα πολιτικά πρόσωπα του τόπου που θα δώσουν το παρόν στην εθνική και στρατιωτική φιέστα, θα εμφανιστεί και ο Κασιδιάρης, το πρώην νο. 2 της χρυσής αυγής, ο οποίος θέλει να δώσει ομιλία στο ξενοδοχείο capsis που φημίζεται για τη θαλπωρή που προσφέρει ανά τα χρόνια στους εγχώριους φασίστες. Η μέρα αυτή θα μας βρει στο δρόμο, λοιπόν, για να καταστεί σαφές πως όσα χρόνια κι αν περάσουν, όσα ονόματα εθνικιστικών οργανώσεων κι αν παρελάσουν από το δημόσιο βίο, όσα χρόνια “σωφρονισμού” και αν έχουν στην πλάτη, οι νεοναζί και οι κολαούζοι τους είναι ανεπιθύμητοι στις πόλεις και στις γειτονιές μας.




Η σημερινή συγκυρία μας βρίσκει αν μη τι άλλο υπό μια δυσοίωνη σημειολογία: ανοιχτά ακροδεξιές πολιτικές δυνάμεις οδηγούν τις εξελίξεις σε κεντρικό πολιτικό επίπεδο στα ισχυρά κράτη της Ευρώπης και στις ΗΠΑ, ενώ με την αποφυλάκιση του νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη και τις αναγγελιές του για νέο κόμμα στα πρότυπα των παραπάνω, επικρατεί ένα πανηγύρι μεγαλοστομίας και εντυπωσιασμού στα σόσιαλ και τα παραδοσιακά μίντια. Ταυτόχρονα, βιώνουμε και την απτή αποτύπωση αυτής της ρητορικής: μέσα σε διάστημα μιας εβδομάδας, οι ντόπιοι νεοναζί έχουν μαχαιρώσει έναν αντιφασίστα στην Ελευσίνα και έναν πρόσφυγα μαθητή στο κέντρο της Αθήνας. Η κοινωνία μας, ωστόσο, δεν θα φάει το παραμύθι αμάσητο, ούτε θα επιτρέψει να ξαναγίνουν οι πλατείες μας σφαγεία.




Η λαϊκιστική ακροδεξιά μπορεί να μπαίνει και πάλι από το παράθυρο, ως μια δήθεν αντισυστημική και αυθόρμητη πολιτική δύναμη για να συντηρήσει και να επιδιορθώσει τα κακώς κείμενα της αστικής διακυβέρνησης, όπως το έχει κάνει ιστορικά. Η αντισυστημικότητα για την οποία καμαρώνει, βέβαια, σταματάει εκεί όπου αρχίζουν τα χαριεντίσματα με τα γεμάτα πορτοφόλια (βλ. τα σάλια μεταξύ Δ. Γιαννακόπουλου και Η. Κασιδιάρη) και φαίνεται ακόμα πιο έκδηλα αυτή την περίοδο όπου μπάτσοι, στρατός, φασίστες, ακροδεξιοί οπαδοί και κάθε λογής αντιδραστικό στοιχείο έχουν αναλάβει από κοινού το ρόλο της αντεπανάστασης σε όποιο τόπο υπάρχουν μαζικές κινητοποιήσεις. Αυτοί, δηλαδή, που πλασάρονται ως η έξοδος και η εναλλακτική από την τωρινή κατάσταση, είναι οι ίδιοι που πασχίζουν με κάθε δύναμη να τη συντηρήσουν πλάι στα όργανα της τάξης και ενάντια σε κάθε κοινωνική κίνηση που εξεγείρεται ενάντια στο υπάρχον.




Είναι δεδομένο και ιστορικά τεκμηριωμένο, πως ο ρόλος της ακροδεξιάς είναι βαθιά συστημικός και η πολιτική της ατζέντα αλληλοεπικαλύπτεται σε πολλά σημεία με αυτές των φιλελεύθερων κομμάτων: ξενοφοβία, αντιμεταναστευτική πολιτική, έπαρση του εθνικού φρονήματος, επίθεση κατά των κοινωνικών αγώνων και διεκδικήσεων, επίθεση στις κοινωνικά περιθωριοποιημένες ομάδες, συμμετοχή στα διακρατικά στρατόπεδα και στα πολεμικά μέτωπα μεταξύ άλλων. Μέσα σε όλα, η διάκριση μεταξύ των παραδοσιακών πολιτικών δυνάμεων γίνεται ολοένα και πιο αφηρημένη, αφού η κανονικοποίηση του ακροδεξιού, αντιδραστικού, ξενοφοβικού και σεξιστικού λόγου είναι γεγονός τόσο στον επίσημο πολιτικό λόγο, όσο και στη δημόσια σφαίρα μέσω των ΜΜΕ. Σήμερα, και ενώ σε πολλούς τόπους ταυτόχρονα εκδηλώνονται μαζικές και διαρκείς εξεγέρσεις ενάντια στην επιβεβλημένη ακρίβεια και την υποτίμηση της ανθρώπινης ζωής, οι νεοφιλελεύθεροι προετοιμάζουν το έδαφος στους φασίστες για να εξασφαλίσουν την καπιταλιστική σταθερότητα.




Σε μια παγκόσμια συνθήκη πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, είναι αναμενόμενο έννοιες όπως πατρίδα και έθνος να μονοπωλούν το ενδιαφέρον της εξουσίας και να κατέχουν κεντρική θέση στην ιδεολογική της αναπαραγωγή και την μιλιταριστική κατήχηση της κοινωνίας. Ήδη γίνεται φανερό από τις στρατιωτικές μεταρρυθμίσεις και τις πολεμικές δαπάνες του ελληνικού κράτους ότι βαδίζουμε στους ρυθμούς μιας πολεμικής οικονομίας, η οποία τοποθετεί το καθολικό συμφέρον της κοινωνίας εν ελλάδι στις διακρατικές συμφωνίες που συνάπτει το κράτος και στις γεωπολιτικές συμμαχίες του με τον άξονα ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ-Ισραήλ. Ταυτόχρονα, η αντιπολίτευση που δέχεται η ΝΔ επιδιώκει μια ακόμη μεγαλύτερη ευθυγράμμιση με την παγκόσμια ακροδεξιά λαίλαπα, μια εντονότερη αντιμεταναστευτική πολιτική (παρότι το κράτος δολοφονεί εκατοντάδες μεταναστών στα σύνορα, όπως έκανε και πριν μερικές μέρες στη Σάμο και τη Λέσβο) και μια απαγκίστρωση από τη λεγόμενη “woke agenda”. Από αυτά και μόνο μπορεί να γίνει αντιληπτή η ιδεολογική φούσκα στην οποία ζει η alt right. Δικό μας χρέος είναι ταυτόχρονα με τις μεγάλες εθνικές αφηγήσεις να απορρίψουμε κάθε σκέψη για συμμετοχή στους διακρατικούς πολέμους και τον στρατό, αλλά και να μην εγκαταλείψουμε τις κοινωνικές διεκδικήσεις για ισότητα και ελευθερία.




Ο εθνικισμός και οι ακροδεξιές κοινοβουλευτικές του εκδοχές τρέφονται και αναπαράγονται από την κοινωνική αδράνεια, όπως και από την εμπέδωση της πολιτικής ηττοπάθειας και της αδυναμίας να φανταστούμε και να υλοποιήσουμε ένα διαφορετικό κοινωνικό φαντασιακό, αισθήματα ιδιαίτερα κοινά αυτή τη στιγμή. Οι πραγματικές υλικές συνθήκες που έχουν διαμορφώσει οι αλλεπάλληλες κρίσεις του καπιταλισμού τις τελευταίες δύο δεακετίες, όπως και τα αισθήματα δυσφορίας που δημιουργούν, είναι το βούτυρο στο ψωμί των ακροδεξιών τσαρλατάνων για να διασπείρουν τη μισαλλόδοξη ρητορική τους. Μπροστά σε μια προεκλογική περίοδο και σε χίλια δύο σημεία μιας ακόμα διαφαινόμενης καπιταλιστικής κρίσης, είναι σημαντικό να μην υποκύψουμε ξανά στην παραφιλολογία της ψήφου αγανάκτισης. Ο φασισμός επωάζει όταν δεν ονοματίζεται ως τέτοιος, όταν αφήνονται να φυσικοποιηθούν οι φανφάρες του για έθνος και φυλή, επομένως οφείλουμε να τον πούμε με το όνομά του. Να αναγνωρίσουμε τον πραγματικό του ρόλο στην κεντρική πολιτική σκηνή, αυτόν της πιο ακραίας, επιθετικής μορφής επικυριαρχίας του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου στη ζωή μας, της εντεινόμενης εκμετάλλευσης της εργατικής δύναμης στην παραγωγή και της ολομέτωπης επίθεσης στις ατομικές ελευθερίες.




Συνολικά, αυτό που πρέπει να κρατήσουμε για τους μελλοντικούς μας αγώνες είναι ότι πέρα από την καθημερινή μάχη με το φασισμό στο δρόμο, στη δουλειά, στα σχολεία και όπου ξετρυπώνει και κάνει δημόσια την παρουσία του, στόχευση μας είναι να ενισχύσουμε ταυτόχρονα και όλα τα υπόλοιπα μέτωπα κοινωνικών αγώνων που διεκδικούν άμεσα την αναβάθμιση των ζωών μας, την κοινωνική χειραφέτηση, τους αγώνες για τα δικαίωματα των μεταναστ(ρι)ών, τους αγώνες ενάντια στο ρατσισμό και την πατριαρχία. Παρεμβαίνοντας δραστικά σε όλα αυτά τα δίκτυα σχέσεων και δομώντας από την αρχή μια διαφορετική καθημερινότητα για μας τις ίδιες και όλους τους εκμεταλλευόμενους, επισφραγίζουμε νίκες σε ένα ευρύ κοινωνικό, αντιφασιστικό κίνημα, νίκες, δηλαδή, των ανθρώπων απέναντι στους φασίστες.




Ελεύθερος Κοινωνικός Χώρος Σχολείο
















ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ:ΤΣΙΡΑΚΙΑ ΤΩΝ ΑΦΕΝΤΙΚΩΝ, ΕΧΘΡΟΙ ΤΗΣ ΤΑΞΗΣ ΜΑΣ.




Την Τετάρτη 28 Οκτωβρίου, ο νεοναζί Ηλίας Κασιδιάρης έχει ανακοινώσει την πραγματοποίηση ομιλίας του στη πόλη μας. Σε ένα ξενοδοχείο που επιλέγει συχνά να στεγάσει εκδηλώσεις του ακροδεξιού εσμού: φυσικά, πρόκειται για το ξενοδοχείο Capsis.


Διανύουμε μία χρονική περίοδο, κατά την οποία οι φασίστες προσπαθούν να ανασυνταχθούν με την υποστήριξη του κεφαλαίου. Σαφώς με την σειρά τους, προσφέρουν άμεση στήριξη στους καπιταλιστές των οποίων αποτελούν εμπροσθοφυλακή, καθώς μοιράζονται από κοινού το ιδεολόγημα της «εθνικής ανάπτυξης» δηλαδή της ειρήνευσης μεταξύ των τάξεων και της υποταγής στον κόσμο της εξουσίας. Δεν είναι τυχαίο πως ο Elon Musk και ο Δ.Γιαννακόπουλος έχουν δηλώσει την ανοιχτή στήριξη τους στον Κασιδιάρη. Όπως, δεν είναι κρυφό πως η Χ.Α από τα πρώτα χρόνια του ξεσπάσματος της καπιταλιστικής κρίσης μέχρι και το τσάκισμα και την υποχώρηση της από το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα, αναλάμβανε να φέρει σε πέρας τη βρώμικη δουλειά του κεφαλαίου, ζητώντας φοροαπαλλαγές για το εφοπλιστικό κεφάλαιο, πραγματοποιώντας επιθέσεις σε βάρος συνδικαλιστών, και στήνοντάς απεργοσπαστικούς μηχανισμούς.


Η απόπειρα τους για επαναφορά στη κεντρική πολιτική σκηνή, έβρισκε και θα βρίσκει απέναντι το εργατικό και το κοινωνικό κίνημα. Σε μία περίοδο στην οποία το κεφάλαιο εντείνει την επίθεση του σε βάρος της εργατικής τάξης σε παγκόσμια κλίμακα, πετσοκόβοντας μεθοδικά από τις ανάγκες μας στο όνομα των πολεμικών εξοπλισμών και του κοινού «εθνικού συμφέροντος», επενδύοντας στη καταστολή και επιδιώκοντας να τρομοκρατήσει τους καταπιεσμένους/ες και όσους και όσες αγωνίζονται, βρίσκει ως αποκούμπι του τους γνωστούς εχθρούς της ελευθερίας, για πολλοστή φορά. Η απάντηση θα δοθεί στους χώρους εργασίας, τις γειτονιές, τις σχολές, τα σχολεία και τους δρόμους και είναι μία: Μηδενική ανοχή στον κοινωνικό εκφασισμό! Ούτε στη Θεσσαλονίκη ούτε πουθενά, τσακίστε τους φασίστες σε κάθε γειτονιά!







Η Τ.Ε Θεσσαλονίκης της Αναρχοσυνδικαλιστικής Πρωτοβουλίας Ροσινάντε καλεί στην αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου, Τετάρτη 28 Οκτωβρίου στις 16:00.

title: Nosso Povo Tá Na Rua
content:
La notte del ballottaggio tra Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro si conclude con una enorme manifestazione di gioia della classe lavoratrice brasiliana: l’avenida Paulista di São Paulo è piena da scoppiare di gente e di bandiere rosse; nelle favelas delle principali città del paese i fuochi d’artificio scoppiano insieme a colpi di armi da fuoco sparati in aria per festeggiare. La vittoria di Lula al secondo turno è data matematicamente per certa intorno alle 9 di sera, ora brasiliana, con oltre 4 milioni di voti di differenza rispetto al candidato dell’estrema destra e il capovolgimento del risultato del primo turno, tenutosi il 4 ottobre.







«Bora Bora Bora Lula,




Bora Bora Bora Virar




Nosso Povo Tá Na Rua




A Mudança Continua»




Avanti Avanti Avanti Lula,




Avanti Avanti Avanti Ribaltiamo (il risultato),




Il nostro popolo è per strada,




Il cambiamento continua.




(

Bora Lula Bora Pra Rua

, “Avanti Lula Avanti per Strada”, jingle a favore di Lula uscito 4 giorni prima del ballottaggio)







La campagna di Lula per il primo turno è stata considerata da più parti una campagna fredda, imperniata intorno alla storia personale del presidente e alla celebrazione dei risultati del governo, e non è riuscita a stimolare la partecipazione attiva della base sociale storica del Partito dei Lavoratori e della sinistra brasiliana. L’estrema destra bolsonarista, al contrario, aveva condotto una campagna elettorale aggressiva, cercando di organizzare la rabbia contro la crisi sociale e presentandosi come forza di rottura, ma allo stesso tempo tutelando gli interessi economici che producono la crisi e spostando la frustrazione dei brasiliani verso l’ostilità contro altri lavoratori, le donne, le persone LGBTQIA+, i migranti e i popoli indigeni. Bolsonaro Jr prometteva aggressive politiche anti-criminali ed elogiava apertamente le operazioni militari condotte dai governatori bolsonaristi nelle favelas, che avevano causato massacri ed omicidi di massa. Si presentava fieramente come alleato degli Stati Uniti nella regione ed esortava il suo elettorato a dare la spallata finale alla sinistra latino-americana, garantendo che il sostegno servile di Brasilia agli interessi americani nella regione avrebbe portato alla crescita economica del paese. Il bolsonarismo, che condivide i propri interessi economici con la destra liberale, aveva infine stretto alleanze con i grandi proprietari terrieri del centro-sud, le industrie forestali ed i grandi capitali industriali promettendo l’abbattimento di ogni barriera legale alla deforestazione, sdoganando il fracking e lo sfruttamento intensivo dei bacini minerari del paese.




A questo bisogna aggiungere – da un lato – la spudorata ingerenza dell’imperialismo americano nella campagna elettorale, come al solito condotta dagli americani senza carota ma con tanto bastone: dagli endorsement ufficiali di Trump alle minacce di un crollo dei mercati finanziari in caso di vittoria di Lula, fino ad arrivare all’adozione ufficiale da parte del Brasile di sistemi di conteggio dei voti progettati negli USA e dipendenti dalle tecnologie satellitari Starlink di Elon Musk. Dall’altro lato, anche la magistratura brasiliana storicamente legata a doppio filo all’estrema destra aveva fatto il suo, aprendo ad arte – al culmine della campagna elettorale – due inchieste per corruzione contro alcuni ministri del PT e contro lo stesso figlio di Lula. Al primo turno, diversi stati in cui la vittoria di Lula era data per garantita dal PT sono quindi andati al bolsonarismo e l’astensione si è collocata intorno al 20%.




Un dato significativo della prima tornata, tuttavia, risulta essere l’elezione (o la rielezione) con il PT o altri partiti della coalizione (tra cui il PSOL e il PCdoB) di decine di militanti provenienti da differenti settori sociali in lotta, un elemento che conferma come il massiccio e combattivo movimento sociale brasiliano abbia, nel corso degli ultimi anni, puntato sul Lulismo come vetrina elettorale: tra loro, Rick Azevedo, leader del movimento 

Vida Além do Trabalho

 (Vita Prima del Lavoro), ex-commesso che si batte da anni per l’abolizione della scala 6×1 (6 giorni di lavoro, 1 di riposo); Rosa Amorim, storica dirigente del 

Movimento Sem Terra

; Ana Júlia Ribeiro, dirigente del movimento studentesco in prima linea durante le occupazioni delle scuole del Paraná; Erika Hilton, attivista LGBTQIA+ e storica militante per i diritti delle persone trans e nere. 




Proprio le rivendicazioni portate dai movimenti sociali brasiliani hanno, dopo il primo turno, dato slancio e forza alla campagna elettorale di Lula in vista del ballottaggio. La prima risposta alla sconfitta del 4 ottobre è arrivata dai giovani brasiliani: dal giorno dopo il voto gli studenti hanno cominciato a convocare assemblee e manifestazioni che si sono diffuse in diverse città del paese; iniziative con una forte spinta spontanea, ma appoggiate e anche dalle storiche organizzazioni studentesche del Brasile. Dal 5 ottobre le piazze brasiliane non si sono più svuotate e hanno progressivamente visto la partecipazione alle manifestazioni di lavoratori, sindacati e moltissime organizzazioni popolari. Da un lato, il movimento esprimeva in piazza la paura e la preoccupazione per una vittoria di Bolsonaro, e prometteva una dura opposizione di strada se il ballottaggio avesse visto vincere l’estrema destra: una vittoria del bolsonarismo avrebbe rappresentato la possibilità di attaccare frontalmente ed indebolire le organizzazioni popolari ed ampliare il controllo sulle istituzioni e sulla magistratura, uno scenario reso ancora più pericoloso dal fatto che Bolsonaro Jr avrebbe potuto contare sull’esperienza accumulata nel precedente governo di estrema destra e su un contesto internazionale e latino-americano di generale sottomissione agli interessi dell’imperialismo statunitense. Dall’altro lato, la mobilitazione di piazza delle ultime tre settimane ha effettivamente imposto al PS le condizioni per una sua vittoria, ed i termini della sua seconda campagna elettorale: dall’abolizione del 6×1 alla fine dell’assedio poliziesco contro i quartieri proletari, dalla riduzione dell’orario di lavoro a parità di salario alla riforma agraria, dalla ripartizione delle terre allo stop all’abbattimento della foresta amazzonica. L’impegno più importante chiesto a Lula – ed a sua volta una promessa che l’ex-presidente aveva fin da subito messo al centro della propria campagna – è la richiesta di impegnare battaglia contro l’imperialismo americano e di mantenere intatta la sovranità nazionale del Brasile.




Il movimento ha contato perché ha saputo costruire un rapporto di forza diffuso in (quasi) tutto il paese, che è dipeso dalla capacità collettiva di trasformare una posizione politica, inizialmente derivante dalla paura per una vittoria della reazione, in una presenza sociale organizzata capace non solo di influenzare decisivamente la campagna elettorale, ma anche di far avanzare concretamente l’agenda di classe del Brasile – costringendo i candidati a misurarsi sui temi del costo della vita, della riproduzione sociale, della violenza della polizia e del futuro modello economico del paese. Un terreno su cui Lula, da vecchio sindacalista e capo-popolo delle mobilitazioni sociali degli anni 80, ha avuto l’intelligenza di spostarsi e la capacità di dominare: memorabile, in questo senso, il dibattito elettorale trasmesso in TV qualche giorno prima del ballottaggio, in cui un arrogante Bolsonaro Jr ha deriso Lula con l’appellativo «nove dita», facendo riferimento al suo mignolo amputato. Un inferocito Lula, ricordando a Bolsonaro come avesse perso il dito a 17 anni, quando era costretto a fare (illegalmente) i turni di notte in fabbrica per portare a casa il pane, ha riscoperto dentro sé stesso l’odio di classe dei suoi giorni giovanili – e, cosa più importante, lo ha risvegliato in milioni di telespettatori davanti agli schermi. 




Basta un’occhiata ai commenti sotto le clip della risposta di Lula che girano a migliaia su Youtube e Instagram per rivelare come decine di migliaia di brasiliani e brasiliane incazzate abbiano considerato l’insulto rivolto a Lula un affronto contro tutti i lavoratori e le lavoratrici, ed abbiano reagito definendo Bolsonaro un figlio di papà e rivendicando la fine delle condizioni di lavoro disastrose, degli incidenti e dei licenziamenti. Allo stesso tempo, negli ultimi giorni della campagna sui social hanno spopolato i jingle fatti con l’IA o i pezzi dei 

funkeiros

, dj famosi soprattutto nei quartieri popolari, a favore di Lula, con hit come “Ele investiu em VC” di MC Carol, 

funkeira

 di Niterói (Rio de Janeiro) e militante dei movimenti femministi, che ha totalizzato 10 milioni di visualizzazioni in soli 2 giorni: «Bolsonaro é um caralho / essa porra é Lula da Silva / Ele já investiu em você / ele já mudou sua vida / Com Farmácia Popular e também Bolsa Família» («Bolsonaro non vale un cazzo / è Lula da Silva, porca miseria / che ha già investito su di te / ti ha già cambiato la vita / con “Farmácia Popular” [programma di distribuzione popolare di farmaci] e anche con il “Bolsa Família” [sussidio per le famiglie, due storici programmi di sostegno sociale dei primi governi PT che Lula ha promesso di ampliare e difendere di fronte alla promessa di Bolsonaro di eliminarli]»).




Con l’emergere di questa massiccia mobilitazione popolare – che ha trascinato la campagna sul terreno della risposta ai bisogni materiali della popolazione impoverita e ha imposto i termini della sfida – si possono almeno parzialmente spiegare i motivi della storica rimonta del candidato del PS, che ha vinto ieri con uno scarto di oltre 4 milioni di voti. Facendo un po’ di matematica, rispetto al primo turno Lula ha ricevuto oltre 10,3 milioni di voti in più, passando da 53,88 milioni ai 64,2 con cui si è concluso il conteggio ieri sera, mentre Bolsonaro è riuscito a crescere di solo 3,7 milioni di voti, passando dai 56,1 del primo ai 59,8 milioni di suffragi al secondo turno. La sinistra brasiliana ha recuperato i voti degli indecisi e di chi al primo turno aveva votato un altro candidato, ma ha anche sottratto voti al bolsonarismo ed è riuscita a portare alle urne oltre 3 milioni di elettori che si erano astenuti il 4 ottobre. Un successo giocatosi, in gran parte, sul terreno della risposta ai bisogni sociali del Paese: nell’impoverito Nord del Brasile, Lula ha guadagnato tra 5 e 7 punti per Stato; complessivamente, il PS ha ricevuto, al secondo turno, il 62% dei voti degli afro-brasiliani; il 55% del voto femminile; il 63% dei voti di chi prende il salario minimo; il 57% dei voti di chi ha solo la licenza elementare; l’80% dei suffragi dei prigionieri e delle prigioniere. Un ultimo dato a conferma di questa ipotesi è il ribaltamento del risultato nello Stato di Minas Gerais, uno dei bastioni del bolsonarismo, dove al primo turno il PS aveva preso il 43% ed al secondo, invece, ha vinto con il 50,5% dei voti: un distretto nella cui zona nord, siderurgica ed operaia, l’astensione aveva raggiunto picchi altissimi, mentre il sud agricolo e latifondista votava compatto l’estrema destra, ha visto un radicale aumento dell’affluenza culminata con la vittoria del Lulismo.




Bolsonaro ha ufficialmente annunciato che disconosce il risultato delle elezioni. A chi pensa che sia solo il raglio dell’asino sconfitto, bisogna ricordare che l’estrema destra brasiliana controlla ancora la maggior parte degli organi legislativi del Brasile, esprime diversi governatori e comanda su grossi pezzi di magistratura, oltre ad avere a sua disposizione decine di migliaia di agenti di polizia e criminali (i cosiddetti 

milicianos

) impegnati in una guerra di sterminio contro le favelas e i settori sociali proletari del paese. Un blocco sociale reazionario che pochi anni fa ha organizzato un colpo di Stato in piena regola cercando di prendere il potere a Brasilia, e che può contare – da adesso – con l’appoggio politico, economico e logistico degli Stati Uniti e dei governi suoi alleati nella regione. Difficile, quindi, pensare che la partita sia chiusa.




Osservata sul piano globale, tuttavia, la vittoria di Lula rappresenta innegabilmente due cose. La prima: l’estrema destra latino-americana, il cavallo di Troia degli interessi americani nel continente, ha subito una battuta d’arresto di portata storica, venendo sconfitta nell’unico tassello che mancava per completare l’assoggettamento del continente agli USA – ed, elemento non indifferente, questo tassello è il più popoloso paese latino-americano, e la principale potenza economica della regione. Un bel guaio per chi, a Washington, sperava di fare cappotto definitivamente nel “cortile di casa” . Non è un caso che ieri notte gli Stati Uniti abbiano immediatamente esercitato la loro piccola, meschina vendetta spedendo in Venezuela l’esiliata di estrema destra Maria Corina Machado – in mezzo a bagni di folla organizzati ad arte -, per dimostrare al mondo di poter scatenare a proprio piacimento il definitivo tramonto di quel poco che rimaneva del governo bolivariano del Venezuela. La seconda cosa: la sconfitta di Bolsonaro permette di tirare un sospiro di sollievo a Cuba, l’unica esperienza rivoluzionaria ancora viva e combattiva del continente, stretta nella morsa dell’assedio economico statunitense, e che potrà continuare a contare sul Brasile come un alleato, sebbene forse non all’altezza del proprio compito, quantomeno disponibile a lottare per sostenere l’isola.




Sul piano nazionale, è difficile predire se un ottuagenario come Lula, per quanto combattivo, e la sua alleanza politica traballante (che contiene anche forti correnti liberali) saranno capaci di dare risposte concrete alla mobilitazione dei movimenti sociali che li ha portati alla vittoria, o se presto o tardi finiranno per tradire le promesse fatte in campagna elettorale e cercheranno di mantenere il potere con accordi ed equilibrismi con la destra moderata e le associazioni padronali. La vittoria di Lula non rappresenta certamente un passaggio politico rivoluzionario per il Brasile, ed anzi corre il rischio concreto di limitarsi ad amministrare il presente in termini riformisti e fungere da argine elettorale allo sviluppo di un reale rapporto di forza capace di trasformare la società. Questa scelta rappresenta la tomba storica della sinistra latino-americana, la risposta deleteria ad una sfida su cui si sono schiantati con gran fragore la maggior parte degli esperimenti di governo più o meno radicali della regione: dal cileno Boric alle ultime espressioni del peronismo di sinistra argentino. I danni sarebbero enormi: da un lato, una vittoria a valanga dell’estrema destra sarebbe solo rimandata; dall’altra, i movimenti sociali potrebbero subire un iniziale recupero da parte del Lulismo, che si tradurrebbe in un loro depotenziamento ed in una delega in bianco al governo, per poi uscire da uno scenario di potenziale tradimento con le ossa rotte e la fiducia sotto i tacchi, giustamente indisposti a sostenere ancora una volta il PT ma incapaci di difendersi e rispondere di fronte agli attacchi violenti della destra. Lungi da noi, quindi, lo scadere in facili entusiasmi per le vittorie elettorali di una sinistra riformista che troppo spesso, nel continente latino-americano, ha finito per ripiegare in disordine di fronte all’incapacità di sciogliere le proprie contraddizioni e spalancare le porte dei propri paesi alla peggiore reazione.




Dall’altro lato, ciò che dobbiamo sempre ricordare quando si parla del Sud America e si guarda ai suoi processi politici dalle nostre latitudini, è che il rapporto antagonista tra le classi popolari e la reazione si articola su delle dimensioni di scontro estremamente esplicito, dispiegato e violento che per noi appartengono (almeno per adesso…) al passato. Nella difficoltà di reggere la durezza di questo scontro seguita al tramonto negli anni 90 dei grossi movimenti insorgenti latino-americani, la scommessa di molti movimenti sociali del continente di sostenere elettoralmente opzioni che, per quanto riformiste, garantiscono comunque l’agibilità politica 

minima

 necessaria per organizzarsi e far avanzare le proprie rivendicazioni non va sottovalutata, né liquidata come puro elettoralismo. I fuochi d’artificio esplosi dalle favelas di Rio de Janeiro dopo l’annuncio della vittoria di Lula sono la gioia di chi sa che, da oggi, i 

milicianos

 del clan Bolsonaro avranno qualche difficoltà in più ad entrare e sparare a vista su qualsiasi cosa si muova. L’esperienza delle mobilitazioni e dei movimenti che da decenni lottano in Brasile ha bisogno di spazi di elaborazione, formazione e avanzamento politico: garantire questi spazi, oltre a saperli sfruttare, sarà centrale per trasformare la disponibilità dei movimenti sociali brasiliani ad appoggiare Lula in una forza politica conflittuale ed organizzata, capace di contare al di fuori delle urne e di sostenere l’urto contro l’estrema destra latinoamericana e l’imperialismo statunitense e l’agenda che essi continueranno spietatamente ad imporre al continente.

author: Amy Romer, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: After a ‘mind-blowing’ encounter at a ‘New York’ museum, a Sḵwx̱wú7mesh weaving returns home
content:
On Sept. 14, a ceremony at the Museum of North Vancouver welcomed a tumpline from Sen̓áḵw back to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory. The tumpline was collected in 1898 during the Jesup North Pacific Expedition. Photo by Alison Boulier 




Sḵwx̱wú7mesh master weaver Chief Janice George had visited New York’s American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) before.




George and her husband, Buddy Joseph, had previously travelled to the museum to examine their collection of Coast Salish weavings.




But when the couple returned in 2024, to research an exhibition George was co-curating at the Burke Museum in “Seattle,” they were surprised to be shown something they hadn’t seen during prior visits.

Among the pieces brought out for them to view was a tumpline — a woven belt used to carry heavy loads. It was beautiful, she remembers thinking, and she admired its master craftsmanship as Joseph searched the museum’s records for information about its origins.

And then he found it. The tumpline was from Sen̓áḵw, the ancient Sḵwx̱wú7mesh village currently being 

reimagined

 for 21st century living — and where George was working as a cultural advisor at the time.

“It was just mind-blowing,” George said.




George describes the tumpline as a “woven jewel,” pointing to the fineness of the wool, its vivid colours and the care taken with every detail.




She experiences the tumpline not just as a master weaver, but as a hereditary chief and curator. “It makes me feel emotional to even think about it,” she said.

Rushing to find somewhere to connect the call with her colleagues, she said she felt like the encounter was a message from the ancestors, affirming that she and Joseph were on the right path. 




She excitedly shared what she found — and began working to bring the tumpline back to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh.

At 73 and 69, respectively, George and Joseph have spent years travelling to museums and collections across the world in search of Sḵwx̱wú7mesh weavings. “My relatives call us teenagers because we’re always on the run,” she laughed.

The more belongings the couple are able to locate and bring home, the more future generations can learn from the knowledge, histories and cultural practices carried within them.

“The energy comes with the work,” George said, recalling her husband’s words. “This is work that we’re meant to do.”




After a long journey home, the tumpline is now on temporary display in George’s latest exhibition, 

Gifts to be shared, protected and carried forward

, at the Museum of North Vancouver (MONOVA) until March 2027. But while its return to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory marks a significant milestone, what happens to the weaving after the exhibition closes remains uncertain.




The Sen̓áḵw tumpline, a woven strap traditionally used to carry baskets of harvested foods, is on display at the Museum of North Vancouver until March 2027. Photo by Alison Boulier




‘It’s unlike anything we’ve seen before’




A tumpline is a long, narrow woven strap used to carry bundles of harvested foods, such as berries, herbs or seafood.




Tied to either side of a basket, the strap rested across the forehead, allowing the wearer to carry the load on their back. Among Sḵwx̱wú7mesh and other Coast Salish peoples, women often made and used tumplines to carry whatever they gathered.




The Sen̓áḵw tumpline was recorded in the AMNH collection in 1898, during the Jesup North Pacific Expedition. Led by anthropologist Franz Boas, the expedition collected Indigenous belongings across the North Pacific region, reflecting a colonial-era approach to studying Indigenous peoples and their cultures.

Visible repairs suggest the tumpline had already been used for some time before it entered the museum’s collection, potentially dating it to the early 19th century or earlier, said George.




Master weaver and hereditary chief Janice George and her husband, Buddy Joseph admire the Sen̓áḵw tumpline during its welcome ceremony at the Museum of North Vancouver on Sept. 14. Photo by Alison Boulier




George believes it was woven from mountain goat wool, possibly spun with hair from woolly dogs that Sḵwx̱wú7mesh and other Coast Salish peoples bred for their fibre. The practice dates back at least 5,000 years, but eventually disappeared as colonialism disrupted Coast Salish communities and cultural traditions.

Depending on when the tumpline was made, its wool may have been dyed with natural materials such as alder or combined with red yarn unravelled from commercially made garments.




“It’s unlike anything we’ve seen before,” said George, who was struck by the fineness of the wool, the vivid colours and the intricate braiding at the ends, where the strap would have been tied to the basket. She had the tumpline mounted in the exhibit so visitors could appreciate the artistry.

“You can tell how much care went into making it,” she said. Women often made tumplines for their own use, said George. “So they are designs you know they really love.”

For Zoe Mackoff de Miranda, MONOVA’s director, having the tumpline on loan from New York is “a pretty big deal.”

She doubts the loan would have happened without George’s involvement. “It’s here because of Chief Janice,” she said.

But securing the loan took persistence. George requested the tumpline for 

Woven in Wool

, the exhibition she co-curated at the Burke Museum in “Seattle”, which ran from September 2025 to August 2026.

George hoped that getting the tumpline to Seattle would bring it closer to home — and eventually to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory. With the Burke and MONOVA backing the request, she asked the AMNH to extend the loan to “North Vancouver.” The museum initially refused, citing concerns about the tumpline’s fragility and the risks of further travel.




So George wrote a letter explaining what it would mean for her community to see the weaving returned, even temporarily, to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh lands. She wanted local weavers to be able to study the work of their ancestors and take pride in its intricacy.




Eventually, the museum agreed.




Zoe Mackoff de Miranda, director of the Museum of North Vancouver, attends a ceremony welcoming the Sen̓áḵw tumpline to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory on Sept. 14. Photo by Alison Boulier




It’s unclear whether AMNH ever displayed the tumpline publicly. Only a small fraction of a museum’s collection is typically on display at any given time, Mackoff de Miranda said. Some objects may never be exhibited, either because they don’t fit a particular exhibition or because the collection is simply too vast.

The New York museum holds more than 30 million items, according to its 

website

, describing them as “one of the most important scientific collections in the world.”

The records accompanying Indigenous belongings collected during the Jesup expedition were not always detailed. The expedition, funded by Morris K. Jesup, then president of the museum, amassed cultural belongings from Indigenous communities across the North Pacific, but the surviving documentation leaves gaps in the histories of individual pieces.




“It depended on who wrote it and who collected it,” said George. And for women’s crafted belongings, even less information was gathered.




“That’s kind of the sad part of it,” George said. “But we do the best we can to make sure everybody feels ownership for it.” 




George understands how precious it is to spend time with the belongings of her ancestors, particularly one as unique as the Sen̓áḵw tumpline. 







Chief Janice George speaks at a Sept. 14 ceremony welcoming the Sen̓áḵw tumpline to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory. She believes bringing ancestral belongings home is vital to passing cultural knowledge on to future generations. Photos by Alison Boulier




For George, the tumpline carries deeper significance after generations of First Nations people endured the residential “school” system and what she describes as “legislated poverty.” Its return to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory, even temporarily, feels like a gift from the ancestors.




“They reveal themselves when they think the time is right,” she said. 




Finding the Sen̓áḵw tumpline at the museum just minutes before a meeting about the artwork for the new Sen̓áḵw village was one of those moments. “It’s all just pretty amazing,” said George. 




‘It’s why I do this work’




At a ceremony at MONOVA on Sept. 14, Sḵwx̱wú7mesh weavers and singers gathered to welcome the tumpline back to the territory.




Peter Baker, director of Territory and Culture Services at Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw, was also in attendance. The exhibition marks the first time the department has funded a museum exhibition. According to Mackoff de Miranda, that decision reflects a growing interest in connecting language, culture and territory in ways that reach the broader community.




“He could see what it meant to the people,” said George. “Seeing how everybody felt so connected and proud and so emotional about having our ancestors’ work here. It’s why I do this work.”




IndigiNews reached out to Baker, but did not receive a response in time for publication.




Community members gather with the Sen̓áḵw tumpline during a ceremony welcoming the ancestral weaving back to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory. Photo by Alison Boulier




Mackoff de Miranda doubts the loan would have happened without George’s persistence. But she also credits MONOVA’s Class A exhibition space, which meets strict climate-control standards that allow museums to borrow fragile objects from other collections.




Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw doesn’t have its own Class A facility, Mackoff de Miranda said, making collaborations with institutions like MONOVA essential piece of the puzzle in bringing cultural belongings home.




“We would definitely have to have proper storage and display,” said George.




George hopes to bring more belongings back to the territory through what she describes as a “repatriation taskforce” that she’ll lead for the nation.




“We’re going to be looking at belongings all around the world,” she said.




As a hereditary chief, George sees this work as “the most important thing” she can do. She said she may eventually need to step back from, or delegate, other responsibilities to focus on bringing belongings home.




Mackoff de Miranda said the museum is “largely supportive of the concept of belongings returning to where they came from.” But under the terms of its loan to MONOVA, the tumpline is due to return to the AMNH in March 2027.




MONOVA is currently drafting a policy to guide the return of belongings in its collection. The policy will set out how the museum should respond when communities request a belonging, as well as how it can proactively identify objects in its collection that have no direct connection to “North Vancouver” and may be better held elsewhere.




Mackoff de Miranda hopes the policy will be finalized and made public in 2027.




George and Joseph are already putting what they learn from the tumpline into practice. The pair have been commissioned to create a triptych of the tumpline for sméṅhem (Tower Two) at Sen̓áḵw, adapting the ancestral design into a larger-scale weaving for a contemporary setting.




Studying the original helps them understand how its maker structured the design — knowledge George said is invaluable for weavers today.




tl’eltl’élnup (Tower One, right) and sméṅhem (Tower Two, left) at Sen̓áḵw, where Janice George and Buddy Joseph have been commissioned to create a triptych replicating the tumpline for display in Tower Two. Photo by Amy Romer




When she and Joseph began teaching, many of the older weavers had passed away. They had to work out how to recreate designs without the guidance of those who had made them, a process George describes as “reverse engineering.”




Now, she hopes the next generation won’t have to do the same.




“Buddy and I both come from leadership families, and understand that it is our responsibility to help the next generation,” she said. 




Now, she sees young people taking up that work themselves. Their interest in weaving and cultural knowledge gives her hope that future generations won’t have to piece together what was lost.




“I feel like it’s such a cultural renaissance happening right now with our people,” she said. “I feel so positive about the future.”




The post 

After a ‘mind-blowing’ encounter at a ‘New York’ museum, a Sḵwx̱wú7mesh weaving returns home

 appeared first on 

Indiginews

.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El Gobierno expulsó a la científica que detectó la presencia de agroquímicos en personas en Argentina
content:
El Consejo Directivo del INTA armó una causa y exoneró finalmente a Virginia Aparicio, investigadora del proyecto SPRINT que estudió la presencia de agroquímicos en 86% de personas, en ambiente y especies, en Argentina.




Virginia Aparicio, ingeniera agrónoma, doctora en Ciencias Agrarias e investigadora del INTA.




Finalmente, el Consejo Directivo del INTA exoneró este lunes a Virginia Aparicio, la investigadora de la Unidad Integrada Balcarce que coordinó en la Argentina el proyecto SPRINT y midió residuos de agroquímicos en el ambiente y en el cuerpo de voluntarios.




Es la sanción más grave que prevé el empleo público nacional y la deja fuera del INTA y del sector público.




La medida figura en la resolución 366 del organismo, fechada este mismo lunes, y basada en lo tratado en la reunión del 27 de agosto por la Comisión Directiva del organismo, que dio por concluido el sumario abierto en diciembre de 2023.




Su artículo 11 dispone textualmente: “Aplícase a la agente Virginia Carolina APARICIO (Legajo N° 17.205) la sanción de EXONERACIÓN por la violación comprobada de las prohibiciones del artículo 24, incisos e) e i)” de la ley marco de empleo público.




De acuerdo a la resolución, el inciso e) prohíbe usar las facultades del cargo para fines ajenos a la función, y el Consejo Directivo lo aplica a la relación de Aparicio con José Luis Costa, un investigador retirado del INTA.




Según la resolución, “COSTA integraba el grupo familiar de APARICIO en calidad de conviviente”, algo que el organismo da por probado con las declaraciones juradas del legajo de la investigadora, que registran una unión de hecho desde septiembre de 2005.




La causa armada por el INTA contra Aparicio




El texto sostiene que la coordinadora “empleó sus prerrogativas de coordinación para conferir a su conviviente una posición particular de participación, conducción fáctica e inspección de datos reservados, sin autorización del INTA, sin formalización por el órgano decisor del Consorcio ni exteriorización específica del conflicto que permitiera su evaluación independiente”.




Agrega que Costa “se encontraba retirado del INTA y carecía de vínculo institucional vigente”, aunque el documento de información entregado a los voluntarios lo incluía, junto con Aparicio y otro investigador del equipo, entre las personas habilitadas para inspeccionar datos incluso sin codificar.




Virginia Aparicio recibió una notificación de la Dirección General del INTA en 2023, en la que le prohibían difundir los resultados de la investigación SPRINT.




Uso indebido del patrimonio, la otra excusa del INTA




También, el inciso i) castiga el uso indebido del patrimonio estatal y se apoya en el manejo de los fondos europeos, que ingresaron a la contabilidad del INTA. La resolución consigna ingresos por 5.661.483,83 pesos, egresos por 5.527.359,58 y un saldo de 134.124,25. Entre ellos menciona un pago a World Courier de 1.688.445,82 pesos en julio de 2022 por el envío de muestras a los Países Bajos, unos 13.122,95 euros según la cotización del Banco Central.




El propio Consejo Directivo aclara que esos importes no pueden identificarse “por sí solos, con un perjuicio fiscal equivalente, cuya existencia y cuantía no han sido objeto en este procedimiento de una determinación fundada”.




Explica que igual corresponde sancionar porque la prohibición “comprende la utilización indebida de bienes y recursos públicos como supuesto autónomo, sin requerir necesariamente la producción de un perjuicio fiscal, su apropiación, obtención de un beneficio personal o destino a fines particulares”.




Envío de muestras a Holanda




La decisión de centralizar los análisis en el exterior, concluye, fue “adoptada e impulsada por la sumariada APARICIO sin contar con la autorización institucional exigible”. Reconoce además la “ausencia de beneficio económico acreditado” y de antecedentes disciplinarios, pero afirma que esas circunstancias “no permiten atenuar la relevancia de la falta cometida”.




La lista de reproches es más larga. El Consejo Directivo le atribuye haber reemplazado al comité de ética previsto en el acuerdo de subvención por el del Programa Temático Interdisciplinario en Bioética de la Universidad Nacional de Mar del Plata, sin pasar por los órganos del INTA. Señala diferencias entre el protocolo, que preveía 72 participantes repartidos en tres grupos de 24, y la presentación de junio de 2023, que habla de 20 productores, 28 vecinos y 25 consumidores.




Aparicio y la nulidad del sumario




Aparicio había planteado la nulidad del sumario, además de indefensión y trato discriminatorio. El Consejo Directivo rechazó el pedido “por no verificarse el incumplimiento del procedimiento y haberse garantizado el ejercicio de la defensa con asistencia letrada”. También respondió al argumento de que la coordinadora general del consorcio, Violette Geissen, conocía y avalaba el esquema: ese conocimiento o conformidad operativa, dice, “resultaban insuficientes para formalizar esas decisiones”.




La resolución incluye además un párrafo sobre los resultados. Cita un documento del propio proyecto SPRINT (el entregable D2.4, publicado el 28 de febrero de 2023), según el cual “ninguna de las ingestas calculadas superó la ingesta diaria admisible de referencia en los grupos estudiados” de glifosato. Agrega que los autores consideraron que los niveles estimados “no deberían representar un riesgo potencial para la salud según ese criterio”, y que advirtieron que los datos de salud disponibles no eran adecuados para un análisis epidemiológico.







#Ahora El #INTA acaba de confirmar la expulsión del organismo de la científica #VirginiaAparicio por investigar los efectos del uso de agroquímicos en personas, y en el ambiente. Detectó fertilizantes prohibidos en 86% de personas, en especies y cursos de agua. La echaron. https://t.co/dwAqvQJTHf




— Periferia (@periferiacts) 

October 26, 2026







Los otros agentes implicados en la exoneración




El sumario alcanzó a otros trece agentes. El director de la EEA Balcarce, Facundo Quiroz, recibió quince días de suspensión, y Eduardo De Gerónimo, veinticinco. Los demás quedaron eximidos, entre ellos Horacio Berger, que había sido vinculado en calidad de imputado y que días atrás, como director del Centro Regional Buenos Aires Sur, le escribió al Concejo Deliberante de Balcarce para marcar distancia del trabajo de Aparicio.




La resolución ordena además comunicar los hechos a la Oficina Anticorrupción “ante la eventual configuración de delitos de acción pública” y pide a la Dirección Nacional un informe sobre la liquidación del acuerdo de subvención “a efectos de determinar si resulta procedente la apertura de un procedimiento de responsabilidad patrimonial”.




Un conflicto que viene de 2023




El conflicto viene de lejos. El INTA aprobó su participación en SPRINT, financiado por el programa Horizonte 2020 de la Unión Europea y coordinado por la Universidad de Wageningen, en mayo de 2020. El 15 de junio de 2023 le ordenó a Aparicio suspender la reunión en la que iba a presentar los datos, una medida que la resolución define hoy como “diligencias preventivas”.




El 7 de diciembre de 2023 el Consejo Directivo dispuso la salida del proyecto (Resolución 1081) y ese mismo día ordenó el sumario (Resolución 1082).




El 15 de octubre presentó, a título personal, los resultados de sus mediciones en el Concejo Deliberante de Balcarce. En paralelo, APINTA y ATE Conicet impulsaban un formulario con la consigna “No a la exoneración de Virginia Aparicio”.




El INTA difundió además un comunicado titulado “Resolución del Consejo Directivo del INTA sobre el Proyecto SPRINT”, en el que no figura el nombre de la investigadora. Dice que el organismo “reafirma su compromiso con la evidencia confiable, el respeto riguroso a los protocolos científicos, éticos y administrativos”. Sostiene que “la respuesta institucional es fortalecer la ciencia, con inversión en equipamiento y capacidades analíticas para generar evidencia confiable”.







Fuente: 

https://periferia.com.ar/politica-cientifica/el-gobierno-expulso-a-la-cientifica-que-detecto-la-presencia-de-agroquimicos-en-personas-en-argentina/




La entrada 

El Gobierno expulsó a la científica que detectó la presencia de agroquímicos en personas en Argentina

 se publicó primero en 

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

author: Chris Walker
title: Alaska Officials Seek Dismissal of DOJ Suit Aiming to Block Election Results
content:
Officials have “taken significant steps to distinguish” two candidates with the same name on the ballot, they said.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On Monday, Alaska election officials filed a motion calling for the “immediate” dismissal of a lawsuit, brought forward last week by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), that seeks to invalidate the state’s U.S. Senate race if the Republican candidate loses.

The race features three main candidates. Democrat Mary Peltola is neck and neck in polls with incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R). Meanwhile, a third candidate, also named Dan Sullivan, is running as an independent.

Although the latter Sullivan maintains he is running a legitimate campaign, Alaska officials alleged that he was trying to cause confusion among voters and initially kept him off the ballot. However, the independent sued the state, and won the right to be included in the election after the state Supreme Court found that his candidacy was proper and legal.

Despite the independent already appearing on the primary election ballot and early voting for the general election already starting, the DOJ filed a lawsuit last Thursday, demanding that the state refuse to certify the results if the incumbent Sullivan loses (most likely to Peltola).

“It is vital that Defendants not certify any election result that may be impacted by voter confusion,” the DOJ lawsuit said, adding that one of the conditions demonstrating the outcome could have been “impacted by voter confusion” is if “Senator Sullivan does not win the election.”

Democrats, including Peltola, responded to the suit by requesting it be fast-tracked and, eventually, for a judge to deem it unfounded, especially since elections are largely meant to be administered by the states without federal interference. Shortly after U.S. District Court Judge Sharon Gleason approved fast-tracking the motion, Alaska election officials filed their own paperwork with the court, asking for the DOJ lawsuit to be dismissed outright.

The filing was submitted jointly by Carol Beecher, director of the Division of Elections, and the Elections Boards of the State of Alaska, as well as the State Ballot Counting Review Board for the state, collectively calling themselves “the Division.” The officials recognized the situation was a rare one, but argued that shouldn’t allow the federal government to preemptively intervene in the race’s outcome.

“Although Alaska faces an unusual situation in which two candidates for U.S. Senator share a first and last name, the Division has taken significant steps to distinguish them on the ballot so that voters can easily determine which candidate is which,” the Division’s filing stated, noting that there is a “lack of evidence of any problems (or indeed, any legal cause of action)” described in the DOJ’s lawsuit.

The federal government also “lacks authority to intervene in state elections at all, much less in support of a favored candidate,” the filing said.

The Division pointed out that it has taken steps to minimize confusion among voters, including differentiating the two Sullivans on the ballot by listing one as the incumbent Republican senator, and the other as the independent challenger. Both men also have their middle initials included to alert voters to the fact that they are different candidates.

Beyond those actions, the Division noted that Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system will ensure voters have the opportunity to pick both Sullivans, if one of the choices is their true preference over Peltola.

“If any Sullivan-supporting voter remains uncertain which Sullivan is which despite this clear differentiation on the ballot, the voter can ask for assistance from others or look up information about the candidates using a smart phone or an election pamphlet,” the Division stated. “And if the voter is still uncertain, Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system provides another solution: the voter can rank the Sullivans as his first and second choices. That way, if the voter’s first-ranked Sullivan is eliminated, his vote would transfer to the other Sullivan.”

“The Court should promptly dismiss the complaint with prejudice so that Alaska can proceed to administer its elections consistent with state and federal law and without unwarranted interference by the United States,” the Division’s filing concluded.

Beyond the unprecedented nature of preemptively calling for an election result to be dismissed, the DOJ’s filing was unusual in that President Donald Trump ordered it to happen. In previous years, the DOJ has tried to appear, at the very least, nominally independent from the president in its decision making process for filing lawsuits or criminally charging people, but that practice has been abandoned under this administration.

“I’m the one that said do it,” Trump bragged to reporters last week, regarding who decided to file the lawsuit against the state.

Answering questions about the lawsuit and other actions his department has taken, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated that he wouldn’t rule out disrupting the results of other states’ electoral contests.

“It is not DOJ’s intention to, and it’s never our intention to, improperly interfere with elections or the state confirmation process or certification process,” Blanche told reporters on Thursday, but added the department could take such actions in a “doomsday scenario.”

“To say that there’s no circumstances that we would ever do that…of course, I’m not going to say that,” Blanche said.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

title: At least 87 people executed in Iran in 20 days
content:
The wave of executions in Iran continues. According to the “No Execution Tuesdays” campaign, at least 87 people have been executed in just 20 days. Death sentences have also reportedly been handed down to numerous other prisoners. The protest movement, which has been campaigning against the death penalty and the Iranian regime’s execution practices for more than two and a half years, is now continuing its actions in 66 prisons. On Tuesday, the campaign entered its 144th week.




In a statement, participants warned of the scale of state repression as hundreds, possibly even thousands, of prisoners in Iran are awaiting execution. “The regime uses the death penalty not only to kill people but also to spread fear throughout society and silence opposition voices. Each execution also leaves families in deep grief.”




The campaign highlighted the large number of executions carried out during the Iranian month of Mehr, which lasted from September 22 to October 19. According to the campaign, this development demonstrates how systematically the regime uses the death penalty as a tool of intimidation. “Yet history has shown that no gallows can tear the desire for freedom and equality from people’s hearts. No repression can silence forever the voices of those who fight for their rights,” the statement said.




The prisoners appealed to human rights organizations, political and trade union activists, relatives of those sentenced to death, and all democratic forces to strengthen their solidarity. They stressed that the names of those facing execution must not be forgotten through silence and indifference. The campaign called for the public condemnation of all death sentences, an immediate halt to ongoing executions, and an expansion of the collective struggle for the complete abolition of the death penalty in Iran.

author: Unknown
title: Convicted rapist Musa Orhan acquitted of charge of inciting suicide
content:
Turkish former non-commissioned officer Musa Orhan, who was sentenced to ten years in prison for raping 18-year-old Kurdish woman İpek Er, has been acquitted in a separate criminal case. On October 22, a court in Batman ruled that it could not be proven that Orhan had incited the young woman to take her own life. The acquittal came despite her suicide note, incriminating witness testimony, and his previous conviction for serious sexual violence. Orhan remains free and has yet to begin serving his prison sentence.




The case of İpek Er sparked outrage far beyond Kurdistan in 2020 and became a symbol of impunity for sexual violence committed by uniformed state personnel. Women’s organizations and the Kurdish women’s movement protested against Orhan’s repeated release from custody and the Turkish judiciary’s handling of the young woman’s case. Even his subsequent conviction did not change the fact that the former soldier remained free.













İpek Er reported being held captive and raped




İpek Er had met Musa Orhan online. In the suicide note she later left behind, she described how the professional soldier, who was stationed in the district of Beşiri at the time, had held her captive for several days, drugged her, and raped her. On July 7, 2020, she filed a criminal complaint with the public prosecutor’s office in the neighboring province of Siirt. Nine days later, the 18-year-old girl attempted suicide and was hospitalized with life-threatening injuries. After 34 days, she died on August 18, 2020. Her suicide note and statements from medical personnel became key pieces of evidence. İpek Er had alerted the doctors and nurses who first examined her after her admission to the violence she had suffered, telling them, “Musa has destroyed me.”




Sentenced to ten years in prison, yet still free




The Turkish judiciary’s handling of Orhan following the disclosure of the rape sparked widespread protests. He was initially detained on July 16, 2020, but was released under judicial supervision after questioning. It was only after İpek Er’s death and amid growing public outrage that he was arrested again on August 19 and subsequently placed in pretrial detention. Around a week later, Orhan was released from custody once more at his lawyer’s request. His dismissal from public service also came only after a decision by the High Disciplinary Board of the Turkish Ministry of Interior. He was subsequently expelled from the Gendarmerie.




In December 2021, a criminal court in Siirt sentenced Orhan to twelve years in prison for aggravated sexual assault. The sentence was reduced to ten years under Article 62 of the Turkish Penal Code, which provides for discretionary sentence reductions. Despite the conviction, the court declined to order his detention and imposed only a travel ban. The regional appeals court in Diyarbakır later upheld the prison sentence by a majority decision. One judge even argued for an acquittal in a dissenting opinion. The Diyarbakır Bar Association’s Women’s Rights Center’s request for a harsher sentence was rejected.




Court finds evidence insufficient




The proceedings that have now concluded concerned whether Orhan could also be held criminally responsible for İpek Er’s suicide. In its closing arguments, the prosecution had requested a conviction for inciting suicide. However, the court concluded that there was no concrete evidence beyond reasonable doubt that Orhan had incited İpek Er to take her own life, encouraged her to do so, or reinforced her decision. It invoked the principle of criminal law that any doubt must be resolved in favor of the defendant.




The court therefore did not consider Orhan’s previous rape conviction, İpek Er’s suicide note, or her statements to hospital staff sufficient grounds for establishing additional criminal liability. The acquittal relates exclusively to the charge of inciting suicide and does not overturn his earlier conviction for sexual violence.




Lawyers for the victim’s family denied time to respond




The court’s handling of the verdict also raises questions. The lawyers representing the victim’s family had requested permission to respond in writing to the prosecution’s closing arguments. The court denied their request for additional time and immediately issued its acquittal. The written reasoning for the verdict was entered into the Turkish judicial system the very next day, October 23. At the same time, the court lifted the travel ban imposed on Orhan in the proceedings concerning the charge of inciting suicide.
