title: Art Basel, la foire du Pillage
content:
« L'époque contemporaine est finie (…). Autant en finir aussi avec les dîners de gala » La foire internationale du Grand Palais « Art Basel », supposée rassembler les nouvelles « scènes artistiques émergentes », a, pour la première fois de son histoire, été l'objet d'un véritable happening, d'une véritable émergence, le 24 octobre dernier : un appel à « reprendre le Palais », signé « Pillage de classe ». Il ne s'en est pas fallu davantage pour que les organisateurs spéculent sur l'irruption d'un peu de réel. La galerie fut suffisamment épatée pour fermer pendant trois jours. Spéculera bien qui spéculera le dernier !




Comme tous les ans à Paris, Art Basel – la foire internationale d'art contemporain – devait se dérouler la semaine dernière au Grand Palais dans un bêlement sédatif. Une foire préparée bien en avance pour laquelle il valait mieux ne pas se tromper, vu les prix de location astronomiques des stands à plusieurs dizaines de milliers de dollars. Depuis quelques jours, professionnels et pique-assiettes étaient dans les starting-blocks pour enchaîner jusqu'au dimanche soir les soirées en plastique dans des clubs en toc, pour courir les événements du off (en concurrence les uns contre les autres), et pour subir les programmes de discussion assommants habituels (« les nouvelles scènes émergentes »). Tout aurait pu continuer tranquillement jusqu'à dimanche. C'était sans compter l'intrusion d'un phénomène très concret au cœur de la machinerie d'Art Basel : celui du mouvement en cours.




Mardi soir, premier coup de semonce. Alors que des ultra-riches s'agglutinaient à la preview, le compte Instagram Documentations.art publiait un appel à « reprendre le Palais le 24 octobre » signé d'un collectif : Pillage de classe. Le 24 octobre, soit le jour de l'acte II du mouvement social et insurrectionnel en cours. Le post, liké par milliers et relayé par la presse bourgeoise fut interprété comme une invitation à piller la foire. Menace symbolique ou réelle, toujours est-il que des appels à se rassembler aux abords du Palais pour déborder l'appareil sécuritaire mis en place pour le protéger commencèrent à se répandre.







 

 










Pour enfoncer un peu plus le clou, et prouver aux organisateurs que l'énorme dispositif de sécurité mis en place était incapable d'empêcher les intrusions – et, donc, que la foire ne serait pas protégée le 24 octobre en cas de débordement –, des actions sont organisées le jeudi 22 lors du vernissage publique : distribution de vrais-faux programmes détournant le graphisme d'Art Basel, collage d'affiches dans les toilettes dénonçant « la foire du pillage », déploiement d'une banderole dénonçant la collusion du marché de l'art et de l'armement…




Jeudi, la rumeur est confirmée : Art Basel fermera définitivement ses portes dès le vendredi soir. Plus de temps à perdre. Les transporteurs et les régisseurs sont rappelés en 4

e

 vitesse pour décrocher. Il faut changer les billets de train et d'avion… Malgré le vernissage en cours, l'humeur en berne et le visage morose de certain

·

es galeristes trahissent la fuite de Varennes qui s'organise au même moment en toute discrétion.




Sans surprise, une partie du monde de l'art tente de décrédibiliser cette victoire éclatante d'une mobilisation collective, révélant une fois de plus la posture contre-insurrectionnelle qui échoit à ce secteur. Il était de bon ton chez les professionnels de minimiser l'action, affirmant que les plus grosses transactions ayant eu lieu dès mardi soir, la fermeture anticipée du week-end n'aurait aucun impact sur le marché de l'art. Et qu'a contrario, en contraignant la foire à fermer ce week-end, nous pénalisions le « grand » public qui avait payé ses billets (47 euros !) et les « petites » galeries courageuses qui faisaient « un travail formidable de prospection pour soutenir de nouvelles pratiques ». Nous n'avons que faire des leçons des anti-communistes de l'art, qu'elles soient morales ou stratégiques !




La fermeture du week-end est une victoire qui résulte de la force tactique conférée par la puissance des mobilisations débordantes qui ont souvent lieu le week-end depuis les Gilets Jaunes. Certains semblent avoir des leçons à nous donner. Les mêmes qui nous demandent pourquoi ne pas avoir organisé un rassemblement le mardi soir, sont ceux qui nous accusent aussi d'approximations. Les journalistes du Monde, du Figaro, les professionnel

·

les de l'art, vous vous plaigniez d'un manque de précisions. Et nous vous demandons : Qu'avez-vous à cacher derrière vos œuvres d'art ? Vos cours si bien révisés de défiscalisation ? Votre compromission avec les business les plus sales ? Ou bien nous avions mal compris et vous étiez prêts à piller le Palais dès le mardi ? Appelez-nous la prochaine fois. 







 

 










Quoi qu'il en soit, l'impact financier de cette mobilisation sur l'ensemble de la foire a été considérable. Il touche en premier lieu les petites et moyennes galeries – plus fragiles, moins résilientes –, et ce n'est pas notre affaire. D'un point de vue systémique, ce sont ces petites galeries qui apportent le vernis progressiste dont l'art a besoin de se parer. Elles ont une fonction structurelle intégrative : ce sont elles qui repèrent les nouveaux artistes, les nouvelles formes, les nouvelles pratiques pour les transformer en marchandises et les intégrer à l'ensemble du système capitaliste. les intégrer a l'ensemble du système capitaliste. Pour autant, les mégas galeries auraient-elles couru le risque de voir leurs booths pillés ? Ce n'est pas nous qui regretterons que les petites galeries n'ait pas pu vendre ce weekend. Nous ne faisons pas de distinction morale entre bonnes et mauvaises galeries, gros ou petits commerçants au sein d'Art Basel. Chacune d'elle participe d'un système que nous souhaitons abolir, et non réformer ! 







 

 







Programme distribué devant la foire :




Nous nous sommes glissé-es dans la brèche laissées par la mise en concurrence des nombreuses entreprises de sous-traitants à qui reviennent les missions de sécurité, d'accueil, de médiation et nous avons pris une mission de distribution d'un tract au public de la foire. « Art Basel, vous voulez le programme d'Art Basel ? »




Nous serions en droit de questionner l'intérêt stratégique d'attaquer une foire telle qu'Art Basel. Pourquoi perdre son temps en d'aussi vaines occupations alors qu'il suffirait juste de de s'en détourner ? Nos modes de sociabilisation et d'action n'ont pas besoin de ceux du monde de l'art pour s'épanouir. Nous savons en revanche pourquoi il existe, ce rendez-vous mondial qui rassemble inlassablement, année après année, artistes, galeristes, curateurs, public, collectionneurs, agents, commissaires-priseurs, etc.. Et nous connaissons le rôle qu'il a pris au sein du système capitaliste impérialiste. En 2025, la pièce la plus chère s'y est vendue à 23 millions d'euros. Les quelques acheteurs (les fameux 1 %) y font leurs emplettes dans les conditions les plus opaques possibles, et le tout financé grâce à l'enchâssement obscur de puissants fonds d'investissement et holdings états-uniennes (Art Basel by MCH by Lupa Systems).




Pendant ce temps, dans des quartiers et des lycées qui auraient besoin d'argent public, la jeunesse a lancé un puissant mouvement social. Le 17 octobre, ils ont été rejoints par toutes celles et ceux qui dénoncent l'augmentation indécente du coût de la vie et la captation des richesses par quelques-uns. Certain

·

es brisent courageusement les vitrines de Chanel au risque de leur vie et de la répression judiciaire. L'opulence, le style de vie, le luxe, ils prennent tout ce qu'ART BASEL et son monde présentent comme désirable. Et la presse bourgeoise appelle cela du pillage.




Comment s'appelle ce que fait ART BASEL ?




Un véritable pillage organisé ! Les ultra-riches s'y retrouvent pour acheter, vendre et spéculer sur des œuvres devenues des actifs financiers. À ce marché s'ajoutent les dispositifs de mécénat et les fondations privées, qui permettent aux grandes fortunes et aux entreprises de bénéficier d'avantages fiscaux considérables, tout en exerçant une influence sur la production et la consécration artistiques. Autant de recettes auxquelles les États renoncent, voyant de potentielles richesses publiques s'évanouir dans des manœuvres d'optimisation fiscale, grâce à l'entremise de fondations ou autres sociétés-écrans, alors qu'on entend sans cesse répéter que cet argent manque cruellement pour nos besoins élémentaires. La liste des cadeaux faits aux plus privilégiés s'allonge chaque fois qu'on se penche sur elle (retrait de l'ISF, refus de la taxe Zucman, augmentation du seuil de la taxation sur l'héritage...).




Les œuvres couvrent la violence de classe. Elles sont des « valeurs refuges » pour les bourgeois dans des moments où la spéculation est moins efficace ailleurs. Pour ne rien voir, tout doit briller ! D'ailleurs personne ne veut savoir que James Murdoch, via sa holding Lupa Systems, premier actionnaire de l'organisateur d'ART BASEL (MCH), a également un fonds « défense », étroitement lié au complexe militaire américain et dont le directeur a proposé une réforme ouvrant davantage le ministère de la défense des États-Unis aux géants de la tech.




ART BASEL incarne les deux faces d'une même bourgeoisie transnationale qui assure son hégémonie culturelle grâce aux conditions militaires et politiques de son enrichissement – au prix, s'il le faut, d'un génocide en Palestine.




Les foires d'art contemporain veulent se donner bonne conscience, et on aime citer Debord, Butler, Federici, Fanon et le "décolonial". Mais quand les artistes et les étudiant

·

es demandent une sécurité sociale de la culture et un salaire étudiant, le marché de l'art et son monde les traite de casseurs.




L'époque contemporaine est finie : son système capitaliste aussi. Commençons par en finir avec les dîners de gala.




Le Grand Palais et les fantômes coloniaux qui le hantent doivent disparaître en même temps que les projets qu'il accueille. À l'instar des enseignes du grand luxe de la rue Saint-Honorée, saccagées lors de l'insurrection du 17 octobre, nous avons contraint la vitrine somptuaire de l'art contemporain et du capitalisme à baisser précipitamment le rideau ! Et nous recommencerons, autant de fois qu'il le faut.

title: Families in Washokani Camp stage protest: We want to return to our homes before winter
content:
Families who were forcibly displaced from Serêkaniyê and Til Temir and are living in Washokani Camp staged a protest today. Blocking the Til Temir–Hesekê road, the families demanded to return to their homes as soon as possible.




The protesters stated that they were facing numerous difficulties in the camp and that no organization was providing them with assistance anymore.




Camp resident Mûsa Mihemed from the village of El Menacîr, said that no organization was helping them anymore and that their living conditions were poor. He explained that winter was approaching and that when it rained, water poured through their torn tents, leaving them exposed to the rain. He demanded that they be enabled to return to their homes as soon as possible.




Another resident of the camp, Cabir Ebdulrehman, said: “I am from the village of El Kêf in Til Temir. We are organizing protests because we want to return to our homes as soon as possible. Our situation is difficult, theft has increased, there is chaos, and we have no means of making a living. We want the return convoys to include all displaced people.”




Mihemed Ebdulrehman, from the village of El Kinêhir in Til Temir, stated: “The return convoys only include people from certain areas. We want to return to our village before winter arrives.”

title: 25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity
content:
25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together different political currents and strengthen resistance against the rise of right-wing and fascist forces, imperialist war policies, and state repression. At the same time, the participating organizations intend to support the peace and democratic society process in Turkey and advocate for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.




The agreement stems from a meeting held on October 17 at the Cologne headquarters of the Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK). Representatives from various political traditions and social movements gathered at the invitation of eight organizations. In a joint final declaration issued today, the participants reaffirm their determination to preserve their organizational independence while establishing a lasting foundation for joint political action.




Against militarism, fascism and imperialist war policies




In their declaration, the organizations describe a world marked by growing international tensions. They warn that wars and conflicts driven by imperialist centers of power are increasing the risk of a broader military confrontation, potentially escalating into a new global war over the redistribution of power and resources. While ever-greater resources are being devoted to armament and warfare, they say, poverty and social inequality are deepening. The consequences, they argue, are borne primarily by working and oppressed sections of society, women, and the natural environment.




The signatories view the growing strength of right-wing and fascist movements as part of this development. They argue that militarism, racism, sexism, hostility toward refugees and migrants, and the destruction of the natural foundations of life are interconnected. At the same time, social forces opposing these developments are increasingly being criminalized.




The organizations therefore call for stronger international coordination among movements of struggle. They remark that resistance movements from India to France and the United States, as well as Yemen and Rojava, must not remain isolated from one another. “Their experiences must be brought together and transformed into a shared framework of internationalist solidarity. Peace, democracy, and social justice cannot be expected from the very power structures responsible for war, exploitation, and oppression. Instead, the key lies in strengthening ties between working and oppressed populations across national borders.”













Joint resistance against AKP-MHP policies




Another key focus of the declaration is the political situation in Turkey. According to the organizations, the AKP-MHP government is exploiting the international shift to the right to consolidate its authoritarian system of rule on a permanent basis. They point out that repression against the political opposition, arrests, bans, and restrictions on democratic rights are aimed at suppressing social resistance and weakening organized opposition forces.




According to the organizations, those particularly affected include workers, trade unions, democratic organizations, intellectuals, artists, and opposition political groups. At the same time, the collective rights of the Kurdish and Alevi populations continue to be disregarded. Women face patriarchal violence and discrimination, while the protection of children and the right to life of animals, as well as the preservation of nature, are systematically neglected.




The organizations do not regard these policies as an isolated development in Turkey. Rather, they see them as part of a broader authoritarian offensive through which capitalist centers of power and reactionary governments are responding to social crises. This, they argue, makes it necessary to connect democratic and social struggles in Turkey with those in Europe and other regions of the world.




Democratic solution to the Kurdish question as a shared responsibility




The participating organizations explicitly address the peace and democratic society process, stating: “Although Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK have paved the way for political and democratic dialogue through their decisions to end the armed struggle, the AKP-MHP government and the Turkish state continue to refuse to take the necessary steps toward genuine progress.”




The final declaration stresses that the process initiated by Öcalan must enable the release of political prisoners, the democratic and political participation of former guerrilla fighters, and the return of exiled politicians. “It must also pave the way for full equality for the Kurdish population. This includes, in particular, collective rights to the mother tongue, identity, culture, and freedom of organization.”




According to the declaration, a democratic solution to the Kurdish question would serve not only the interests of the Kurdish population but also those of all peoples and oppressed social groups in Turkey. At the same time, the organizations oppose subordinating peace efforts to the political calculations of the government and the state or exploiting them for their own interests. Peace, democracy, and equal citizenship rights, they argue, are not concessions granted by those in power but must be achieved through collective social struggle.




Lasting cooperation instead of temporary alliances




In addition to the political situation, the Cologne meeting addressed the organizational requirements for building a joint movement. Previous experiences with alliances such as ABDEM, HDK-Europe, and ADGB were evaluated. The participants agreed that joint statements and occasional actions alone were insufficient. Instead, they aim to establish continuous cooperation that brings together different social movements and political organizations.




The aim is not to create a single organization in which the participating groups would have to abandon their political identities, structures, or programs. Rather, the alliance is intended to be based on shared objectives, mutual recognition, and equal participation. Political decisions are to be made through joint discussions, while solidarity is to be strengthened through concrete struggles. The alliance’s precise political orientation, organizational structure, and working methods will be developed through further consultations. To ensure that the alliance can take action even during its founding phase, the participants agreed to establish a joint communication group.




20 organizations declare their readiness to join as founding members




According to the final declaration, 20 organizations have expressed their willingness to participate in the new alliance as founding members. These include:







Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK)




Kurdistan Democratic Communities Congress in Europe (KCDK-E)




Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP-Europe)




Confederation of Oppressed Migrants in Europe (AVEG-KON)




Confederation of Democratic Rights in Europe (ADHK)




Purple-Red Collective




Association of Migrant Workers in Europe (AGEB)




Confederation of Workers from Turkey in Europe (ATIK)




European Revolutionary Democratic Communes Initiative (ADDKI)




International Struggle Collective (EMK)




Green Left Party Europe




Socialist Women’s Union (SKB Europe)




Council of Revolutionary Communes in Europe (ADKM)




Federation of Democratic Dersim Associations in Europe (ADEF)




Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E)




European Forum for Freedom and Peace (EFFP)




European Council in Exile (ASM)




Federation of Democratic Alevis (FEDA)




Democratic Alevi Women’s Union (YJAD)




New Woman and the TÜDAY Human Rights Association







The Platform for Workers’ Unity and the Brotherhood of Peoples (BIR-KAR), the European Front for Labour and Freedom, the Anti-Imperialist League (AIL), and the Red Alliance will initially participate as observers and actively contribute to the alliance’s further development. In the coming weeks, talks are planned with additional progressive, revolutionary, and democratic organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan that are active in Europe.




Call to build an internationalist solidarity front




In closing, the participating organizations issued a joint appeal to democratic and revolutionary forces in Europe, stating the following:




“We want the first step we have taken in Cologne to converge with the democratic struggles in Europe and Turkey, as well as with resistance forces in different parts of the world. We are convinced that this common platform of struggle must become part of an internationalist network of solidarity in which peoples and social forces from different regions strengthen one another.




In the face of rising fascism and international war policies, such cooperation is more urgent than ever. We must stand together for peace, democracy, fundamental rights and freedoms, and intensify our joint struggle against rising fascism, racism, sexism, hostility toward migrants, imperialist aggression, and anti-democratic repression.




Differences in political programs and organizational structures do not stand in the way of cooperation. We share a broad common foundation in our commitment to an equal, free, and just society.




To jointly institutionalize, firmly establish, and expand this common foundation, we call on all progressive, revolutionary, and democratic organizations and individuals from Turkey, Kurdistan, and migrant communities in Europe to join our founding process.”

title: Panel discussion on Jineolojî and self-defense in Marseille
content:
A panel discussion and commemoration event focusing on Jineolojî and the formation of women’s armed forces was held in Marseille, France, organized by the Association of Martyrs’ Families (KOMAW), the Marseille Arîn Mîrkan Women’s Council, and members of Jineolojî Provence. The event, held at the Marseille Kurdish Democratic Community Center, was attended by numerous Kurdish women from the region, as well as representatives of French internationalist women’s movements.




The event began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the Kurdistan freedom struggle, represented by Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), described as an immortal commander of the Kurdish women’s struggle, as well as international women revolutionaries who lost their lives defending life.




This was followed by a video presentation highlighting Bêrîtan’s commitment to the principles of women’s freedom and the resistance of Kurdish women in their struggle for liberation. During the screening, chants of “Şehîd namirin” (“Martyrs are immortal) frequently echoed through the hall.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/c389a11c_20261025174114_2026-10-25-marsilya-jineoloji-paneli-1.mp4













‘The formation of women’s armed forces and Jineolojî in the pursuit of women’s freedom’




Speaking at a seminar titled “The Formation of Armed Forces within the Kurdistan Women’s Movement and Jineolojî,” Sîdar Feraşîn, a member of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E), discussed the historical development of the Kurdish women’s movement, awareness of self-defense, and the importance of organizing women’s armed forces.




Feraşîn emphasized that Jineolojî should play a greater role in women’s gatherings and areas of struggle, not merely as an institutional identity but also as a guiding perspective. She also highlighted the importance of the principles of women’s freedom.




Feraşîn stated that Kurdish women continue their organizing efforts in various fields, particularly politics, diplomacy, culture, and the arts, while work on Jineolojî is also ongoing. She noted that educational activities conducted across Europe through camps, seminars, workshops, and conferences have encouraged women to develop new ways of questioning and critical thinking. She emphasized the need to adapt organizational structures to the existing potential.




Discussions focused on the role of Jineolojî, as the science of women, in social transformation. Participants emphasized that strengthening the principles of women’s freedom is essential to building an alternative way of life. They also highlighted the resistance of Bêrîtan, who lost her life in the struggle, as one of the symbols of the Kurdish people’s and Kurdish women’s struggle for a free life.




Message of solidarity from internationalist women




In a statement issued by members of Jineolojî Provence and representatives of international women’s movements, violence against women and femicide were described as being linked to the persistence of the patriarchal system and fascism. The statement emphasized women’s determination to strengthen their struggle for freedom in different parts of the world.




The statement also stressed that keeping the memory of women revolutionaries alive provides strength and courage to continue the struggle, concluding with the message “Berxwedan Jiyan e” (“Resistance is life”).




Elefteria Hambi and Nagihan Akarsel commemorated




The event also commemorated Elefteria Hambi, an internationalist revolutionary who lost her life in Rojava, and Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineolojî Academy who was killed in Sulaymaniyah in an assassination carried out by the Turkish state.




A speech honoring Elefteria Hambi (Eva Maria Steiger) recalled that she traveled to Rojava in 2018 and fought against ISIS in the ranks of the YPJ before joining the guerrilla struggle in the Garê and Qandil regions. A tribute written in memory of the German revolutionary was read aloud.




The portraits prepared jointly by Jineolojî Provence and the Third District Neighborhood Committee were described as symbols of remembrance and internationalist solidarity.




In the final part of the program, a poem written in memory of Nagihan Akarsel, the Kurdish journalist and academic who was killed, was recited.




The event concluded with a performance by a choir formed under the Arîn Mîrkan Women’s Council.

title: Girê Spî Committee calls for the protection of families trapped in Regional Directorate building
content:
A group of Kurdish residents from Girê Spî, who were returning to their homes at the invitation of the Girê Spî Regional Directorate, were attacked while entering the building earlier today.




The Girê Spî Committee for the Forcibly Displaced reported that more than 100 Kurdish families were under siege inside the Regional Directorate building.




The committee described the attack against Kurds as an assault on their safety and their legitimate right to return. It called for the protection of the families and for an immediate investigation into those responsible.




The committee stated that it had been coordinating with relevant parties and following up on efforts to enable forcibly displaced families to return to their homes and properties. These efforts have so far yielded no results, it added.




The committee emphasized that the Regional Directorate officials must fulfill their responsibilities to protect the residents against such attacks.




Drawing attention to the plight of more than 100 Kurdish families, including women and children, trapped inside the Girê Spî Regional Directorate building, the committee called on the relevant authorities to intervene immediately to protect the residents from further attacks.




The committee stated that anyone wishing to return to Girê Spî should contact and coordinate with the committee so that their return can be organized, followed up with the relevant parties, and appropriate conditions can be established to ensure their safety.




The committee called on the relevant authorities to launch a thorough and transparent investigation into the attacks, hold all those responsible accountable, take appropriate measures to ensure residents’ safety and prevent further violations, facilitate the safe return of families, and protect their legitimate rights.

title: Temelli: Steps toward democratizing the Republic must not be delayed
content:
At a press conference held in Parliament, DEM Party Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Sezai Temelli addressed the peace and democratic society process. He called for the opportunity presented by the process to be seized and for the necessary steps to be taken without delay.




“The democratic resolution to the Kurdish question is the most important step toward comprehensive democratization and the democratization of the Republic,” Temelli said.




Temelli pointed out that the Kurdish question has remained unresolved throughout the Republic’s 100-year history, and that its democratic resolution is of critical importance for the democratization of the Republic.




He emphasized the need to guarantee freedom of the press and expression, protect human rights, and end political bans.




Drawing attention to the continued imprisonment of political figures in Turkey, Temelli cited Figen Yüksekdağ and Selahattin Demirtaş, who are imprisoned in connection with the Kobanê trial, as well as Can Atalay.




Criticizing the Turkish state’s failure to implement rulings of the European Court of Human Rights, Temelli stated that the Republic must embrace democracy and freedoms.




“The Republic must be at peace with democracy. The path to lasting social peace lies through a democratic state governed by the rule of law, based on equal citizenship. It is therefore essential that we establish such a state governed by the rule of law as soon as possible,” Sezai Temelli said.




Emphasizing that democracy is not limited to political institutions, Temelli stated that prison conditions, freedom of expression, trade union rights, women’s participation in politics, and the fight against poverty are also fundamental indicators of democratization.

author: Mada Masr
title: Parliament gives Sisi mandate to back Saudi Arabia militarily, opposition rejects ‘blank-check authorization’
content:
Parliament authorized President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Monday to “take the necessary measures to support the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, following coordination between the two countries, to defend its territory, sovereignty and holy sites against any external attacks,” 

according 

to a statement issued by House of Representatives Speaker Hesham Badawy.




Lawmakers in the House, who had gathered for the third-closed door session on the matter in proceedings that began over an hour later than planned, stood in order to vote in support of the authorization, with a majority of two-thirds casting their votes in favor.




Twelve lawmakers from the Egyptian Social Democratic Party, along with four other opposition MPs — Diaa Dawoud, Atef Maghawry, Ahmed Farghaly and Abdel Alim Dawoud — refused to endorse the mandate, remaining seated during the vote, according to two parliamentary sources who spoke separately to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity. Lawmakers from pro-government parties voted in favor, they added.




Riyadh has made no official public statement, neither on Sisi’s request for parliamentary authorization nor on Parliament’s approval of it. Badawy’s statement, however, used the phrase “following coordination between the two countries,” instead of “if we are asked to do so,” the phrase Sisi 

used 

when he asked for the mandate earlier this month.




Saudi daily Okaz 

used

 Badawy’s formulation in its commentary on the decision, which it said “comes within the framework of Egyptian-Saudi coordination on the security challenges facing the region.”




One of the parliamentary sources said that Badawy did not open any of the three sessions by reading out the proposed measure or the relevant constitutional provision, as is customary when Parliament considers a presidential decree, agreement or similar measure. Instead, he merely 

asked 

lawmakers to indicate their positions and vote on authorizing the president to take “defensive measures” to protect Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requested them, he added.




The same source stressed that parliamentary custom requires that lawmakers be given specific details — not shared with the press — including the nature of any mission assigned to Egyptian military forces that are to operate abroad, the size and composition of the force and the mission’s duration. None of these details was presented during the sessions, the source said. Instead, Parliament only gave the president authority to act in coordination with Saudi Arabia, he added.




The Constitution requires parliamentary approval when troops are sent on a combat mission outside the borders, making it necessary to provide lawmakers with basic information about the mission, the source said. Granting the president “blank-check authorization,” the source argued, is a contentious issue.




Egyptian Social Democratic Party member Freddy al-Bayady likewise told Mada Masr that no details were presented in either of the two previous sessions, as well as in Monday’s, on the nature and limits of the military mission, the duration and scope of the authorization, its financial and human risk or the risk of the conflict widening and affecting Red Sea and Suez Canal navigation. 




Bayady holds a seat in the House, butunable to attend Monday’s session as he was out of the country, he told Mada Masr.




He stressed that his party’s MPs stand in solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reject attacks on its territory, but need enough information to make a decision after weighing the consequences.




Egypt has previously provided military support to Saudi Arabia during Operation Decisive Storm in 2015, and to the United Arab Emirates earlier this year, without putting the matter before Parliament, the parliamentary source noted.




In their viewpoint, bringing the matter before Parliament this time indicates that the planned support could go beyond a limited deployment of equipment or troops, something that he argued compelled the state to seek out parliamentary approval this time.




Article 152 of the Constitution 

requires 

the president to consult the National Defense Council before declaring war or sending armed forces on combat missions outside the country. It also requires approval from two-thirds of the members of the House, voting in a closed session under Article 130 of the House’s bylaws.




In May, Egypt sent a “

detachment

” — a limited military formation drawn from one or several corps — to the UAE. Sources at the time said that the word “detachment” came to “signal the limited size of the formation and the limited duration of the presence,” a gesture of Egyptian support for the UAE against Iranian attacks that stopped short of real Egyptian involvement in the war.




Before that, Egypt had taken part in Operation Decisive Storm, the coalition that Saudi Arabia has led in Yemen since 2015. It 

dispatched 

four naval vessels to secure the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Gulf of Aden, alongside air force participation. Cairo 

said 

at the time that it is prepared to send ground troops “if the situation warrants,” but it never did.




On October 17, Sisi called for an emergency parliamentary session during the Egyptian Military Academy graduation ceremony, asking lawmakers to authorize him to take any measures necessary to protect Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks “if we are asked to do so.”




“We are not looking for a role to play, but it makes no sense whatsoever for us to allow any harm to come to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its security or its stability,” he said during the ceremony.




He appealed to “everyone in the Gulf” to stop the war. “Regardless of this appeal, whether it is heeded or not, Egypt, in line with His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohamed bin Salman’s directives, will carry out any measure to protect and defend you,” he added.




The president stressed that he is not speaking “in order for us to fight anyone or attack anyone. We are speaking only in defense.”




After Sisi’s remarks, House Speaker Hesham Badawy called an emergency plenary session for the following morning. 




Before Parliament convened on October 18, the presidential spokesperson 

announced

 three points agreed upon by the National Defense Council at a meeting chaired by Sisi earlier that day. The council declared Egypt’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, out of a belief that Saudi national security is tied to Egyptian and Arab national security, and pledged to provide the country with all necessary and available forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources and territorial integrity and safeguard Islamic holy sites.




The council also called for continued and intensified political and diplomatic efforts, in coordination with relevant regional and international parties, to de-escalate tensions across the region and peacefully resolve the crisis affecting it.




Then, Parliament held a three-hour closed-door session before postponing a final decision. The vote was deferred to sessions scheduled for October 19 and 20. On October 19, however, lawmakers postponed the vote again until Monday, citing the need to give all MPs an opportunity to express their views.




As Parliament held its first session last week, the grand imam of Al-Azhar, Ahmed al-Tayeb, 

called 

for the urgent formation of a mediation committee comprising respected, wise figures from Arab and Muslim countries. The committee, he said, should work to halt armed conflicts across the region and bridge differences between the parties involved. He expressed his readiness to support its efforts but stopped short of explicitly opposing Egyptian military defense measures to protect Saudi Arabia.




In a new statement, Tayeb 

condemned

 on Monday morning the Houthi attacks on Mecca, Madinah and Saudi civilian infrastructure, calling for them to stop and renewed his appeal for the committee’s formation.




With Parliament’s decision still pending, Foreign Minister Badr Abdel Atty and General Intelligence Service chief Hassan Rashad 

traveled

 to Riyadh on October 21, where they met Crown Prince Mohamed bin Salman and delivered a message from Sisi to King Salman bin Abdel Aziz. 

According 

to Abdel Atty, the message reaffirmed Egypt’s support for Saudi Arabia in the face of the attacks while stressing the need to seek a political solution to the crisis.




Earlier that day, Sisi had also 

said 

that any Egyptian military support for Saudi Arabia would be aimed at protecting the kingdom’s territory and borders, not launching attacks on Yemen.




The Saudi-Houthi front is witnessing its most violent 

escalation 

since the collapse of the truce that had held since 2022.




On Monday, the Houthis 

said 

they attacked oil pumping stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline and Riyadh airport. The Saudi-led coalition, meanwhile, announced that it destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, one of which it said had been used to fire a missile toward Riyadh.




According to data from aviation analytics firm Cirium published on Monday, around 86 percent of scheduled flights at King Khalid International Airport were canceled between October 8 and October 25.




In July, the Houthis declared a “naval blockade” of the kingdom and attacked Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. In September, they launched a ground attack, capturing the Yemeni Port of Mokha, which had been under the control of the Saudi-led coalition’s joint forces, effectively controlling Bab al-Mandab. By early October, the two sides were escalating: the internationally recognized Yemeni government launched the Fajr al-Yemen Operation to retake Sanaa, backed by extensive Saudi air support, while the Houthis attacked facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco and 

struck

 King Khalid International Airport, killing 12 people and wounding hundreds.

The post 

Parliament gives Sisi mandate to back Saudi Arabia militarily, opposition rejects ‘blank-check authorization’

 first appeared on 

Mada Masr

.

author: Redação
title: A democracia tem que ser defendida na unha
content:
O resultado do segundo turno neste domingo, uma virada inédita do presidente Luís Inácio Lula da Silva, demonstra que a política, como a conhecíamos, acabou de vez.




O 

resultado

 foi fruto de uma mobilização cidadã como nunca se viu desde que as redes sociais se tornaram onipresentes na vida dos brasileiros. A campanha digital, mobilizada especialmente por meio de um canal no WhatsApp que concentrou 5% da população — 1 em cada 10 eleitores de Lula — demonstrou que, na era digital, a política se faz com mobilização e participação. Este engajamento conseguiu dominar a conversa digital, saiu das redes e foi para as conversas no bar, em filas de supermercado. Conseguiu superar o boicote descarado da Meta, Big Tech que tem maior controle sobre a esfera de debate público no Brasil — são 110 milhões de usuários no Facebook, 130 milhões no Instagram e 160 milhões no WhatsApp. Foi também a mobilização da sociedade civil que levou essa empresa a ser questionada pela ONU, intimada pelo TSE e investigada pelo Ministério Público Federal.




Os jornalistas investigativos — em especial os de veículos independentes — trabalharam obstinadamente, incansavelmente. Do caso Dark Horse às ligações de Flávio com o Careca do INSS, foi graças ao trabalho de nossos colegas que o público foi informado sobre o passado do candidato do PL, fatos de interesse público fundamentais para o cidadão decidir seu voto.




Aqui na 

Agência Pública

, revelamos as 

suspeitas

 de corrupção e omissão nos hospitais federais do Rio que eram o “feudo” de Flávio Bolsonaro durante o governo do seu pai; detalhamos 

laços do amigo de Flávio

, Willer Tomaz, com o Careca do INSS; levantamos o 

estilo de vida

 de Eduardo Bolsonaro e Paulo Figueiredo nos EUA, descobrimos uma 

empresa que Eduardo abriu

 com o passaporte Italiano no Bahrein, apuramos as 

medidas da Meta

 para prejudicar postagens da campanha de Lula. Mostramos como o assunto que mais afeta os brasileiros — a segurança pública — impacta nossas vidas. Revelamos 

mensagens inéditas

 que evidenciam como Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, mantém uma relação umbilical com figuras da direita brasileira, e também da imprensa. Foi nosso jornalismo que revelou ao Brasil a história da professora Vânia de Souza Borges, que perdeu seu filho, Rafael Borges, para o vício em Bets, no especial 

Jogo Perigoso: o Brasil das Bets

. No meio da campanha eleitoral, Vânia foi pessoalmente pedir ao presidente Lula a proibição das Bets – e foi atendida.




Nosso trabalho resultou em ataques, intimidação e assédio digitais. Também enfrentamos o boicote da Meta — tanto pela redução do alcance do Instagram quanto pela censura descarada de pelo menos um post que denunciamos na véspera do segundo turno. Mesmo assim, as revelações que apuramos voaram: foram amplamente republicadas, embasaram episódios da série documental do Youtube Revelando, viraram postagens de influenciadores e memes.

André Janones transformou uma de nossas matérias em uma “missão” do Canal Exército do Lula, comandando a tropa a pesquisar a frase “FLÁVIO BOLSONARO ESQUEMA PANDEMIA”. O primeiro resultado a aparecer foi a investigação da 

Agência Pública

. No último domingo, antes da votação, no debate da TV Bandeirantes, o caso virou um questionamento ao candidato do PL em rede nacional. ⁠




Neste momento, a recusa de Flávio Bolsonaro em aceitar a derrota e as denúncias de “golpe” por parte de nomes importantes da extrema direita vão fortalecer a narrativa de perseguição, de fraudes nas urnas e de uma suposta “ditadura”. Figuras como Nikolas Ferreira, Pablo Marçal e Eduardo Bolsonaro já começaram a dizer que a ampliação do período de votação constitui “roubo”. Os contra-ataques à eleição popular serão fortalecidos, ainda, pelo controle do Senado e da Câmara Federal, onde o partido PL obteve a maior bancada desde 1990. É uma bancada empenhada em desconstruir avanços como a proibição das bets, o fim da escala 6 x 1, a proteção do meio ambiente e dos direitos dos indígenas e a regulação das Big Techs.




O contexto pós-eleitoral se complica ainda mais porque o repuxo bolsonarista insere-se em um movimento global de forças antidemocráticas que querem matar justamente o tipo de mobilização cidadã que se viu no Brasil. Os EUA e seus aliados mais próximos no continente — como a Argentina de Milei — não reconheceram, até o momento, a eleição de Lula.




Neste contexto, nosso jornalismo será ainda mais necessário. Nosso compromisso é seguir investindo no jornalismo investigativo, ampliar nossa presença no Youtube para participar cada vez mais do debate que ocorre em vídeos nas telas de todos os brasileiros, além de fortalecer as redes de colaboração internacionais que distribuem nossos conteúdos e ampliam a vigilância sobre a democracia brasileira. Sabemos que o jornalismo cada vez mais faz parte de uma disputa que não se esgota na votação. Defender a democracia é, neste novo contexto, uma tarefa cotidiana que continuará a impulsionar nosso trabalho ao lado da sociedade civil e de movimentos organizados.




Há muito trabalho a ser feito. Vamos a ele.

author: Lisa Xu
title: UFCW Members Protect Local Election After Sham Merger Attempt
content:
An insurgent slate is challenging the longtime incumbents in Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW), in what may be the local’s first competitive election in decades. And now, after protecting the election from a sham merger attempt that would have canceled the election, the battle is on. 




Ballots are set to be mailed on November 21. But when members first saw the election notice in the local’s newsletter, they discovered a big “but.” The notice stated that the election would not proceed if Local 8 merged with another union, the 

Staffing Agencies Federated Employees

 (SAFE), before the end of the year. 




Members said they had never heard about this possible merger, or SAFE, before reading about it in the final sentence of the election notice, mailed to members on October 16. 




What is SAFE? Publicly available information about the organization, which has multiple ties to Local 8 President Jacques Loveall, raised more questions than answers. Neither Local 8, the UFCW International union, nor SAFE has responded to inquiries about the merger.




With the help of Essential Workers for Democracy, a UFCW reform organization focused on member education and union democracy, the insurgent slate urged the Department of Labor to investigate SAFE and the merger. After a federal investigator began to probe, the local told them the merger had been “postponed indefinitely.” 




A FAMILY AFFAIR







Local 8 represents 23,000 workers in grocery, meatpacking, health care, and cannabis across northern California and the Central Valley. End to end, it would take 10 hours to drive the length of the local’s jurisdiction. 




The reform slate 

At What Cost

 is running on opening up negotiations to members and training stewards in every workplace. Wages for grocery workers have stagnated across California. A 

2025 study

 sponsored by several other UFCW locals on understaffing at Kroger and Albertsons found a high degree of financial insecurity among their workers. 




“Grocery careers, once dignified, have been reduced to second jobs for most,” said Eric Marcuz, a veteran Safeway worker who is running for president on the At What Cost slate. The local has not had a competitive election in at least 40 years.




Marcuz’s slate created a 

page

 to try to provide members more information about the merger, and sent a 

letter of complaint

 to Local 8, UFCW International, and the Department of Labor over what they saw as an effort to avoid a democratic election. 




The At What Cost slate is running against a slate of incumbents—the 

Solidarity Works Team

— headed by Loveall, who has been president of Local 8 and its predecessor union, Local 588, since 2004. He took over the position from his father, 

Jack Loveall

, who became president of Local 588 in 1984, after working in high-level positions for the UFCW International and one of its predecessor unions, the Retail Clerks, for many years. 




When the elder Loveall retired, he was one of the highest-paid union officers in the country, earning more than $567,000 in compensation a year, equivalent to over a million dollars today. 




“The Loveall family has led our union for decades,” said Marcuz. “Over that time they have consolidated power at the top and completely distanced themselves from the workers they claim to represent. While their wealth and wages have ballooned, the members have been left behind.” 




On his LinkedIn page, the younger Loveall describes himself as “Chief Executive Officer of trade organization (UFCW8.org).” He received $306,000 in total compensation from the local last year, plus another $20,000 salary as an International Vice President and 

$34,752

 from his role as a trustee of the UFCW Vacation Compensation Trusts. Loveall is also the director and co-founder of Solidaritus, a for-profit health care company that Local 8 has purchased millions of dollars of shares in, as have other unions. 




‘THAT’S THEIR MODE OF OPERATING’




Leaders of the local have used a merger to avoid a competitive election before. In 2006, a slate of 

reformers

 planned a challenge to the leadership of then-Local 588, including Loveall. But prior to the scheduled election, Local 588 

merged

 with Local 1288 to form Local 8-Golden State, and elections were put off until 2008. 




Meanwhile, Doug Slaydon, a 25-year meat cutter and the reform slate’s candidate for union president, was 

fired

 from Safeway on the pretext of a customer complaint in 2006. The firing occurred a day after a 20-store campaign blitz by his slate, 588 Members for a Democratic Union.




“That's their mode of operating,” Slaydon said, referring to the mergers. “That's how they got around my attempt at an election.” 




“Federal law is clear: local unions must hold officer elections at least every three years,” said Will Bloom, a professor at the CUNY School of Law and a board member of the Association for Union Democracy. “Any attempt to forestall an election through a sham merger, in an effort to quash dissent and make member participation more difficult, goes against the basic principles of union democracy law.”




A REAL UNION?




The proposed merger with SAFE immediately raised the eyebrows of members and the Department of Labor. 




It is not clear who SAFE represents, or whether it is even a union. On its 

website

, SAFE calls itself a “labor-driven initiative committed to securing union inclusion and equitable treatment for workers employed through staffing agencies.” 




However, there are no union election filings by SAFE with the National Labor Relations Board, nor any other public documentation of where members are being organized. The organization’s website is filled with stock photos, rather than photos of actual members.




An initial 

LM-1 form

 for SAFE was filed on February 9, 2026 by Patricia Schreiter, who 

appears

 to be a 

relative

 of Loveall, and has no other public connection to the labor movement. Schreiter was not listed on SAFE’s website as an officer, although the LM-1 form lists her as president. After members and a federal investigator from the Department of Labor began asking questions, the page listing SAFE’s officers and staff was removed from its site. 




As of early last week, the SAFE homepage stated the organization was 

“9,800 Strong and Growing,”

 but this figure has since been removed. A legislative update on the SAFE site from September 30 included a 

reference

 to union mergers as a strategy “to build a larger, stronger, more unified organization,” as “bigger unions win bigger protections”, but this language has also been removed.




The SAFE website features dozens of articles about the SAFE Act, or SB 1032, a California state senate bill sponsored by Senator Eloise Reyes that would tighten regulatory standards for temporary staffing agencies and require them to buy workers’ compensation insurance. Loveall has been a vocal supporter of the bill via the UFCW Western States Council, the bill’s co-sponsor.




However, an aide for Senator Reyes told 

Labor Notes

 that the SAFE union was not registered as a group in support of the bill, or one that they had personally interacted with.




WEB OF CONNECTIONS




There are a number of suggestive ties between SAFE and an organization called 

The PACT

, which claims to be a 501(c)5 labor organization for temp workers. Until early last week SAFE’s organizing director was 

listed

 as Fernando Cisneros, whose LinkedIn 

profile

 states that he is also a full-time “Growth Leader” at The PACT. (Cisneros’s name disappeared when SAFE removed that section of its website.)




The PACT has an arrangement with a company called 

Samuel Hale

, which provides workers’ compensation insurance to the employers of temp workers and acts as a co-employer of those workers. 




“In addition to passing along savings to our customers, Samuel Hale also reinvests a percentage of every payroll dollar worked into a benefits fund managed by The PACT, a 501c5, exclusively focused on developing and administering new benefits to our growing 10,000+ member population,” Samuel Hale writes on its website. These workers appear to be mostly immigrant workers in sectors including warehouse work, food processing, and domestic services.




As of earlier this week, SAFE’s website had a section called 

“Health Care & Retirement Benefits,”

 which stated that SAFE members will receive a defined benefit pension plan, as well as comprehensive medical coverage. These are both benefits which 

The PACT claims to offer

 to its employees. This section on the SAFE website, too, has since been removed. 




Samuel Hale and Local 8 appear to have a collective bargaining agreement, and  seem to be utilizing California’s Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) carve-out, a state law that allows for workers’ compensation claims to be directly arbitrated between a union and employer, bypassing the state’s worker compensation board. A collective bargaining agreement must be in place in order to qualify for the carve-out.




Loveall of Local 8 (then Local 588) appears to have signed a 

collective bargaining agreement

 in 2005 with Samuel Hale on behalf of The Professional and Commercial Trades Association (PACT), according to a 

video

 posted on the company’s Facebook page. In a 

2025 workers’ comp appeal

 case, a Samuel Hale spokesperson said that the Samuel Hale employees are covered by a UFCW CBA and that The PACT is “a wing of the UFCW.” However, the details of this agreement are unclear and cannot be found online. The worker who filed the appeal also said that Local 8 was unable to provide “any information regarding alleged union membership,” even as Samuel Hale affirmed that union dues were being deducted from employee paychecks.




Samuel Hale says that it can help employers cut workers’ comp claim costs by up to 50 percent, and boasts that it is the only entity covered by the California ADR carve-out that can extend the carve-out’s protection to other employers, thanks to its CBA with Local 8.




In addition to the web of connections between SAFE, The PACT, Samuel Hale, and Local 8, SAFE’s 

articles of incorporation

 were filed July 17, 2025 by 

Ellen Anreder

. Anreder is the CEO of 

Bleiweiss Communications

, a major vendor for Local 8. Website 

metadata

 indicates that SAFE’s website was also created by Bleiweiss. 




Anreder and Loveall together serve on several non-profit boards that Local 8 has financial ties to, including 

CORPaTH

, the 

Food and Drug Conference

, the 

Loveall Foundation for Children

, and 

All Trusts Cooperative

 (of which Anreder and Loveall are the only two board members), with a collective net assets of over $10 million.




FUTURES AT STAKE




In the UFCW, local union bylaws typically allow for elections to be called at any point in a six-month window preceding the end of a term, giving incumbents a powerful advantage, since challengers can't be sure when exactly they might need to take time off to collect nomination signatures or campaign to turn out the vote. What’s more, Local 8 has scheduled ballots to be mailed during the week of Thanksgiving, a universal blackout period for time off in the grocery retail sector. That’s exactly the week when candidates could most effectively campaign at worksites.




The At What Cost slate notified the local union of their intent to run in August 2025, although reformers have been publicly agitating in the local since late 2024.




But even talking about doing more to engage members has had repercussions. After Marcuz read Jane McAlevey’s organizing guide 

No Shortcuts

, he brought up the possibility of opening up bargaining to his union rep. A few days later, he was removed from his position as steward, and was told that more “loyalty” was expected from him. 




Marcuz and his co-workers encountered similar resistance when they collected 300 petition signatures for Zoom access to union meetings, which are only held in-person at the union office in Roseville—a several-hour drive for many members of the local, which is spread out across 40 counties. The same happened when they organized bowling socials.




During their campaign, union staff representatives have allegedly told members that it’s illegal to wear At What Cost buttons or to provide contact information to the slate. At a Safeway store in Turlock, a rep physically pulled a member away from speaking to Marcuz. 




“Workers face exploitation through contract violations, wage theft, and unsafe staffing and working conditions,” Marcuz said. “We could organize against these issues, but our leadership seems more interested in collaborating with the corporations creating these conditions than with the members who pay their salaries.”




In early November, members of the slate will be working to collect 443 petition signatures—2 percent of active members—to get on the ballot and force the first competitive election in memory.

author: anonerror
title: [Valladolid] Apertura de nuevo local de CNT
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.




Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.




A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla Mimo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.




A continuación hemos puesto en marcha unas jornadas de inauguración de las que tenéis información en las redes y web de CNT.




Reproducimos a continuación el manifiesto que refleja esta nueva etapa:




Hoy, sábado, 17 de octubre, inauguramos una nueva etapa en CNT Valladolid.




Estrenamos un espacio más amplio. Un espacio donde pueda entrar más gente, donde podamos encontrarnos, organizarnos y construir juntas una respuesta colectiva a la realidad que vivimos.




Porque este local no es solamente un lugar nuevo. Es un espacio de encuentro para quienes entendemos que nuestros derechos no son concesiones, que la dignidad no se negocia y que nuestra fuerza está en la lucha obrera.




Y cuando decimos clase trabajadora, no hablamos solo de quienes tienen un contrato o un empleo. También hablamos de quienes trabajan sin derechos, de quienes sostienen los cuidados y de quienes encuentran las puertas cerradas al empleo por su identidad o su condición.




Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario: 

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.




Por eso abrimos este espacio.




Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.




Porque somos CNT.




CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales. 




Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos




Somos anarcosindicalistas. Entendemos que quienes vivimos de nuestro trabajo tenemos capacidad para defender nuestros derechos colectivamente y para construir otras formas de relacionarnos y organizarnos frente a la explotación. 




Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos. 

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.




Porque el sistema contra el que se organizaron quienes nos precedieron no ha desaparecido. La explotación adopta nuevas formas. La precariedad se normaliza. Trabajar ya no garantiza unas condiciones de vida dignas. Y quienes acumulan riqueza siguen teniendo capacidad para decidir sobre nuestras vidas.




Por eso estamos aquí.




Porque la lucha sigue.




Y esa lucha sigue hoy en múltiples frentes que se complementan.




Una de ellas es la 

lucha antifascista

.




Estamos viendo crecer discursos que alimentan el odio y el miedo para enfrentar a la clase trabajadora e impedir que veamos las causas de fondo de la desigualdad.




Lo vemos en el avance de la extrema derecha, en las políticas contra las personas migrantes, en la violencia contra determinados colectivos y también aquí, en nuestros barrios, con la aparición de grupos neonazis.




Entendemos que la lucha antifascista debe responder cuando la extrema derecha aparece en la calle. Y también tenemos que combatir las condiciones que permiten que esos discursos crezcan. 




Porque cuando la precariedad aumenta, los derechos se recortan y los recursos escasean, la pobreza se enquista en determinados barrios. Y es ahí donde los grupos de extrema derecha encuentran un terreno fértil para extender su odio y enfrentar entre sí a quienes más sufren las consecuencias de este sistema.




Por eso, cuando nos quieren enfrentadas, la respuesta tiene que ser la misma: 

apoyo mutuo y solidaridad

.




Somos anticapitalistas.




Porque el capitalismo no es únicamente una manera de organizar la economía. Es un sistema que convierte nuestras necesidades básicas en negocios y nuestros derechos en privilegios para quien puede pagarlos.




Y si hay un ejemplo claro de esto, es la vivienda. Hay muchas personas que no pueden acceder a una casa mientras unas pocas acumulan propiedades. No podemos aceptar pagarle a un rentista una parte cada vez mayor de lo que ganamos.




Esto no es un problema individual. Es una violencia económica ejercida y amparada por el sistema capitalista. El capital se apropia de nuestro tiempo, explota nuestros cuerpos y hace recaer sobre la clase trabajadora el coste de sostener una sociedad profundamente desigual.




Porque violencia es que quienes están empachados nos pidan que agradezcamos las migajas.




Nos negamos a sobrevivir para enriquecer a quienes nos explotan. 

Queremos una vida que no esté sometida al capital ni al beneficio de unos pocos. 




Igualmente nos oponemos a un sistema que explota la tierra, los animales y los recursos naturales poniendo el beneficio económico por encima de la vida. Porque tampoco puede haber justicia social sin justicia ambiental. Nuestra lucha también es ecosocial. Por un sistema sostenible que ponga la vida en el centro y respete el lugar que habitamos.




Somos antirracistas.




No podemos hablar como clase trabajadora sin hablar del racismo que atraviesa nuestras vidas y nuestros espacios de trabajo. 




La Ley de Extranjería convierte la situación administrativa en una herramienta de control, esclavitud y explotación. Un sistema que ilegaliza a miles de personas para someterlas a condiciones sociolaborales que nadie debería aceptar. 




Y no podemos hablar de racismo sin nombrar el antigitanismo, una forma histórica de discriminación que continúa atravesando instituciones, empleo, vivienda, educación y acceso a derechos.




El racismo está en las fronteras. Está en la discriminación cotidiana. Está en los controles policiales. Está en la precariedad laboral. Está en la sospecha permanente sobre determinados cuerpos y determinados barrios. 




Mientras tanto, discursos políticos y mediáticos deshumanizan a las personas racializadas, las convierten en chivos expiatorios y alimentan el odio que sostiene esta desigualdad.




No hay justicia social mientras se permita que una parte de la clase trabajadora sea explotada con menos derechos que otra. Por eso, combatir el racismo, la xenofobia y el antigitanismo es una tarea sindical.




Somos transfeministas.




Porque tampoco hay justicia social mientras el patriarcado siga condicionando nuestras vidas y nuestros cuerpos.




El asesinato machista es su expresión más brutal. Sí, nos matan, pero la violencia que sufrimos no empieza con el asesinato. Empieza con el control, el miedo, la dependencia económica, la desigualdad y la impunidad. Se refuerza con la precariedad laboral, la carga de los cuidados y todas las barreras que dificultan nuestra autonomía. 




Las múltiples violencias machistas se manifiestan de diversas formas: agresiones sexuales, explotación, acoso, violencia obstétrica y la falta de acceso a un aborto seguro, libre y en nuestro hospital.




Sabemos que estas violencias no afectan a todas por igual: la clase, el origen, la identidad de género o la orientación sexual también condicionan las posibilidades de vivir libres y seguras.




Por eso somos transfeministas, porque luchamos contra el patriarcado, el machismo, la LGTBIfobia y todas las formas de dominación que castigan a quienes desobedecen los mandatos de género y pretenden decidir cómo debemos vivir, amar y habitar nuestros cuerpos.




Frente a quienes niegan, minimizan o justifican estas violencias, no vamos a callarnos ni a dar un paso atrás. Organización, autodefensa y lucha transfeminista.




Y también 

somos internacionalistas.




Porque no podemos hablar de justicia mientras existan guerras, ocupaciones, genocidios y pueblos sometidos. Defendemos la soberanía de los pueblos y su autodeterminación. 




Que viva la lucha del pueblo palestino, y de tantos otros pueblos que resisten la opresión. 




Todas estas luchas forman parte de una misma. No podemos combatir la explotación sin enfrentarnos al racismo, al patriarcado y al fascismo; ni defender la dignidad y los derechos de todas las personas sin combatir las distintas formas de opresión que atraviesan nuestras vidas.




Estas luchas no se contradicen ni compiten entre sí; sino todo lo contrario. Se complementan y se necesitan para responder con organización y solidaridad.




Nuestra lucha será colectiva, o no será.




Pero no queremos que nuestra respuesta sea únicamente resistir. También queremos construir.




Porque hacer política no es solo denunciar las injusticias y enfrentarnos a quienes nos oprimen. También es encontrarnos en nuestras diferencias, compartir cultura, celebrar la alegría y reconocernos como parte de un todo que apuesta por otro modelo de sociedad.




Queremos construir comunidad, tejer redes de apoyo mutuo y recuperar la capacidad de sostenernos colectivamente frente a un sistema que nos quiere aisladas y compitiendo entre nosotras.




Queremos hacer barrio, ocupar las calles y que este espacio que inauguramos hoy sea un ejemplo de lugar de encuentro y organización, pero también un lugar donde construir vínculos que pongan los cuidados en el centro.




Reivindicamos las relaciones de apoyo, organizarnos desde abajo y acompañarnos para dejar de afrontar individualmente problemas que son colectivos.




Porque 

cuidarnos no es una cuestión privada ni una responsabilidad individual, es una cuestión política.




Por eso necesitamos más organización, más participación y más lucha.




Queremos una CNT viva, abierta y presente en Valladolid. Una CNT que esté en los centros de trabajo, pero también en los barrios, en las calles y en todos esos espacios donde se construyen nuestras vidas. Que conecte luchas, que teja alianzas y que sea una herramienta útil para quienes creemos que la lucha colectiva puede conquistar derechos.




Lo hemos comprobado y lo vemos a día de hoy en la lucha por la vivienda y en la Huelga General. Cuando nos organizamos, podemos plantar cara a quienes pretenden convertir nuestras necesidades en un negocio. Esos avances nos dan motivos para seguir organizándonos y fuerzas para alimentar las luchas obreras.




Por eso os invitamos a participar, a acercaros a CNT, a organizaros con nosotras. A traer vuestras luchas, vuestras ideas y vuestras ganas de transformar las cosas. Este local es también vuestro.




Porque Valladolid la hacemos quienes la habitamos, quienes la sostenemos y quienes participamos en ella. Queremos hacer ciudad desde abajo, desde los barrios, desde el apoyo mutuo, desde la solidaridad de clase y desde la organización colectiva.




Hoy abrimos una puerta. Ahora toca llenarla de gente, de luchas, de encuentros y de vida.




¡Salud, organización y lucha! ¡Viva la CNT!

author: Sharon Zhang
title: New Evidence Allegedly Ties Trump to 11 Sexual Assaults Related to Epstein
content:
A new report notes several patterns of conduct that Trump and Epstein shared in recruiting victims.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The House Judiciary Committee Democrats have released a trove of evidence regarding allegations of sexual assault, including a new rape allegation, against President Donald Trump in relation to Jeffrey Epstein that the lawmakers say has been deliberately covered up by the Department of Justice.

The 50-page report, released Monday, contains testimony from 11 women who either accuse Trump of rape or sexual assault or say that they had been offered to Trump for sex by Epstein or Ghislaine Maxwell, with most cases happening in the 1990s.

The accounts were pulled together through interviews conducted by the committee, as well as FBI records and the portion of the Epstein files that have been released; the evidence was cross-referenced for timelines and corroboration of testimony between alleged victims. In all, the evidence sharply contrasts Trump’s claims that he was merely an acquaintance of Epstein, and instead paints a picture of Trump as a serial sexual assault perpetrator who collaborated closely with Epstein to find and traffic victims.

“These women have spoken to investigators and, in some cases, testified under oath, yet Trump’s Justice Department has shut down investigations, deliberately withheld evidence and, through Todd Blanche, prevented Ghislaine Maxwell from discussing a survivor whose account implicated Trump,” said the committee’s ranking member, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Maryland). “Trump’s Justice Department appears to be covering up these crimes to protect the President.”

Five women said that Trump raped or assaulted them while Epstein was present or was in his company, as detailed in the report. The report also reveals, for the first time, Trump’s alleged rape of Beatrice Keul, who has previously said that Trump groped her.

Keul said that she was recruited to attend the Donald J. Trump American Dream Pageant in November 1993, and was approached by Trump at an event in the Plaza Hotel, which he owned at the time. She says that her passport was taken away when she entered the pageant, and that Trump promised her favors, including saying that then-modelling agent Paolo Zampolli — who was recently fired from a high-level position within the State Department — would “take care” of obtaining a visa for Keul, who is from Switzerland.

The report notes that Trump promised Keul that he could get her admitted to New York University — a promise that Epstein often made “to lure in and then control his victims,” the report says.

After that conversation, Epstein approached her, introducing himself as “Don’s best friend.” As Trump looked on, Epstein also made promises to Keul, including that he would arrange for her to travel to Mar-a-Lago for a party. “You know I can take care of you. We organize many parties with Don,” Epstein allegedly told her. Keul says that Trump raped her later that day, after sending an associate to invite her to a hotel room for a meeting; she described the rape as “brutal.”

The report corroborates Keul and Trump’s meeting with accounts from other women who say that Trump and Epstein used the pageant as a “hunting ground” to prey upon women.

The Democrats also collate other assaults committed by Trump in relation to Epstein, including numerous occasions where Trump allegedly forcibly kissed or groped a girl or woman while Epstein was present, as well as compiled evidence on the alleged assaults of young girls like the case of “Katie Johnson.”

The report establishes several patterns of behavior by Trump and Epstein in relation to victims.

The report notes, for instance, that Trump called Keul several months after the alleged assault to reiterate his offer for favors. Similarly, Trump also sent a postcard to model Stacey Williams, who briefly dated Trump, several months after allegedly assaulting her in Epstein’s presence to invite her to Mar-a-Lago.

The report notes that Epstein had a practice of calling foreign models to visit them in Florida, and that: “Trump and Epstein seemed to share the same playbook for recruiting and abusing women, all the way down to the university they promised admission to and the timing of their follow-up phone calls.”

The Democrats also found that at least five women “related extremely similar facts regarding how Trump and Epstein were fiercely competitive in their pursuits of women and girls, and several related similar instances where Epstein showed off ‘his women’ to Trump but then reprimanded and punished them when Trump initiated or attempted to have sexual contact with them.”

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El batacazo de Lula, ¿la primera de una serie de derrotas para el eje Trump, Netanyahu y Milei?
content:
La elección en Brasil golpea fuerte a la alianza global de ultraderecha, que en los próximos días enfrentará dos paradas complejas: Israel este martes y el 3 de noviembre en EEUU. Sin brújula ni bajada de línea desde Washington, Milei sigue sin reconocer la victoria de Lula.







La victoria popular en la principal economía de América Latina puso un límite a lo que aparentaba ser un avance sin límite del bloque ultraderechista que a nivel global lidera Donald Trump, pero cuyas ramificaciones o poderes subsidiarios incluyen a Javier Milei.




En este sentido, la reelección de Lula también se puede interpretar como un reconocimiento de las políticas sociales frente al vaciamiento estatal, la reivindicación de los derechos ante la precarización de las condiciones de vida y la autodeterminación de los pueblos como contrapartida al alineamiento automático con los intereses corporativos globales.




Un mapa global bajo asedio y sin brújula 




El revés en la nación vecina expone la fragilidad de una entente internacional (¿Trump, Netanyahu y Milei, acaso?) que ahora aguarda con extrema tensión un calendario electoral complejo.




En cuestión de horas, el entramado ultraconservador enfrentará definiciones críticas en Medio Oriente, con la elección que definirá el futuro de Israel, mientras que el próximo 3 de noviembre la ciudadanía estadounidense concurrirá a las urnas en un escenario donde el liderazgo republicano acumula un marcado desgaste político.




La cadena de citas electorales pone a prueba la hegemonía de un esquema de poder que apostaba a consolidar su influencia a través de la polarización extrema y el disciplinamiento financiero de los Estados periféricos.




El repliegue de la Casa Rosada y el aislamiento regional 




Por lo pronto, el gobierno argentino no sale de su estado de parálisis ante el resultado en Brasil: habituado a tuitearse encima, Milei continúa en silencio y a la espera de un mensaje desde Washington, que aún no define si acepta o no la realidad o acompaña la impugnación del acto electoral que intentó ayer Flavio Bolsonaro.




Así, sin una bajada de línea clara proveniente de la capital estadounidense, el gobierno argentino profundiza su aislamiento político dentro del bloque sudamericano.




La semana pasada, durante la gira de Milei por España, ya habíamos visto otro signo de esta crisis en materia de política exterior, cuando ni siquiera los aliados ultraderechistas se dignaron a recibir al mandatario argentino.




La subordinación incondicional de la política exterior a los designios de Washington deja al Ejecutivo nacional expuesto ante el nuevo escenario geopolítico, evidenciando los costos de pretender subordinar los intereses soberanos a una agenda de choque ideológico en retirada.
