author: Publicación Abierta
title: Perdió y ahora quiere anular las elecciones: así juega la ultraderecha
content:
Perdió y ahora quiere anular las elecciones: así juega la ultraderecha




Pedir la prórroga y después llorar por ella




La ultraderecha tiene una curiosa manera de entender la democracia: acepta las reglas cuando le convienen, pero, cuando pierde, se convierte en víctima de una conspiración. No importa que los hechos contradigan su discurso ni que sus propias decisiones dejen en evidencia su hipocresía. Si gana, el resultado es legítimo; si pierde, hay fraude.




Brasil vuelve a ofrecernos un ejemplo de este comportamiento. Flávio Bolsonaro se niega a aceptar la derrota y anuncia que pedirá la anulación de la segunda vuelta electoral. Su principal argumento es la prórroga de dos horas en el horario de votación.




Pero aquí aparece un pequeño problema para el relato de la ultraderecha: esa ampliación del horario había sido solicitada por ambos bandos.




El Partido de los Trabajadores pidió más tiempo para votar ante los problemas de transporte que dificultaban el acceso a las urnas de miles de personas, especialmente en Bahía. Por su parte, el partido de Bolsonaro también solicitó dos horas adicionales de votación en diecisiete municipios de São Paulo, Paraná y Santa Catarina.




Cuando la prórroga podía favorecer sus intereses, era una medida necesaria. Cuando el resultado no les gusta, se convierte en un supuesto instrumento de fraude.




Esto no es defender la democracia. Es pretender que las reglas solo sean válidas cuando permiten ganar a los de siempre.




La cuestión es bastante sencilla: si existen irregularidades, deben investigarse con pruebas y mediante los procedimientos legales correspondientes. Pero utilizar una medida que el propio bando solicitó como argumento para cuestionar el resultado revela, cuando menos, una enorme contradicción política.




La democracia no consiste en ganar siempre. Consiste también en saber perder.




Y hay quienes, por su concepción autoritaria de la política, parecen incapaces de entender algo tan básico.




La ultraderecha que conocí en Brasil




Pasé seis meses en Brasil. No pretendo presentar esa experiencia como si bastara para conocer a fondo un país enorme, complejo y diverso. Pero fue tiempo suficiente para observar realidades que ayudan a comprender cómo funciona una parte de su política.




Brasil es un país de enorme riqueza cultural, con personas de orígenes muy diferentes y una sociedad atravesada por profundas desigualdades. Y es precisamente en esas desigualdades donde la ultraderecha encuentra uno de sus terrenos más favorables.




Lo que vi fue una política marcada, en demasiadas ocasiones, por el clasismo, el elitismo y la falta de empatía hacia las personas que viven en condiciones más difíciles.




Durante mi estancia, coincidiendo con un período electoral, pude observar prácticas de compra del voto: se ofrecía a la gente un saco de arroz a cambio de su apoyo en las urnas.




Pensemos en lo que significa esto. Una persona que vive en la pobreza puede verse sometida a la presión de aceptar una pequeña ayuda inmediata a cambio de comprometer una decisión política que afecta a su futuro y al de su familia.




Pero no confundamos a las víctimas con los responsables. El problema no es quien pasa hambre y acepta un saco de arroz; el problema es quien utiliza el hambre como instrumento para conseguir poder.




Cuando la necesidad se convierte en una herramienta electoral, la libertad política queda condicionada por la desigualdad económica. Y quien se aprovecha de esa situación no está defendiendo la libertad: está explotando la vulnerabilidad ajena.




También me llamó la atención el peso de determinadas iglesias evangélicas, algunas de las cuales funcionan como auténticas estructuras empresariales y políticas, capaces de movilizar a miles de personas y orientar su voto.




No se trata de cuestionar la libertad religiosa ni el derecho de cada persona a profesar sus creencias. Se trata de denunciar la utilización de la fe como instrumento de poder, especialmente cuando se combina con intereses económicos, discursos autoritarios y campañas políticas que favorecen a la ultraderecha.




En determinados sectores de estas redes religiosas confluyen, además, posiciones de apoyo a Estados Unidos y al sionismo político. Un fenómeno que merece ser analizado sin simplificaciones, porque no todas las iglesias evangélicas ni todas las personas creyentes piensan igual.




Y esto no sucede únicamente en Brasil. En diferentes países de América Latina, la desigualdad, la precariedad, el poder económico y la influencia de determinadas estructuras religiosas forman parte de una disputa política en la que la clase trabajadora suele pagar las consecuencias.




Las trabas para votar: la democracia también se defiende garantizando el voto




En unas elecciones, el derecho al voto no debería depender del barrio en el que vivas, del dinero que tengas en la cuenta bancaria o de la voluntad de tu empresario.




Si una persona no puede llegar a las urnas porque no tiene transporte, su derecho político existe sobre el papel, pero se ve limitado en la práctica.




Por eso, los problemas de transporte denunciados durante estos comicios no son una cuestión menor. Precisamente, la necesidad de facilitar que la ciudadanía pudiera ejercer su derecho al voto estuvo en el origen de la petición de ampliar el horario de votación.




También me han llegado testimonios de personas residentes en Brasil que hablan de empresas que habrían puesto obstáculos para que trabajadores de barrios humildes acudieran a votar, así como de situaciones en las que la policía habría preguntado a la ciudadanía adónde se dirigía y por quién pensaba votar.




Hay que ser rigurosos: son relatos que me han trasladado otras personas y que, por sí solos, no permiten afirmar que esos hechos estén probados. Es necesario investigarlos, contrastarlos y determinar si existieron prácticas ilegales o coacciones.




Pero tampoco debemos mirar hacia otro lado ante la posibilidad de que sucedan. La historia demuestra que el poder económico puede utilizar su influencia para condicionar la participación política y que la presión sobre las personas más vulnerables no siempre adopta formas evidentes.




El voto es secreto y libre. Ninguna empresa tiene derecho a decidir por quién votan sus trabajadores. Ningún poder político puede convertir a la policía en un instrumento de intimidación electoral.




Y cuando existen sospechas de presiones o irregularidades, lo que corresponde es investigarlas con seriedad, no utilizarlas selectivamente según quién gane o pierda.




También debemos prestar atención a las injerencias extranjeras y a los intereses económicos que operan en la política latinoamericana. Estados Unidos y las grandes multinacionales tienen una larga historia de influencia en la región. Pero, para demostrar una injerencia concreta en estas elecciones, hacen falta pruebas específicas. La historia sirve para identificar riesgos y formular preguntas; no sustituye la investigación de los hechos.




Cuando pierde la ultraderecha, el problema siempre es la democracia




Hay una característica recurrente en los movimientos ultraderechistas: presentan sus derrotas como injusticias y a sus adversarios como enemigos ilegítimos.




No aceptan fácilmente que una mayoría social pueda decidir un camino diferente al que ellos proponen. La ciudadanía es soberana cuando los apoya; cuando no lo hace, aparecen las acusaciones, las sospechas y los intentos de deslegitimar el resultado.




El problema va mucho más allá de una familia política o de un país concreto. Es una manera autoritaria de entender el poder.




La democracia no se reduce a introducir una papeleta en una urna cada cierto tiempo. También requiere que la ciudadanía pueda votar libremente, que se respeten los derechos, que los resultados se sometan a los procedimientos legales y que nadie esté por encima de las reglas.




Por eso, quien denuncia un fraude debe aportar pruebas. Y quien pretende anular unas elecciones debe demostrar que existen motivos legales para hacerlo. La derrota electoral, por sí sola, no es una irregularidad.




La ultraderecha no puede reclamar para sí una democracia a la carta: válida cuando gana e ilegítima cuando pierde.




Ganó el pueblo. Ahora toca defender lo que decidió




Cuando la ciudadanía acude masivamente a las urnas, está ejerciendo un derecho fundamental. Y cuando lo hace para impedir que avance una opción política que considera peligrosa para sus intereses, está expresando una decisión que debe ser respetada.




Pero tampoco debemos idealizar los procesos electorales ni pensar que una victoria resuelve por sí sola los problemas de una sociedad.




La pobreza no desaparece la noche electoral. La precariedad laboral no termina porque se cuente el último voto. La desigualdad no se resuelve simplemente impidiendo que gobierne la ultraderecha.




La derrota electoral de una fuerza reaccionaria puede abrir una oportunidad, pero esa oportunidad solo tendrá sentido si se traduce en mejoras reales para la mayoría social: salarios dignos, vivienda accesible, servicios públicos sólidos, derechos laborales y una distribución más justa de la riqueza.




La clase trabajadora no puede limitarse a votar cada cierto tiempo para frenar lo peor. Necesita también organización, conciencia política y capacidad para defender sus propios intereses.




Y debemos aprender de lo que sucede en América Latina. Las experiencias políticas de Argentina, Ecuador, Honduras o Chile son diferentes entre sí y no pueden meterse todas en el mismo saco, pero ofrecen ejemplos que merecen ser analizados para comprender el avance de las derechas, sus consecuencias sociales y las dificultades de las fuerzas populares para responder a sus desafíos.




El trumpismo no es una salida para quienes viven de su trabajo. Los discursos que prometen libertad mientras debilitan los derechos sociales, favorecen los intereses de los más ricos o alimentan el odio contra los más vulnerables no ofrecen una solución a los problemas de la mayoría.




Y esto también nos afecta en el Estado español.




No podemos pensar que estamos inmunizados frente a la ultraderecha ni que la historia va a resolver por nosotros lo que no seamos capaces de hacer colectivamente. El avance reaccionario no se combate únicamente denunciando a sus dirigentes. También se combate luchando contra las condiciones sociales que permiten que sus discursos ganen terreno.




Por eso, cuando llegue la hora de votar, no podemos quedarnos en casa y después lamentarnos de los resultados. Hay que participar, movilizarse e impedir que el descontento popular sea utilizado por quienes pretenden gobernar contra los intereses de la propia clase trabajadora.




A veces tendremos que votar por la opción que consideremos menos mala para evitar un mal mayor. Pero no debemos confundir esa decisión táctica con la renuncia a construir una alternativa propia, firme y transformadora.




La ultraderecha no tiene miedo de que la gente vote. Tiene miedo de que la gente comprenda quién defiende sus intereses y quién utiliza su necesidad para conseguir poder.




La democracia no se defiende aceptando que los poderosos hagan lo que quieran. Se defiende garantizando que el pueblo pueda decidir libremente y que su voluntad sea respetada.




Porque, cuando la clase trabajadora se organiza, toma conciencia de su fuerza y participa, deja de ser una simple espectadora de la política para convertirse en protagonista de su propia historia.




Y esa es la batalla que debemos librar aquí y allá: contra la explotación, contra el autoritarismo y contra todos los que pretenden que los privilegios de unos pocos estén por encima de los derechos de la mayoría.




 




¡Hasta la victoria siempre!




 




André Abeledo Fernández




La entrada 

Perdió y ahora quiere anular las elecciones: así juega la ultraderecha

 se publicó primero en 

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

title: Camcı: Urban Commune must be established to combat poverty
content:
Deep poverty in Diyarbakır (Amed) is reflected in unemployment, precarious working conditions, food insecurity and difficulties accessing basic necessities. According to 2024 data from the Ministry of Family and Social Services, 196,530 households in the city received social assistance, with the total amount reaching 4.47 billion Turkish lira. These figures reveal that poverty is not merely a matter of individual income loss but a structural problem affecting different aspects of social life.




Field research conducted in the Bağlar and Sur districts of Diyarbakır also reveals the tangible effects of deep poverty on neighbourhoods. Approximately 93 per cent of the women who participated in the research reported reducing their food purchases, while 95 per cent said they had cut spending on clothing. Many families are forced to take on debt to meet their basic needs.




Children living in damp homes affected by water leaks and inadequate heating are reportedly experiencing health problems. The fact that 196,530 households in Diyarbakır received social assistance in 2024 further illustrates the scale of poverty across the city.




Mehmet Şerif Camcı, former chair of the Sarmaşık Association, which was shut down by a Decree-Law (KHK), said that poverty was rooted in the economic policies pursued by the state in Kurdistan over the past century. He stressed that the solution could not be reduced to distributing aid. Camcı called for the establishment of an “Urban Commune” in the city to carry forward the principles and vision of the Sarmaşık Association.




‘State policies are deepening poverty’




Şerif Camcı discussed the reasons why poverty has become increasingly visible in the city, stressing that the problem cannot be understood solely in terms of unemployment and inadequate social support. While acknowledging the global dimensions of poverty, Camcı said that state economic policies were the decisive factor in Kurdistan and Diyarbakır.




Camcı said, “The primary factor deepening poverty in Kurdistan is policies created by human intervention, or more precisely, by the state. Poverty is, of course, a global problem. Another major cause lies in the choices made by capitalist modernity regarding production and distribution. However, what gives poverty its particular character and depth in Kurdistan, and especially in Diyarbakır, is the economic policies that the state has pursued in Kurdistan for the past century.”




‘After Sarmaşık, people were left at the mercy of the state's charity culture’




Camcı said that the closure of the Sarmaşık Association by decree-law had left a significant gap in the city's solidarity networks. He stressed that the association had not merely provided support to people in need but had also developed a model that strengthened social solidarity. Camcı also addressed the social consequences of capitalist relations of production and distribution: “Capitalist relations of production and distribution do not merely produce negative economic consequences. They also erode society's moral foundations, weaken its political reflexes and render people passive and powerless. The most important aspect of the Sarmaşık experience was that it enabled citizens to support one another through solidarity. At the same time, through the model and methods it developed, it helped turn solidarity and a sense of collective responsibility into a shared public consciousness capable of resisting the forces that undermine society.”




Camcı said that the closure of the association had weakened the ability of the city's poor to organise on the basis of solidarity. Criticising existing social assistance mechanisms, he continued: “After Sarmaşık, the urban poor were deprived of their capacity for self-defence. They were pushed back into the traditional relationship between the state and its citizens and left at the mercy of the state's culture of charity. Through its charity-based practices and the handouts it presents as support, the state is effectively telling people: ‘You depend on me. You can only survive through the assistance I provide.’”




‘An Urban Commune should be established based on Sarmaşık's principles’




Camcı also discussed the responsibilities of local authorities, civil society organisations, professional associations and the business community in combating poverty. He stressed that these actors should not confine their efforts to mechanisms that simply distribute aid.




Camcı stressed the need for a fundamental change in existing approaches to poverty: “Local authorities in particular, along with other actors in the city, must abandon assistance programmes that merely reproduce a poor imitation of the state's practices. Above all, these local actors must return to the principles of Sarmaşık. They should update the Sarmaşık model in keeping with the needs of the present and implement solidarity policies through an Urban Commune.”




‘Citizens must become active participants in solidarity’




Camcı added that combating poverty should not be limited to meeting basic needs such as food, housing, education and healthcare. He stressed that people should not be placed in a position of permanent dependence on assistance. Instead, the solution lay in developing a solidarity model in which citizens participate directly in decision-making and governance.




Mehmet Şerif Camcı emphasised that independent citizens' organisations should form the foundation of his proposed Urban Solidarity Commune. Camcı said, “Independent citizens' organisations must be the driving force behind the Urban Solidarity Commune. Institutions and other actors in the city should be involved from the outset and take the lead in establishing it. However, responsibility for managing the commune must be transferred to citizens themselves, particularly those experiencing poverty, as soon as possible. In other words, it must become a model of solidarity built by citizens for one another.”

title: ‘Terror-free Turkey’ rhetoric and security directive mark new university term
content:
The new academic year has begun under the shadow of security-oriented policies, alongside chronic problems such as inadequate student grants, safety concerns in dormitories run by the Credit and Dormitories Institution (KYK), dysfunctional democratic mechanisms and sexism on campuses. The Ministry of Interior's 17-point circular on “Security Measures at Universities”, issued on 9 September 2026, effectively treats campuses as “crime scenes”. Together with the Council of Higher Education's (YÖK) instruction to address the theme of “Terror-free Turkey” in the first lecture, it reflects the government's efforts to tighten its control over universities.




ANF spoke to Sude Şener from Labour Youth, Yasin Incekara from the Revolutionary Youth Union (DGB) and Özcan Berber from Student Activity about the new academic year, the government's security policies at universities and how students plan to organise in the coming period.




‘The Council of Higher Education promotes nationalism under the guise of peace’







 







Sude Şener from Labour Youth said the government and the Council of Higher Education were seeking to reduce the question of peace to a matter of “terrorism” through these measures. Şener said, “We must establish our own perspective in response to the presidential regime's attempts to restrict struggles for rights. Although the government fuels nationalist sentiments, what matters to us is the Kurdish people's struggle for freedom and peace.”




Özcan Berber from Student Activity said the government's recent policies, including its “Terror-free Turkey” initiative, were fundamentally aimed at neutralising social opposition. Berber said the demands of workers, students and the wider public, including growing calls for peace and democracy, were being suppressed through the rhetoric of “counterterrorism”. He said the government's rhetoric served a political agenda extending beyond security concerns, adding that even the most basic gatherings, information stands and awareness-raising activities on campuses were being treated as potential criminal offences.







 







Berber described the policy as follows: “As a continuation of neoliberal policies, they want to divide students, make them focus solely on their individual careers and prevent them from questioning social issues. They want a system in which we cannot trust one another or act collectively. They know that when we come together, we will begin to question this system. By isolating us, they aim to make us remain silent as even our most fundamental rights are taken away.”




Yasin Incekara, a member of the Revolutionary Student Union, said they had witnessed a series of attacks by the capitalist state against social opposition in general and universities in particular. Incekara said, “Organising events at universities under the banner of ‘Terror-free Turkey’ is seen as a means for the capitalist government, the reactionary AKP administration, to continue spreading its ideological and cultural propaganda on campuses. The events announced by the Council of Higher Education today are being presented as part of ‘Terror-free Turkey’. Yet we live in a country where even the most fundamental democratic rights and freedoms of all sections of social opposition are being trampled upon. The Council of Higher Education, which has promoted chauvinism, nationalism and other misguided ideas and attitudes in previous years, now appears to be taking certain steps under the banner of ‘Terror-free Turkey’ with an insincere approach.”




Incekara said the presidential regime viewed the peace process as an opportunity to bring a national liberation movement under its control and, in a sense, confine it within the boundaries of the existing system. He added that the growing repression at universities and attacks against students, which amounted to a veiled threat, clearly demonstrated how insincerely the government was approaching the process and how it was proceeding through deception.




‘They want to create an atmosphere of fear’




Sude Şener described the ministry's 17-point circular as a reflection of security-oriented policies on university campuses, saying that the deployment of police officers and detention vehicles outside universities was intended to marginalise the student movement. Şener said, “They are trying to turn universities into places where people are afraid, as though only a handful of students were raising their demands or taking action. We have never experienced a period with so many plainclothes police officers on campus and university entrances filled with riot police, police cars and detention vehicles.”




Şener said the atmosphere of fear being created on campuses was intended to isolate students, adding that police measures had nothing to do with student safety. She recalled the killing of Hilal Özdemir, a 15-year-old child worker who was shot dead on 30 August 2025 while working at a wedding at Boğaziçi University's Kennedy Lodge Social Facilities, pointing to where the real security failures lay.




Özcan Berber said the security circular issued by the Ministry of Interior was a continuation of similar directives introduced periodically over the past five years. He argued that these regulations effectively served as “authorisation documents”, legitimising the harsh treatment of students by university security personnel and police officers.







 







Berber said restrictive measures had been introduced at universities as the student youth movement gained strength around 19 March 2025. He recalled that students who set up information stands, distributed leaflets or voiced their demands in university cafeterias had been placed on police watchlists, detained in raids on their homes or seized in the streets as though they were being abducted, and subsequently criminalised. Berber said the latest circular indicated that repression would intensify in the new academic year, but insisted that no amount of pressure could prevent students from demanding their rights and seeking accountability from those responsible for abuses.




Yasin Incekara said they had been confronted with a directive from the Istanbul Governor's Office immediately after 19 March 2025 that effectively declared a state of emergency inside universities. He said the Ministry of Interior's 17-point circular was not the first of its kind, recalling previous attempts to discredit the revolutionary youth movement by labelling it as “terrorist”. He also referred to Ulaş Yıldırım, a member of the Revolutionary Youth Union, who was detained after being subjected to torture on campus and subsequently imprisoned.




Incekara said: “We were forced to confront a similar circular four years ago. Our most fundamental democratic rights have already been trampled upon, yet they are now trying to discredit all progressive and revolutionary activities at universities through the demagogy of terrorism.




On 19 March, we witnessed a youth uprising. We saw masses of young people confronting barricades in Saraçhane Square and students breaking through barricades at Istanbul University. The capitalist government is undoubtedly aware of the potential of the youth movement. That is why it now seeks to discredit our struggle at universities and the activities of students fighting for their rights, freedoms and future by branding them as terrorism.




Our comrade Ulaş Yıldırım from Ege University was arrested for intensifying the call to struggle against the fascist circulars sent to universities by the Council of Higher Education. Our fellow students at Ege University also set up a stand against this fascist circular under the slogan, ‘The circulars are yours, the universities are ours.’ They raised the call for resistance against the fascist repression and tyranny of the presidential regime from their campuses.




Ulaş was among those detained and subjected to torture. Our comrade was subsequently imprisoned unlawfully. We know that his imprisonment was not directed merely against one individual or an information stand, but against the entire youth movement.”




The impact of the economic crisis on universities




Sude Şener said students were facing deepening poverty as a result of the Medium-Term Programme (OVP) and cuts to public budgets, alongside growing repression on campuses. She drew attention to rising prices for basic necessities, saying students at Boğaziçi University had staged mass protests against an increase in the price of a cafeteria meal to 85 Turkish lira. Similar increases had also been introduced at Middle East Technical University, Istanbul University, Namık Kemal University and several universities in Kayseri.




Şener said growing poverty was forcing students to work under harsh and precarious conditions. “Working while studying should not be a necessity. The most fundamental need of young people is to intensify the struggle for the right to free, quality education,” she said.




Özcan Berber said poverty and the economic crisis affected not only students but society as a whole, pointing to the direct connection between declining educational standards on campuses and the policies of the state and capital. He said students were effectively struggling to survive amid rising transport costs, inadequate nutrition and exorbitant dormitory fees.




Berber criticised the allocation of university budgets, saying funding for social sciences, literature, philosophy and other socially oriented disciplines was being reduced, while public resources and university funds were being channelled into security mechanisms and the arms industry.




He said even university cafeterias funded through public budgets were being operated for profit. Berber also recalled that academics at foundation universities were being dismissed en masse and replaced by government-appointed staff. He added that engineering students were being drawn into projects run by companies developing military technologies because of their economic hardship, placing them in an ethical dilemma.




Yasin Incekara said the Revolutionary Youth Union had identified the main concerns and priorities of young people, emphasising the importance of a united struggle. He outlined these priorities as follows: “We believe young people have four fundamental concerns. The first and greatest is the economic crisis. Closely connected to this is the lack of prospects for the future, alongside increasing fascist repression and tyranny. Another major concern is the imperialist wars and aggression taking place in our region and internationally. As university students and young people, we face many problems. We have called for an organised struggle against these problems from the very beginning. Therefore, as we develop our course of struggle, we must organise around these fundamental issues and build a united struggle based on our most concrete demands.”




‘United struggle against hopelessness’




Sude Şener said they would organise faculty by faculty in the new academic year under the slogan “Democratic, autonomous universities; an independent, democratic country”. She cited international student movements as examples of resistance to the wave of hopelessness created by the government and said: “From France to Germany, from young people taking to the streets for Palestine in New York to those resisting economic policies in Argentina, a powerful wave of protest is rising across the world. We know that the same anger is simmering in Turkey. We can only overcome the atmosphere of fear designed to isolate us by drawing strength from our unity.”




Şener added that femicides, violence against women, sexual harassment and many other issues facing young women today, including the killing of Hilal Özdemir, were among the most urgent concerns of the student movement. She said the struggle of young women on campuses, like many other areas of resistance, needed greater unity and strength. Şener announced that Labour Youth would enter the new academic year determined to mobilise all its resources towards this goal.




Özcan Berber said students and different sections of society, despite their diverse backgrounds, were suffering as a result of the same underlying crisis. He described the central task facing the student movement as follows: “The problems faced by a student who grew up in Istanbul and protests against rising cafeteria prices, a Kurdish student who comes from their hometown and faces discrimination because of their mother tongue or identity, a woman resisting sexual harassment on campus, or a miner killed in a workplace accident all stem from the same crisis. Campuses are our living spaces, and decisions concerning them must be made by the university community.”




Berber concluded by saying that resistance to war, poverty, declining academic standards and political repression could only succeed through a united social struggle that exposed the common source of all these crises.




Yasin Incekara said, “The Mecca Alliance is being signed, and messages are being sent that imperialist wars in our region will intensify.” He continued: “The AKP government aims to suppress all young people who speak out against this system and, beyond simply expressing their opposition, actively struggle against it. In response, we once again declare that our organised struggle will continue and that we will raise the banner of resistance. As the Revolutionary Youth Union, we call on young people to organise a struggle around our most concrete, legitimate and just demands during this period and to build a united revolutionary youth movement on common platforms.”

author: Unknown
title: Karamus: Joint national strategy essential for Kurdish UN representation
content:
The international conference organised by the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) to secure representation and observer status for the Kurdish people at the United Nations (UN) was held in Brussels, the capital of Belgium, on 3 October 2026. Political representatives, academics and experts from all four parts of Kurdistan and the diaspora attended the conference, which discussed the diplomatic path towards Kurdish representation at the UN and the next stages of the process.




KNK Co-Chair Ahmet Karamus spoke to ANF about the work to be carried out following the conference. He highlighted the importance of political contacts in South Kurdistan (Başûr), establishing a commission involving all four parts of Kurdistan and the diaspora, and preparing a joint roadmap.




Karamus said efforts to secure observer status at the UN should be developed with the participation of different political and social groups and coordinated through joint diplomatic work.




Karamus explained that the idea for the conference had emerged at a KNK congress and was followed by approximately a year of preparations. He said discussions had been held with different groups, proposals had been evaluated and efforts had been made to ensure broad participation in the conference.




Karamus described the conference's objectives and preparations: “This project was not the result of a single day's work. It was first proposed at a KNK interim congress meeting. We then spent approximately a year preparing, meeting with different groups and evaluating proposals. “Our aim was to launch a serious initiative to secure recognition of the Kurdish people's status and their representation at the UN. That is why we wanted all political parties, organisations, social institutions and experts to participate in the conference. Bringing together representatives from all four parts of Kurdistan and the diaspora was important to us.”




Karamus said the conference had attracted broad participation and received a significant response from the Kurdish public. He added that support for the initiative from different political groups was particularly important. He said the conference should not remain merely a meeting and that its decisions needed to be followed by organised and coordinated efforts.




Karamus clarified that the initiative was not seeking full UN membership. Instead, its objective was to secure international recognition of the Kurdish people and their representation through observer status. He pointed out that observer status differed from the full membership held by UN member states and underlined the importance of international recognition of the Kurdish people's existence.




‘This is no longer KNK's project, but the Kurdish people's project’




Karamus said the scope and responsibility of the initiative had changed following the conference and that it should no longer be regarded as a project belonging solely to KNK. He said the participation of different political and social groups in the conference and their support for the initiative were important in this respect.




Karamus said: “With the conference, this initiative ceased to be a KNK project and became a project of the Kurdish people. Therefore, responsibility for it no longer rests solely with KNK. The work to secure recognition of the Kurdish people's status and their representation concerns every section of society. All political parties, institutions, social groups and the Kurdish people as a whole must participate in this process.”




Karamus said advancing the initiative would require not only political support but also an institutional structure and a shared approach to working together. He added that the collective determination demonstrated at the conference needed to be translated into concrete action.




Political contacts in South Kurdistan




Karamus said they had held meetings with political actors in South Kurdistan during preparations for the conference, including representatives of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and the Kurdistan Region Presidency. He said these meetings were important for assessing the positions of different political groups towards the initiative and broadening the scope of the work.




Karamus said the political contacts established in South Kurdistan should also continue in other parts of Kurdistan. He added that meetings would be held with political parties, institutions and social groups in North Kurdistan (Bakur), Rojava and East Kurdistan (Rojhilat). He also pointed to the importance of involving Kurdish institutions and representatives in the diaspora.




Karamus acknowledged that political conditions and approaches differed across the regions and said the views of all groups needed to be considered to develop a joint approach. He said the initiative for national representation should not remain confined to any particular political group but should be developed through the participation of different sections of Kurdish society.




A commission representing all four parts of Kurdistan and the diaspora




Karamus said one of the most important priorities following the conference was establishing a commission to coordinate the work. He said the commission should represent all four parts of Kurdistan and the diaspora, take responsibility for efforts to secure Kurdish representation at the UN and maintain relations with different groups.




Karamus said preparations for establishing the commission were continuing. He said: “Certain mechanisms need to be established for this project to move forward. Institutions, committees and commissions must be formed, and the scope of the work must be expanded. We want to establish a commission that will take responsibility for coordinating all these efforts. This commission should coordinate the work aimed at securing recognition of the Kurdish people's status and their representation at the UN.




We are continuing our discussions with all political parties, organisations and social institutions on this matter. The structure of the commission is also extremely important. Kurds from all four parts of Kurdistan and those living in the diaspora must be represented on it. Representation must be ensured democratically. Different groups must be able to express their views and participate in the work. This is not something that can be carried out by a single institution. If we are talking about representing the Kurdish people, the different sections of Kurdish society must also have a place on the commission.”




Karamus said the commission should not be limited to conducting political contacts and highlighted the importance of carrying out its work regularly and in a coordinated manner. He added that the commission's responsibilities needed to be clearly defined, proposals from different groups evaluated and these proposals developed into a joint working plan.




‘Academics, politicians and diplomats must contribute’




Ahmet Karamus said the commission would need contributions not only from political representatives but also from academics, intellectuals, historians, diplomats and people with experience in bureaucracy. Karamus said discussions were continuing with people who had knowledge and experience in different fields, adding that their expertise should be used in developing the initiative for Kurdish representation.




Karamus said: “We are holding discussions with academics, intellectuals, historians, diplomats and people working in diplomacy. We are also meeting with people who have experience in bureaucracy. We want to benefit from their knowledge and experience. However, our approach is not to carry out all the work ourselves and then hand it over to others. For this project to move forward, different groups must take responsibility and contribute to the work.”




Karamus said society should also be part of the process and announced plans to establish a digital platform through which people could submit their proposals directly. He said allowing Kurds living in different regions and countries to communicate their views to the commission, have their proposals considered and contribute to its work would further strengthen the process.




Karamus also said: “We are preparing a website where everyone will be able to send their views and proposals to the commission electronically. People must be able to make their voices heard and put forward their suggestions. These proposals should be taken seriously and considered in the work to be carried out. We want to create a space where everyone can express their ideas and make a contribution.”




Karamus said it was important for different sections of society to take ownership of the national representation initiative. He added that everyone working in political, academic, diplomatic and social fields could contribute according to their knowledge and experience.




Karamus also pointed to the need for the work to be conducted in an organised and disciplined manner, with clearly defined duties and responsibilities for the commission. He said that while the process should remain open to everyone's contributions, its coordination and institutional structure must also be secured.




‘We must properly analyse the threats to the Kurdish people's existence’




Karamus said the national representation initiative could not be considered separately from regional and international developments. He pointed out that developments in the Middle East, the policies of international powers and events across all four parts of Kurdistan were decisive for the future of the Kurdish people.




Karamus continued: “When we look at the global situation, developments in the Middle East and conditions in all four parts of Kurdistan, we see that we are facing serious dangers and threats. Of course, the Kurdish people have also made gains. However, the Kurdish movement has suffered serious setbacks over the past year or two. Developments in Rojava and other areas, the direction of international politics in the region and the conditions that have emerged are not working in favour of the Kurdish people. That is why we must analyse the current situation correctly. We must recognise the dangers we face and shape our assessments of the future accordingly.




We must achieve unity among the Kurdish people, strengthen our collective will and develop a national strategy. We must draw the necessary lessons from what has happened and develop a common approach that will secure our future. 




We need to struggle for recognition of the Kurdish people's existence. This recognition will not come about on its own. Work must be carried out in politics, lobbying, diplomacy and international relations. For this to happen, all political parties, organisations, social groups and individual members of the Kurdish people must assume serious national responsibility.”




‘We must build national unity while preserving our differences’




Karamus said the call for national unity did not mean eliminating the different political views and circumstances across the four parts of Kurdistan. He said it was necessary to identify common ground and act together while respecting those differences.




He said: “We may have differences and disagreements. Not everyone has to think alike. However, we must be able to identify what we have in common and develop mutual understanding while respecting our differences. We need a common national strategy for the future of the Kurdish people. In developing this strategy, we must take into account the conditions in each part of Kurdistan. We can no longer act according to the circumstances of the past. We are now in a period when the Kurdish people can protect their achievements through their unity, national will and collective strength. That is why political parties, organisations and social groups must act together on issues of common concern. We can develop a common strategy while preserving our differences and continue our work on that basis.”




Karamus added that national unity should not be limited to political statements but strengthened through joint efforts. He highlighted the importance of political parties and institutions developing relations on shared issues, strengthening ties between the different parts of Kurdistan and working towards common objectives.




Joint diplomacy, Newroz and national commemorations




Ahmet Karamus said the need for joint action should extend beyond diplomatic initiatives to social and cultural activities.




Karamus said: “In the coming period, we must work together in diplomacy, both in the diaspora and in our homeland. We must pursue joint diplomacy and collectively uphold our national symbols. We must also act together during Newroz celebrations, national days and commemorations of the tragedies experienced by the Kurdish people. We must conduct our political activities through democratic methods and organise joint activities in Europe, the diaspora and Kurdistan. Different groups need to act together and stand side by side on issues of common concern. This is a responsibility we all share.”




Karamus said the threats facing the Kurdish people made joint action even more necessary, adding that everyone could contribute to the process according to their resources and areas of activity. He said, “Every political party, every organisation, every institution and every section of Kurdish society must support this process. Everyone should contribute while maintaining their own distinct identity and perspectives. This is not merely an initiative. It is a responsibility concerning the existence, future and international recognition of the Kurdish people. We must all take on this responsibility.”

title: Announcement on Integration in Shengal to be made today
content:
Preparations are continuing on Mount Shengal ahead of the announcement. It has been learned that commanders from YBŞ and YJŞ, along with Iraqi army officials, will attend the ceremony.




The announcement is expected to outline the details of the official integration of the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ) into the Iraqi army.




All preparations for the formal announcement of the integration have been completed, and the parties are expected to make a joint statement in the coming hours.




In addition to YBŞ and YJŞ commanders, 60 fighters, Êzîdî mothers, and Êzîdî religious scholars are also expected to be present at the announcement.




Representing Iraq, military commanders, the Governor of Mosul, Iraq’s Deputy Prime Minister, and numerous other Iraqi officials are also reported to be attending the ceremony.

title: Iraqi Government: We reaffirm our full responsibility to protect Yazidi rights
content:
Sabah Numan, spokesperson for the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office, shared details of the Iraqi government’s statement regarding the integration of YBŞ and YJŞ into Iraq’s security institutions.




The statement read as follows: “Under the leadership of Mr Ali Zeydi, Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, an official ceremony will be held today, 26 Monday October 2026, to formalise the military status of the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and integrate them into Iraq’s security forces. The ceremony will also mark the process of transferring responsibility for the security of Mount Shengal to federal forces.




This process is taking place within the framework of the policy of regulating weapons under state control, as decided by the Iraqi government and incorporated into its official programmes and ministerial directives. It is also regarded as an achievement that will establish the foundation for assuming responsibility for the security situation in Shengal.




In this context, the Iraqi government greatly values the significant and unique sacrifices made by the Yazidi community in the face of terrorism and extremist agendas targeting all of Iraq, and particularly the Shengal region.




This step once again demonstrates the commitment of members of the Yazidi community to national principles. On this basis, the Iraqi Constitution prohibits any activities outside the legal framework. This message also makes clear that bearing arms is not an end in itself, but a means of defending the country in accordance with the Constitution and the law.




Adhering to the decisions of the federal government will help strengthen state authority, support national decision-making processes, and enhance state institutions’ capacity to uphold their constitutional obligations and protect the rule of law.




The Iraqi government once again reaffirms its full responsibility to protect the rights of the Yazidi people, who resisted terrorism and suffered grave injustices in the process, including loss of life, injuries, the abduction of family members, and displacement. It also reiterates its commitment to providing compensation to those who lost loved ones as a result of terrorist attacks and to rebuilding Shengal.”

author: Mada Masr
title: Maybe, tomorrow
content:
On a good week, our job feels like the ideal job. You don’t need to wrestle with making sense of the big picture and then pull a break to focus on your own life. Your life is all about trying to make sense with and for everyone around you, and to do so, you summon your tools, nourish them, sharpen them. These include looking for the facts, especially the hidden ones. You sift through material, you speak to sources, you go back to the material in ongoing loops. You need the history to draw the context. It changes all understanding of facts. You need the social sciences to read the data critically. You need the aesthetics of form to weave the story and start journeying it to the public. You need some philosophy for the whole thing to come together, because there is just a lot of paradox. You are also tempering a little with time, because understanding might instruct a thing or two for tomorrow. 




Isn’t one fortunate, theoretically speaking, to be a journalist? We know you might not agree with us.




This past week would have been an ideal one for all the above. First, the president announced, for the first time in Egyptian modern history, what was widely read as a serious intention for a transition of power by the end of this term. This is while a multilayered war continues to change the shape of the region, 

with Egypt’s looming intervention

. And back at home, as part of the domestic power calculus, a six-day forum was rolling on broadcast to showcase the government’s achievements in the last years. In the background, the Egyptian pound kept losing value and now the dollar crossed an unprecedented LE55 mark. 




Throughout this week, we 

raised our questions

 about the president’s plans and published a 

podcast

 reflecting on the different possibilities of this shift in mode of rule, but, also, what is it that we should be doing now, as political subjects, in the wait? What does waiting politically look like? In our investigative work, we get to inhabit a common triumphalist moment in journalism where hard questions are answered and the answer is usually difficult to get, shocking to receive, scandalizing for those in power. But on some days, when we don’t have the answers, as in a significant moment where the president is speaking about power transfer and a shift in the mode of rule, we don’t shy away from asking questions and publishing them. It’s a moment where journalism embeds itself more tightly with the people it is rooted in, collectively wondering: what’s next? 




This past week, we also published this 

piece

 about the return of some families to their villages occupied by Israel in South Lebanon in the recent war. We have been looking into the region, not from the standpoint of a regional media, but more out of a sense of urgency to record where drastic change is unfolding, whether as tangible reality on the ground, or as ideation by those in power from their closed rooms. We have expanded in different directions because that’s a way to make sense of what’s happening. On the same day, we published our weekly 

Palestine bulletin

, a bulletin that started with the genocide in 2023, where we keep reporting about Gaza and Palestine as a whole, even after a ceasefire inked on a paper was sold to the world as the end of the war. On the weekend, we published the weekly 

Sudan bulletin

, a space that has been gathering developments on the ground and on power politics, highlighting why it is important not to sever Sudan from the regional calculus. 




In the same week, we joined an initiative of a collective newsroom made up of eight independent media in the region, to fill up the silenced space of Matsda2sh, the fact-checking platform whose entire newsroom of six journalists were arrested last month. Together with the other organizations, we worked on fact-checking information presented at the aforementioned government forum. 




To this date, our colleagues in Matsda2sh are still being held in remand detention. Some reported being subjected to mistreatment, and all of them shared with their families upon first prison visits the feeling that they are enclosed in a nightmare that has no end. 




We have worked with some of the six journalists before they moved on to Matsda2sh; we knew them as young, aspiring journalists wanting to genuinely learn how to understand what is happening around us and how to communicate a record of this understanding to the broader public. Before it became a nightmare, they also thought journalism could be an ideal job, especially in tumultuous times.  




We are going to court on Tuesday on accusations that we are an illegal entity. It is an interruption through which we repeat our own version of the story uttered against us time and again, dancing with absurdity time and again: We are a legal entity because we are always seeking to be legal, we are defending the law against its constant recoil as a tool of power, so much so that it is risking losing itself to total nullity, a crisis for the whole country. We are not just fighting for ourselves, but to re-expand the law as it should be, to be a space through which we can operate, a space in which our colleagues in Matsda2sh and every other journalist in custody can be free. The real threat to those in power, before it being a threat to us, is the entire removal of that space.




We understand that interruptions and disruptions are normal parts of this ideal job of journalism, when it entails making sense against the grain of power, power that thinks of itself as consolidated, locked, comfortable. The trick is always in how to absorb the rupture and return, how to delay the end if an end has to be imposed upon you, how to keep today going, on our terms, perhaps tomorrow too. This is perhaps how we learned to wait in the dark, in times of crisis, to be active in the waiting, regardless of that which we are fearing the wait for.




We understand that a sword will most likely be raised above our heads very soon. Even the faintest spark shakes darkness to the grounds. We still think of all of this as an interruption, because that’s how you fight a political fight. You remember that time is not linear, ends are not pre-written. You are powered by the uncertainty of the maybe.




And so, in this ongoingness of normalcy and crisis, perhaps a feature of our world today, but also a mastery we have mastered in the region, in learning to live in the world with the genocide on Gaza, we will go to court on Tuesday while continuing to publish Sunday through Saturday. 




And we are open to receiving love letters in the middle.




There is something psychically bordering on horror when you see your own image as a journalist, instead of your journalism, surfacing on repeat through the scrolling movement of the Internet. But, in a moment like this, there is no tomorrow without solidarity and journalism. Put together, they point to the collective that springs out in a moment of danger. It’s a community of our imagining that comes down tangibly, a journalism receiving its feedback loop, a people united in their desire to know, to think together and to defend and protect that space from closure.




We are reassured, once more, that the journalism we do is not for itself. And together with the few independent voices wrestling with sense-making and truth-snatching in a world where power condescendingly tells us to give up, this is not just about a small 

us

, Mada Masr, but a much bigger 

we.

  

The post 

Maybe, tomorrow

 first appeared on 

Mada Masr

.

author: dev
title: La bande à « Balance ton Claude »
content:
Nous avons déjà longuement abordé les ressorts de l'« affaire Thélyson Orélien » dans nos pages (nous renvoyons, entre autres, à 

cet excellent texte de Jean Claude Noel

). L'enquête qui suit porte sur ses délateurs, la bande à « Balance ton Claude » du nom du compte X à l'origine de la polémique. On y découvre que l'affaire Thélyson Orélien, est un double écran de fumée qui masque une convergence d'intérêts, financiers, idéologiques et géopolitiques, entre l'industrie de l'IA, les libertariens de la Silicon Valley, les christo-fascistes de l'administration Trump, et leurs imitateurs bien-de-chez-nous.




« Démarche complètement apolitique », « lanceur d'alerte », anonymat nécessaire pour éviter les attaques 

ad hominem

… Toutes ces auto-justifications offertes par la bande à « Balance ton Claude », qui est derrière la polémique Thélyson Orélien, servent à ripoliner une opération idéologique, menée par un groupe de jeunes « libéraux-conservateurs » (doux euphémisme), très actifs dans l'espace médiatique, depuis les colonnes du Figaro, et les fabriques à propagande du projet Périclès. En outre, ces alarmes hypocrites s'inscrivent dans les récits 

IApocalyptiques

 déployés par l'industrie pour faire gonfler investissements publics et privés. Une bulle profitant surtout aux nouveaux technoligarques, qui sont prêts à jeter la démocratie et l'humanité entière dans le chaudron de la valorisation et de la domination sans partage.




Les problèmes posés par la rédaction 

I

A

ssistée 

cachent une autre forme d'imposture : les allégations de neutralité politique répétées par la bande à « Balance ton Claude ». Une fine équipe, composée de cinq membres, d'après le premier accusateur anonyme sorti du bois

 [

1

]

, et qui n'a pas eu droit à la même attention que Thélyson Orélien.




« 

Notre démarche était complètement apolitique

 [

2

]

 

 »

, déclarait ainsi Samuel Fitoussi dans 

Le Point

, après avoir tombé le masque. Pourtant, le profil de nos Claudettes risque d'affoler votre détecteur à 

bullshit

. Pas besoin du logiciel Pangram, vous allez voir, pour confondre ces immenses tartufes, présentés comme des « 

lanceurs d'alerte 

ayant

 l'amour de la vérité chevillé au coeur 

et dénonçant les impostures intellectuelles

 [

3

]

 ».




Samuel Fitoussi




Commençons par vous donner une idée de l'honnêteté intellectuelle de M. Fitoussi. Quelques heures après avoir lancé la polémique sur le livre de Thélyson Orélien depuis le compte X « Balance ton Claude » (encore anonyme à ce moment-là), le chroniqueur du 

Figaro

 intervient sur Radio J, où il déclare : « 

comme aujourd'hui, le RN n'est pas un parti particulièrement violent ou antisémite ou quoi que ce soit, [renvoyer dos à dos les extrêmes] c'est en fait banaliser la dangerosité de cette gauche pro-Hamas...

 »




La journaliste lui fait alors remarquer que l'extrême-droite est quand même « 

très proche de l'AfD, un parti néo-nazi

 ». Réponse de Samuel Fitoussi : « 

J'ai beaucoup de critiques à l'égard de ces partis. Pour le RN, par exemple, je les trouve étatistes, socialistes, relativement incompétents

 […] 

mais je pense qu'il faut reconnaître que les choses ont évolué, que le RN n'est plus le RN d'il y a 30 ans, et c'est même plus le RN d'il y a dix ans, qui voulait sortir de l'Union européenne, et c'est plus le RN antisémite

 [

4

]

 ». 

L

'amour de la vérité chevillé au cœur

, on vous dit.




Par ailleurs, l'intérêt de M. Fitoussi pour les implications de l'IA générative n'est pas pure curiosité, étant donné qu'il travaille pour le fonds d'investissement FRST CAPITAL, spécialisé dans l'industrie naissante du 

machine learning 

(un des domaines informatiques que l'on trouve derrière la formule générique « IA », et dont les avancées ont notamment permis le développement des « grands modèles de langage » – ou 

LLM

 – comme le célèbre ChatGPT).




Incidemment, FRST CAPITAL est une ancienne filiale d'OTIUM CAPITAL, la holding de Pierre-Edouard Stérin, milliardaire christo-libertarien qui utilise ses gains pour financer un projet de conquête politique par l'extrême-droite, baptisé « Périclès » (pour Patriotes, Enracinés, Résistants, Identitaires, Chrétiens, Libéraux, Européens, Souverainistes), et doté d'un budget de 150 millions d'euros

 [

5

]

.




Cerise sur le gâteau : FIRST CAPITAL n'investit pas seulement dans les « laboratoires d'IA », mais également dans la fabrique d'opinion, en produisant des sondages douteux sur la popularité d'Elon Musk ou l'attrait des Français pour un Pédégé de la République

 [

6

]

.




Samuel Fitoussi baigne dans l'ambiance de San Francisco, très bien décrite ici par Pierre Entremont, associé-fondateur de FRST CAPITAL :







« Ce qu'il se passe en ce moment à San Francisco est complètement dingue. Des gamins de 20 ans travaillent 18h par jour et dorment sous leurs bureaux pour arriver à l'AGI les premiers, tant ils sont persuadés - à tort ou à raison - que c'est le dernier moment pour “escape the permanent underclass” [échapper à la sous-classe humaine non-détentrice de capital qui serait privée de travail et de revenus par une automatisation généralisée] qui définira alors le reste de l'humanité. Des startups atteignent $100m de CA en 12 mois, $500m en 24. Plusieurs entreprises investissent des centaines de milliards par an pour grandir à des rythmes jamais vus, et prévoient de passer la barre des 10 000 milliards de valorisation prochainement. Les grands CEO, anticipant l'ère de l'abondance et de la fin du travail, appellent à en finir avec la pensée de la rareté et des jeux à sommes nulles pour se mettre à la hauteur de l'époque qui verra enfin la culture s'affranchir de la nature, après 2,5 millions d'années d'évolution humaine. Même les pessimistes sont optimistes. Les révolutions technologiques produisent parfois des bulles financières, concèdent-ils, mais l'explosion de la bulle IA ne sera d'après eux qu'un soubresaut de court-terme, négligeable à l'échelle de l'enjeu et du développement de l'humanité.

 [

7

]

 »







Voilà sans doute pourquoi, parallèlement à ses « alertes » sur la catastrophe du « slop » (production 

IAgénérée

 de qualité médiocre), qui ne sont qu'une variante des discours

title: Le 17 octobre ou le retour du ludique
content:
« Délinquance d'opportunisme », « grève-vacances », « absence de maturité politique », « cosplays enfantins », « destructions irréfléchies », « actes de rages », tous ces énoncés ennemis utilisés pour disqualifier l'insurrection en cours ont vu naître leurs antonymes politiques : « réappropriation matérielle », « revendications pour des conditions d'études », « conscientisation politique », « mises en scènes joyeuses », etc. Le 17 octobre aura été l'occasion d'une production tous azimuts d'une quantité faramineuse de contre-interprétations, de textes théoriques, d'hypothèses, sur ce qui anime le mouvement. Pourtant, une dimension souterraine à ses gestes et partout omniprésente nous paraît encore être ignorée : le 

ludique

. Sans revenir à un examen approfondi des causes sous-jacentes du mouvement, ni à une lecture prescriptive de sa suite—guidée le plus souvent par l'intention de « manager » le mouvement—, nous tenions ici à ressaisir la passion à l'œuvre derrière les gestes émeutiers et la fougue lycéenne.







« Je te tiens, tu me tiens, 


Par la barbichette, 


Le premier de nous deux qui rira 


Aura une tapette »




Début de la partie 




Notre hypothèse, pouvant coexister avec d'autres, consiste à penser que le « ludique » entre en jeu comme une notion singulièrement opérante pour saisir l'activité émeutière fondamentalement joyeuse autour de laquelle se sont noués et organisés, affectivement, les subjectivités ayant pris part à l'insurrection.




Que ce soit dans les charivaris, carnavals ou les parades de lycéens déguisés en super-héros de comics, la chose est connue : le jeu couplé au rire constitue un domaine indéniable de tactiques et de ruses permettant de se défaire temporairement de l'emprise d'un dominant. Mais ce ludique-là n'est ni un simple renversement formel des positions ou une parodie impuissante du pouvoir. Il est une réfutation en acte des techniques apprises de protestation et autres gémissements revendicatifs. La lassitude des milieux militants traditionnels laissée derrière, et voilà déjà qu'un nouvel horizon d'actes joyeux et créatifs se dessine.




L'habileté stratégique lycéenne réside dans la réutilisation de codes jugés inoffensifs et beaucoup trop enfantins pour être réprimés et considérés : les super-héros, les déguisements, les trends Tik Tok, etc… Or, à chaque fois, ils les reconduisent dans un contexte d'assaut et d'offensives, entraînant la confrontation physique ou non, envers les forces de l'ordre. Exemple : Captain America lance une attaque suivie par des centaines d'individus en noirs. Elles mettent davantage encore à nu l'illégitimité foncière des policiers à user de la force. Et puis ; que peut faire un policier contre un Batman qui entame une danse devant lui ? Enrager, frapper ou éprouver son ennui, endurer sa docilité (ces deux dernières obligations étant habituellement réservées aux lycéens). Comment arrêter une battle d'aura, apothéose de l'absurde et de l'humour ? D'aucune autre manière qu'en rabat-joie. Une dernière : que peut faire un policier devant un militant de gauche, un prosélyte quelconque, mégaphone à la main, qui prononce les mêmes mots d'ordres quelconques ? L'ignorer comme un décor quelconque.




Lucidité(s) retrouvé(s) 




L'un des attributs manifeste des complicités en présence avant et pendant le 17 octobre (gen Z, étudiants, intérimaires, banlieusards, subalternes, gilets jaunes, bref, subjectivités en voie de prolétarisation) c'est sa propension au « ludique ». Le geste anodin de déclencher une battle d'aura comme de briser une vitrine, même s'ils n'entretiennent aucune équivalence de fond, manifestent ce même rapport joueur à l'imposition métropolitaine d'un espace marchand. On aurait tort d'opposer actes de rage, de destructions et manifestation d'une joie retrouvée, ou autrement dit, actes de pillage, de mettre le feu, et jeu de rôles, battle d'aura, déguisement en super-héros. Ils condensent et procèdent des mêmes affects : en synthèse, une joie de détruire ou l'anticipation de détruire avec joie. Contre les mouvements et déplacements contenus, réguliers et monotones, donc toujours assignés à un but du monde urbain et marchand, ils opposent et démontrent aussi la possibilité hic et nunc d'une activité libre, d'une reprise en main de l'espace, sans but énoncé ni fonction préétablie. Dans Homo Ludens, Huizinga définit le jeu comme suit :




« 

on peut (…) définir le jeu comme une action libre, sentie comme fictive et située en dehors de la vie courante, capable néanmoins d'absorber totalement le joueur ; une action dénuée de tout intérêt matériel et de toute utilité ; qui s'accomplit en un temps et dans un espace expressément circonscrits

 » et plus loin, 

« (il, le jeu) suscite dans la vie des relations de groupes s'entourant volontiers de mystère ou accentuant par le déguisement leur étrangeté vis-à-vis du monde habituel ».




L'appropriation matérielle par la destruction de biens ou l'auto réduction et l'amusement sous ses diverses formes de mise en scène se retrouvent dans le ludique. Enfin, il n'y a rien d'étonnant dans ce retour du ludique si on le comprend et l'inscrit dans le long déclin de l'institution scolaire qui a cherché sans relâche à conjurer tous les avatars possibles du jeu et du réappropriation de la vie quotidienne : distractions, amusement, détournement, et jusqu'à même récemment usage du téléphone. Le ludique doit être différenciée de la conception petite bourgeoise de la lutte comme folklore festif avec ces fameuses danses technos, pointe avancée de l'inoffensivité militante.




Devant les lycées et ailleurs, ces actes ont pour fonction la mise à nu le sérieux adulte et ses postures d'exemplarité, derniers éléments de camouflage d'une complicité toujours latente avec les institutions scolaires répressives (combien de réactions offusquées et révélatrices ont été provoqués par l'incendie de Nelson Mandela ?). Mise en suspens de l'ennui, exfiltration de l'espace scolaire de dressage, apprentissage de gestes indépendants de leur finalité marchande et professionnelle, refus de s'astreindre à la résignation et à l'immobilité devant la catastrophe, voilà dans quelles domaines le jeu est une option.




Mais pourquoi affirmer que cette propriété ludique est susceptible d'éclairer l'étonnante et puissante offensive de samedi dernier ? Une meilleure analyse ne suppose-t-elle pas de déceler dans la conjoncture matérielle ce qui présupposait le mouvement ? Sûrement.




Bien souvent, la volonté d'expliquer les causes d'un processus insurrectionnel contient une intention prescriptive. On cherche à mieux l'assimiler et à rendre sa continuation plus efficiente encore. L'effort est louable. Mais cela revient souvent à dire ce qu'il s'est passé pour mieux dire ce qui doit se passer ensuite. Comme le soulignait Benjamin en son temps : « Le caractère destructeur n'a aucun intérêt à être compris. Les efforts qu'on déploie dans ce sens lui paraissent superficiels. Être compris est une affaire de bourgeois. Le destructeur, lui, s'en moque. Il ne veut pas de disciples. Il préfère être seul, car c'est la seule façon pour lui de témoigner de la solitude de ce qui est détruit. » L'incompréhension suscitée par le pillage doit parfois être accompagnée d'un refus de toute explication chronophage, de toute tentative de se rendre respectable. Néanmoins, considérer que cette activité est minimalement « ludique », que casser une vitrine, s'introduire à l'intérieur des magasins, dérober parfois à l'aveugle et le plus rapidement possible des marchandises, dire que c'est un acte relevant du jeu, c'est souvent plus clair que toutes les justifications imaginables. Recevoir les leçons de l'efficacité du 17 octobre doit donc se faire sans vouloir déduire, figer ou projeter les formes souhaitables d'insurrection à venir. Sinon, le risque est de réincorporer l'évènement à un corpus militant de manières, de gestes, de savoirs, profondément antithétique et impuissant.




Contre la vigilance 




Le coup-d 'éclat du 17 octobre découle en partie d'une conjonction de l'effervescence ludique avec le refus de l'inquiétude habituelle des « conséquences ». En effet, l'offensivité lycéenne tient aussi à ce qu'elle court-circuite les réflexes de vigilance des autonomes informés. Régulièrement, les actes étaient réalisés à visages découvert, retransmis en direct et parfois même, les émeutiers posaient fièrement avec leurs trophées.

 

Certains camarades le remarquent en l'appréciant, d'autres, plus nombreux, et partant des condamnations en série, le déplorent. Nous ne défendons pas qu'il faille aller aveuglément à l'assaut de vitrines sans mesurer l'étendue de la surveillance et des moyens mobilisés ex-post ; ou, plus bêtement et simplement encore, d'encourager chacun à foncer dans le tas. Mais il y a dans ce déchaînement ludique d'actes de pillages, une espèce d'élan inconséquence qui vient en premier, une inconscience qui traduit au fond ce que représente cette lutte : un enjeu existentiel, une pulsion de vie qui se traduit dans un quoi-qu'il-en-coûte et un peu-importe-les-répercussions. Loin de fonder une politique de l'émeute ou un outil de compréhension parfait, cette « inconséquence » permet d'opérer un déplacement avec nos conceptions traditionnelles de l'engagement bien souvent corrélés à la crainte de la répression. Plutôt que de concevoir la lutte comme un calcul rationnel d'aléas et de risques (« comment risquer moins et faire plus ? »), le geste émeutier lui refuse une assignation à cette logique comptable. Il faut faire ici et maintenant, retrouver un 

kaïros

 compatible avec le désir collectif, avant d'abord de penser anticipation du pire et par conséquent, de refouler dans un futur fictif et détaché de notre temps l'agir révolutionnaire. Car ce que charrie la diffusion des pratiques d'anti-répression dans leur ensemble, bien qu'elles soient toujours bienvenues, c'est la volonté d'une stabilisation de l'après-insurrection, un désir de figuration d'un modèle serein et compréhensible de révolte. Or, par essence, le prolongement de la révolte, c'est un saut dans l'inconnu le plus total, nouveauté avec laquelle il faut s'efforcer de composer.




Par ailleurs, si les geôles et les procès à n'en plus finir nous effraient, l'existence qui nous est promise s'y apparente de très près. Dans ces circonstances, retrouver le ludique peut aussi consister, à l'image de Ritchy Thibault et ses irrévérencieuses audiences-tribunes, à refuser de fléchir devant la mascarade juridique et ses jeux de dupes.




Garder cette inconséquence ludique, c'est court-circuiter le pouvoir de dissuasion de la logorrhée sécuritaire ambiante, caractérisée par une diffusion en continu de nouvelles mesures, d'outils et de forces de répressions sophistiqués : usage de l'IA, pistolets ADN, liquide qui s'imprègne durablement sur les vêtements, déploiement du Raid, du GIGN, de l'Armée… Nul besoin de développer sur la panoplie à disposition de l'état en matière de contre-insurrection. Les lycéens et la GenZ, nouveaux conspirateurs professionnels en chefs, nous indiquent la voie pour les mettre hors d'état de nuire ; conjurer le risque, embrasser l'inconséquence.

Œuvres : Vol. II

 (p. 361-363). Gallimard. (Œuvre originale publiée en 1931). 


Huizinga, J. (1988). 

Homo ludens : Essai sur la fonction sociale du jeu

 (C. Seresia, trad.). Gallimard. (Ouvrage original publié en 1938)

title: Xelatên Pêşbirka Helbestê ya Arjen Arî dê bi merasîmeke bê dayîn
content:
Encama Pêşbirka Helbestan a Arjan Ariyî diyar bûn. Îsal dê merasîma xelatdayîna Pêşbaziya Helbestê ya Arjen Arî ya 13emîn, roja Înê di 30yê Cotmehê de li Salona Xwendinê ya Arjen Arî ya Şaredariya Peyasê bê lidarxistin. 




Merasîm bi hevkariya Şaredariya Peyasê û Weşanên Sor tê lidarxistin. Di pêşbirkê de Hoşeng Nizarî û Simeya H. Lalîn bi du dosyeyên cuda bûn yekem. Her weha Xelata Rûmetê jî dan Michael L. Chyet. Xelatgir dê merasîmê de xelatên xwe werbigirin.




Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Welat di çarçoveya bernameyê de dê panelêk li ser Arjen Arî jî bê lidarxistin.




Îsal du dosye bûn yekem




Di Pêşbaziya Helbestê ya Arjen Arî ya 13emîn de, ku encamên wê di 15ê Gulanê, Roja Zimanê Kurdî de hatin ragihandin, dosyeya Hoşeng Nizarî ya bi navê “Bîra Beyabanê” û dosyeya Simeya H. Lalîn ya bi navê “Hestiyên Tivinga Min” bûn yekem. Jûriya pêşbaziyê, ku ji Berken Bereh, Necla Arî, Gulîzer, Emerîkê Sidîqayê û Nuroj Munzur pêk dihat, dosyeyên 13 helbestvanên ciwan ên ku beşdarî pêşbaziyê bûbûn nirxand. Her du dosyeyên ku layiqî xelatê hatin dîtin, ji aliyê Weşanên Sor ve wekî pirtûk hatin çapkirin.




Xelata Rûmetê ya vê salê jî dê ji ber xebatên wî yên di warê ziman û edebiyata Kurdî de, bide zimanzan û Kurdolog Michael L. Chyet.




Bername




Di çarçoveya bernameya çalakiyê de, dê di destpêkê de saet 12:30an li Goristana Yenikoyê ya Amedê, li ser gora Arjen Arî bîranîn bê lidarxistin.




Di merasîma xelatdayînê de ku dê saet 18:00an dest pê bike, dê xelatên Hoşeng Nizarî û Simeya H. Lalîn, ku bûne yekem, bên dayîn. Piştî pêşkêşkirina xelatan, Simeya H. Lalîn dê pirtûkên xwe ji bo xwendevanan îmze bike.

Helbest û mîrata edebî ya Arjen Arî dê bên nîqaşkirin.




Di çarçoveya bernameyê de, saet 19:00an dê panelêk li ser helbest û mîrata edebî ya Arjen Arî bê lidarxistin. Osman Ozçelîk û Rêzan Diljen dê wekî axêver beşdarî panelê bibin. Mîna Acer jî dê moderatoriya panelê bike.







Derbarê Arjen Arî de




Arjen Arî 1ê Nîsana 1956an de li herêma Omeriya li gundê Çalê hatiye dinyayê. Di 1979an de Enstituya Perwerdeyî ya Diyarbekirê Beşa Zimanê Tirkî qedand. Cara peşî li kovara Tîrêjê de helbestên wî weşiyan. Weke gelek helbestvan û nivîskarê Kurd wî jî bi Tirkî dest bi helbestê kir. Di sala 1976an de li Nisebînê ji ber belavkirina belavokekê hate girtin. Wê demê polisan dest danîn ser helbestên wî yên Kurdî û Tirkî. Qasî hefteyekê  hepsê de ma. Ew derket lê helbestên wî heta niha jî hepsî ne.




  Piştî 12ê îlonê ew li welêt ma, helbestên wî di kovarên li derveyî welêt wekî Berbang, Kurdistan Press, Nûdem, Çira, Pelîn û Rewşenê de hatin weşandin. Di sala 1992"an de li navçeya Nisêbînê li ber deriyê mala xwe rastî êrişeke çekî bû û birîndar rakirin Nexweşxaneya Zanîngeha Dîcleyê. Ji mirinê filitî. Piştî wê bûyerê êdî li Amedê ma.  Helbestvan Arjen Arî ji ber nexweşiya penceşêrê 30ê Cotmeha 2012an de çû ser dilovaniya xwe.




   Niha jî ez ê çend helbest û nivîsên wî ên di kovarên cuda cuda de hatiye çapkirin û berhemên wî bi we re parve bikim..

title: A Luta não pode parar! Apoie a Rede de Sementes da Teia dos Povos
content:
👉 Apoie pelo link: [apoia.se/teiadesementes]




Em um gesto de reciprocidade, Edilsa, da etnia Tupinambá de Olivença, retornou sementes à Rede de Sementes da Teia dos Povos, entregando-as a Mestre Valmir. Ela contou que recebeu as sementes em Terra Vista, no encontro das mulheres, plantou, colheu e agora devolve parte da colheita para que o ciclo continue. Além de retribuir a Valmir, ela também compartilhou as sementes com parentes.




Edilsa reforçou que vai ter semente sempre para si e para retribuir àqueles que também querem plantar. Mestre Valmir agradeceu a atitude da companheira, destacando que ela levou a semente, plantou e está fazendo o trabalho que a Rede de Sementes pede: plantar, distribuir para as outras aldeias e para os outros parentes. Ele lembrou que esse é o trabalho da rede, sempre dividindo com quem precisa levar para vários territórios.




Esse é o ciclo que a campanha da Rede de Sementes quer multiplicar. Quem ainda não contribui pode se juntar a partir de R$ 2 por mês e fazer mais trocas como essa acontecerem.




Quem tem terra, semeia. Quem não tem, apoia. Ninguém fica para trás.
