Мак-Кинли, глава североамериканской олигархии, орудие и защитник крупных капиталистов, предатель кубинцев и филиппинцев, человек, санкционировавший расправу над бастующими в Хэзлтоне, пытки шахтёров Айдахо и тысячу гнусностей, ежедневно совершаемых против рабочих в «образцовой республике», тот, кто воплощал милитаристскую, завоевательную, империалистическую политику, в которую ринулась американская буржуазия, пал жертвой револьвера анархиста.

О чём вы хотите, чтобы мы скорбели, если не о судьбе, уготованной великодушному человеку, который – уместно или неуместно, с хорошей или плохой тактикой – принёс себя в жертву делу равенства и свободы?

Повторим это и в данном случае, как и во всех аналогичных: поскольку мы находимся в обществе волков, где насилие окружает нас и разит со всех сторон, мы, продолжая спокойно бороться за то, чтобы прекратилась эта ужасная необходимость отвечать на насилие насилием, – хотя и желая, чтобы скорее наступил день, когда антагонизмы интересов и страстей между людьми можно будет разрешать человеческими и цивилизованными средствами, – бережём свои слёзы и свои цветы для других жертв, а не для этих людей, которые, становясь во главе эксплуататорских и угнетательских классов, берут на себя ответственность и идут на риск, связанный с их положением.

И всё же нашлись анархисты, которые сочли полезным и прекрасным оскорблять угнетённого, который восстаёт, не имея ни слова осуждения для угнетателя, понёсшего кару за преступления, которые он совершил или позволил совершить!

Это извращение, это нездоровое желание получить одобрение противников, или же неосмотрительная ловкость, которая хотела бы завоевать свободу пропаганды своих идей, добровольно отказываясь от права выражать истинное и глубокое чувство души, – более того, искажая это чувство, притворяясь не тем, что есть?

Я делаю это с сожалением, но не могу не выразить боль и возмущение, которые вызвали во мне и во всех товарищах, каких мне довелось видеть в эти дни, необдуманные слова, посвящённые Agitazione покушению в Буффало.

Чолгош – несознательный человек! Но знают ли они его? Его поступок – обычное преступление, не имеющее ни одного из признаков, необходимых для того, чтобы подобный акт мог считаться политическим!

Полагаю, что ни один государственный обвинитель – королевский или республиканский – не осмелился бы утверждать нечто подобное. В самом деле, есть ли хоть какой-нибудь повод судить о Чолгоше как о человеке, движимом личными интересами или личной злобой? Разве не ясно, что он действовал по мотивам общественного порядка и намеревался – с основанием или без основания, но, несомненно, искренне и самоотверженно – принести себя в жертву ради дела? И разве не эти элементы придают факту наиболее яркий характер политико-социального покушения?

Впрочем, неправильно говорить о преступлении в подобных случаях. Кодекс это делает, но кодекс создан против нас, против угнетённых, и не может служить критерием для наших суждений.

Эти факты – акты войны; и если война есть преступление, то она преступление для тех, кто в ней стоит на стороне несправедливости и угнетения. Преступниками могут быть, являются английские захватчики Трансвааля; ими не являются буры, когда защищают свою свободу, даже если защита была бы безнадёжной.

Поступок Чолгоша (могла бы ответить Agitazione) нисколько не продвинул дело пролетариата и революции: Вместо Мак-Кинли придет Рузвельт, такой же, как и он, и всё останется как прежде, разве что положение анархистов станет немного труднее. И, возможно, Agitazione была бы права; более того, в американской среде, насколько я её знаю, мне это кажется вероятным.

Это значит, что на войне есть ходы удачные и ошибочные, есть бойцы осмотрительные и есть те, кто, увлекаемые энтузиазмом, подставляют себя лёгкой мишенью врагу и даже компрометируют положение товарищей; это значит, что каждый должен советовать, защищать и применять ту тактику, которую считает наиболее пригодной для достижения победы в кратчайшее время и с наименьшими возможными жертвами; но это не может изменить фундаментального факта: ясно, что тот, кто борется – хорошо или плохо – против нашего врага и с теми же намерениями, что и мы, есть наш друг и имеет право – не, конечно, на наше безоговорочное одобрение, но на нашу сердечную симпатию.

Неважно, кем является борющаяся единица – коллективом или отдельным человеком, – моральная сторона вопроса от этого не меняется. Вооружённое восстание, предпринятое не вовремя, может нанести действительный или кажущийся ущерб той социальной войне, которую мы ведём, – так же, как и индивидуальное покушение, оскорбляющее народное чувство; но если восстание предпринято ради завоевания свободы, ни один анархист не откажет ему в своей симпатии, и прежде всего никто не осмелится отказать побеждённым повстанцам в звании политико-социальных борцов. Почему же должно быть иначе, если восставший – один?

Agitazione верно сказала, что бастующие всегда правы против хозяев, и сказала хорошо, хотя очевидно, что не все стачки разумны, ибо неудавшаяся стачка может при известных обстоятельствах вызвать уныние и дезорганизовать рабочие силы. Почему же то, что верно в экономической борьбе против хозяев, не должно быть верно в политической борьбе против правителей, которые ружьём солдата и наручниками жандармов хотят поработить нас для них самих и для капиталистов?

Здесь речь не о том, чтобы обсуждать тактику. Если бы речь была об этом, я бы сказал, что в общем предпочитаю коллективное действие индивидуальному – уже потому, что на коллективное действие, требующее довольно обычных средних качеств, можно более или менее рассчитывать, тогда как на исключительный героизм, по природе своей спорадический, требующий индивидуальной жертвы, рассчитывать нельзя. Сейчас речь о более высоком вопросе: речь о революционном духе, о том почти инстинктивном чувстве ненависти к угнетению, без которого мертвая буква программ ничего не значит, как бы ни были либертарными заявленные намерения; речь о том духе борьбы, без которого даже анархисты становятся ручными и кончают – тем или иным путём – в болоте легалитаризма…

Честно говоря, я не могу поверить, что статья Agitazione соответствует истинным чувствам редакторов этой газеты, и я слишком хорошо их знаю, чтобы быть уверенным, что их вдохновила какая-либо трусливая мысль о личном спокойствии. Для этого достаточно было бы промолчать. Они, должно быть, думали, что спасают относительную (ох! весьма относительную!) свободу пропаганды, которая в этот момент им оставлена; должно быть, думали, что служат интересам нашей партии, наших организаций, наших газет – всё это я считаю превосходным, но это не возмещает ущерба, который наносит измена собственным убеждениям.

Глупо ради спасения жизни разрушать основания жизни. К чему могут служить революционные организации, если дают умереть революционному духу? К чему свобода пропаганды, если больше не пропагандируют то, что думают?

И хуже всего то, что анархисты-антиорганизационисты, те, кто против участия в рабочей борьбе, против образования партии и так далее, не преминут сказать и поверить, что это угасание революционного духа есть следствие метода, который они не одобряют. Они не будут правы, но будут казаться правыми, и это повредит нашему делу больше, чем все возможные преследования.

По-моему, секрет нашего успеха в том, чтобы уметь сочетать революционный дух и революционное действие с повседневной практической работой; в том, чтобы уметь участвовать в малых битвах, не теряя из виду битву великую и окончательную. И мне это не кажется трудным.

Надеюсь, что друзья Agitazione сумеют заставить забыть минуту дурного вдохновения и сохранить газете тот честно революционный характер, который соответствует анархическим принципам.

author: Μπάμπης Μπίκας
title: Οι φοιτητές κονταροχτυπούν στα ίσα (και) εκλογικά το καθεστώς Βούτσιτς
content:
Το κίνημα που αναπτύχθηκε στη Σερβία τα δύο τελευταία χρόνια, μετά την κατάρρευση του στεγάστρου του ανακαινισμένου σιδηροδρομικού σταθμού στο Νόβι Σαντ που σκότωσε 16 ανθρώπους και πυροδότησε δυναμικές και μαζικές αντιδράσεις, αποτέλεσε τον καταλύτη για τη διεύρυνση των διαδηλώσεων κατά της κυβέρνησης αλλά και την ευρύτερη αμφισβήτηση της λειτουργίας του κράτους. Με βασικά αιτήματα για τη διαφθορά, τη διαφάνεια, τις δημόσιες υπηρεσίες και τη μαφιόζικη λειτουργία του καθεστώτος Βούτσιτς. Εκείνο το κίνημα με κορμό τους φοιτητές και τις καταλήψεις στα πανεπιστήμια, στην αρχή του είχε χαρακτηριστικά οριζόντιας λειτουργίας και στόχευση ακόμη και μια νέα συντακτική συνέλευση, αποφάσισε τελικά να κινηθεί στη λογική της κυβερνησιμότητας με ρεφορμιστικά και εθνικά χαρακτηριστικά. Κατεβαίνει στις εκλογές με τη “Φοιτητική Λίστα – Οι Φοιτητές Νικούν”.




Ο μέχρι πρότινος πρόεδρος Αλεξάντερ Βούτσιτς, που δεν είχε δικαίωμα για νέα θητεία,  παραιτήθηκε για να διεκδικήσει τη συνέχεια της εξουσίας του μέσω της πρωθυπουργίας. Μόνο που δεν ανέμενε ότι ο εκλογικός συνδυασμός που κατέθεσαν οι φοιτητές θα αναδεικνυόταν στον βασικό αντίπαλό του σε αυτές τις εκλογές που διεξάγονται σήμερα στη Σερβία. Οι δημοσκοπήσεις μάλιστα φέρνουν τη «Φοιτητική Λίστα – Οι Φοιτητές Νικούν» που κατεβαίνει στην εκλογική αναμέτρηση να αναμετράται στα ίσα με την κυβερνητική «Ενωμένη Σερβία», με αμφότερους να κυμαίνονται στο συν/πλην 45%.







Στην τελική τους συγκέντρωση στη Σλάβια του Βελιγραδίου συμμετείχαν πάνω από 150.000 πολίτες και κύριο σύνθημα: Σερβία ή μαφία! Οι φοιτητές πλέον διεκδικούν την εξουσία. Αλλά κανένανς από αυτούς δεν συμμετέχει στους συνδυασμούς για την ανάδειξη των νέων 250 βουλευτών. Αποφάσισαν αυτό και απευθύνθηκαν σε προσωπικότητες του ακαδημαϊκού χώρου, καλλιτέχνες, αθλητές, την κοινωνία των πολιτών.




Το στρατόπεδο του Βούτσιτς, που κυριαρχεί στην πολιτική ζωή από το 2012, και ο προπαγανδιστικός μηχανισμός του κατηγορεί τη Φοιτητική Λίστα ότι κινείται ως όργανο ξένων μυστικών υπηρεσιών με στόχο την ανατροπή του και την αποσταθεροποίηση της χώρας, που σχοινοβατεί γεωπολιτικά μεταξύ Ρωσίας, ΕΕ, ΗΠΑ. Μάλιστα στη φαρέτρα χρησιμοποιείται ακόμη και το ζήτημα του Κοσόβου για να χτυπήσουν τον αντιπολιτευόμενο συνδυασμό.




Η πόλωση που καταγράφηκε, η χρησιμοποίηση του κρατικού μηχανισμού και του προπαγανδιστικού συστημικού μιντιακού οπλοστασίου, προκάλεσαν πλήθος καταγγελιών για τις συνθήκες της προεκλογικής εκστρατείας. Πέραν των διαφόρων διεθνών παρατηρητών, 24 οργανώσεις της κοινωνίας των πολιτών προειδοποίησαν ότι δεν πληρούνται οι απαραίτητες προϋποθέσεις για τη διεξαγωγή «ελεύθερων και δίκαιων εκλογών». Η έντονη πόλωση αφήνει ερωτηματικά ακόμη και για την αποδοχή ή μη ενός εκλογικού αποτελέσματος από την πλευρά του καθεστώτος Βούτσιτς.




ΡΕΠΟΡΤΑΖ + ΦΩΤΟ ΠΡΟΕΚΛΟΓΙΚΗΣ ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗΣ ΤΗΣ «ΦΟΙΤΗΤΙΚΗΣ ΛΙΣΤΑΣ – ΟΙ ΦΟΙΤΗΤΕΣ ΝΙΚΟΥΝ» ΑΠΌ ΤΟ Ν1




Ποτάμια ανθρώπων στη Σλάβια στην τελική συσυγκέντρωση της Φοιτητικής Λίστας: «Θυμίζει 15 Μαρτίου και μυρίζει ελευθερία»







Η «Φοιτητική Λίστα – Οι Φοιτητές Νικούν» διοργάνωσε την τελευταία προεκλογική συγκέντρωση πριν από τις έκτακτες βουλευτικές εκλογές την Κυριακή 25 Οκτωβρίου στην πλατεία Σλάβια στο Βελιγράδι. Στο δρόμο προς τη Σλάβια, ξεκίνησαν οργανωμένοι σε έξι πορείες από διαφορετικά μέρη της πόλης.




Οι υποψήφιοι της «Φοιτητικής Λίστας – Οι Φοιτητές Νικούν» και οι φοιτητές που τους υποστηρίζουν δήλωσαν στην τελική συγκέντρωση ότι οι εκλογές της Κυριακής δεν είναι μεταξύ 18 συνδυασμών, αλλά μεταξύ δύο αρχών και δύο οραμάτων – «Σερβία ή μαφία· ελευθερία ή δουλεία· ευημερία ή παρακμή».




Ατελείωτες φάλαγγες πολιτών κατευθύνθηκαν προς τη Σλάβια από έξι κατευθύνσεις, από το Νόβι Βελιγράδι, από το Ζέμουν από την Τσουκαρίτσα, ενώ λίγο αργότερα, φάλαγγες ξεκίνησαν επίσης από την Πλατεία Φοιτητών, από το κτίριο της Τεχνικής Σχολής στη Λεωφόρο Κράλιε Αλεξάνδρα, καθώς και από την Αυτοκομάντα.




Κατά τη διάρκεια της ημέρας οργανώθηκαν αρκετές αυτοκινητοπομπές από διάφορα μέρη της Σερβίας.




Στο τέλος της συνάντησης, όλοι οι υποψήφιοι της Φοιτητικής Λίστας κατέβηκαν από τη σκηνή ανάμεσα στους πολίτες, παρατάχθηκαν σε κύκλο γύρω από το σιντριβάνι στη Σλάβια, κρατώντας ψηλά το Σύνταγμα της Σερβίας.




Οι υποψήφιοι βουλευτές της Φοιτητικής Λίστας μίλησαν για το πώς θα μοιάζει η Σερβία από τις 26 Οκτωβρίου, την επόμενη μέρα των εκλογών, η οποία περιλαμβάνει, μεταξύ άλλων, μια απελευθερωμένη δικαστική εξουσία και εισαγγελία, αλλά και εκπαίδευση και υγειονομική περίθαλψη εξίσου προσβάσιμες σε όλους.




Της συγκέντρωσης με τίτλο «Η Νίκη σε καλεί» στη Σλάβια προηγήθηκαν πολυήμερες φοιτητικές πορείες σε όλη τη χώρα, από την ανατολική, τη δυτική και τη βόρεια Σερβία, και την προηγουμένη μπροστά από την Πρυτανεία στο Βελιγράδι .

title: Meteoroloji'den sağanak uyarısı: Bazı bölgelerde yağış, iç kesimlerde sis bekleniyor
content:
Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü (MGM) tarafından yayımlanan son tahmin raporuna göre, yurt genelinde havanın parçalı ve yer yer çok bulutlu geçeceği tahmin ediliyor.

Ülkenin batı kıyılarında ve doğu kesimlerinde yağış beklenirken, sabah ve gece saatlerinde iç bölgelerde pus ve sis etkili olacak.

Doğu Anadolu’nun doğusu ile Muğla ve Aydın’ın kıyı kesimleri, Bingöl ve Mardin çevrelerinde sağanak ve gök gürültülü sağanak yağış geçişleri bekleniyor.

Sabah ve gece saatlerinde Marmara, İç Ege, Göller Yöresi, Batı Karadeniz’in iç kesimleri ile Orta Karadeniz genelinde pus ve yer yer sis olayı öngörülüyor. Görüş mesafesinde düşüş yaşanabilecek bu bölgelerde sürücülerin dikkatli olması isteniyor.

Sıcaklıkların batı kesimlerde mevsim normalleri civarında, iç ve doğu bölgelerde ise normallerin yer yer üzerinde seyretmeye devam edeceği tahmin ediliyor.

Rüzgarın genellikle kuzeyli, güney ve doğu kesimlerde ise güneyli yönlerden hafif, ara sıra orta kuvvette esmesi bekleniyor.

title: Kapalı Oturum: Seçmen kelepçe görmek istiyor!
content: İktidarda fon vurgunu tartışması: 'Siyasi bedel ödetilsin' Yüzbinlerce mağdura, milyarlarca lira zarara yol açan fon vurgununda "siyasi ayak" aranırken iktidar partisindeki birçok siyasetçi asıl sorumlu olarak bürokrasiyi işaret ediyor. Öyle ki Meclis kulislerinde oran verenler bile var: "Yüzde 20 siyasetçiler suçlu ise bürokrasinin sorumluluğu yüzde 80!" Hatta ortaya çıkan vurgunla ilgili “yaşanan bir bürokrasi darbesi” nitelemesi yapanlar da var. Cumhurbaşkanlığı sistemi ile “bürokratik bir vesayet” oluştuğu şikayeti yeni değil. Adalet ve Kalkınma Partisi kulislerinde sıkça duyulan bu eleştiri, yaşanan fon krizi ile daha da ete kemiğe bürünmüş durumda. Duruma dair iktidar mensubu bazı siyasetçilerin şu değerlendirmeleri de çarpıcı: “Davul bizim boynumuzda, tokmak bürokraside. Bu krizi fırsata çevirip hızlıca bir değişim ve arınma sürecine girebiliriz. Denetim mekanizmaları ve siyasetçilerin etkisi daha da güçlendirilebilir. Şu ana kadar yapılanlar yetersiz. Bürokraside çok daha hızlı bir değişim ihtiyacı ve beklentisi var. Siyaseten de bedel ödetilmeli. Örneğin Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya şu an tutuklu olsaydı verilen mücadele daha inandırıcı olurdu. Hem de sorunu çözmek adına yapılacak diğer çalışmalar için zaman kazanılırdı. Seçmen bedel ödetildiğini görmek istiyor. Bir anlamda kelepçe görmek istiyor.”

author: Unknown
title: Food as an Act of Resistance
content:
The Thirty-Second Art Bulletin (October 2026)










The images in this art bulletin are from the exhibition 

MST: 40 Years

, an online exhibition of illustrations celebrating four decades of struggle for land and agrarian reform by Brazil’s 

Landless Rural Workers’ Movement (MST)

, organised in partnership with Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research and other organisations.










Listen to ‘

A desalambrar

’ (Tear Down the Fences!), written and performed by Uruguayan singer-songwriter Daniel Viglietti and also performed by Chilean singer-songwriter and theatre director Víctor Jara.







‘A desalambrar’ raises a fundamental question: who owns the land, and who has the right to cultivate it? The song’s call for agrarian reform and collective control over the resources that sustain life resonates with the struggle for food sovereignty.




Every 16 October, on World Food Day, 

La Via Campesina

 and its member organisations around the world mobilise for the International Day of Action for Peoples’ Food Sovereignty and against Transnational Corporations. Their mobilisation affirms that food systems should serve peoples’ needs and protect nature rather than generate profits. The movement also calls for the defence of peasant seeds – seeds that farming communities have cultivated, selected, saved, and exchanged over generations – and communities’ rights to save, reproduce, exchange, and sell them.




To explore how the struggle for food sovereignty extends from the land to the kitchen, encompassing the preservation of seeds, cultural knowledge, and collective traditions, we interviewed four cooks, chefs, and organisers. 

Anita Epulef Panguilef

, a Mapuche cook and seed keeper from Curarrehue in Chile’s Araucanía Region, demonstrates how food sovereignty is practised through everyday relationships with land, water, biodiversity, and community. Norma Listman and Saqib Keval, chefs and co-owners of 

Masala y Maíz

 in Mexico City, explore the connections between Mexican, South Asian, and East African culinary traditions, using cooking to recover histories obscured by colonialism and shaped by migration and displacement. Ana Chã, a member of the MST and coordinator of the Elza Soares Cultural Centre in São Paulo, explains how these practices become part of a collective political project in which the struggle for land extends all the way to the table.




Together, their experiences show that defending food sovereignty means defending more than what ends up on our plates. It means defending peoples’ right to decide what is planted, who grows it, which seeds circulate, how food is prepared, whose knowledge is recognised, and how communities gather to eat.







Credit: Ricardo Keferaus.







In Curarrehue, nestled among the mountains, forests, and rivers of southern Chile, Anita Epulef reminds us that food sovereignty is not an abstract concept but an everyday practice that begins long before a pot is placed over the fire. Her daily life involves selecting seeds for planting, preparing a 

trafkintu

 (a traditional Mapuche gathering for exchanging seeds and knowledge), checking whether frost has damaged the plants, gathering food from the vegetable garden, observing streams and other waterways, tending to 

lawen

 (medicinal plants), reading the clouds, and greeting fellow community members. She describes these practices as a dialogue with 

itrofillmogen

, a Mapuche concept encompassing the diversity of life and the relationships among all living beings.




The word ‘Mapuche’ itself means ‘people of the land’. The name expresses more than an identity tied to a particular territory. For Anita, the relationship with the land shapes people’s understanding of nourishment, health, knowledge, and responsibility. ‘If the land becomes sick, the food becomes sick too’, she explains. Caring for the land therefore means caring for life.




Yet this relationship is threatened by the growing concentration of agricultural land in fewer and fewer hands. According to a 2026 

report

 jointly published by the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO), the International Land Coalition, and the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development, there are approximately 570 million farms worldwide. About 85% of the world’s farms are smaller than two hectares, yet they account for only 9% of agricultural land. By contrast, farms larger than 1,000 hectares represent just 0.1% of all farms but operate more than half of that land. The report also finds that the largest 10% of landholders operate 89% of the total.




The struggle over food therefore begins with the struggle over the means of producing it: land.







Credit: Marieli Ribeiro.







This understanding is central to the MST’s struggle for food sovereignty in Brazil. Ana Chã explains that land provides the material basis for communities to decide what to produce, how to live, how to care for nature, and how to organise themselves. Access to land alone, however, is not enough if farmers remain dependent on corporate seeds, agrochemicals, other agricultural inputs, and markets controlled by large companies.




Control over seeds is therefore also essential to food sovereignty.




‘Seeds are everything’, Anita tells us. In her community, saving seeds allows families to plant their own crops and produce food for the coming winter without depending on commercial seed suppliers. But this autonomy is threatened by efforts to privatise seeds that communities have freely saved and exchanged for generations. For Anita, such efforts threaten not only communities’ ability to produce food independently but also their collective knowledge and memory. She describes this as an act of ‘robbing the memory of a people’.




The loss of seed diversity is another concern. FAO has long 

cited

 an estimate that around 75% of crop genetic diversity was lost during the twentieth century, as farmers increasingly replaced local varieties – including those adapted to local growing conditions over generations – with genetically uniform, high-yielding varieties. When a seed variety disappears, the possibility of cultivating it is lost, while the knowledge of how to grow, preserve, prepare, and pass it on to future generations is also put at risk.




For La Via Campesina, the defence of peasant seeds is at 

the heart of the struggle for food sovereignty

. The movement calls on peasant families and communities to become guardians of seeds, ensuring their preservation, reproduction, exchange, and collective protection.




The struggle over seeds does not end in the fields. It continues in the kitchen, where food is prepared, shared, and remembered.







Credit: Camila Camomila.







For Anita, the connection between land, seeds, and food is also reflected in the ingredients she uses – gathered from local forests and vegetable gardens or grown from locally cultivated seeds. Her account brings together the autumn gathering of 

ngülliw

 (seeds from the 

pewen

, or monkey puzzle tree), the harvesting of broad beans by older women in the community, the gathering of 

lleuques

 (fruit from the Chilean plum yew) by young people, and the smoking and cooking of chillies over a wood fire. Together, these practices reflect the relationship between food, land, and the transmission of knowledge across generations.




Preserving agricultural diversity is also a way of ensuring that communities can continue to grow their own food. For Anita, keeping several varieties of potatoes, for example, is not merely a matter of taste. If a variety disappears from the market, the community can still grow it. When she teaches someone to grind chilli, she also tells them how her grandmother used it. In this way, knowledge passes ‘from hand to hand’.




Traditional or ancestral knowledge is not a fixed collection of dishes from the past. It is practical knowledge accumulated over generations: knowing when to plant, which seeds are suited to a particular climate, which plants can be gathered from the forest, how food can be preserved, the medicinal properties of plants, how recipes change with the seasons, and how this knowledge is passed on.




Norma Listman and Saqib Keval similarly challenge the idea that culinary traditions are confined within national borders. At their restaurant, Masala y Maíz, they draw on histories of migration and exchange connecting Mexico, South Asia, and East Africa. Their dishes combine native Mexican maize, wild 

quelites

 (edible wild greens), cacao, vanilla, and Mexican chillies with South Asian and East African ingredients and cooking techniques.




For Norma and Saqib, sourcing native and traditional ingredients is ‘non-negotiable’. They argue that every peso spent on a native variety helps sustain its cultivation and keep its seeds in circulation, rather than contributing to its disappearance under industrial agriculture. But they also insist that chefs must look beyond the ingredients themselves and recognise the labour and knowledge of the people who cultivate them. Established chefs often have access to financial resources and public platforms that many agricultural producers lack. Norma and Saqib argue that this privilege comes with a responsibility to pay producers fairly and consistently, acknowledge their contributions publicly, and support the preservation of the agricultural knowledge behind each dish.







Credit: Estela Carvalho.







For Anita, cooking with young people, women, and children is an opportunity to share stories while preparing food together. As the water boils for soup, people chop, knead, talk, and remember. She teaches because she does not want younger generations to feel the same shame about their traditional foods that previous generations experienced. The kitchen becomes a place where language, memory, and cultural pride are passed on along with culinary knowledge.




‘When I teach, I am defending Mapudungun’, Anita explains, referring to the Mapuche language, which is preserved through the names of ingredients and traditional practices. Her everyday activities – from tending the garden to cooking for her family and visitors – become ways of defending her community’s relationship with the land.




Norma and Saqib describe a similar process of preserving cultural knowledge through recipes. Recipes can survive displacement, migration, colonisation, famine, drought, and genocide because they can be passed down through generations and recreated in everyday life. They do not depend solely on written records or institutions for their survival. Instead, they are preserved and transformed as people cook, adapt, teach, and share them. Preserving culinary knowledge is therefore less about maintaining an unchanging tradition than ensuring its continuity across generations.







Credit: Pablo Placencia Lagos.







Ana Chã explains that collective kitchens are among the first spaces established in the MST’s encampments and also play an important role in the movement’s schools, cooperatives, meetings, and training centres. In these spaces, people share responsibilities, exchange knowledge and memories, build relationships, and prepare meals together. Through its Cozinhas Sem Terra (Landless Kitchens), the MST prepares healthy food using locally produced ingredients whenever possible while celebrating the culinary traditions of different regions of Brazil.




A meal can connect the person who saves the seed to the person who grows the crop, the person who cooks it, and the person who eats it. In doing so, it can make visible the people and the labour behind food – connections often obscured by the industrial food system.




For Ana, this collective approach to food is also a form of resistance to a system that treats food as a commodity and makes people increasingly dependent on large corporations. Recovering a grandmother’s recipe, planting a crop variety at risk of disappearing, exchanging seeds, bringing food from agrarian reform settlements to a school or urban community, organising a food fair, or teaching children where their food comes from are all ways of strengthening communities’ control over food and preserving the knowledge associated with its production and preparation.




These practices are part of the MST’s broader vision of popular agrarian reform, which links the democratisation of access to land with agroecology, seed protection, biodiversity, healthy food, cooperation, fair markets, the recovery of food cultures, and alliances between rural and urban communities.




This is food sovereignty as praxis: a political project realised through everyday collective action.




Although rooted in different histories and experiences, Anita’s seed keeping, Norma and Saqib’s cooking, and Ana’s organising through the MST all raise a common question: who gets to decide how food is produced and how the knowledge associated with it is preserved and passed on?







Credit: Madalena Ayam Ubrais Barco.







Food sovereignty means returning control over how food is produced and shared to peoples and communities.




But protecting seeds and securing land are only part of the struggle. As Ana reminds us, food sovereignty also requires transforming how we grow, prepare, eat, and share food, as well as our relationship with nature.




On 16 October, movements around the world once again affirmed that food is not merely a commodity. The challenge is to make this conviction a reality – in the soil, through seeds, in the kitchen, and at the table.




Anita offers a powerful metaphor for this struggle: ‘Every time I cook, for my family or in public, every interview, every post, every conversation is a trench.’




But a trench is not only a place to defend what remains. It is also a place to plant the seeds of a different future.




Warmly,




Soledad Varela




Operations Manager, Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research




Soledad studied culinary arts at the Escuela Culinaria Francesa in Santiago, Chile.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Political Parties Spar Over Taiwan’s Demographic Woes
content:
THE KMT HAS hit out at the DPP’s failure to correct Taiwan’s demographic woes, crticizing the decline in the national population. According to the National Development Council, Taiwan’s population is expected to fall below 20 million by 2045. Taiwan’s population is expected to halve by 2075.

Specifically, the KMT has made a new savings plan it proposed that the DPP rejected, the Taiwan Youth Development and Future Account Act, as proof that the DPP does not care about the issue. The act would have allocated an “Education and Development Account” and “Taiwan Future Account” to each child, the former of which would be able to be used at any time, and the latter of which would be accessible at age 18. 60,000 NT would be provided to each child per year under the proposal. The KMT has also hit out at the inability of the government to construct more social housing.

Nevertheless, one notes that the DPP rejected the Taiwan Youth Development and Future Account Act on the basis that it, in allowing for corporate sponsors, it could increase the gaps in inequality. The DPP has instead proposed a similar proposal that would also allow for 60,000 NT to be allocated to each child annually.

Otherwise, one notes that the DPP plans to increase subsidies for housing, education, and childcare, with particular efforts to spread costs between the government and families in childcare. Likewise, the DPP has stated that it intends to extend the amount of parental leave that can be subsidized to nine months, extend maternity leave to 12 weeks, extend marriage leave to 14 days, and increase the amount of leave that a husband can take to accompany his spouse to prenatal examinations to 14 days.

More generally, the approach would be to increase existing subsidies while extending existing leave programs. Nevertheless, one imagines that the KMT would have more or less adopted the same approach if it were in power–there is little difference between the two major parties when it comes to the political imagination of how to solve Taiwan’s declining birthrate.

Indeed, more generally, both major parties are unwilling to make the larger systematic changes that would allow for such issues to be solved. For example, there continues to be widespread reluctance to open up Taiwanese society to immigrants, with Taiwan only allowing blue-collar migrant workers to come here as individuals, without their families, and also not allowing blue-collar migrant workers to stay in Taiwan beyond twelve or fourteen years.

To this extent, Taiwan’s issues with a declining birthrate often stem from social pressures on newly expectant parents–especially mothers–issues that cannot be solved through simply throwing money at the issue. In this sense, Taiwan’s declining birthrate is likely only to be a political issue used by both sides to hit out at each other, rather than that either side of the political aisle would seriously consider solutions.

title: Israel Launches Major Ethnic Cleansing Escalation in West Bank, Targeting Hebron
content:
The operation follows a Palestinian resistance attack on an illegal West Bank military checkpoint.

Israeli forces on Friday began demolishing homes and businesses and forcibly evacuating residents near Hebron in the illegally occupied West Bank following a Palestinian resistance attack that killed two Israeli soldiers.

title: Ballot Measures Will Impact LGBTQ+ Rights in 7 States This Election
content:
Voters will decide how trans youth can participate in school sports, access gender-affirming health care, and more.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Voters in seven states this fall will weigh more than half a dozen ballot initiatives with direct bearings on LGBTQ+ people — disproportionately on transgender youth. They come as LGBTQ+ rights issues feature heavily in campaigns for candidates on either side of the aisle in the final stretch of November’s midterm elections, which will determine party control of Congress and several key governorships.

Nearly half of LGBTQ+-related ballot initiatives this year would restrict trans student-athletes from competing in line with their gender identity, an issue championed overwhelmingly by Republicans and by a rising share of Democrats. Others would ban certain transition-related treatments for minors — another focus of conservative candidates and President Donald Trump’s second administration.

Since 2021, more than half the nation has adopted laws barring trans students from playing on school sports teams matching their gender identity, and 27 states have banned gender-affirming care for trans youth. Nationally, the number of trans students who participate in school sports is unknown, but is believed to be relatively low: The Williams Institute estimates that just over 300,000 13- to 17-year-olds in the United States are trans, and not all of them will play sports.

In Washington state, where voters will decide this fall whether to ban trans student-athletes from teams matching their gender identity, the organization governing high school sports told The 19th that it is aware of about 10 trans middle and high schoolers who play sports out of more than 200,000 students who compete statewide.

Other ballot initiatives appearing before voters this fall include measures to change the state constitution to expand nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQ+ people; formally repeal language against same-sex marriages and modify students’ and parents’ rights in schools.

Here’s where LGBTQ+ rights are on the ballot this November.

Arizona voters will decide this fall whether trans student-athletes may continue to compete on school sports teams that align with their gender identity. A ballot initiative introduced late last year by state Rep. Selina Bliss, a Republican running for reelection, would effectively restore a 2022 state law restricting trans athletes’ participation that a federal appeals court had blocked in 2024.

Kris Mayes, Arizona’s Democratic attorney general, has declined to defend the law in court.

Bliss’ proposal would require public and qualifying private schools to designate K-12 sports teams as exclusively “male,” “female” or “coeducational” based on participating students’ “biological status at birth.” It would also bar trans students from using restrooms, locker rooms and other spaces “integral to athletic engagement” that match their gender identity.

In July, a lawsuit challenging the measure claimed it violated a requirement that Arizona ballot initiatives address only a single subject and was “misleading to the point of fraud.” A state superior court judge later ruled that the initiative could remain on the November 3 ballot.

Colorado voters will decide whether to bar trans student-athletes from competing in line with their gender identity by designating K-12 and collegiate sports teams based on students’ “biological reproductive systems.” The ballot initiative qualified for the general election after Protect Kids Colorado, the organization behind it, collected more than 168,000 signatures statewide.

Voters will also decide whether to ban transition-related surgeries for minors, and whether state or federal funds, Medicaid reimbursements or insurance coverage can be used to help pay for them. Such surgeries are already rare. The measure, also introduced by Protect Kids Colorado, does not directly mention nonsurgical care.

State medical organizations, including the Colorado Academy of Family Physicians and the Colorado Medical Society (CMS), the state’s largest organized group of practitioners, have publicly opposed the healthcare-related initiative. “CMS members hold diverse political views but share a core principle: medical decisions belong in the exam room,” Brigitta Robinson, the organization’s president, said in September.

That initiative also runs counter to “shield laws” safeguarding access to gender-affirming healthcare, as well as abortion, in Colorado.

In Missouri, voters will decide whether to reverse a 2024 amendment adding abortion protections to the state constitution. The new proposal would ban abortions in almost all cases, with exceptions for rape and incest, though only through the first trimester, and in medical emergencies throughout pregnancy.

It would also add language to the state constitution banning gender-affirming medical care for trans minors — prohibited by law in Missouri since 2023. An ultimately unsuccessful effort to disqualify the proposal from the November ballot, led by the ACLU of Missouri, claimed the measure violated the state’s single subject clause for ballot initiatives and failed to adequately inform voters of its intent.

Voters in Nebraska will decide whether to add language to the state constitution requiring public and qualifying private schools to designate athletic teams based on “biological sex,” and expressly declare that girls’ sports “shall not be open to students of the male sex.”

The ballot initiative qualified for the general election in August, after organizers collected more than 130,000 signatures from across the state. The following month, Nebraska voter Cara Ulman filed a lawsuit to disqualify the measure. Her legal team argued before the state Supreme Court in September that the measure’s sponsors had failed to “adequately inform the public of what they are trying to accomplish” with the initiative.

Because Nebraska’s secretary of state has already certified its general election ballot, the measure will go before voters regardless of the court’s decision, which is expected by October 27. But a ruling in Ulman’s favor would invalidate the results.

Nebraska law already prohibits trans student-athletes from participating in sports in line with their gender identity from kindergarten through college.

Voters in Vermont will decide this fall whether to add an equal rights amendment to the state constitution. The proposal, introduced in 2023 by a coalition of Democratic state lawmakers, would prohibit unequal treatment “on account of a person’s race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or national origin.” In Vermont, a constitutional amendment must pass two legislative sessions before it can go before voters.

Virginia voters will decide whether to repeal language in the state constitution barring same-sex couples from marrying, and instead establish an affirmative right to marriage between two consenting adults regardless of their sex, gender or race. The proposal, first introduced in 2024, qualified for the November ballot after several failed attempts. In Virginia, proposed amendments to the constitution must be approved by the state House and Senate twice before they can appear before voters.

Virginia’s ban on gay marriage, added to its constitution in 2006, has been unenforceable since 2015, when the Supreme Court established a federal right to marry for same-sex couples in the United States. But marriage equality advocates have argued that recent decisions and public statements by the high court’s conservative supermajority have put that right in jeopardy. The Supreme Court declined to take up a case challenging its same-sex marriage ruling last fall.

Voters in Washington will decide whether to bar trans student-athletes from girls’ school sports teams by requiring every girl in the state to have her sex assigned at birth verified by a doctor — through either genetic or hormone tests or an examination of her reproductive anatomy — to determine eligibility for K-12 sports.

Opponents of the initiative have said it can be easily exploited, putting both trans and cisgender girls at risk of abuse. In a July op-ed, women’s soccer superstar Megan Rapinoe, a Washington native, argued the measure would drive some girls out of sports altogether.

The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association has allowed trans students to compete in line with their gender identity since 2007.

The initiative qualified for the November ballot in January, after Let’s Go Washington, the political action committee behind it, collected more than 440,000 petition signatures from across the state. The group, founded by conservative hedge fund manager Brian Heywood, is also behind a second ballot measure to restore a 2024 state law regarding students’ and parents’ rights in public schools.

Washington’s Democratic-controlled legislature amended the law, known as the parental “bill of rights,” last spring, saying it was necessary to comply with existing state and federal laws. The new proposal would effectively reverse the 2025 changes.

State LGBTQ+ organizations and Democratic politicians — including Gov. Bob Ferguson — have opposed the initiative, arguing that it would put LGBTQ+ students at risk of being outed to unsupportive parents, among other safety and privacy concerns.

title: New Study Finds EPA May Be Vastly Underreporting PFAS Levels in Drinking Water
content:
The researchers found the Environmental Protection Agency’s minimum reporting levels masked widespread contamination.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

US drinking water could contain double the PFAS levels currently reported by regulators, according to a new study from Texas Christian University.

The study, published in Cell Reports Sustainability, used computer modeling to estimate that the latest reports from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) capture only 44% of the average combined concentration of 25 polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in US water systems.

PFAS, also known as “forever chemicals,” are known to persist in the environment and are linked to some cancers, high cholesterol, reproductive issues, and other health problems.

Researchers analyzed more than 1.8 million PFAS measurement records from the EPA’s January 2026 release of monitoring data from water systems across the country. They found most individual PFAS test results in the dataset fall below the EPA’s minimum reporting levels (MRLs).

These data points are often treated as zero when agencies and researchers summarize average PFAS levels in drinking water.

The authors found that 98% of PFAS test results were below the MRL. The MRL generally means a concentration that most laboratories can reliably measure and report. However, the study’s authors argue that this doesn’t mean that the water tested is PFAS-free or that it’s safe.

“Below the reporting limit does not mean zero. Our study shows why that distinction matters when summarizing PFAS concentrations,” said lead author Gehendra Kharel, associate professor of environmental and geological sciences at Texas Christian University.

Kharel and his team used computer models applied to data from the EPA’s Fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR 5), a nationwide program that requires public water systems to test drinking water for specific PFAS. They used this dataset to estimate possible concentrations for PFAS records listed below the EPA’s MRL.

They averaged hundreds of data points to come up with an estimate, performing this calculation for all 25 PFAS that had been detected at least once in the EPA’s dataset.

Under the study’s primary statistical model, they found that treating below-limit results as zero captured only 44% of the average combined concentration of the 25 PFAS monitored across 9,991 community water systems.

Jesse Goodrich, assistant professor in the division of environmental health at the University of Southern California, said that while municipal drinking water data explains why certain people have elevated chemical levels, these findings clarify why so many Americans, regardless of location or water source, have detectable PFAS in their blood.

“People traditionally have thought that drinking water is a large source of exposure to different PFAS compounds. And so when you look at the UCMR results, you see a lot of zeros, and that is hard to reconcile based on the human biomonitoring studies, where you see that everyone is actually exposed,” Goodrich said.

The results of this study are model-generated predictions rather than measurements of actual concentrations. However, Goodrich believes the results explain how trace contamination builds up.

“There’s very low levels of PFAS in drinking water, and over time, since compounds have such a long half life, that can add up to measurable, kind of ubiquitous exposure in the population,” Goodrich said.

Kharel believes the study could help provide a more complete picture of PFAS levels in US drinking water and improve how environmental monitoring data are interpreted, bridging the gap between official estimates and the actual level of chemicals in our water.

Alissa Cordner, co-director of the PFAS Project Lab at Northeastern University, said the EPA takes a more conservative approach by treating unmeasurable chemical samples as zero, which results in the lowest possible contamination estimates.

Cordner argues scientists can use better methods. Instead of assuming zero, researchers often estimate low-level presence by dividing the lab’s detection limit by either two or the square root of two.

“Either of those approaches are going to give you a less conservative and potentially more environmentally relevant measure of what’s actually going on in these samples,” she said.

Kharel recommends that agencies supplement traditional reporting methods by including estimates for below-limit results, alongside clear disclosures of detection limits, the percentage of unmeasurable samples, and margins of error.

“These practices would complement existing compliance procedures, not replace them or change health standards,” he said. Kharel and his team developed PFAS-CAST, an open-source tool designed to let agencies explore this approach with their own monitoring data.

This study comes after another report, which was published by Environment America Research & Policy Center last week, found that PFAS pollute more than 80% of tested US waterways.

In May, the EPA proposed dropping limits for four cancer-linked “forever chemicals” in drinking water established during the Biden administration, prompting concern from scientists who say even low dose exposure to PFAS can be harmful to human health over time.

“PFAS have been shown to impact human health at extremely low levels of exposure,” said Cordner. Just because standard lab tools can’t detect a chemical, “that doesn’t mean everything is zero.”

title: The Entire Journalism Industry Is on a Collision Course With AI
content:
News publishers either fight tech oligarchs or we lose the Fourth Estate.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

While it is not yet possible to say that the group of technologies currently called “AI” is harmful to literally everyone, that tech is already harming large numbers of people in many different ways: jeopardizing their jobs, health, privacy, and lived environment. And I can say with certainty that the way these technologies are being built, deployed, and used has been extremely harmful to the journalism industry in general and to small news outlets in particular.

It is for that reason that my organization, the Boston Institute for Nonprofit Journalism, recently joined with 59 other publishers to file a mass-action lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft. Together, this group of plaintiffs, represented by the mission-driven law firm Platkin LLP, controls more than 500 news outlets large and small across the United States.

Our main complaint is that OpenAI and Microsoft took our articles without asking our permission and definitely without providing us payment of any kind, in violation of well-established copyright law, in order to build the large-language models that are the core of their AI businesses.

This is only one type of damage that the AI giants in question have inflicted on news outlets all over the U.S. and the world. And the exposure for these companies due to that damage is absolutely huge when one combines the potential amount that our lawsuit could cost OpenAI and Microsoft with the potential amount similar lawsuits could cost those defendants — as well as the truly massive New York Times suit against the same companies on the same grounds that has been wending its way through the legal system for three years. Which, clearly, is why we are suing on those grounds.

But there are other ways the vast corporations that make up the nascent AI industry have harmed news organizations. Perhaps the worst of those is that the volume of traffic to news outlets from web search has been dropping since the AI boom began a few years ago (a dilemma that Truthout leaders have ably elucidated in two recent commentaries). We all rely upon that traffic for maintaining and, more importantly, growing our audiences over time. Audiences translate to revenue for news publications as with every other business on the web, be that revenue donations for nonprofit news groups or advertising for both nonprofit and commercial ones.

According to a January 2026 report by the University of Oxford’s Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism that used a survey “drawn from a strategic sample of 280 digital leaders from 51 countries and territories” to look at major threats faced this year by the news industry, “Aggregate data, sourced from the analytics company Chartbeat for this report, show that Google traffic from organic search to over 2,500 sites was down by a third (33%) globally between Nov 2024 and Nov 2025 and by 38% in the United States, but it is not clear how much of this is down to AI overviews.”

The news “editors, CEOs, and digital executives” surveyed for the Reuters Institute report forecast another 43 percent drop in organic search traffic to news sites this year, but we’ll have to wait until the next report to see how accurate that prediction was.

“In the past year, 170 newspapers have closed or merged, at a rate of nearly three a week, and many of these were the last remaining source of original news in their communities.”

And the fact that the study did not determine how much of that drop was due to AI search summaries does not mean that effect was insignificant. The Pew Research Center tracked 68,879 real Google searches by 900 U.S. adults in March 2025 and compared what happened when an AI search summary box (called “AI Overview” on Google) appeared on top of a search results page versus when it didn’t. The percentage that clicked through to a non-Google website link when there was no AI Overview box on top of the search results page was 15 percent. The percentage when there was an AI Overview box on top of the search results page was 8 percent. Meaning that almost half the people who would normally click through to a non-Google website link from Google search did not do so when an AI Overview box was present on top of a Google search results page.

The Pew study also found that only about 1 percent of users clicked a source link inside the AI Overview box itself. Users who saw a search summary were more likely to end their session entirely (26 percent with a summary and just 16 percent without one). So lots of people are simply reading the AI Overview on Google and then stopping their search without going to any other site, including news sites, as the Reuters Institute study showed.

Thus, a significant portion of news outlets’ audiences are being effectively blocked from finding us even as the chatbots scrape the professionally produced articles published by the news industry to answer people’s questions. This in turn strangles the reach of most news outlets and results in our audiences shrinking.

Guess what that does to our revenue streams? It’s not pretty.

All of this is happening, mind you, in an era when the news industry is already dying the death of a thousand cuts. Private equity firms and hedge funds have been buying up news outlets, mining them for profit, and selling off whatever assets were left for decades. We had already lost most of our advertising dollars to Google, our classifieds income first to Craigslist and then to other corporations, and our audiences to all the social media giants like Meta’s Facebook — which we had gamely helped bring our audiences to starting in the 2000s (“join us on Facebook!”), only to have them start to charge us to reach those same audiences not long after we helped deliver them on silver platters.

For most of the last two decades, I have been saying that the news industry is in rolling collapse, with small local and regional publications shutting down with increasing regularity.

Now I say that American journalism is in terminal collapse.

According to the 2026 State of Local News report released this month by the Medill School of Journalism at Northwestern University, 7,500 newspaper jobs were lost nationwide between 2024 and 2025. This, in an industry where many reporters already don’t have full-time jobs but are forced to be freelancers and find other gigs outside journalism to make ends meet. Also, the report states, “In the past year, 170 newspapers have closed or merged, at a rate of nearly three a week, and many of these were the last remaining source of original news in their communities.”

The Medill report authors try to put a happy face on the situation by pointing out that their research shows that “8,400 news outlets make up the American local news ecosystem.” But they also demonstrate that we’ve had a net loss of 3,400 local newspapers since 2005, and that “total newspaper employment has decreased by 75% over the past two decades” (2005 to 2025).

From long experience and constant communication with dozens of fellow news publishers, I will add that I believe too many of the surviving news outlets in the U.S. are as close to shutting down as my organization — continuing to survive only by the underpaid labor of an ever-shrinking number of wildly overworked staffers shored up by a legion of “stringers” (freelancers), usually uncounted by research centers like Medill, who have little hope of ever getting a “job job” in a dying profession.

AI giants walking off with the content of news outlets like mine and blocking us from our audience with AI search summaries look to be the final nails in the coffin of the news industry as major news organizations join smaller ones in suffering significant staff cuts or going under outright.

As flawed as American journalism has always been, news publishers are beset by these manifold crises while the tech lords are amassing wealth at historic levels and using that wealth to dominate politics in ways that threaten democracy in the United States and beyond.

I believe that this crushing of remaining U.S. news outlets by oligarchs is not a bug but a feature of the tech-driven American economy. Billionaires in the tech industry (and other major industries besides) are singularly uninterested in anybody shining the light of day on their political and economic activities and those of their conglomerates.

That is why the Boston Institute for Nonprofit Journalism is committing to fighting tooth and nail to continue producing news in the service of democracy. And part of that fight is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for ripping us off — small and perennially on the brink of financial ruin though we have been throughout our entire 11+ year run to date.

We are extraordinarily pleased to be joined in this fight by many other news publishers like us, including close friends The Shoestring of western Massachusetts, ecoRI News, East Greenwich News of Rhode Island, InDepth NH, the Pelham Examiner of New York, and the Austin Chronicle of Texas.

We hope that more folks who are aware that their lives and livelihoods have been harmed by the AI giants and other tech giants will be inspired by our action and follow in our footsteps. If enough people demand redress through the legal and political system, perhaps the oligarchs will see their industries collapse before they succeed in wiping ours out — brought down by an army of regular people defending our democratic rights. On top of the deleterious effects of the growing speculative bubble forming in an AI industry unable to create products that most people are willing to pay for.

A bubble that is looking more ready to burst by the day.

author: Lauren Rankin
title: Abortion Rights Are on the Ballot in 4 States in the 2026 Midterms
content:
Voters in Missouri, Idaho, Virginia, and Nevada will decide the fate of abortion rights in their states.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Abortion is once again on the ballot. While the fate of the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House both hang in the balance, the Trump administration can still wreak havoc on abortion rights with or without congressional approval, including a backdoor ban on medication abortion. That’s why state-level measures on abortion in the 2026 midterms elections will be so consequential in the fight for reproductive rights.

This November, voters will decide the fate of abortion rights in four states. Three of those states — Idaho, Nevada, and Virginia — have initiatives that would protect abortion rights in the state. Missouri has an amendment on the ballot that undoes the results of the referendum two years ago, in which voters approved a measure to enshrine reproductive freedom in the state constitution.

Here’s a closer look at the stakes for abortion rights in each of those four states:

If you thought Missouri just did this, you’re not wrong. After Roe v. Wade was struck down in 2022, Missouri became the first state to enact a total abortion ban, without exceptions for rape or incest. But Missourians weren’t okay with that. In the 2024 general election, despite overwhelmingly going for Trump, Missouri voted to enshrine the right to abortion in the state constitution, becoming the first state to overturn an abortion ban by the direct vote of the people. That should have been the end of it — abortion was a protected right that could not be infringed by lawmakers in the state. Abortion providers and advocates began challenging the state’s restrictions in court, including an essential ban on providing medication abortion, and won.

But far right leaders like the Attorney General Catherine Hanaway and the Republicans in the Missouri state legislature have simply refused to accept defeat. Now, they’ve enjoined a near-total abortion ban (this one does contain exceptions for rape and incest, as well as fetal anomalies) with a ban on gender-affirming care for minors. Nevermind that gender-affirming care for minors is already banned in Missouri. This is a nakedly political attempt to use transphobic backlash to undo the will of the people and sneak in a ban on abortion.

If Missouri voters approve Amendment 3, nearly all abortions and gender-affirming care for minors will be banned, and a host of anti-abortion measures will also become law, including a ban on public funding for abortion and TRAP (Targeted Regulation of Abortion Providers) laws that are designed to make it more difficult for reproductive health clinics to operate.

Idaho has had a total abortion ban in effect since August of 2022, and it has had devastating consequences for the state. After its draconian abortion ban went into effect, the state lost approximately 35 percent of its practicing obstetricians, and at least three rural hospitals have shuttered their labor and delivery departments as a result. This last left Idahoans with an acute lack of access to reproductive health care, and left the remaining OBGYNs in the state overwhelmed with an increased patient load. The results are catastrophically long wait times — in Boise, it can take up to nine months to secure an appointment for an annual exam.

With Proposition 1 on their midterm ballot, Idaho voters now have a chance to reverse some of that harm. This ballot initiative would establish a fundamental right to reproductive freedom and privacy in the state. If voters approve this initiative, it would give providers and advocates an avenue to challenge the state’s total abortion ban in court and potentially legalize abortion services.

Voters in these four states will have a rare opportunity to directly vote on the status of bodily autonomy, and the results could affect us all.

While Proposition 1 is a step in the right direction, it wouldn’t carry the same weight as a constitutional amendment. Instead of codifying abortion as an inherent right in the state’s constitution, Proposition 1 would instead create a “statutory right” to abortion. Statutory rights are easier to change than constitutional rights and remain subordinate to the constitution — they can be challenged in court with a lower threshold than a constitutional amendment. If Proposition 1 passes, it would hopefully ease some of the severe restrictions facing the state, but it would be the beginning of that fight, rather than the culmination of it.

Voters in Virginia, meanwhile, have the opportunity to enshrine the right to an abortion in their state’s constitution with Question 1, the Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment. Unlike Idaho, abortion is currently legal in Virginia up to 26 weeks and 6 days of pregnancy. Virginia and North Carolina remain the only two states with legal abortion past 12 weeks in the Southeast, and Virginia is the only Southeastern state with legal abortion services past the first trimester. As such, Virginia has become a critical hub for abortion seekers — from 2020 to 2025, the number of abortions performed in the state has increased by 114 percent.

If passed, this amendment likely wouldn’t change the current status of abortion access in Virginia. The provision does allow for some restrictions on abortion in the third trimester, though abortion is currently banned in the third trimester now. But it would establish the right to an abortion in the state constitution, which makes it harder to restrict the procedure overall. And it would be an important signal to the region that it’s not just enough for abortion to be legal — it must be constitutionally protected. Abortion is a fundamental right, and by enshrining it in the state constitution, Virginians would show that no matter what the federal government does, this right will remain intact within their state’s borders.

Like Virginia, abortion is currently legal in Nevada, but with Question 6, the Right to Abortion Initiative on the 2026 ballot, Nevadans have a chance to enshrine the right to an abortion in the state constitution. This effort, led by Nevadans for Reproductive Freedom, would guarantee the right to an abortion in Nevada until the point of fetal viability, or the point at which the fetus can survive outside the womb, typically considered 24 weeks. Essentially, Question 6 would codify Roe v. Wade in Nevada and make it far more difficult for abortion opponents to ban abortion before the third trimester. It would, however, leave the door open to restrictions on abortion in the third trimester, which are already incredibly rare; only 1 percent of all abortions occur after 21 weeks.

Nevada, like Virginia, has also experienced a surge in abortion seekers since the fall of Roe in 2022. In the first year after Dobbs, Nevada experienced a 33.5 percent increase in the number of abortions. As a neighboring state to Idaho, which currently has a total abortion ban in effect, Nevada has been a mini-haven in the region for abortion seekers. If Question 6 passes, it will further entrench abortion rights in the state.

So much is at stake in this year’s midterm elections. With an entrenched autocrat in the White House, a sycophantic Congress willing to do his bidding, and a Supreme Court willing to rubber stamp some of his most heinous policies, defending the constitution and our fundamental rights has never been more essential. The White House has intentionally delayed attacks on abortion until after the midterm election, assuming that they will be politically unpopular. Voters in these four states will have a rare opportunity to directly vote on the status of bodily autonomy, and the results could affect us all.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

title: Fransa’da eylemler sürüyor: Gündüz yüz binler yürüdü akşam polis saldırdı
content:
Fransa’da son haftalarda hayat pahalılığına, ücretlerin yetersizliğine ve kamu hizmetlerindeki sorunlara karşı büyüyen protestolar, 24 Ekim Cumartesi günü de farklı kentlerde sürdü. Protestolara yüz binlerce kişi katılırken akşam saatlerinde polis saldırısı başladı.

Fransa genelinde gün boyu düzenlenen eylemlere İçişleri Bakanlığına göre 410 bin, sendikalara göre 800 bin kişi katıldı.

Gündüz saatlerinde yüz binlerce kişinin katıldığı eyleme müdahale etmeyen polis, akşam saatlerinde göz yaşartıcı gaz ve tazyikli su kullandı.

17 Ekim'den bu yana 2 bin 700'den fazla kişinin tutuklandığı belirtildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Amanda Audi
title: Uma sala e 90 empresas: o mapa que liga Flávio Bolsonaro, Willer Tomaz e o careca do INSS
content:
Uma única sala comercial em Águas Claras, no Distrito Federal, reúne no papel o candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, seu advogado e amigo, Willer Tomaz, e parte da rede investigada pelo desvio de dinheiro de aposentados do INSS, que inclui Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes, o “careca do INSS”. 

A Agência Pública levantou os registros das 90 empresas que já tiveram sede na sala 2601 do Edifício Connect Towers e achou 25 citadas nas investigações sobre as fraudes no INSS, ligadas a Antunes, além de outras seis pessoas indiciadas pela CPMI.




Um elo entre essas empresas é a Voga, um escritório de contabilidade instalado no prédio desde 2009, cujos e-mail e endereço se repetem nos cadastros obtidos pela 

Pública

. O ICL Notícias 

revelou

 a ligação da sala com uma empresa de Flávio, a Bravo Grafeno (que já teve Jair Bolsonaro como sócio), e 16 outras ligadas ao escândalo do INSS, em setembro deste ano.




A Voga é comandada pela família dos Reis. Alexandre Caetano dos Reis, sócio do “careca”, está preso desde dezembro, apontado pela Polícia Federal (PF) como contador no esquema de lavagem de dinheiro. A irmã dele, Letícia Reis, administra o escritório de advocacia de Flávio Bolsonaro, como 

revelou

 a 

Pública

 em 2022.




A 

Pública

 também descobriu que Willer Tomaz, investigado junto ao senador no STF por lavagem de dinheiro com bets, defende a Voga num processo trabalhista.

 Ele também tem uma empresa em nome da irmã na mesma sala.
















Na mesma sala onde foi registrada a empresa de Flávio Bolsonaro, existem outras 25 citadas no escândalo do INSS




Uma contabilidade, muitas empresas




A principal conexão entre as muitas empresas registradas na sala 2601 é a Voga, uma empresa de contabilidade. O primeiro documento que a 

Pública

 encontrou é de 2009, quando a empresa foi registrada no Edifício Connect Towers, em salas ao lado da 2601, segundo a Receita Federal.
















Na mesma sala do edifício comercial, estão registradas 90 empresas, incluindo a que tem Flávio Bolsonaro como sócio




Um dos sócios da empresa é Alexandre Caetano dos Reis, preso desde dezembro do ano passado por decisão do ministro André Mendonça do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). Segundo a 

PF

, Caetano atuou como contador de diversas empresas do “careca” em atividades de lavagem de dinheiro no esquema de fraudes do INSS.




A Voga tem uma empresa “filha”, chamada Voga Serviços, essa sim com sede na sala 2601 e aberta em 2021. O termo filha não é ao acaso: essa segunda Voga tem no registro Paula Batista dos Reis, a filha de Alessandra Batista Perdigão dos Reis, esposa de Alexandre.

 O email de Paula é usado tanto no cadastro da Voga Serviços, quanto da Voga Contabilidade aberta em 2009.




É neste endereço da sala 2601, além dos emails de Paula e da própria Voga que se conectam um emaranhado de 90 empresas nas quais os membros da família dos Reis se revezam nas sociedades.




É importante lembrar que a família dos Reis está ligada diretamente a Flávio Bolsonaro: é a irmã de Alexandre, Letícia Caetano dos Reis, que administra o escritório de advocacia de Flávio — o mesmo escritório 

registrado

 na mansão milionária do senador, cuja compra foi 

financiada

 pelo Banco de Brasília (BRB) e que teve o empréstimo quitado em tempo recorde.
















Amigo de Flávio, Willer atua como advogado para empresa de contabilidade que liga empresas registradas na sala 2601




Willer Tomaz defende Voga em processo contra família dos Reis




A 

Pública

 tentou visitar a sala da Voga na manhã desta sexta-feira, 23 de outubro. O acesso, contudo, foi barrado. A circulação no edifício foi limitada após a imprensa ter revelado o local.




Os 90 empreendimentos registrados na sala 2601 têm atividades variadas. A maioria é de consultoria e serviços administrativos (26), seguido por construção civil e incorporação imobiliária (19), comércio (16) e holdings (13).
















Entrada da sala foi limitada após revelação de que Flávio Bolsonaro e careca do INSS têm escritório no mesmo local




A 

Pública

 teve acesso a um processo trabalhista que reforça os laços entre as empresas da sala.

 É o mesmo processo 

noticiado

 pelo Uol neste sábado, 24 de outubro. Na ação, um profissional afirma que trabalhou mais de dez anos para a Voga, até 2025. A pessoa afirma que a jornada de trabalho era extenuante e não remunerada. 

E ainda que foi obrigada pela chefia a apagar dados que poderiam comprometer a empresa junto ao escândalo do INSS.

 Alexandre atuaria diretamente como “chefe”, dando ordens de destruição dos arquivos.




Na peça, o profissional acusa os sócios de usarem “CPFs de terceiros, comumente denominados “laranjas”, para frustrar o cumprimento de obrigações legais e dificultar a satisfação de créditos trabalhistas”. A acusação contra a Voga é direcionada à família dos Reis: Alexandre; Alessandra, sua esposa; e Paula.




Quem defende a Voga e os membros da família dos Reis nesse processo é Willer Tomaz.




A reportagem procurou a assessoria do advogado para esclarecer qual a relação dele com a Voga e as demais empresas registradas na sala 2601, além de um posicionamento sobre a acusação trabalhista, mas ainda não tivemos resposta até a publicação. O espaço segue aberto à manifestação.




Outra ligação também aproxima Willer das empresas registradas na sala 2601. É a Bonsucesso, consultoria criada em setembro de 2025 na sala da Voga.

 A 

Pública

 apurou que, no mesmo dia em que foi constituída, ela foi transferida para um endereço em São Paulo.




A empresa foi registrada em nome de Lídia Mazelli, 

apontada

 como suposta laranja de Tomaz por assinar os papéis de 14 empreendimentos ligados a ele. Depois, 

em julho de 2026, a Bonsucesso foi transferida para Flavia Oliveira Correa Tomaz, esposa de Willer.




A família Bolsonaro e a sala 2601




A ligação mais direta entre a família Bolsonaro e as empresas da sala 2601 é a Bravo Grafeno, loja online que vende capacetes estilizados com as cores da bandeira do Brasil, como mostrou o ICL. A grafeno foi aberta em junho de 2024.




A sociedade reúne Flávio, seu irmão Carlos Bolsonaro, recém-eleito senador por Santa Catarina, e outras três pessoas. O ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro também já fez parte do quadro societário.




A Bravo Grafeno também tem como sócio Pedro Luiz Dias Leite, ex-sócio de Marcello de Oliveira Lopes, marqueteiro de Flávio que deixou a pré-campanha em maio. A saída ocorreu após a crise envolvendo a revelação pelo Intercept Brasil de que o senador pediu R$ 134 milhões ao ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro para o filme Dark Horse, sobre seu pai. A PF também identificou um 

repasse

 de Lopes para a produtora do filme.




Os outros sócios da empresa de capacetes são o ex-assessor do senador, Fernando Nascimento Pessoa, que chegou a ser investigado no caso da rachadinha no gabinete de Flávio na Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro, e o personal trainer Paulo Giordano Bernardi.




A 

Pública

 descobriu que outra pessoa ligada à família Bolsonaro tem um negócio na sala 2601: o fisioterapeuta Kleber Caiado, que atende Jair desde agosto de 2025

, quando o ex-presidente passou a cumprir prisão domiciliar. Quando ele foi condenado, a defesa do ex-mandatário pediu autorização para que as sessões de fisioterapia com Caiado tivessem continuidade na cela da PF.
















Acusados de envolvimento com o “careca do INSS” também têm empresas no endereço




Mais empresas ligadas ao escândalo do INSS na sala 2601




Era 23 de setembro de 2025, a Polícia Legislativa da Câmara dos Deputados foi acionada para 

prender

 o economista e empresário Rubens Oliveira Costa, por falso testemunho e ocultação de documentos na Comissão Parlamentar de Inquéritos (CPMI) do INSS. O pedido foi feito tanto pelo presidente da comissão, o deputado Carlos Viana (Podemos-MG), quanto pelo relator Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), após mais de sete horas de reunião.




Costa foi ouvido na condição de testemunha, amparado por um 

habeas corpus,

 concedido pelo ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) Luiz Fux. Ele não respondeu à maioria das perguntas feitas pelos parlamentares sobre a sua relação com o “careca” e teria apresentado contradições em suas falas, o que levantou a suspeita dos interrogadores.




A suspeita de relação com a fraude do INSS se estende também às três empresas em seu nome: a Fronteira Consultoria e Gestão Financeira, a Silva e Rodrigues Consultoria e Assessoria Empresarial (Brain Consultoria) e a Capify Gestão e Consultoria Financeira. 

A 

Pública

 apurou que essas três empresas dividem a mesma sala 2601 com a Voga.




Procurada, a defesa do empresário afirmou que “Rubens Oliveira Costa jamais foi proprietário de qualquer empresa, tendo atuado exclusivamente como administrador financeiro contratado”, afirmou o advogado Bernardo Simões Coelho. Ele acrescentou ainda que o seu cliente não mantinha negócios com políticos ou integrantes da administração pública. 

Leia a nota na íntegra.




Já o técnico em contabilidade e empresário Milton Salvador de Almeida Júnior aparece como sócio ou diretor de pelo menos 11 empresas de ramos variados, e em oito delas, ele divide a sociedade com o “careca”. Em 19 de setembro de 2025, ele foi convocado para depor na CPMI do INSS, após nove requerimentos, sendo um deles do próprio relator da comissão, o deputado Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) – hoje vice na chapa com Flávio Bolsonaro.




Quatro empresas ligadas a Almeida Júnior estão na sala 2601 do Contect Tower: a Prospect Consultoria Empresarial,  Plural Intermediações de Negócios, RPLD Construtora e Incorporadora e a DRPL Comercialização e Locação de Veículos.




A Prospect Consultoria é citada no relatório da Polícia Federal como uma das empresas utilizadas para executar o esquema fraudulento. A empresa foi fundada em janeiro de 2022, está em atividade e tem capital social de R$ 30 mil. Procurada, a defesa de Almeida Junior não respondeu aos questionamentos da reportagem. O espaço segue aberto para manifestações.




Romeu Carvalho Antunes, filho de Antunes, também aparece na sala 2601, em sociedade com Almeida Junior na Plural Intermediações de Negócios.




Romeu foi preso na manhã de 18 de dezembro de 2024 na Operação Sem Descontos. Além da relação com as empresas do pai, a PF identificou um aumento abrupto nos rendimentos do filho do “careca”, cujo crescimento seria incompatível com o seu histórico profissional.




Procurada pela reportagem, a defesa de Romeu disse que ele tem apenas 1% de participação na Plural, e que suas empresas estão baixadas há um ano, não mantendo “relação comercial com absolutamente ninguém mais”. Além disso, a defesa alega que ele nunca teve qualquer relação com a família Bolsonaro e Willer Tomaz. Os advogados também informaram que não tiveram acesso à informação de que o patrimônio era incompatível. 




Já Cristiana Alcântara Alves Zago é sócia de oito empresas na sala 2601. Segundo o relatório final da CPMI do INSS, ela figuraria como “suporte” contratada pelo “careca”

 para, inicialmente, realizar serviços de consultoria relacionados à estruturação de negócios no setor de cannabis medicinal”, e teria recebido créditos bancários de investigados no esquema de fraudes envolvendo o INSS. Ela teria recebido ao menos R$ 610 mil dos investigados, de acordo com o relatório.




Procurada, a defesa de Zago não respondeu.




Já a defesa de Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes, o “careca do INSS”, afirmou que ele não tem nenhum elo com as empresas de Willer Tomaz e nem da família Bolsonaro.
